principality-of-heitersheim.t: The seat of the Knights of Saint John's Grand Priory of Germany, whose grand priors ruled a tiny principality in the Breisgau.
principality-of-heitersheim.o: The [[e:knights-hospitaller|Order of Saint John]], the Knights Hospitaller, acquired [[e:heitersheim|Heitersheim]] near [[e:freiburg-im-breisgau|Freiburg]] in the 13th century, and from 1505 it was the residence of the order's Grand Prior of [[e:germany|Germany]]. In 1548 [[e:charles-v-holy-roman-emperor|Emperor Charles V]] raised the grand prior to a prince of the empire, making Heitersheim a small principality.
principality-of-heitersheim.r: The grand prior governed [[e:heitersheim|Heitersheim]] and a few neighbouring villages directly and oversaw the order's [[e:commandery|commanderies]] in [[e:germany|Germany]], which sent knights and revenues to [[e:malta|Malta]]. The principality lay within the sphere of [[s:further-austria|Further Austria]], and the [[e:habsburg-dynasty|Habsburgs]] disputed its full independence. It remained Catholic.
principality-of-heitersheim.e: In 1806 [[e:baden|Baden]] annexed [[e:heitersheim|Heitersheim]], and the Grand Priory was dissolved. The priors' castle, the Malteserschloss, survives as a convent and museum.

principality-of-schaumburg-lippe.t: Tiny north German state at Bückeburg that survived from the Thirty Years' War to 1918, famed for a soldier-count's military academy.
principality-of-schaumburg-lippe.o: When the counts of Schaumburg died out in 1640, their lands were divided in 1647. Philip, a younger brother of the Count of Lippe, received a share including [[e:buckeburg|Bückeburg]] and [[e:stadthagen|Stadthagen]], founding Schaumburg-Lippe, while the rest went to [[s:electorate-of-hesse|Hesse-Kassel]] and Brunswick-[[e:luneburg|Lüneburg]].
principality-of-schaumburg-lippe.r: [[e:william-count-of-schaumburg-lippe|Count William]], in the 18th century, was a military reformer who built the island fortress of [[e:wilhelmstein|Wilhelmstein]] in the [[e:steinhuder-meer|Steinhuder Meer]] and ran a school for officers where [[e:gerhard-von-scharnhorst|Gerhard von Scharnhorst]] trained. He also commanded allied forces in Portugal in 1762. The princely title came in 1807. The economy relied on farming and sandstone quarries, and the princes became wealthy landowners.
principality-of-schaumburg-lippe.e: Schaumburg-Lippe joined the [[s:german-confederation|German Confederation]] and in 1871 the [[s:german-empire|German Empire]] as one of its smallest states. Prince [[e:adolf-ii-prince-of-schaumburg-lippe|Adolf II]] abdicated in November 1918, and it continued as the [[s:free-state-of-schaumburg-lippe|Free State of Schaumburg-Lippe]].

principality-of-schwarzburg-rudolstadt.t: A small Thuringian principality ruled from the Heidecksburg above Rudolstadt, whose last prince was the last German monarch to abdicate in 1918.
principality-of-schwarzburg-rudolstadt.o: The counts of [[s:county-of-schwarzburg|Schwarzburg]] were among the oldest noble houses of [[e:thuringia|Thuringia]]. After the death of Count [[e:gunther-xli-of-schwarzburg-arnstadt|Günther XLI]] in 1583 and a period of joint rule, the [[e:treaty-of-stadtilm|Treaty of Stadtilm]] of 1599 divided the County of Schwarzburg between brothers, creating the [[e:rudolstadt|Rudolstadt]] and [[e:sondershausen|Sondershausen]] lines.
principality-of-schwarzburg-rudolstadt.r: The counts, raised to princes in 1710, ruled two separate blocks of territory, the Upper Lordship around [[e:rudolstadt|Rudolstadt]] and part of the Lower Lordship in northern [[e:thuringia|Thuringia]], and gradually shook off [[e:saxons|Saxon]] overlordship. The Lutheran court rebuilt the [[e:heidecksburg|Heidecksburg]] palace in [[e:baroque|Baroque]] style after a fire in 1735. [[e:friedrich-schiller|Schiller]] first met [[e:johann-wolfgang-von-goethe|Goethe]] in Rudolstadt in 1788.
principality-of-schwarzburg-rudolstadt.e: Schwarzburg-[[e:rudolstadt|Rudolstadt]] joined the [[s:german-confederation|German Confederation]] and the [[s:german-empire|German Empire]]. Its last prince, [[e:gunther-victor-prince-of-schwarzburg|Günther Victor]], who had ruled both [[s:county-of-schwarzburg|Schwarzburg]] states since 1909, abdicated in November 1918, the last German monarch to do so. In 1920 it merged into the [[s:free-state-of-thuringia|Free State of Thuringia]].

phimai-regime.t: A short-lived Siamese breakaway regime on the Khorat plateau after Ayutthaya's fall, led by a prince of the old royal house.
phimai-regime.o: When the [[s:ayutthaya-kingdom|Ayutthaya Kingdom]] fell to the Burmese in 1767, its provincial governors and princes set up rival regimes. At [[e:phimai|Phimai]], on the [[e:khorat-plateau|Khorat plateau]], [[e:thepphiphit|Prince Thepphiphit]], a son of King [[e:borommakot|Borommakot]] who had earlier been exiled to [[e:ceylon|Ceylon]], gathered followers and claimed authority as the legitimate heir.
phimai-regime.r: The regime controlled the north-eastern plateau around [[e:phimai|Phimai]] and [[e:nakhon-ratchasima|Nakhon Ratchasima]], a region with old [[e:khmer-empire|Khmer]] temples and Lao and Khmer populations. Its power rested on [[e:thepphiphit|Thepphiphit's]] royal prestige and local nobles. It was one of five main contenders for the Siamese succession.
phimai-regime.e: In 1768 [[e:taksin|Taksin]] of the [[s:thonburi-kingdom|Thonburi Kingdom]] attacked [[e:phimai|Phimai]] and defeated its forces. [[e:thepphiphit|Thepphiphit]] was captured and executed, and the plateau was brought under Thonburi rule.

principality-of-halberstadt.t: Former prince-bishopric in the Harz foreland turned into a Brandenburg-Prussian principality by the Peace of Westphalia.
principality-of-halberstadt.o: The Bishopric of [[e:halberstadt|Halberstadt]], founded around 804, had become Lutheran during the [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]] and was ruled by administrators. At the [[e:peace-of-westphalia|Peace of Westphalia]] in 1648 it was secularised and given to [[e:brandenburg|Brandenburg]] as compensation for its claims to [[s:duchy-of-pomerania|Pomerania]], becoming the Principality of Halberstadt.
principality-of-halberstadt.r: The principality was governed by Brandenburg-Prussian officials through a provincial government, with the cathedral chapter kept as a Protestant institution. It was a fertile grain-growing region with a sizeable garrison. In the 18th century the poet [[e:johann-wilhelm-ludwig-gleim|Johann Wilhelm Ludwig Gleim]] lived there as cathedral secretary, gathering a circle of writers.
principality-of-halberstadt.e: After [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia's]] defeat in 1806, [[e:halberstadt|Halberstadt]] was given to the [[s:kingdom-of-westphalia|Kingdom of Westphalia]] in 1807. It returned to Prussia in 1815 and became part of the [[e:province-of-saxony|Province of Saxony]]; the town is now in [[e:saxony-anhalt|Saxony-Anhalt]].

pharsalus.t: Thessalian city of Phthiotis, long ruled by aristocratic families, whose plain saw Caesar's victory over Pompey in 48 BCE.
pharsalus.o: Pharsalus stood on a hill above the plain of the [[e:enipeus-thessaly|Enipeus]] in southern [[e:thessaly|Thessaly]], in the region Greek myth linked to [[e:achilles|Achilles's]] [[e:phthia|Phthia]]. It became a city in the Archaic period and one of the leading members of the [[s:thessalian-league|Thessalian League]] with [[s:larissa|Larissa]] and [[s:tyranny-of-pherae|Pherae]].
pharsalus.r: Pharsalus was dominated by aristocratic families such as the Echecratidae. In the 370s BCE [[e:polydamas-of-pharsalus|Polydamas]] governed the city and was forced to submit to [[e:jason-of-pherae|Jason of Pherae]]. [[e:daochus-ii|Daochus]], a Pharsalian, served [[e:philip-ii-of-macedon|Philip II]] as tetrarch of [[e:thessaly|Thessaly]] and set up a family monument at [[s:delphi|Delphi]].
pharsalus.e: Pharsalus passed under Macedonian rule, was freed by [[e:rome|Rome]] in 196 BCE and came under Roman control by 146 BCE. In 48 BCE [[e:julius-caesar|Julius Caesar]] defeated [[e:pompey|Pompey]] nearby at the [[e:battle-of-pharsalus|Battle of Pharsalus]].

principality-of-achaea.t: Most successful crusader state in Greece, a French chivalric society in the Peloponnese whose story is told in the Chronicle of the Morea.
principality-of-achaea.o: In 1205 [[e:william-of-champlitte|William of Champlitte]] and [[e:geoffrey-i-of-villehardouin|Geoffrey of Villehardouin]], crusaders of the [[e:fourth-crusade|Fourth Crusade]], conquered the western [[e:peloponnese|Peloponnese]] after defeating local [[e:greeks|Greeks]] at the [[e:battle-of-the-olive-grove-of-koundouros|Olive Grove of Koundouros]]. Geoffrey I took control after Champlitte left, and his family ruled for three generations under the nominal suzerainty of the [[s:latin-empire|Latin Empire]].
principality-of-achaea.r: The principality was a model feudal state, divided into twelve baronies, such as [[e:karytaina|Karytaina]], [[e:akova|Akova]] and [[s:barony-of-patras|Patras]], whose lords sat in the prince's council. Its laws were codified as the [[e:assizes-of-romania|Assizes of Romania]]. The court at [[e:andravida|Andravida]] and the port of [[e:glarentza|Clarentza]] were famed for French culture, and the castle of Chlemoutsi guarded the coast. Greek archons kept their lands.
principality-of-achaea.e: Captured at [[e:battle-of-pelagonia|Pelagonia]] in 1259, [[e:william-ii-of-villehardouin|William II of Villehardouin]] ceded [[e:mystras|Mistras]] and [[e:monemvasia|Monemvasia]] to [[s:byzantium|Byzantium]], creating the base of the [[s:despotate-of-the-morea|Despotate of the Morea]]. Angevin, Navarrese and [[e:zaccaria|Zaccaria]] rulers followed. [[e:thomas-palaiologos|Thomas Palaiologos]] annexed the rest of the principality in 1430-1432.

principality-of-wales.t: The Welsh state built by the princes of Gwynedd and recognised by England in 1267, the high point of native Welsh political independence.
principality-of-wales.o: [[e:llywelyn-the-great|Llywelyn ap Iorwerth]], Llywelyn the Great, made [[s:kingdom-of-gwynedd|Gwynedd]] dominant in [[e:wales|Wales]], and at [[e:aberdyfi|Aberdyfi]] in 1216 the other Welsh rulers accepted his overlordship. His grandson [[e:llywelyn-ap-gruffudd|Llywelyn ap Gruffudd]] took the title [[e:prince-of-wales|Prince of Wales]], which [[e:henry-iii-of-england|Henry III]] recognised in the [[e:treaty-of-montgomery|Treaty of Montgomery]] in 1267.
principality-of-wales.r: The principality was a feudal overlordship over lesser Welsh lords such as those of [[s:powys-fadog|Powys Fadog]] and [[s:powys-wenwynwyn|Powys Wenwynwyn]]. Its princes ruled from Gwynedd's courts, including Aber Garth Celyn, and used Welsh law, stone castles such as [[e:dolwyddelan-castle|Dolwyddelan]] and a growing chancery.
principality-of-wales.e: Llywelyn's refusal to do homage to Edward I led to war in 1277, and a revolt begun by his brother [[e:dafydd-ap-gruffydd|Dafydd]] in 1282 ended in conquest. He was killed near [[e:cilmeri|Cilmeri]] in 1282, and his brother Dafydd executed in 1283. The [[e:statute-of-rhuddlan|Statute of Rhuddlan]] of 1284 annexed the principality to the [[s:kingdom-of-england|Kingdom of England]].

principality-of-koknese.t: A small Orthodox principality on the Daugava, vassal of Polotsk, swallowed by the crusading Bishopric of Riga in 1208.
principality-of-koknese.o: Koknese, called Kukenois by the Germans, was a fortified centre on the [[e:western-dvina|Daugava]] in what is now [[s:republic-of-latvia|Latvia]], inhabited by [[e:latgalians|Latgalians]] and [[s:selonians|Selonians]]. By the late 12th century it was ruled by a prince of Rus' origin, [[e:vyachko|Vyachko]], as a tributary of the [[s:principality-of-polotsk|Principality of Polotsk]]. It is known almost entirely from the chronicle of [[e:henry-of-livonia|Henry of Livonia]].
principality-of-koknese.r: The principality controlled a stretch of the [[e:western-dvina|Daugava]] trade route between [[e:polotsk|Polotsk]] and the Baltic and collected tribute from the surrounding Baltic peoples. Its prince and his retinue were [[e:eastern-orthodox-church|Orthodox]] Christians, while most of the population remained pagan. When German crusaders founded Riga in 1201, Koknese came under pressure from [[e:albert-of-riga|Bishop Albert]].
principality-of-koknese.e: In 1207 [[e:vyachko|Vyachko]] gave half his land to the [[e:bishop|bishop]] in return for protection. Quarrels with German knights followed, and in 1208 he burned his castle and fled to Rus'. The bishop built a stone castle on the site, and Vyachko died defending [[e:tartu|Tartu]] against the crusaders in 1224.

patna-state.t: A Chauhan Rajput state in western Odisha, once head of a cluster of eighteen hill forts, whose last Maharaja became Chief Minister of Orissa.
patna-state.o: Tradition holds that [[e:ramai-deva|Ramai Deva]], a [[e:chauhan|Chauhan Rajput]], founded the dynasty at Patnagarh in the mid-14th century and became overlord of the surrounding chiefs, a group known as the Athara Garhjat, or eighteen forts. A branch of the family later founded [[s:sambalpur-state|Sambalpur State]].
patna-state.r: [[e:patna|Patna]] was a large inland state of [[e:rice|rice]] fields and forest, home to [[e:kondh|Kondh]], Binjhal and other communities. Its capital later moved to [[e:balangir|Bolangir]]. Under the [[e:maratha-empire|Marathas]] it was tributary to the [[e:bhonsles|Bhonsles]] of the [[s:nagpur-kingdom|Nagpur Kingdom]], and under the British it belonged to the [[e:orissa-tributary-states|Orissa Tributary States]] from 1905.
patna-state.e: [[e:patna|Patna]] merged into [[e:odisha|Orissa]] on 1 January 1948. Its last ruler, [[e:rajendra-narayan-singh-deo|Rajendra Narayan Singh Deo]], entered politics and served as Chief Minister of Orissa from 1967 to 1971. The area is now [[e:balangir|Bolangir]] district.

principality-of-rostov.t: An appanage principality based on the ancient town of Rostov on Lake Nero, gradually bought out by Moscow.
principality-of-rostov.o: [[e:rostov|Rostov]] is one of the oldest towns of north-eastern Rus', first mentioned in 862 in the land of the [[e:merya|Finnic Merya]], and was long the seat of a [[e:bishop|bishop]]. In 1207 [[e:vsevolod-the-big-nest|Vsevolod the Big Nest]] gave it to his eldest son Konstantin, and his descendants ruled it as a principality within the [[s:vladimir-suzdal|Vladimir-Suzdal]] lands.
principality-of-rostov.r: [[e:rostov|Rostov]] was a religious and commercial centre with a long tradition of chronicle writing. Its prince [[e:vasilko-konstantinovich|Vasilko Konstantinovich]] was captured and killed by the [[e:mongols|Mongols]] after the [[e:battle-of-the-sit-river|Battle of the Sit]] in 1238. Later the principality was split between two lines, each ruling half the town, and it became a minor power between [[e:moscow|Moscow]] and Tver.
principality-of-rostov.e: [[e:moscow|Moscow's]] influence grew through the 14th century, and the [[e:rostov|Rostov]] princes sold the first half of their rights to Moscow in the 15th century. In 1474 the last princes sold the remaining half to [[e:ivan-iii|Ivan III]]. The town remained a great church centre, and its kremlin was built by [[e:iona-sysoyevich|Metropolitan Jonah]] in the 17th century.

cr.a: Goran tek-en, following request by and knowledge from Veverve

principality-of-hereti.t: A small Christian principality between Georgia and Caucasian Albania whose Queen Dinar is remembered for bringing it into the Georgian Orthodox church.
principality-of-hereti.o: Hereti lay along the Alazani and Iori rivers and around [[e:shaki-azerbaijan|Shaki]], a borderland between [[s:kingdom-of-iberia|Kartli]] and the old [[s:caucasian-albania|Caucasian Albania]]. In the 9th century, as Arab power waned, a local dynasty with ties to the former [[s:mihranid-principality-of-albania|Mihranid Principality of Albania]] established its own rule, sometimes called the kings of the Rans.
principality-of-hereti.r: Its population mixed [[e:georgians|Georgians]], [[e:armenians|Armenians]] and Caucasian [[e:albanians|Albanians]], and its church long followed the anti-Chalcedonian Armenian tradition. In the 10th century Queen [[e:dinar|Dinar]], of Georgian [[e:bagrationi-dynasty|Bagratid]] descent, converted the principality to [[e:georgian-orthodox-church|Georgian Orthodoxy]]. Its rulers fought the [[s:emirate-of-tbilisi|Emirate of Tbilisi]] and competed with [[s:principality-of-kakheti|Kakheti]], controlling farmland and routes to the Caspian.
principality-of-hereti.e: Hereti was absorbed by the [[s:principality-of-kakheti|Principality of Kakheti]] in the late 10th century, and around 1010 the two formed the [[s:kingdom-of-kakheti-hereti|Kingdom of Kakheti-Hereti]]. The name survived as a province of the Georgian kingdom.

principality-of-brandenburg-bayreuth.t: The Franconian margraviate of the Hohenzollerns, ruled from Kulmbach and Bayreuth and made a rococo showcase by Margravine Wilhelmine.
principality-of-brandenburg-bayreuth.o: When the [[e:house-of-hohenzollern|Hohenzollern]] rulers of the [[s:burgraviate-of-nuremberg|Burgraviate of Nuremberg]] divided their Franconian lands in 1398, the territory 'above the mountains' around [[e:kulmbach|Kulmbach]] and the [[e:plassenburg|Plassenburg]] went to [[e:john-iii-burgrave-of-nuremberg|John III]]. After the family gained the [[s:margraviate-of-brandenburg|Margraviate of Brandenburg]] in 1415, its Franconian principalities were usually ruled by younger sons with the title of margrave.
principality-of-brandenburg-bayreuth.r: Margrave [[e:albert-alcibiades-margrave-of-brandenburg-kulmbach|Albert Alcibiades]] devastated [[e:franconia|Franconia]] in his wars of the 1550s. The territory was Lutheran, and the court moved from [[e:kulmbach|Kulmbach]] to [[e:bayreuth|Bayreuth]] in the early 17th century. [[e:wilhelmine-of-bayreuth|Margravine Wilhelmine]], sister of [[e:frederick-the-great|Frederick the Great]], and her husband [[e:frederick-margrave-of-brandenburg-bayreuth|Frederick]] made Bayreuth a cultural centre, building the Margravial Opera House and founding the university at [[e:erlangen|Erlangen]] in 1743.
principality-of-brandenburg-bayreuth.e: In 1769 [[e:bayreuth|Bayreuth]] passed to [[e:charles-alexander-margrave-of-brandenburg-ansbach|Charles Alexander]], margrave of the [[s:principality-of-brandenburg-ansbach|Principality of Brandenburg-Ansbach]], who in 1791 ceded both principalities to the [[s:kingdom-of-prussia|Kingdom of Prussia]]. [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]] gave Bayreuth to the [[s:kingdom-of-bavaria|Kingdom of Bavaria]] in 1810. [[e:richard-wagner|Richard Wagner]] later built his festival [[e:theatre|theatre]] in the town.

pre-islamic-mecca.t: The sanctuary town of the Kaaba, governed by the clans of Quraysh, whose trade and pilgrimage made it the birthplace of Islam.
pre-islamic-mecca.o: Arab tradition credits [[e:qusayy-ibn-kilab|Qusayy ibn Kilab]] with gathering the [[e:quraysh|Quraysh]] clans in [[e:mecca|Mecca]] in the 5th century and taking control of the [[e:kaaba|Kaaba]], a shrine already visited by pilgrims from across western [[e:arabia|Arabia]]. He distributed the hereditary offices of the sanctuary: guarding the Kaaba, giving water and food to pilgrims and holding the war banner.
pre-islamic-mecca.r: [[e:mecca|Mecca]] had no king. Clans such as [[e:banu-hashim|Hashim]], [[e:banu-makhzum|Makhzum]], [[e:banu-umayya|Umayya]] and Abd al-Dar shared power through an assembly of elders. The town lived on the pilgrimage, the sacred months that protected trade, nearby fairs such as [[e:souq-ukaz|Ukaz]] and caravans to [[s:syrian-arab-republic|Syria]] and [[s:republic-of-yemen|Yemen]]. The [[e:kaaba|Kaaba]] housed images of many deities, [[e:hubal|Hubal]] chief among them, and [[e:allah|Allah]] was recognised as a high god.
pre-islamic-mecca.e: Muhammad, of the [[e:banu-hashim|clan of Hashim]], began preaching around 610, met growing opposition and left for [[e:medina|Medina]] in 622. After years of war, [[e:mecca|Mecca]] surrendered to the [[s:islamic-state-of-medina|Islamic state of Medina]] in 630; the idols of the [[e:kaaba|Kaaba]] were destroyed and the town became the holiest city of [[e:islam|Islam]].

phitsanulok-regime.t: A breakaway regime in northern Siam led by the governor of Phitsanulok, one of the rivals Taksin had to overcome after Ayutthaya's fall.
phitsanulok-regime.o: After the Burmese sack of the [[s:ayutthaya-kingdom|Ayutthaya Kingdom]] in 1767, the governor of [[e:phitsanulok|Phitsanulok]], a Thai noble named Rueang, declared himself ruler of the northern provinces of the central plain, an area that included the old cities of [[s:sukhothai-kingdom|Sukhothai]] and [[e:phichit|Phichit]]. He took royal style as Chao Phitsanulok.
phitsanulok-regime.r: The regime controlled the upper [[e:chao-phraya-river|Chao Phraya]] and Nan river region, a rich [[e:rice|rice]]-growing area with strong defensive positions. It repelled an early attack by [[e:taksin|Taksin]] in 1768, during which Taksin was wounded. Little else is known of its administration, which probably continued the provincial structures of [[s:ayutthaya-kingdom|Ayutthaya]].
phitsanulok-regime.e: Chao [[e:phitsanulok|Phitsanulok]] died in 1768, soon after crowning himself, and his territory was seized by the neighbouring [[s:sawangkhaburi-regime|Sawangkhaburi regime]] of [[e:chao-phra-fang|Chao Phra Fang]]. [[e:taksin|Taksin]] of the [[s:thonburi-kingdom|Thonburi Kingdom]] conquered the whole north in 1770.

portuguese-mombasa.t: Portugal's main stronghold on the Swahili coast, centred on Fort Jesus, which fell to Oman after a siege of nearly three years.
portuguese-mombasa.o: After decades of hostility with [[s:mombasa|Mombasa]], the Portuguese occupied the island in 1593, built [[e:fort-jesus|Fort Jesus]] to an Italian design and installed the ruler of [[s:malindi|Malindi]] as sultan. The fort became the headquarters of Portuguese power north of [[s:portuguese-mozambique|Mozambique]], guarding the routes to [[e:india|India]].
portuguese-mombasa.r: A Portuguese captain commanded the fort and collected customs, while a client [[e:swahili|Swahili]] sultan governed the town. Relations were tense: in 1631 [[e:sultan|Sultan]] [[e:yusuf-ibn-al-hasan|Yusuf ibn al-Hasan]], raised as a Catholic in [[e:goa|Goa]] as Dom Jeronimo Chingulia, returned to [[e:islam|Islam]], massacred the Portuguese garrison and briefly held the fort before abandoning it. Catholic missions had little lasting success.
portuguese-mombasa.e: The [[s:omani-empire|Omani Empire]], after expelling the Portuguese from [[e:muscat|Muscat]], besieged [[e:fort-jesus|Fort Jesus]] from 1696 until it fell in December 1698. Portugal briefly regained it in 1728 to 1729, but [[s:mombasa|Mombasa]] passed to Omani governors and then the [[s:mazrui-sultanate|Mazrui Sultanate]]. Fort [[e:jesus|Jesus]] is a [[e:unesco-world-heritage-site|UNESCO World Heritage Site]].

provisional-government-of-schleswig-hols.t: Rebel German government set up in Kiel in 1848 to free Schleswig and Holstein from Denmark, which fought the First Schleswig War and lost.
provisional-government-of-schleswig-hols.o: In March 1848, as revolutions spread across [[e:europe|Europe]], [[e:denmark|Denmark's]] new liberal government moved to tie [[e:schleswig|Schleswig]] more closely to the kingdom. German nationalists in the duchies responded by forming a provisional government at [[e:kiel|Kiel]] on 24 March, led by [[e:wilhelm-hartwig-beseler|Wilhelm Hartwig Beseler]] and [[e:prince-frederick-of-noer|Prince Frederick of Noer]], claiming both duchies for the [[s:german-confederation|German Confederation]].
provisional-government-of-schleswig-hols.r: The government raised a [[e:schleswig-holstein|Schleswig-Holstein]] army and received support from [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] and the [[s:german-confederation|German Confederation]], whose troops fought the [[e:danes|Danes]] in 1848-1849. It governed from [[e:kiel|Kiel]] with the backing of the German-speaking estates, while Danish-minded inhabitants of northern [[e:schleswig|Schleswig]] opposed it. Great-power pressure forced Prussia to make peace with [[e:denmark|Denmark]] in 1850.
provisional-government-of-schleswig-hols.e: Fighting alone, the [[e:schleswig-holstein|Schleswig-Holstein]] army was defeated at [[e:battle-of-isted|Isted]] (Idstedt) in July 1850. Under pressure from [[e:austria|Austria]] and [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]], the government dissolved in early 1851, and Danish rule was restored. The [[e:london|London]] Protocol of 1852 confirmed the settlement, but the dispute reignited in the war of 1864.

pashalik-of-vidin.t: Rebel domain of Osman Pazvantoğlu on the Danube, who defied the Ottoman sultan and let loose raiders across Bulgaria and Wallachia.
pashalik-of-vidin.o: [[e:osman-pazvantoglu|Osman Pazvantoğlu]], a [[e:janissaries|janissary]] from [[e:vidin|Vidin]], opposed [[e:sultan|Sultan]] [[e:selim-iii|Selim III's]] military reforms and seized control of Vidin around 1794. He gathered disbanded janissaries and kardzhali bandits, and in 1798 defeated a large Ottoman army sent to besiege the town. Unable to remove him, the sultan pardoned him and appointed him pasha of Vidin.
pashalik-of-vidin.r: [[e:osman-pazvantoglu|Pazvantoğlu]] ruled as a warlord with his own army and treasury, and conducted his own diplomacy with [[e:russia|Russia]] and [[e:france|France]]. His bands raided much of [[s:bulgaria|Bulgaria]] and crossed into [[s:principality-of-wallachia|Wallachia]], burning [[e:craiova|Craiova]] in 1800. He backed the [[e:janissaries|janissary]] dahije who seized power in the [[e:sanjak-of-smederevo|Pashalik of Belgrade]], whose abuses helped provoke the Serbian uprising of 1804.
pashalik-of-vidin.e: [[e:osman-pazvantoglu|Pazvantoğlu]] died in 1807, and his successors soon returned [[e:vidin|Vidin]] to Ottoman control. His career showed the weakness of central authority under [[e:selim-iii|Selim III]]; Bulgarian memory recalls the kardzhali years as a time of terror.

principality-of-leiningen.t: A Palatinate county ruled by the Leiningen family from the Haardt hills, raised to a principality in 1779 before being swept away by the French.
principality-of-leiningen.o: Count Emich I of Leiningen appears around 1128, with castles in the [[e:haardt|Haardt]] hills of the [[s:electoral-palatinate|Palatinate]]. The original line died out in 1220, and the lands passed through a sister to the [[e:saarbrucken|Saarbrücken]] family, who took the Leiningen name. The family split in 1317 into Leiningen-Hardenburg and Leiningen-Dagsburg.
principality-of-leiningen.r: The counts ruled scattered territories in the [[s:electoral-palatinate|Palatinate]] and [[e:alsace|Alsace]], with castles at Hardenburg and Altleiningen. They were often in rivalry with the Electoral Palatinate. The Hardenburg line moved its residence to [[e:bad-durkheim|Dürkheim]] in the 18th century and was raised to princely rank in 1779.
principality-of-leiningen.e: French revolutionary forces annexed the left bank of the [[e:rhine|Rhine]] in the 1790s. In 1803 the princes received former church lands at [[e:amorbach|Amorbach]] in [[e:franconia|Franconia]], but these were mediatised in 1806 and divided between [[e:baden|Baden]], [[e:bavaria|Bavaria]] and [[e:hesse|Hesse]]. [[e:queen-victoria|Queen Victoria's]] half-brother [[e:carl-3rd-prince-of-leiningen|Carl]] was a prince of Leiningen.

principality-of-yuryev-polsky.t: A small appanage of the Vladimir-Suzdal lands, best known for the richly carved Cathedral of Saint George.
principality-of-yuryev-polsky.o: [[e:yuri-dolgoruky|Yuri Dolgoruky]] founded [[e:yuryev-polsky|Yuryev-Polsky]] in 1152 in the open fields, the polye, between Vladimir and [[e:pereslavl-zalessky|Pereslavl-Zalessky]]. When [[e:vsevolod-the-big-nest|Vsevolod the Big Nest's]] sons divided his lands, [[e:sviatoslav-vsevolodovich|Sviatoslav Vsevolodovich]] received [[e:tartu|Yuryev]] in 1212 and it became a separate [[e:appanage|appanage]].
principality-of-yuryev-polsky.r: It was a small agricultural principality whose rulers were closely tied to Vladimir. [[e:sviatoslav-i-of-kiev|Sviatoslav]] built the [[e:st-georges-cathedral-yuryev-polsky|Cathedral of Saint George]] between 1230 and 1234, whose walls are covered with carved stone reliefs of saints, beasts and plants. The town was sacked by the [[e:mongols|Mongols]] in 1238.
principality-of-yuryev-polsky.e: [[e:sviatoslav-i-of-kiev|Sviatoslav's]] descendants held the principality as a minor [[e:appanage|appanage]]. It came under the control of the [[s:grand-duchy-of-moscow|Grand Duchy of Moscow]] in the first half of the 14th century, and by around 1340 its separate princely rule had ended.

provisional-government-of-lithuania-1941.t: Lithuanian government formed during the June Uprising of 1941, which hoped to restore independence but was dissolved by the Germans after six weeks.
provisional-government-of-lithuania-1941.o: When [[e:germany|Germany]] invaded the [[s:soviet-union|Soviet Union]] on 22 June 1941, the [[e:lithuanian-activist-front|Lithuanian Activist Front]] launched the June Uprising against Soviet rule. On 23 June it proclaimed restored independence on [[e:kaunas|Kaunas]] radio and formed a Provisional Government. Its intended head, [[e:kazys-skirpa|Kazys Škirpa]], was held in [[e:berlin|Berlin]], so [[e:juozas-ambrazevicius|Juozas Ambrazevičius]] served as acting prime minister.
provisional-government-of-lithuania-1941.r: The government tried to reverse Soviet nationalisation and re-establish Lithuanian institutions, but the Germans did not recognise it. It also issued anti-Jewish regulations while killings of [[e:jews|Jews]] by German units and Lithuanian collaborators began, a record that remains deeply controversial.
provisional-government-of-lithuania-1941.e: The Germans set up their own civil administration within [[s:reichskommissariat-ostland|Reichskommissariat Ostland]], and on 5 August 1941 the Provisional Government dissolved itself rather than become a German instrument. [[s:republic-of-lithuania|Lithuania]] remained under German occupation until 1944 and then became the [[s:lithuanian-soviet-socialist-republic|Lithuanian Soviet Socialist Republic]] again.

principality-of-mstislavl.t: An appanage of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania in eastern Belarus, ruled by descendants of Algirdas until 1529.
principality-of-mstislavl.o: [[e:mstislavl|Mstislavl]], on the [[e:sozh-river|Sozh]], was a town of the old [[e:smolensk|Smolensk]] lands. After the [[s:grand-duchy-of-lithuania|Grand Duchy of Lithuania]] took it in the mid 14th century, it was given as an [[e:appanage|appanage]] to sons of [[e:algirdas|Algirdas]], first [[e:karigaila|Karigaila]] and later [[e:lengvenis|Lingvenis]], whose descendants ruled it for over a century.
principality-of-mstislavl.r: [[e:mstislavl|Mstislavl]] was a frontier principality facing [[e:smolensk|Smolensk]] and [[e:moscow|Moscow]], with a largely [[e:eastern-orthodox-church|Orthodox]] Ruthenian population. [[e:lengvenis|Lingvenis]], who ruled from about 1390 to 1431, also served as a commander in [[e:veliky-novgorod|Novgorod]] and fought at [[e:battle-of-grunwald|Grunwald]]. His line, and later the Mstislavsky family through marriage, held the land as [[e:vassal|vassals]] of the grand duke.
principality-of-mstislavl.e: In 1526 Prince Fyodor Mstislavsky fled to [[e:moscow|Moscow]], where his family became leading boyars. [[e:mstislavl|Mstislavl]] reverted to the grand duke, and in 1529 it lost its separate status, later becoming the Mstislavl Voivodeship.

principality-of-novosil.t: One of the Upper Oka principalities, founded by a son of Mikhail of Chernigov and caught between Lithuania and Moscow.
principality-of-novosil.o: After [[e:mikhail-of-chernigov|Mikhail of Chernigov]] was killed at [[e:batu-khan|Batu]]'s camp in 1246, his lands were divided among his sons. [[e:semyon-mikhailovich-of-novosil|Semyon Mikhailovich]] received [[e:hlukhiv|Glukhov]] and [[e:novosil|Novosil]] on the upper [[e:oka-river|Oka]], and Novosil became the senior seat of a group of small principalities known as the Upper Oka principalities.
principality-of-novosil.r: These were frontier lands, open to raids from the steppe and the [[s:golden-horde|Golden Horde]]. [[e:novosil|Novosil]] itself was ruined in the 14th century, and the princes moved their seat to [[e:odoyev|Odoyev]], so the line became known as the Odoyevsky. Related branches ruled [[e:belyov|Belyov]] and Vorotynsk. They usually served the [[s:grand-duchy-of-lithuania|Grand Duchy of Lithuania]] while bargaining with [[e:moscow|Moscow]].
principality-of-novosil.e: In the late 15th century the Upper [[e:oka-river|Oka]] princes went over to [[e:ivan-iii|Ivan III]], and the peace of 1494 between [[e:moscow|Moscow]] and [[s:grand-duchy-of-lithuania|Lithuania]] confirmed their lands as part of the [[s:grand-duchy-of-moscow|Grand Duchy of Moscow]]. The Odoyevsky and Vorotynsky princes became prominent Russian nobles.

provisional-military-dictatorship-of-mug.t: A short-lived regime of Russian settlers in the Mughan steppe of south-eastern Azerbaijan, which resisted the Azerbaijan Democratic Republic in 1918-1919.
provisional-military-dictatorship-of-mug.o: The Mughan steppe and Lankaran area had many Russian settler villages, including [[e:molokans|Molokans]] and [[e:old-believers|Old Believers]], established in the 19th century. When the Russian administration collapsed in 1918, local settlers and former Russian officers formed their own armed government at Lankaran rather than accept the new Azerbaijani state.
provisional-military-dictatorship-of-mug.r: The regime was run by Russian officers and settler councils as a military administration, aligned with the anti-Bolshevik [[e:white-movement|White movement]] of the [[s:russian-state|Russian State]] and receiving some British and White support. It controlled the Russian villages and fought local [[e:talysh|Talysh]] and Azerbaijani forces loyal to the [[s:azerbaijan-democratic-republic|Azerbaijan Democratic Republic]]. Little is known of its internal administration beyond military rule.
provisional-military-dictatorship-of-mug.e: In spring 1919 a regional congress of Mughan settlers turned against the military leadership, and the [[e:communist-party-of-the-soviet-union|Bolsheviks]] took power, proclaiming the [[s:mughan-soviet-republic|Mughan Soviet Republic]]. The region was soon brought under Azerbaijani control.
provisional-military-dictatorship-of-mug.re: Russian Orthodox Christianity; Molokan and Old Believer communities

principality-of-anhalt-kothen.t: One of the Anhalt principalities of central Germany, home of the Fruitbearing Society and of the court where Johann Sebastian Bach wrote much of his instrumental music.
principality-of-anhalt-kothen.o: [[s:principality-of-anhalt|Anhalt]] was partitioned in 1603 among the sons of Prince [[e:joachim-ernest-prince-of-anhalt|Joachim Ernst]], and [[e:kothen|Köthen]] fell to Ludwig, who founded the line of Anhalt-Köthen. Ludwig was a learned prince who in 1617 co-founded the [[e:fruitbearing-society|Fruitbearing Society]] (Fruchtbringende Gesellschaft), the first society devoted to refining the German language.
principality-of-anhalt-kothen.r: The principality was a small Calvinist state in the Saale-[[e:elbe|Elbe]] region, living from agriculture. Its court is best known for Prince [[e:leopold-prince-of-anhalt-kothen|Leopold]], a music lover who employed [[e:johann-sebastian-bach|Johann Sebastian Bach]] as [[e:kapellmeister|Kapellmeister]] from 1717 to 1723, when the [[e:brandenburg-concertos|Brandenburg Concertos]] and much chamber music were composed. In 1665 the line of [[s:principality-of-anhalt-plotzkau|Anhalt-Plötzkau]] inherited [[e:kothen|Köthen]], continuing it under a new branch.
principality-of-anhalt-kothen.e: [[e:kothen|Köthen]] became a duchy in 1807 under [[e:napoleon|Napoleon's]] patronage and joined the [[s:german-confederation|German Confederation]]. When its last duke died without heirs in 1847, the territory passed to [[s:principality-of-anhalt-dessau|Anhalt-Dessau]] and [[s:principality-of-anhalt-bernburg|Anhalt-Bernburg]], and was absorbed into the united [[s:duchy-of-anhalt|Duchy of Anhalt]] by 1863.

principality-of-masserano.t: A tiny papal fief in northern Piedmont ruled by the Ferrero-Fieschi family until it was sold to the kings of Sardinia in 1767.
principality-of-masserano.o: Masserano and Crevacuore, small towns in the hills between [[e:biella|Biella]] and the [[e:sesia|Sesia]] valley, belonged to the Fieschi family and then to the Ferrero, who took the Fieschi name. In 1598 [[e:pope-clement-viii|Pope Clement VIII]] raised them to a principality held as a fief of the [[s:vatican-city|Holy See]], giving the family sovereign status.
principality-of-masserano.r: The Ferrero-Fieschi princes governed a few thousand subjects, minted coins and kept a small court, while often serving foreign rulers as soldiers and diplomats, especially [[e:spain|Spain]]. Surrounded by the [[s:duchy-of-savoy|Duchy of Savoy]], the state survived through papal protection and its rulers' connections abroad. Little else is recorded of its government.
principality-of-masserano.e: The [[e:house-of-savoy|House of Savoy]], now kings of the [[s:kingdom-of-sardinia|Kingdom of Sardinia]], long sought to absorb the enclave. In 1767 the prince ceded his [[e:sovereignty|sovereignty]] to [[e:charles-emmanuel-iii-of-sardinia|Charles Emmanuel III]], ending the principality.

praisos.t: East Cretan city of the Eteocretans, a pre-Greek people whose language survives in a few undeciphered inscriptions.
praisos.o: Praisos stood on hills in the interior of eastern [[e:crete|Crete]]. [[e:herodotus|Herodotus]] and [[e:strabo|Strabo]] say its people were [[e:eteocretans|Eteocretans]], 'true Cretans' descended from the island's pre-Greek inhabitants, and the settlement continued from the end of the [[e:bronze-age|Bronze Age]] into the [[e:iron-age|Iron Age]].
praisos.r: Inscriptions from Praisos, written in the Greek alphabet between the 6th and 3rd centuries BCE, record a non-[[e:greek-language|Greek language]] that remains undeciphered. The city controlled the sanctuary of [[e:diktaean-zeus|Diktaean Zeus]] for a time and quarrelled with [[s:itanos|Itanos]]. It had harbours on both coasts of eastern [[e:crete|Crete]].
praisos.e: Praisos was destroyed by its neighbour [[s:hierapytna|Hierapytna]] c. 145 BCE, which took over its land. Its inscriptions are the main evidence for the Eteocretan language.
praisos.re: Cretan religion; cult of Diktaean Zeus

principality-of-hatuqwai.t: A small princely Circassian tribe of the western Caucasus foothills, known mainly from 18th- and 19th-century Russian and travellers' accounts.
principality-of-hatuqwai.o: The Hatuqwai were one of the smaller aristocratic [[e:circassians|Adyghe]] tribes of [[s:circassia|Circassia]], living between the [[e:belaya-river-kuban|Belaya]] and [[e:laba-river|Laba]] rivers near the [[s:principality-of-temirgoy|Temirgoy]]. Little is known of their early history; they appear as a distinct community in sources of the 18th century.
principality-of-hatuqwai.r: Like other princely Circassian groups, they were ruled by princes and nobles over free peasants and serfs, following the [[e:circassians|Adyghe]] code of conduct and living by farming, [[e:horse-breeding|horse breeding]] and livestock. They usually acted in alliance with the neighbouring [[s:principality-of-temirgoy|Temirgoy]] and shared in the wider Circassian struggle against [[e:russia|Russia]].
principality-of-hatuqwai.e: The [[s:russian-empire|Russian Empire]] conquered their lands in the final campaigns of the [[e:russo-circassian-war|Russo-Circassian War]], completed in 1864. Almost all Hatuqwai were expelled to the [[s:ottoman-empire|Ottoman Empire]], where their descendants were absorbed into the Circassian diaspora.

provisional-government-of-saskatchewan.t: The government declared by Louis Riel at Batoche in 1885, whose defeat ended the North-West Resistance and led to Riel's execution.
provisional-government-of-saskatchewan.o: [[e:metis|Métis]] families who had moved west from [[e:red-river-colony|Red River]] to the [[e:south-saskatchewan-river|South Saskatchewan River]] after 1870 feared losing their river lots to surveys, while [[e:cree|Cree]] nations faced hunger after the buffalo vanished. In 1884 they invited [[e:louis-riel|Louis Riel]] back from [[e:montana|Montana]]. When [[e:ottawa|Ottawa]] failed to respond to petitions, Riel proclaimed a provisional government at [[e:batoche|Batoche]] in March 1885.
provisional-government-of-saskatchewan.r: Its council was called the Exovedate, a name [[e:louis-riel|Riel]] coined meaning 'from the flock', and it mixed politics with Riel's religious ideas. [[e:gabriel-dumont|Gabriel Dumont]] led its military. [[e:metis|Métis]] fighters defeated the North-West Mounted Police at [[e:battle-of-duck-lake|Duck Lake]] on 26 March, while [[e:cree|Cree]] warriors from [[e:big-bear|Big Bear's]] and [[e:poundmaker|Poundmaker's]] bands fought separately at [[e:frog-lake-massacre|Frog Lake]], [[e:battleford|Battleford]] and Cut Knife.
provisional-government-of-saskatchewan.e: General [[e:frederick-middleton|Frederick Middleton's]] North-West Field Force won at [[e:batoche|Batoche]] in May 1885. [[e:louis-riel|Riel]] surrendered and was hanged in [[e:regina-saskatchewan|Regina]] that November, and eight [[e:cree|Cree]] and [[e:assiniboine|Assiniboine]] men were hanged at [[e:battleford|Battleford]]. The execution deeply divided English and French [[s:canada|Canada]].

principality-of-starodub.t: A small appanage on the Klyazma whose princely line produced the Pozharsky family, including the liberator of Moscow in 1612.
principality-of-starodub.o: Starodub on the [[e:klyazma|Klyazma]], north-east of Vladimir, became the seat of [[e:ivan-vsevolodovich-of-starodub|Ivan Vsevolodovich]], youngest son of [[e:vsevolod-the-big-nest|Vsevolod the Big Nest]]. He is usually said to have received it from his brother Yaroslav in 1238, after the Mongol invasion, rather than in 1218.
principality-of-starodub.r: Starodub was a small forest principality within the [[s:vladimir-suzdal|Vladimir-Suzdal]] lands and later a minor player between [[e:moscow|Moscow]] and the [[s:golden-horde|Golden Horde]]. Its prince [[e:fyodor-ivanovich-of-starodub|Fyodor Ivanovich]] was killed at the Horde in 1330. The family divided its land into tiny estates held by branches such as the Pozharsky, Ryapolovsky, Gagarin and Romodanovsky princes.
principality-of-starodub.e: By the mid 15th century the Starodub princes had become servitors of the [[s:grand-duchy-of-moscow|Grand Duchy of Moscow]], and their land was merged into Muscovite territory. Their descendant [[e:dmitry-pozharsky|Prince Dmitry Pozharsky]] led the militia that freed [[e:moscow|Moscow]] from Polish occupation in 1612.

principality-of-boisbelle.t: A sovereign enclave in Berry, exempt from royal taxes, where Henry IV's minister Sully built the planned town of Henrichemont.
principality-of-boisbelle.o: Boisbelle was a lordship in [[e:berry-province|Berry]] whose holders had long claimed [[e:sovereignty|sovereignty]], a privilege tolerated by the French crown. In 1597 [[e:maximilien-de-bethune-duke-of-sully|Maximilien de Béthune]], later duke of Sully, [[e:henry-iv-of-france|Henry IV]]'s chief minister, bought it and confirmed its status as a principality.
principality-of-boisbelle.r: [[e:maximilien-de-bethune-duke-of-sully|Sully]] founded the town of [[e:henrichemont|Henrichemont]] in 1608, named after the king, on a regular grid around a central square, hoping to attract Protestant settlers and artisans. Its inhabitants paid no royal taxes, which drew some settlers, though the town never grew as planned. The Béthune family ruled the enclave for over 150 years.
principality-of-boisbelle.e: In 1766 the [[e:maximilien-de-bethune-duke-of-sully|Duke of Sully's]] descendants sold the principality to [[e:louis-xv|Louis XV]], ending its [[e:sovereignty|sovereignty]], and it became part of the [[s:kingdom-of-france|Kingdom of France]].
ru: Maximilien de Béthune, Duke of Sully

province-of-senegambia.t: Britain's first crown colony in Africa, created after the capture of French Saint-Louis and lost again during the American War of Independence.
province-of-senegambia.o: British forces captured the French post of [[e:saint-louis-senegal|Saint-Louis]] in 1758 during the [[e:seven-years-war|Seven Years War]]. The [[e:treaty-of-paris-1763|Treaty of Paris]] of 1763 left it in British hands, and in 1765 Parliament created the Province of [[e:senegambia|Senegambia]], joining Saint-Louis with the British post of [[e:kunta-kinteh-island|Fort James]] on the [[e:the-gambia|Gambia]] river. It was the first British crown colony on the African continent.
province-of-senegambia.r: A governor at [[e:saint-louis-senegal|Saint-Louis]] ruled a small garrison, merchants and the town's Afro-French population. The colony existed mainly to control the gum arabic trade of the [[e:senegal|Senegal]] river, valuable for textile dyeing, and to profit from the [[e:atlantic-slave-trade|slave trade]]. The first governor, [[e:charles-ohara|Charles O'Hara]], quarrelled with traders and local rulers, and disease took a heavy toll on the garrison.
province-of-senegambia.e: [[e:france|France]] recaptured [[e:saint-louis-senegal|Saint-Louis]] in 1779 during the [[e:american-revolutionary-war|American War of Independence]]. The [[e:treaty-of-versailles|Treaty of Versailles]] of 1783 restored [[e:senegal|Senegal]] to France as [[s:french-senegal|French Senegal]] and left [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] the [[e:the-gambia|Gambia]], which later became the [[s:gambia-colony-and-protectorate|Gambia Colony and Protectorate]].

principality-of-bari.t: A short-lived Lombard principality carved out of Norman Apulia by a local strongman before Roger II brought it to heel.
principality-of-bari.o: In the weak reign of Duke William II of the [[s:duchy-of-apulia-and-calabria|Duchy of Apulia and Calabria]], the citizen [[e:grimoald-alferanites|Grimoald Alferanites]] took power in [[e:bari|Bari]] in 1119 and called himself prince. Bari, the old seat of Byzantine government in [[e:italy|Italy]], had since 1087 housed the relics of [[e:saint-nicholas|Saint Nicholas]], which made it a major pilgrimage centre.
principality-of-bari.r: Little is known of [[e:grimoald-alferanites|Grimoald]]'s government beyond his alliances with [[e:venice|Venice]] and with other rebellious Apulian barons. He relied on [[e:bari|Bari's]] port, its merchant community and the prestige of the [[e:basilica-of-san-nicola|Basilica of San Nicola]]. He submitted to [[e:roger-ii-of-sicily|Roger II of Sicily]] in 1129 when Roger took over [[e:apulia|Apulia]].
principality-of-bari.e: [[e:grimoald-alferanites|Grimoald]] joined a baronial revolt against [[e:roger-ii-of-sicily|Roger II]], who captured [[e:bari|Bari]] in 1132 and sent him as a prisoner to [[e:sicily|Sicily]]. Bari was absorbed into the [[s:kingdom-of-sicily|Kingdom of Sicily]].

punadra-state.t: A minor chiefship of the Mahi Kantha country in northern Gujarat, one of its many small hereditary estates.
punadra-state.o: Punadra was one of the petty estates of the [[e:mahi-kantha-agency|Mahi Kantha]] region, held by a local chiefly family from around 1600. Its origins are poorly documented.
punadra-state.r: Its ruler held a few villages, paid tribute through the [[e:gaekwads|Gaekwads of Baroda]] and was supervised by the [[e:mahi-kantha-agency|British Mahi Kantha Agency]]. Standard references preserve few details of its history.
punadra-state.e: Punadra was merged into [[s:bombay-presidency|Bombay Province]] in 1948 and became part of [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]] in 1960.

ptolemaic-kingdom-of-cyrene.t: Cyrenaica as a separate Ptolemaic kingdom, created for a quarrelling royal brother and finally bequeathed to Rome.
ptolemaic-kingdom-of-cyrene.o: In 163 BCE [[e:rome|Rome]] settled a quarrel between the brothers [[e:ptolemy-vi-philometor|Ptolemy VI]] and [[e:ptolemy-viii-physcon|Ptolemy VIII]] by giving the younger [[e:cyrenaica|Cyrenaica]] as a separate kingdom, detached from the [[s:ptolemaic-empire|Ptolemaic Empire]]. Ptolemy VIII, nicknamed Physcon, ruled from [[s:republic-of-cyrene|Cyrene]] but constantly sought more, including [[e:cyprus|Cyprus]].
ptolemaic-kingdom-of-cyrene.r: After an assassination attempt in 155 BCE, [[e:ptolemy-viii-physcon|Ptolemy VIII]] published a will, preserved on a stone at [[s:republic-of-cyrene|Cyrene]], leaving his kingdom to [[e:rome|Rome]] if he died without heirs. In 145 BCE he became king of [[e:egypt|Egypt]] and Cyrene was reunited with it. Around 116 BCE the kingdom was separated again for his son [[e:ptolemy-apion|Ptolemy Apion]]. The Greek cities of the [[e:pentapolis-cyrenaica|Pentapolis]] kept their councils, and the region exported grain, horses and the last of its silphium.
ptolemaic-kingdom-of-cyrene.e: [[e:ptolemy-apion|Ptolemy Apion]] died in 96 BCE and bequeathed [[e:cyrenaica|Cyrenaica]] to [[e:rome|Rome]]. The Senate left the cities free at first, then organised the province of [[s:roman-cyrenaica|Roman Cyrenaica]] in 74 BCE, ending three centuries of Ptolemaic involvement in the region.

principality-of-hohenlohe-schillingsfurs.t: Franconian principality of a Catholic Hohenlohe branch, whose family later produced a German chancellor.
principality-of-hohenlohe-schillingsfurs.o: The [[s:county-of-hohenlohe|Hohenlohe]] family ruled lands in north-eastern Württemberg and western [[e:franconia|Franconia]] from the [[e:middle-ages|Middle Ages]] and divided into many lines. The Catholic Waldenburg branch included [[e:schillingsfurst|Schillingsfürst]], on a hill near [[e:rothenburg-ob-der-tauber|Rothenburg]], and in 1744 its head was raised to the rank of prince of the Empire.
principality-of-hohenlohe-schillingsfurs.r: The principality was small, Catholic and rural, governed from a baroque palace at [[e:schillingsfurst|Schillingsfürst]], which still houses a falconry. It belonged to the [[e:franconian-circle|Franconian Circle]] and shared the [[s:county-of-hohenlohe|Hohenlohe]] family's collective vote. Its princes served the emperors in court and army posts.
principality-of-hohenlohe-schillingsfurs.e: In 1806 the principality was mediatised and placed under the [[s:kingdom-of-bavaria|Kingdom of Bavaria]]. The family remained prominent: [[e:chlodwig-zu-hohenlohe-schillingsfurst|Chlodwig zu Hohenlohe-Schillingsfürst]] was Bavarian prime minister and German chancellor from 1894 to 1900.

principality-of-lichtenberg.t: Detached Saar-area exclave of Saxe-Coburg, given at Vienna and sold to Prussia after political unrest.
principality-of-lichtenberg.o: The [[e:congress-of-vienna|Congress of Vienna]] promised the [[e:ernest-i-duke-of-saxe-coburg-and-gotha|Duke of Saxe-Coburg-Saalfeld]] territory for his services against [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]]. In 1816 he received a district around [[e:st-wendel|St. Wendel]] on the upper [[e:nahe|Nahe]] and [[e:blies|Blies]], far from [[e:coburg|Coburg]], which was named the Principality of Lichtenberg in 1819 after the castle near [[e:kusel|Kusel]].
principality-of-lichtenberg.r: The principality had about 25,000 inhabitants, Catholic and Protestant, living from farming and small crafts. It was governed by [[e:coburg|Coburg]] officials who were unpopular, and the region was touched by the radical democratic movement around the [[e:hambach-festival|Hambach Festival]] of 1832. Unrest in [[e:st-wendel|St. Wendel]] in 1832 required troops to restore order.
principality-of-lichtenberg.e: Duke [[e:ernest-i-duke-of-saxe-coburg-and-gotha|Ernest I]] found the distant territory hard to govern and sold it to [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] in 1834 for an annual payment. It became the district of [[e:st-wendel|St. Wendel]] in the [[e:rhine-province|Rhine Province]] and is now part of [[e:saarland|Saarland]].

principality-of-catalonia.t: The union of Catalan counties under the House of Barcelona, a land of parliaments, merchant cities and its own laws within the Crown of Aragon.
principality-of-catalonia.o: Catalonia grew out of the counties of the [[s:marca-hispanica|Marca Hispanica]], gradually gathered under the [[s:county-of-barcelona|County of Barcelona]]. In 1162 [[e:alfonso-ii-of-aragon|Alfonso II]] inherited both [[e:barcelona|Barcelona]] and the [[s:kingdom-of-aragon|Kingdom of Aragon]], and the Catalan counties became one constituent of the [[s:crown-of-aragon|Crown of Aragon]]. The name Principality became usual in the 14th century.
principality-of-catalonia.r: Catalonia was governed under the [[e:usatges-of-barcelona|Usatges of Barcelona]] and its [[e:catalan-courts|Corts]], whose standing committee, the [[e:generalitat-de-catalunya|Generalitat]], was created in 1359. [[e:barcelona|Barcelona's]] merchants traded across the [[e:mediterranean|Mediterranean]] under the [[e:consulate-of-the-sea|Consulate of the Sea]]. Catalan literature flourished with [[e:ramon-llull|Ramon Llull]] and [[e:ausias-march|Ausiàs March]], while the [[e:black-death|Black Death]] and civil war of 1462-1472 brought decline.
principality-of-catalonia.e: The [[e:reapers-war|Reapers' War]] of 1640 led to the loss of [[e:roussillon|Roussillon]] to [[e:france|France]] in 1659. Siding with the [[s:county-of-habsburg|Habsburg]] claimant in the [[e:war-of-the-spanish-succession|War of the Spanish Succession]], [[e:barcelona|Barcelona]] fell in 1714, and the [[e:nueva-planta-decrees|Nueva Planta]] decree of 1716 abolished Catalonia's institutions.

principality-of-wallachia.t: Romanian principality between the Carpathians and the Danube, home of Mircea the Elder and Vlad the Impaler, which united with Moldavia to form Romania.
principality-of-wallachia.o: Romanian voivodeships such as the [[s:voivodeship-of-litovoi|Voivodeship of Litovoi]] and the [[s:voivodeship-of-seneslau|Voivodeship of Seneslau]] were united under [[e:basarab-i|Basarab I]] in the early 14th century; tradition dates the founding to about 1310. In 1330 Basarab defeated [[e:charles-i-of-hungary|Charles I of Hungary]] at [[e:battle-of-posada|Posada]], securing independence.
principality-of-wallachia.r: The voivode (prince) ruled with boyars, and the throne was elective within the ruling family, which bred constant rivalry. [[e:mircea-the-elder|Mircea the Elder]] (1386–1418) fought the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]] at [[e:battle-of-rovine|Rovine]], and [[e:vlad-the-impaler|Vlad III]] fought them in 1462. From the 15th century Wallachia paid tribute to the Ottomans but kept its own rulers and [[e:eastern-orthodox-church|Orthodox]] church. [[e:michael-the-brave|Michael the Brave]] briefly united Wallachia, [[s:principality-of-transylvania|Transylvania]] and [[s:principality-of-moldavia|Moldavia]] in 1600. From 1716 to 1821 the Ottomans appointed [[e:phanariotes|Phanariot Greek]] princes.
principality-of-wallachia.e: After the [[e:treaty-of-adrianople-1829|Treaty of Adrianople]] in 1829 Wallachia came under Russian protection. In 1859 both it and the [[s:principality-of-moldavia|Principality of Moldavia]] elected [[e:alexandru-ioan-cuza|Alexandru Ioan Cuza]] as prince, creating the [[s:united-principalities|United Principalities]], which became [[s:kingdom-of-romania|Romania]].

perak-sultanate.t: A Malay sultanate founded by a son of Malacca's last sultan, grown rich on tin, and still reigning as a state of Malaysia.
perak-sultanate.o: After [[e:malacca|Malacca]] fell to Portugal in 1511, [[e:mahmud-shah-of-malacca|Sultan Mahmud Shah]]'s eldest son, Raja Muzaffar, was invited by the people of the [[e:perak-river|Perak River]] valley to be their ruler. He was installed around 1528 as [[e:sultan|Sultan]] [[e:muzaffar-shah-i|Muzaffar Shah I]], founding a dynasty that still reigns.
perak-sultanate.r: Perak's wealth came from [[e:tin|tin]], mined in the [[e:kinta-valley|Kinta]] and [[e:larut|Larut]] valleys. In the 17th century it fell under the [[s:aceh-sultanate|Aceh Sultanate]] and later signed tin contracts with the [[e:dutch|Dutch]]. Its succession system rotated the throne among branches of the royal family, and the court settled at [[e:kuala-kangsar|Kuala Kangsar]].
perak-sultanate.e: Disputes over succession and violent rivalry among Chinese [[e:tin|tin]] miners led to the [[e:pangkor-treaty-of-1874|Pangkor Treaty of 1874]], which brought a British Resident. The killing of the Resident J. W. W. Birch in 1875 led to the [[e:perak-war|Perak War]]. Perak joined the [[s:federated-malay-states|Federated Malay States]] in 1895 and [[s:malaysia|Malaysia]] in 1963. [[e:nazrin-shah-of-perak|Sultan Nazrin Shah]] reigns today.

principality-of-erfurt.t: Thuringian city-state that Napoleon kept as his personal domain, scene of his 1808 congress with Tsar Alexander I.
principality-of-erfurt.o: [[e:erfurt|Erfurt]], long ruled by the [[s:electorate-of-mainz|Electorate of Mainz]], passed to [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] in 1802. After defeating Prussia at [[e:jena|Jena]] in October 1806, [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]] did not give Erfurt to any of his allies but kept it as a domain reserved to himself, the Principality of Erfurt, administered by French governors.
principality-of-erfurt.r: [[e:erfurt|Erfurt]] was governed directly by French officials and garrisoned by French troops, with the [[e:petersberg-citadel|Petersberg]] citadel as its stronghold. From September to October 1808 [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]] held the [[e:congress-of-erfurt|Congress of Erfurt]] there, meeting [[e:alexander-i-of-russia|Tsar Alexander I]] to renew their alliance and receiving [[e:johann-wolfgang-von-goethe|Goethe]] in a famous audience. The city lived from trade, crafts and garden produce.
principality-of-erfurt.e: After the defeat at [[e:leipzig|Leipzig]], [[e:erfurt|Erfurt]] was besieged by Prussian troops and its French garrison surrendered in 1814. The [[e:congress-of-vienna|Congress of Vienna]] returned the city to [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] in 1815, as part of the [[e:province-of-saxony|Province of Saxony]].

principality-of-the-hevelli.t: A Slavic principality on the Havel centred on Brandenburg, whose last prince bequeathed his land to Albert the Bear and so began the March of Brandenburg.
principality-of-the-hevelli.o: The Hevelli, also called Stodorani, were West Slavic settlers of the [[e:havel|Havel]] lands west of modern [[e:berlin|Berlin]] from the 7th or 8th century. Their chief stronghold was [[e:brandenburg-an-der-havel|Brenna]], the later [[e:brandenburg|Brandenburg]] an der Havel. In 928 to 929 the East Frankish king [[e:henry-the-fowler|Henry the Fowler]] captured it in winter across the frozen marshes.
principality-of-the-hevelli.r: The Hevelli were governed by princes from [[e:brandenburg-an-der-havel|Brenna]], controlling river crossings and fortified settlements on the [[e:havel|Havel]] and [[e:spree|Spree]]. German rule after 929 was lost in the [[e:great-slav-rising|Great Slav Rising]] of 983, and the Hevelli joined, and later stood apart from, the [[s:lutician-federation|Lutician Federation]]. The last prince, [[e:pribislav-henry|Pribislav-Henry]], became a Christian and ruled as a German ally.
principality-of-the-hevelli.e: [[e:pribislav-henry|Pribislav-Henry]] named [[e:albert-the-bear|Albert the Bear]] his heir; on his death in 1150 Albert took [[e:brandenburg|Brandenburg]], securing it in 1157 after a fight with the Slavic prince [[e:jaxa-of-kopenick|Jaxa of Köpenick]]. The Hevelli lands became the core of the [[s:margraviate-of-brandenburg|Margraviate of Brandenburg]].

provisional-central-government-of-vietna.t: A transitional French-backed Vietnamese government of 1948 to 1949, set up to prepare Bao Dai's return as head of state.
provisional-central-government-of-vietna.o: As [[e:france|France]] sought a non-communist alternative to [[e:ho-chi-minh|Ho Chi Minh]], it negotiated with former emperor [[e:bao-dai|Bao Dai]]. In 1948 General Nguyen [[s:early-ly-dynasty|Van Xuan]], president of the government of [[s:french-cochinchina|Cochinchina]], formed the Provisional Central Government of [[s:socialist-republic-of-vietnam|Vietnam]], and the [[e:ha-long-bay|Ha Long Bay]] agreement of June 1948 recognised in principle the independence and unity of [[e:vietnam|Vietnam]] within the [[s:french-fourth-republic|French Union]].
provisional-central-government-of-vietna.r: The government had little real power: [[e:france|France]] retained control of the army, finances and foreign relations, and the [[e:viet-minh|Viet Minh]] held much of the countryside. It merged the separate administrations in the north, centre and south, including the [[s:autonomous-republic-of-cochinchina|Autonomous Republic of Cochinchina]], into a single framework.
provisional-central-government-of-vietna.e: The [[e:elysee-accords|Elysee Accords]] of March 1949 between [[e:bao-dai|Bao Dai]] and President [[e:vincent-auriol|Vincent Auriol]] created the [[s:state-of-vietnam|State of Vietnam]], with Bao Dai as head of state, replacing the provisional government that year.

pathari-state.t: A small Muslim-ruled state of the Bhopal Agency in central India.
pathari-state.o: Pathari became a separate holding in the late 18th century under a Muslim family related to the Afghan nobility of the [[s:bhopal-state|Bhopal]] region.
pathari-state.r: Its Nawab ruled a few villages under the supervision of the [[e:bhopal-agency|Bhopal Agency]]. Little is recorded of its internal history.
pathari-state.e: After accession to [[e:india|India]] Pathari was merged into [[s:madhya-bharat|Madhya Bharat]] in 1948; its lands are now in [[e:madhya-pradesh|Madhya Pradesh]].

patina.t: Patina, a Neo-Hittite kingdom of the Amuq plain whose founder called it Palistin, a name that may link it to the Philistines.
patina.o: After the [[e:late-bronze-age-collapse|Late Bronze Age collapse]], a kingdom arose in the [[e:amuq-valley|Amuq plain]] around [[e:antioch|Antakya]], the former [[s:kingdom-of-mukish|Kingdom of Mukish]]. Inscriptions of [[e:taita|King Taita]], found in the temple of the storm god at [[e:aleppo|Aleppo]], call it Palistin, and its capital was [[e:tell-tayinat|Kunulua]], at Tell Tayinat.
patina.r: Its kings wrote Luwian hieroglyphic inscriptions and built palaces and temples in Syrian-Hittite style; a temple at [[e:tell-tayinat|Tell Tayinat]] yielded an Assyrian treaty tablet. [[e:assyrian-empire|Assyrians]] called the land Pattin or Unqi. It lived from the fertile plain and the route to the [[e:mediterranean|Mediterranean]].
patina.e: Patina paid tribute to [[e:ashurnasirpal-ii|Ashurnasirpal II]] and [[e:shalmaneser-iii|Shalmaneser III]] of the [[s:assyrian-empire|Assyrian Empire]]. After King Tutammu rebelled, Tiglath-Pileser III captured [[e:tell-tayinat|Kunulua]] in 738 BCE and made the land an Assyrian province.

province-of-new-york.t: The English colony created from Dutch New Netherland in 1664, whose port grew into the commercial heart of British North America.
province-of-new-york.o: In 1664 an English fleet under [[e:richard-nicolls|Richard Nicolls]] seized [[e:new-amsterdam|New Amsterdam]], which [[e:charles-ii-of-england|Charles II]] had granted to his brother [[e:james-ii-of-england|James, Duke of York]]. The colony was renamed after James, who ruled it as proprietor through governors under the [[e:dukes-laws|Duke's Laws]] of 1665. The [[e:dutch|Dutch]] briefly recaptured it in 1673 to 1674.
province-of-new-york.r: When James became king in 1685, [[e:new-york|New York]] became a royal province, and in 1688 it was folded into the [[s:dominion-of-new-england|Dominion of New England]]. Its collapse triggered [[e:leislers-rebellion|Leisler's Rebellion]] of 1689 to 1691. A large landholding elite owned [[e:hudson-valley|Hudson Valley]] manors, and New [[e:york-maine|York]] City grew as a trading port with many enslaved Africans. The [[e:john-peter-zenger|Zenger]] trial of 1735 advanced press freedom, and the [[e:albany-congress|Albany Congress]] of 1754 met there. Alliance with the [[s:iroquois-confederacy|Iroquois Confederacy]] shaped frontier policy.
province-of-new-york.e: [[e:new-york|New York City]] hosted the [[e:stamp-act-congress|Stamp Act Congress]] in 1765. In July 1776 the provincial congress endorsed independence and New York became a state of the [[s:united-states|United States]], though British forces occupied New York City until 1783.

provisional-government-of-milan.t: The government formed by the Milanese after the Five Days of 1848 drove out the Austrians, which merged Lombardy with Piedmont before Radetzky returned.
provisional-government-of-milan.o: From 18 to 22 March 1848 the people of [[s:duchy-of-milan|Milan]] fought the Five Days, barricade battles that forced [[e:joseph-radetzky-von-radetz|Marshal Radetzky's]] Austrian garrison to leave the city. A provisional government headed by the mayor [[e:gabrio-casati|Gabrio Casati]] took power, while the democrat [[e:carlo-cattaneo|Carlo Cattaneo]] led the council of war during the fighting.
provisional-government-of-milan.r: The provisional government governed [[e:lombardy|Lombardy]] and called on [[e:charles-albert-of-sardinia|Charles Albert]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-sardinia|Kingdom of Sardinia]], who declared war on [[e:austria|Austria]]. Moderates led by Casati favoured union with [[e:piedmont|Piedmont]], while republicans such as [[e:carlo-cattaneo|Cattaneo]] and [[e:giuseppe-mazzini|Giuseppe Mazzini]] wanted to delay the question. A plebiscite in May and June approved fusion with Piedmont.
provisional-government-of-milan.e: After the Piedmontese defeat at [[e:battle-of-custoza-1848|Custoza]] in July 1848, [[e:joseph-radetzky-von-radetz|Radetzky]] reoccupied [[s:duchy-of-milan|Milan]] on 6 August, and [[e:lombardy|Lombardy]] returned to the [[s:kingdom-of-lombardy-venetia|Kingdom of Lombardy-Venetia]].

pyu-city-states.t: A network of walled brick cities in the dry zone of Myanmar that brought Buddhism, writing and urban life to the Irrawaddy valley for over a thousand years.
pyu-city-states.o: From about the 2nd century BCE the Pyu, a Tibeto-Burman-speaking people, built large walled cities in the dry zone of central [[s:myanmar|Myanmar]], among them [[s:beikthano|Beikthano]], [[s:halin|Halin]], Maingmaw and later [[s:sri-ksetra-kingdom|Sri Ksetra]]. Their growth was tied to irrigated [[e:rice|rice]] farming and trade routes linking [[e:india|India]] and [[e:china|China]].
pyu-city-states.r: Each city was ruled by its own dynasty, and [[s:sri-ksetra-kingdom|Sri Ksetra]] became the leading centre by the 5th century. The Pyu wrote their own language in a script derived from Brahmi, and Chinese sources of the [[s:later-tang|Tang]] period describe a gentle Buddhist people with many monasteries, music and [[e:silver|silver]] coinage. Cylindrical stupas, urn burials and gold [[e:manuscript|manuscript]] leaves survive from their sites.
pyu-city-states.e: Raids by [[s:nanzhao|Nanzhao]] in the 830s, including the sack of a Pyu city, probably [[s:halin|Halin]], in 832, broke Pyu power, and the cities declined as the [[e:bamar-people|Burmans]] settled the [[e:kyaukse|Kyaukse]] plain and built the [[s:pagan-kingdom|Pagan Kingdom]]. Pyu culture was absorbed into Burman society; three Pyu ancient cities became a [[e:unesco-world-heritage-site|UNESCO World Heritage Site]] in 2014.

prince-bishopric-of-bamberg.t: Franconian church state founded by Emperor Henry II, whose cathedral holds the Bamberg Horseman and whose bishops staged notorious witch trials.
prince-bishopric-of-bamberg.o: [[e:henry-ii-holy-roman-emperor|Emperor Henry II]] founded the diocese of [[e:bamberg|Bamberg]] in 1007 and endowed it richly; he and his wife [[e:cunigunde-of-luxembourg|Kunigunde]] are buried in its cathedral. The [[e:bishop|bishops]] gathered lands in [[e:upper-franconia|Upper Franconia]], and after the extinction of the counts of [[e:house-of-andechs|Andechs-Meranien]] in 1248 they consolidated a territory and ruled it as imperial princes.
prince-bishopric-of-bamberg.r: The cathedral chapter elected the prince-[[e:bishop|bishops]]. The Romanesque-Gothic cathedral, with the [[e:bamberg-horseman|Bamberg Horseman]] and the tomb of [[e:pope-clement-ii|Pope Clement II]], symbolises the see's standing. Under [[e:johann-georg-ii-fuchs-von-dornheim|Johann Georg II Fuchs von Dornheim]] the territory suffered one of the worst witch persecutions in [[e:germany|Germany]] between 1626 and 1631. In the baroque era [[e:lothar-franz-von-schonborn|Lothar Franz von Schönborn]] built the New Residence.
prince-bishopric-of-bamberg.e: The prince-bishopric was secularised in 1802 and annexed by [[e:bavaria|Bavaria]], ending more than eight centuries of episcopal rule. [[e:bamberg|Bamberg]] became an archdiocese in 1817, and its largely intact old town is a [[e:unesco-world-heritage-site|UNESCO World Heritage Site]].
ru: Johann Georg II Fuchs von Dornheim

prince-bishopric-of-sion.t: A prince-bishopric in the Valais, Switzerland, whose bishops held the county granted in 999 until the people of the Upper Valais took power from them.
prince-bishopric-of-sion.o: [[e:sion-switzerland|Sion]], in the [[e:rhone|Rhône]] valley, had been a bishopric since the 6th century. In 999 [[e:rudolf-iii-of-burgundy|King Rudolf III of Burgundy]] granted the [[e:bishop|bishop]] the county of [[e:valais|Valais]], making him a temporal lord. When [[s:duchy-of-burgundy|Burgundy]] passed to the Empire in 1032, the bishops became imperial princes.
prince-bishopric-of-sion.r: The [[e:bishop|bishops]] faced the counts of [[s:county-of-savoy|Savoy]], who held the lower [[e:valais|Valais]], and the growing power of the German-speaking communes ([[e:zenden|Zenden]]) of the upper valley. Cardinal [[e:matthaus-schiner|Matthäus Schiner]], bishop from 1499, was a leading diplomat of the Swiss in the [[e:italian-wars|Italian Wars]]. The [[s:province-of-carolina|Carolina]] document claimed [[e:charlemagne|Charlemagne]] had granted the county.
prince-bishopric-of-sion.e: The seven [[e:zenden|Zenden]] gradually reduced the [[e:bishop|bishop]]'s power and in 1613 to 1634 forced bishops to renounce temporal [[e:sovereignty|sovereignty]], making the [[e:valais|Valais]] a republic allied with the [[s:old-swiss-confederacy|Swiss Confederacy]]. The Valais became a Swiss canton in 1815, and the bishops of [[e:sion-switzerland|Sion]] remain spiritual heads.

perinthus.t: Samian colony on the Sea of Marmara that, with Byzantium, defeated Philip II's siege of 340 BCE.
perinthus.o: Colonists from [[s:samos|Samos]] founded Perinthus c. 602 BCE on a promontory on the north shore of the [[e:sea-of-marmara|Propontis]], in [[e:thrace|Thrace]]. They soon fought off attacks by Megarian settlers from neighbouring colonies.
perinthus.r: Perinthus traded with the Thracian interior and along the [[e:sea-of-marmara|Propontis]] route to [[s:byzantium|Byzantium]]. It resisted the Persian general [[e:megabazus|Megabazus]] c. 512 BCE but was conquered. Later it paid tribute in the [[s:delian-league|Delian League]]. In 340 BCE [[e:philip-ii-of-macedon|Philip II]] besieged the city with towers and rams, but Persian [[e:satrapy|satraps]] and [[e:byzantine-empire|Byzantium]] helped it hold out.
perinthus.e: Perinthus kept its independence under Hellenistic kings and the [[s:odrysian-kingdom|Odrysian Kingdom]]'s influence. When [[e:rome|Rome]] made [[e:thrace|Thrace]] a province in 46 CE, it became the provincial capital, later renamed [[s:heraclea-lucania|Heraclea]]; it is modern [[e:marmara-ereglisi|Marmara Ereğlisi]].

principality-of-samos.t: Autonomous Christian principality on the island of Samos under Ottoman suzerainty, created after the Greek War of Independence and united with Greece in 1912.
principality-of-samos.o: [[s:samos|Samos]] fought in the [[e:greek-war-of-independence|Greek War of Independence]], but the [[e:london-protocol-1830|London Protocol]] of 1830 left it outside the new Greek state. As a compromise the Ottoman [[e:sultan|Sultan]] made it an autonomous principality, established in 1834, with a Christian prince appointed by the [[e:sublime-porte|Porte]] and paying an annual tribute. Its first prince was [[e:stefanos-vogoridis|Stefanos Vogoridis]].
principality-of-samos.r: The prince, usually a [[e:phanariotes|Phanariot Greek]], governed with an elected assembly and his own administration, flag and later postage stamps, from [[e:vathy-samos|Vathy]]. Samians paid low taxes and enjoyed religious freedom. The economy rested on wine, especially muscat, tobacco and shipping. Politics were often turbulent, with clashes between princes and local factions.
principality-of-samos.e: During the [[e:first-balkan-war|First Balkan War]], the Samian leader [[e:themistoklis-sofoulis|Themistoklis Sofoulis]] drove out the last Ottoman garrison and the assembly declared union with [[e:greece|Greece]] in November 1912. Greek troops landed in March 1913, and in 1914 the great powers confirmed its union with the [[s:kingdom-of-greece|Kingdom of Greece]].

palace-state-of-phaistos.t: Minoan palace centre of the Mesara plain in southern Crete, famous for its grand staircases and the enigmatic Phaistos Disc.
palace-state-of-phaistos.o: [[s:phaistos|Phaistos]] stands on a ridge above the [[e:mesara-plain|Mesara]], the largest plain of [[e:crete|Crete]], which had been settled since the [[e:neolithic|Neolithic]]. Around 1950 BCE its first palace was built around a paved central court, and Phaistos became the leading power of southern Crete. After destructions in the 18th century BCE the palace was rebuilt on a grander scale.
palace-state-of-phaistos.r: [[s:phaistos|Phaistos]] controlled the agricultural wealth of the [[e:mesara-plain|Mesara]] and probably the nearby port of [[e:kommos|Kommos]], which traded with [[e:egypt|Egypt]] and the [[e:levant|Levant]]. Its archives of clay sealings and [[e:linear-a|Linear A]] tablets reveal a developed palace bureaucracy. Finds include fine [[e:kamares-ware|Kamares ware]] pottery and the stamped clay [[e:phaistos-disc|Phaistos Disc]], whose script is still undeciphered. The nearby villa of [[e:ayia-triada|Ayia Triada]] was closely linked to it.
palace-state-of-phaistos.e: The palace was destroyed c. 1450 BCE and its role passed largely to [[e:ayia-triada|Ayia Triada]] and to [[s:palace-state-of-knossos|Knossos]], which came to dominate [[e:crete|Crete]] under Mycenaean rulers. [[s:phaistos|Phaistos]] later revived as a Greek city-state, described separately as Phaistos. The site was excavated by Italian archaeologists from 1900.

pequot-nation.t: The leading power of 17th-century eastern Connecticut, whose defeat in the Pequot War of 1636 to 1638 opened southern New England to English expansion.
pequot-nation.o: The Pequot lived along the Thames and Mystic rivers in what is now south-eastern [[e:connecticut|Connecticut]]. By the early 17th century they had become the dominant people of the region, collecting tribute from neighbours and controlling the production and trade of wampum shell [[e:bead|beads]], which the [[e:dutch|Dutch]] of [[s:new-netherland|New Netherland]] bought in exchange for cloth and metal goods.
pequot-nation.r: Grand sachems such as [[e:tatobem|Tatobem]] and his son [[e:sassacus|Sassacus]] ruled through councils of lesser sachems and fortified villages. Their wealth from the wampum trade, and their alliance with the [[e:dutch|Dutch]], made them targets: the Dutch killed Tatobem in 1633 or 1634, and rival sachem [[e:uncas|Uncas]] broke away to lead the [[e:mohegan|Mohegan]]. English settlement in the [[e:connecticut|Connecticut]] valley from 1633 brought rising tension.
pequot-nation.e: In 1637 English forces under [[e:john-mason-connecticut|John Mason]], with [[e:mohegan|Mohegan]] and [[e:narragansett-people|Narragansett]] allies, burned the fortified village at Mystic, killing around 400 to 700 people. The [[e:treaty-of-hartford-1638|Treaty of Hartford]] in 1638 dissolved the nation. Survivors later regained reservations at Mashantucket and Lantern Hill.

province-of-north-carolina.t: The British colony between Virginia and South Carolina, a land of small farms and naval stores, where the Regulator revolt foreshadowed the Revolution.
province-of-north-carolina.o: The northern settlements of the [[s:province-of-carolina|Province of Carolina]], around [[e:albemarle-sound|Albemarle Sound]], had long been governed separately, and in 1712 the proprietors gave them their own governor, [[e:edward-hyde-governor|Edward Hyde]]. The colony was then fighting the [[e:tuscarora-war|Tuscarora War]]. In 1729 the Crown bought out seven of the eight proprietors, and North Carolina became a royal province.
province-of-north-carolina.r: Without a good deep-water port, the colony grew more slowly than its neighbours, with small farms, tobacco, and naval stores of tar, pitch and turpentine from the longleaf pine forests. [[e:scotch-irish-americans|Scots-Irish]] and German settlers filled the backcountry. Governor [[e:william-tryon|William Tryon]] built an expensive palace at [[e:new-bern|New Bern]], the capital from the 1760s, and crushed the [[e:regulator-movement|Regulator movement]] of backcountry farmers protesting corrupt officials at the [[e:battle-of-alamance|Battle of Alamance]] in 1771.
province-of-north-carolina.e: Governor [[e:josiah-martin|Josiah Martin]] fled in 1775. In April 1776 the [[e:halifax-resolves|Halifax Resolves]] made North [[s:province-of-carolina|Carolina]] the first colony to instruct its delegates to vote for independence, and it became a state of the [[s:united-states|United States]].
