principality-of-uglich.t: An appanage principality on the upper Volga, split off from Rostov and bought by Ivan Kalita of Moscow.
principality-of-uglich.o: [[e:uglich|Uglich]] on the upper [[e:volga|Volga]] belonged to the [[e:rostov|Rostov]] lands. In 1218 [[e:konstantin-of-rostov|Konstantin Vsevolodovich of Rostov]] gave it to his son Vladimir, who became the first prince of a separate Uglich line.
principality-of-uglich.r: The principality was small, with its wealth drawn from [[e:volga|Volga]] trade and farming. It was sacked by the [[e:mongols|Mongols]] in 1238. Its prince Roman Vladimirovich, who died in 1285, was later venerated as a saint for his charity to the poor. Like other small [[e:appanage|appanages]] of the north-east, [[e:uglich|Uglich]] depended on the grand princes and the [[s:golden-horde|Golden Horde]].
principality-of-uglich.e: After its line declined, the principality was acquired by [[e:ivan-i-of-moscow|Ivan I Kalita]] of the [[s:grand-duchy-of-moscow|Grand Duchy of Moscow]] around 1328, one of his famous purchases of land. [[e:uglich|Uglich]] later became the scene of the death of [[e:dmitry-of-uglich|Tsarevich Dmitry]] in 1591.

principality-of-soyo.t: A Kongo coastal province at the mouth of the Congo River that broke away to become an independent Catholic principality and defeated Portugal in 1670.
principality-of-soyo.o: [[e:soyo|Soyo]] was a province of the [[e:kingdom-of-kongo|Kingdom of Kongo]], ruled by a count ([[e:mani|Mani]] Soyo) from Mbanza Soyo, close to the river mouth. Its control of the port of Mpinda and direct trade with the [[e:dutch|Dutch]] made it rich, and in 1641 Count Daniel da Silva asserted independence from the Kongo king.
principality-of-soyo.r: [[e:soyo|Soyo's]] counts, later styled princes, ruled as Catholic monarchs, hosting Italian Capuchin missionaries. Trade in slaves, [[e:ivory-trade|ivory]] and [[e:copper|copper]] with [[e:dutch|Dutch]] and English merchants funded a strong army. In 1670 Soyo defeated a Portuguese invasion at the [[e:battle-of-kitombo|Battle of Kitombo]], and it later intervened in the [[e:kingdom-of-kongo|Kongo]] civil wars.
principality-of-soyo.e: [[e:soyo|Soyo]] remained autonomous through the 18th and 19th centuries, though its power waned with the end of the [[e:atlantic-slave-trade|slave trade]]. It was incorporated into [[s:portuguese-angola|Portuguese Angola]] after the [[e:berlin-conference|Berlin Conference]] of 1884–85. The town of Soyo is now an Angolan oil centre.

prince-bishopric-of-meissen.t: An Ottonian bishopric among the Sorbs of the middle Elbe whose territory was gradually absorbed by the Wettin rulers of Saxony.
prince-bishopric-of-meissen.o: Otto I founded the bishopric of [[e:meissen|Meissen]] in 968 as part of his reorganisation of the eastern frontier under [[e:magdeburg|Magdeburg]]. It served the conversion of the [[s:sorbs|Sorbs]] and the Slavic lands between the [[e:saale|Saale]] and the [[e:bobr|Bóbr]]. The [[e:bishop|bishops]] shared the castle hill of Meissen with the margraves of Meissen.
prince-bishopric-of-meissen.r: The [[e:bishop|bishops]] held scattered lands around [[e:stolpen|Stolpen]], [[e:wurzen|Wurzen]] and Mügeln and governed a diocese that reached into [[e:lusatia|Lusatia]]. The Gothic cathedral of [[e:meissen|Meissen]], begun around 1260, rose beside the margraves' [[e:albrechtsburg|Albrechtsburg]]. [[e:benno-of-meissen|Benno of Meissen]], bishop in the late 11th century, was canonised in 1523; his relics were moved to [[e:munich|Munich]] during the [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]].
prince-bishopric-of-meissen.e: The [[e:house-of-wettin|Wettin]] dukes and [[e:prince-elector|electors]] steadily controlled the see. After [[e:saxony|Saxony]] became Lutheran, [[e:bishop|Bishop]] [[e:johann-ix-von-haugwitz|Johann IX von Haugwitz]] resigned in 1581 and the territory was annexed to the [[s:electorate-of-saxony|Electorate of Saxony]]. A Catholic remnant in [[e:upper-lusatia|Upper Lusatia]] continued at [[e:bautzen|Bautzen]] and became the modern [[e:diocese-of-dresden-meissen|Diocese of Dresden-Meissen]].

partabgarh-state.t: A Sisodia Rajput state in southern Rajasthan, an offshoot of Mewar, known for its distinctive Thewa jewellery of gold worked onto glass.
partabgarh-state.o: The rulers descended from a branch of the [[e:sisodia-dynasty|Sisodia dynasty]] of [[s:udaipur-state|Mewar]] that settled in the Kanthal region; tradition dates their rule to the early 15th century. The early capital was Deolia, and Maharawat Pratap Singh founded the new capital of Pratapgarh in 1698.
partabgarh-state.r: Partabgarh was a hilly state with a large [[e:bhils|Bhil]] and [[e:meena|Mina]] population. It came under Mughal and then [[e:maratha-empire|Maratha]] domination, paying tribute to [[e:holkars|Holkar]] of [[s:indore-state|Indore State]], and signed a treaty with the British in 1818. Local goldsmiths developed [[e:thewa|Thewa]], a technique of fusing gold filigree onto coloured glass.
partabgarh-state.e: Partabgarh joined the [[s:united-state-of-rajasthan|United State of Rajasthan]] in 1948. Pratapgarh became a separate district of [[e:rajasthan|Rajasthan]] in 2008.

principality-of-kostroma.t: A short-lived Volga appanage whose only prince, Vasily, rose to become grand prince of Vladimir.
principality-of-kostroma.o: [[e:kostroma|Kostroma]] on the [[e:volga|Volga]] was a town of the [[s:vladimir-suzdal|Vladimir-Suzdal]] lands. In 1246, after the death of [[e:yaroslav-ii-of-vladimir|Yaroslav Vsevolodovich]], his youngest son Vasily received Kostroma as his own [[e:appanage|appanage]].
principality-of-kostroma.r: [[e:vasily-of-kostroma|Vasily of Kostroma]] was an active prince who fought the [[e:lithuanians|Lithuanians]] and the Novgorodians. In 1272 he became grand prince of Vladimir with the approval of the [[s:golden-horde|Golden Horde]], ruling from [[e:kostroma|Kostroma]] rather than moving to Vladimir. The principality was a small [[e:volga|Volga]] land with little else recorded.
principality-of-kostroma.e: Vasily died in 1276 without sons, and [[e:kostroma|Kostroma]] passed back to the grand princes of Vladimir. It later became part of the [[s:grand-duchy-of-moscow|Grand Duchy of Moscow]]. The [[e:ipatiev-monastery|Ipatiev Monastery]] near the town later played a part in the election of [[e:michael-of-russia|Michael Romanov]] in 1613.

palatinate-sulzbach.t: Small Wittelsbach duchy in the Upper Palatinate, a centre of religious tolerance and Hebrew printing whose line inherited the Palatinate and Bavaria.
palatinate-sulzbach.o: Sulzbach was split from [[s:palatinate-neuburg|Palatinate-Neuburg]] in 1614 as an [[e:appanage|appanage]] for Augustus, and in 1656 his son [[e:christian-august-count-palatine-of-sulzbach|Christian August]] gained full [[e:sovereignty|sovereignty]] over it as a duchy. Christian August converted to [[e:catholicism|Catholicism]] in 1655 but kept his Protestant subjects' rights.
palatinate-sulzbach.r: [[e:christian-august-count-palatine-of-sulzbach|Christian August]] introduced the simultaneum, letting Catholics and [[e:lutheranism|Lutherans]] share churches, and allowed [[e:jews|Jews]] to settle. Sulzbach became a centre of learning: the Christian Kabbalist [[e:christian-knorr-von-rosenroth|Christian Knorr von Rosenroth]] served at court, and [[e:hebrew|Hebrew]] [[e:printing-press|printing]] presses flourished from 1669. The duchy's economy relied on iron ore and smelting in the [[s:upper-palatinate|Upper Palatinate]].
palatinate-sulzbach.e: [[e:charles-theodore-elector-of-bavaria|Charles Theodore]] of Sulzbach inherited the [[s:electoral-palatinate|Electoral Palatinate]] in 1742, merging Sulzbach into it. In 1777 he also inherited the [[s:electorate-of-bavaria|Electorate of Bavaria]], and the Sulzbach line thus united the Wittelsbach lands.

prince-bishopric-of-eichstatt.t: A Franconian church principality on the Altmühl, founded on the see of Saint Willibald, that became a showcase of Catholic Baroque.
prince-bishopric-of-eichstatt.o: [[e:saint-boniface|Saint Boniface]] made his kinsman [[e:willibald|Willibald]] the first [[e:bishop|bishop]] of [[e:eichstatt|Eichstätt]] in the 740s. For centuries the bishops held little secular land, but in 1305 they inherited much of the lordship of the extinct counts of Hirschberg, laying the foundation of a territorial principality along the [[e:altmuhl|Altmühl]] valley between [[e:franconia|Franconia]] and [[e:bavaria|Bavaria]].
prince-bishopric-of-eichstatt.r: The prince-[[e:bishop|bishop]], elected by the cathedral chapter, governed from [[e:eichstatt|Eichstätt]] and the hilltop [[e:willibaldsburg|Willibaldsburg]], where [[e:johann-conrad-von-gemmingen|Johann Conrad von Gemmingen]] laid out the garden recorded in the [[e:hortus-eystettensis|Hortus Eystettensis]] of 1613. The territory belonged to the [[e:franconian-circle|Franconian Circle]] and lived from farming, forests and limestone quarrying. It remained Catholic, and after the Swedish sack of 1634 the city was rebuilt in [[e:baroque|Baroque]] style by architects such as [[e:gabriel-de-gabrieli|Gabriel de Gabrieli]].
prince-bishopric-of-eichstatt.e: In 1802 the prince-bishopric was secularised. Its lands went to [[e:bavaria|Bavaria]], then largely to [[e:ferdinand-iii-grand-duke-of-tuscany|Ferdinand of Tuscany]]'s [[s:electorate-of-salzburg|Electorate of Salzburg]], before passing to the [[s:kingdom-of-bavaria|Kingdom of Bavaria]] in 1805. The diocese survives, and [[e:eichstatt|Eichstätt]] is home to [[e:germany|Germany's]] only Catholic university.

province-of-west-florida.t: A British Gulf Coast colony stretching from Pensacola to the Mississippi, lost to Spanish forces during the American Revolution.
province-of-west-florida.o: Created by the [[e:royal-proclamation-of-1763|Royal Proclamation of 1763]] from territory [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] gained under the [[e:treaty-of-paris-1763|Treaty of Paris]]: the western part of [[s:spanish-florida|Spanish Florida]] plus French lands east of the [[e:mississippi-river|Mississippi]] around Mobile. [[e:pensacola|Pensacola]] became the capital, and in 1764 the northern boundary was pushed up to the latitude of the [[e:yazoo-river|Yazoo River]].
province-of-west-florida.r: West [[e:florida|Florida]] had an elected assembly alongside royal governors such as [[e:george-johnstone|George Johnstone]] and [[e:peter-chester|Peter Chester]]. Settlers came from the older colonies and [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] to farm along the [[e:mississippi-river|Mississippi]] near [[s:natchez-chiefdom|Natchez]] and [[e:baton-rouge|Baton Rouge]], while [[e:pensacola|Pensacola]] and Mobile lived on the deerskin trade with the [[s:muscogee-confederacy|Muscogee Confederacy]], [[s:choctaw-nation|Choctaw Nation]] and [[s:chickasaw-nation|Chickasaw Nation]]. Like [[s:province-of-east-florida|East Florida]], it stayed loyal to the Crown after 1776.
province-of-west-florida.e: [[e:spain|Spain]] entered the war in 1779, and [[e:bernardo-de-galvez|Bernardo de Gálvez]], governor of [[s:spanish-louisiana|Spanish Louisiana]], took [[e:baton-rouge|Baton Rouge]], Mobile and finally [[e:pensacola|Pensacola]] in 1781. The 1783 peace confirmed Spanish possession; disputes over the region's border later fed the [[s:republic-of-west-florida|Republic of West Florida]].

pahlavi-iran.t: The last Iranian monarchy, under Reza Shah and his son Mohammad Reza Shah, which pursued rapid modernisation until overthrown by the revolution of 1979.
pahlavi-iran.o: [[e:reza-shah|Reza Khan]], an officer of the [[e:persian-cossack-brigade|Persian Cossack Brigade]], seized power in a coup in 1921 and became prime minister in 1923. In 1925 the [[e:national-consultative-assembly|Majlis]] deposed the last ruler of [[s:qajar-iran|Qajar Iran]], and Reza Khan was crowned Reza Shah [[e:middle-persian|Pahlavi]].
pahlavi-iran.r: [[e:reza-shah|Reza Shah]] built a centralised state with a [[e:conscription|conscript]] army, the [[e:trans-iranian-railway|Trans-Iranian Railway]] (completed 1938), the [[e:university-of-tehran|University of Tehran]] and secular law, banned the women's veil in 1936 and asked foreign states to call the country [[e:iran|Iran]] from 1935. The [[e:anglo-soviet-invasion-of-iran|Anglo-Soviet invasion]] of 1941 forced his abdication in favour of his son [[e:mohammad-reza-pahlavi|Mohammad Reza Shah]]. Prime Minister [[e:mohammad-mosaddegh|Mohammad Mosaddegh]] nationalised oil in 1951 but was overthrown in a 1953 coup backed by the [[e:central-intelligence-agency|CIA]] and MI6. The shah's [[e:white-revolution|White Revolution]] of 1963 brought land reform and women's suffrage, while the [[e:savak|SAVAK]] secret police suppressed opponents.
pahlavi-iran.e: [[e:inflation|Inflation]], repression and religious opposition led by [[e:ruhollah-khomeini|Ayatollah Khomeini]] produced mass protests in 1978. The shah left [[e:iran|Iran]] in January 1979, and the [[s:islamic-republic-of-iran|Islamic Republic of Iran]] was proclaimed that April.

cr.a: Original emblem: Government of Iran (1970s) Vectorization and manual modifications by Shfarshid

phaltan-state.t: The Deccan fief of the Nimbalkar family, one of the oldest Maratha houses, into which Shivaji married and which survived as a princely state until 1948.
phaltan-state.o: The [[e:nimbalkar|Nimbalkars]] claim to have held Phaltan since the late 13th century, and they are counted among the oldest [[e:maratha-empire|Maratha]] families. In the 16th and 17th centuries they served the [[s:bijapur-sultanate|Bijapur Sultanate]] as military chiefs.
phaltan-state.r: [[e:saibai|Saibai Nimbalkar]] of Phaltan became the first wife of [[e:shivaji|Shivaji]], linking the family to the founder of the [[s:maratha-empire|Maratha Empire]]. Phaltan later held its lands under the [[e:satara|Satara]] rulers and the [[e:peshwa|Peshwas]]. After 1818 it came under British protection as one of the Satara [[e:jagir|jagirs]] and then the [[e:deccan-states-agency|Deccan States Agency]].
phaltan-state.e: Phaltan merged into [[e:bombay-state|Bombay State]] in 1948. Its last ruler, [[e:malojirao-nimbalkar|Malojirao Nimbalkar]], went on to serve as a minister in [[e:mumbai|Bombay]]. The town is now in [[e:satara|Satara]] district, [[e:maharashtra|Maharashtra]].

principality-of-minsk.t: A small principality of the Polotsk lands whose town grew into the capital of modern Belarus.
principality-of-minsk.o: [[e:minsk|Minsk]] first appears in the chronicle in 1067, when the sons of [[e:yaroslav-the-wise|Yaroslav the Wise]] sacked it during their war with [[e:vseslav-of-polotsk|Vseslav of Polotsk]] and defeated him on the [[e:battle-on-the-nemiga-river|Nemiga]] river. After Vseslav died in 1101 his son [[e:gleb-vseslavich|Gleb]] received Minsk, which became a separate principality.
principality-of-minsk.r: [[e:gleb-vseslavich|Gleb Vseslavich]] made [[e:minsk|Minsk]] a power in its own right and fought [[e:kyiv|Kiev]] and [[e:vladimir-ii-monomakh|Vladimir Monomakh]] until he was captured and died in Kiev in 1119. Afterwards the principality was a minor [[e:appanage|appanage]] of the Polotsk dynasty. Little is known of its later rulers or institutions, and it lived in the shadow of [[e:polotsk|Polotsk]] and the growing [[s:grand-duchy-of-lithuania|Grand Duchy of Lithuania]].
principality-of-minsk.e: By the early 14th century [[e:minsk|Minsk]] was dependent on [[s:grand-duchy-of-lithuania|Lithuania]], and around 1326 a Prince Vasily of Minsk appears as a [[e:vassal|vassal]] of [[e:gediminas|Gediminas]]. It was absorbed into the [[e:grand-duchy-of-lithuania|Grand Duchy of Lithuania]].

paramara-dynasty.t: The Malwa dynasty of the scholar-king Bhoja, whose capital Dhar became a byword for learning and the patronage of poets.
paramara-dynasty.o: The Paramaras emerged in [[e:malwa|Malwa]] in the 9th century, probably as feudatories of the [[s:rashtrakuta-dynasty|Rashtrakuta dynasty]] or the [[s:gurjara-pratihara|Gurjara-Pratihara]]. Later legend said their ancestor sprang from a sacrificial fire on [[e:mount-abu|Mount Abu]]. [[e:siyaka|Siyaka]], also called [[e:harsha|Harsha]], made the dynasty independent and sacked the Rashtrakuta capital [[e:manyakheta|Manyakheta]] in 972.
paramara-dynasty.r: [[e:vakpati-munja|Vakpati Munja]] was a poet and patron who fought the [[s:western-chalukya-empire|Western Chalukya Empire]] and was captured and executed by [[e:tailapa-ii|Tailapa II]]. [[e:bhoja-paramara|Bhoja]], ruling from about 1010 to 1055, was celebrated as a polymath credited with works on poetics, architecture and medicine; he made Dhar a centre of learning, built the [[e:bhojeshwar-temple|Bhojpur Shiva temple]] and was remembered in countless legends. The Paramaras also built the [[e:udayeshwar-temple|Udayeshvara temple]] at [[e:udaipur|Udaipur]] in [[e:malwa|Malwa]].
paramara-dynasty.e: After [[e:bhoja-paramara|Bhoja]]'s defeat by the [[s:chaulukya-dynasty|Chaulukya dynasty]] and the [[s:kalachuris-of-tripuri|Kalachuris of Tripuri]], the kingdom weakened. The [[s:delhi-sultanate|Delhi Sultanate]] attacked repeatedly, and in 1305 an army of [[e:alauddin-khalji|Alauddin Khalji]] conquered [[e:malwa|Malwa]], ending Paramara rule.

prince-bishopric-of-chur.t: Alpine church state ruled by the bishops of Chur, one of the oldest sees north of the Alps, whose temporal power was broken by the leagues of Graubünden.
prince-bishopric-of-chur.o: A [[e:bishop|bishop]] of [[e:chur|Chur]] is recorded in 451, making it one of the oldest dioceses north of the [[e:alps|Alps]]. Carolingian and Ottonian kings granted the bishops immunities, tolls and lands in [[e:raetia|Rhaetia]], controlling routes to the Alpine passes. In 1170 [[e:frederick-barbarossa|Emperor Frederick Barbarossa]] raised the bishop to the rank of an imperial prince, giving the church a recognised secular principality.
prince-bishopric-of-chur.r: The [[e:bishop|bishops]] governed estates in the [[e:rhine|Rhine]] valley, the Engadine and the [[e:vinschgau|Vinschgau]] from their court in [[e:chur|Chur]], with officials in castles along the pass roads. [[e:romansh|Romansh]], German and [[e:kingdom-of-the-lombards|Lombard]] dialects were all spoken in their lands. To resist episcopal power, the subjects formed the [[s:league-of-gods-house|League of God's House]] in 1367, which later joined the [[s:grey-league|Grey League]] and the [[s:league-of-the-ten-jurisdictions|League of the Ten Jurisdictions]] in the [[s:three-leagues|Three Leagues]].
prince-bishopric-of-chur.e: The [[e:ilanz-articles|Ilanz Articles]] of 1524 and 1526 stripped the [[e:bishop|bishop]] of most secular authority and handed it to the communes of the [[s:three-leagues|Three Leagues]]. The bishops kept a few rights and the title of prince until 1803, and the Catholic diocese of [[e:chur|Chur]] continues today.

patrae.t: Achaean city at the mouth of the Gulf of Corinth, a founder of the Achaean League and forerunner of modern Patras.
patrae.o: Patrae was formed, according to [[e:pausanias-geographer|Pausanias]], by uniting the villages of Aroe, Antheia and Mesatis on the coast of western [[e:achaea|Achaea]]. It was one of the twelve Achaean cities and controlled the narrows at the entrance to the [[e:gulf-of-corinth|Gulf of Corinth]].
patrae.r: Patrae was a modest farming and trading town in the Classical period. In 280 BCE it joined [[s:dyme|Dyme]], [[e:tritaea|Tritaea]] and [[e:pharae-achaea|Pharae]] in reviving the [[s:achaean-league|Achaean League]]. In 279 BCE the Patraeans were the only [[e:achaeans-achaea|Achaeans]] to send troops against the invading [[e:gaul|Gauls]], suffering heavy losses. The city had a sanctuary of [[e:artemis|Artemis]] Laphria.
patrae.e: Patrae passed under [[e:rome|Rome]] in 146 BCE. Augustus made it a Roman colony c. 14 BCE, and it became the chief port of the region, growing into the modern city of [[s:barony-of-patras|Patras]].
patrae.re: Greek religion; cult of Artemis Laphria

phulra-state.t: A tiny Tanoli chiefship in the Hazara hills, a neighbour and kinsman of Amb State.
phulra-state.o: Phulra was established in the early 19th century, around 1828, by a branch of the [[e:tanoli|Tanoli]] chiefs of [[s:amb-state|Tanawal]] who also ruled Amb State, during the period of [[e:sikhism|Sikh]] expansion into [[e:hazara|Hazara]].
phulra-state.r: Under British rule it was a very small autonomous holding on the [[e:north-west-frontier-province|North-West Frontier]], governed by a Khan over a Muslim population speaking [[e:hindko|Hindko]]. Little else of its history is recorded.
phulra-state.e: Phulra acceded to [[s:islamic-republic-of-pakistan|Pakistan]] after 1947 and was abolished and merged into the [[e:north-west-frontier-province|North-West Frontier Province]] in 1950; its area is now in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

principality-of-calenberg.t: A Guelph principality between the Deister and the Leine that grew into the Electorate of Hanover and the dynasty of Britain's Georgian kings.
principality-of-calenberg.o: The [[e:house-of-welf|Guelph]] lands of the old [[s:duchy-of-brunswick-luneburg|Duchy of Brunswick-Lüneburg]] were repeatedly divided. In 1432 the territory between the [[e:deister|Deister]] and the [[e:leine|Leine]], named after Calenberg castle, became a separate principality under [[e:william-the-victorious|William the Victorious]], split off from the [[s:principality-of-wolfenbuttel|Principality of Wolfenbüttel]].
principality-of-calenberg.r: Calenberg was ruled from Calenberg castle and other residences, and from 1636 from [[e:hanover|Hanover]]. Duchess Elisabeth, regent in the 1540s, introduced [[e:lutheranism|Lutheranism]]. The principality absorbed [[e:gottingen|Göttingen]] in 1495 and later Grubenhagen. Duke [[e:john-frederick-duke-of-brunswick-luneburg|John Frederick]] brought [[e:gottfried-wilhelm-leibniz|Leibniz]] to Hanover as librarian in 1676, and [[e:ernest-augustus-elector-of-hanover|Ernest Augustus]] built a more centralised state.
principality-of-calenberg.e: In 1692 [[e:leopold-i-holy-roman-emperor|Emperor Leopold]] I made [[e:ernest-augustus-elector-of-hanover|Ernest Augustus]] an elector, and Calenberg became the core of the [[s:electorate-of-hanover|Electorate of Hanover]], which absorbed the [[s:principality-of-luneburg|Principality of Lüneburg]] in 1705. His son George became King of [[s:kingdom-of-great-britain|Great Britain]] in 1714.

provisional-government-of-oregon.t: A self-made government formed by American and Canadian settlers in the Willamette Valley while Britain and the United States both claimed Oregon.
provisional-government-of-oregon.o: Under an 1818 agreement, [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] and the [[s:united-states|United States]] jointly occupied the [[e:oregon-country|Oregon Country]], but neither governed it. Settlers, missionaries and retired [[e:hudsons-bay-company|Hudson's Bay Company]] employees in the [[e:willamette-valley|Willamette Valley]] needed law for property and estates. At [[e:champoeg|Champoeg]] on 2 May 1843 they voted narrowly to create a provisional government, and wagon trains on the [[e:oregon-trail|Oregon Trail]] soon swelled their numbers.
provisional-government-of-oregon.r: The government's [[e:organic-laws-of-oregon|Organic Laws]] provided for a legislature, courts and land claims of up to 640 acres. A three-man executive committee was replaced in 1845 by a single governor, [[e:george-abernethy|George Abernethy]], at [[e:oregon-city-oregon|Oregon City]]. It levied voluntary taxes, banned [[e:slavery|slavery]] but also passed laws excluding black settlers, and raised militia for the [[e:cayuse-war|Cayuse War]] after the Whitman killings of 1847.
provisional-government-of-oregon.e: The [[e:oregon-treaty|Oregon Treaty]] of 1846 gave the area south of the 49th parallel to the [[s:united-states|United States]]. Congress created [[e:oregon-territory|Oregon Territory]] in 1848, and the provisional government ended when Governor [[e:joseph-lane|Joseph Lane]] arrived in March 1849.

province-of-georgia.t: The last of Britain's thirteen mainland colonies, founded by James Oglethorpe as a buffer against Spanish Florida and an experiment without slavery.
province-of-georgia.o: In 1732 [[e:george-ii-of-great-britain|George II]] granted a charter to a board of [[e:trustees-for-the-establishment-of-the-colony-of-georgia-in-america|Trustees]] led by [[e:james-oglethorpe|James Oglethorpe]] for the land between the [[e:savannah|Savannah]] and [[e:altamaha-river|Altamaha]] rivers. Oglethorpe founded Savannah in 1733, with the help of the [[e:yamacraw|Yamacraw]] leader [[e:tomochichi|Tomochichi]]. The colony was meant to shield the [[s:province-of-south-carolina|Province of South Carolina]] from [[s:spanish-florida|Spanish Florida]] and to offer a new start to the poor.
province-of-georgia.r: The [[e:trustees-for-the-establishment-of-the-colony-of-georgia-in-america|Trustees]] banned [[e:slavery|slavery]], limited landholdings and forbade hard liquor, and they recruited Protestant [[e:georgia-salzburgers|Salzburgers]], Scottish Highlanders and others. [[e:james-oglethorpe|Oglethorpe]] defeated a Spanish invasion at Bloody Marsh in 1742. Settlers, envious of Carolina's [[e:rice|rice]] wealth, pressed for slavery, which was allowed in 1751. The Trustees surrendered the charter, and [[s:georgia|Georgia]] became a royal province in 1752, with rice plantations spreading along the coast under governor [[e:james-wright-governor|James Wright]].
province-of-georgia.e: Patriots took control in 1776 and [[s:georgia|Georgia]] became a state of the [[s:united-states|United States]], though British forces reoccupied [[e:savannah|Savannah]] from 1778 to 1782 and restored royal government there. [[e:georgia|Georgia]] adopted its first state constitution in 1777.

principality-of-berat.t: Albanian lordship of the Muzaka family around Berat and the Myzeqe plain, a leading noble realm of late medieval Albania.
principality-of-berat.o: The [[e:muzaka-family|Muzaka]] were powerful Albanian nobles of the [[e:myzeqe|Myzeqe plain]]. Around 1335 [[e:andrea-ii-muzaka|Andrea II Muzaka]] received the Byzantine title of despot for fighting the [[e:capetian-house-of-anjou|Angevins]], and the family built a lordship in the area. [[e:berat|Berat]] itself was taken by the [[s:serbian-empire|Serbian Empire]] in the 1340s and only came firmly into Muzaka hands around 1372.
principality-of-berat.r: The [[e:muzaka-family|Muzaka]] ruled from the fortress of [[e:berat|Berat]] over Albanian peasants and herders, balancing [[s:byzantium|Byzantium]], the [[e:serbs|Serbs]], [[e:venice|Venice]] and the [[e:balsic-noble-family|Balšić]] lords of [[e:zeta-region|Zeta]]. They joined coalitions against the Balšići and against the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]]; [[e:theodore-ii-muzaka|Theodore II Muzaka]] died fighting at [[e:battle-of-kosovo|Kosovo]] in 1389 according to tradition.
principality-of-berat.e: Ottoman pressure grew after their victory at [[e:battle-of-savra|Savra]] in 1385. The [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]] took [[e:berat|Berat]] in 1417, and the [[e:muzaka-family|Muzaka]] lands became part of the Sanjak of [[s:albania|Albania]]. The family later took part in [[e:skanderbeg|Skanderbeg's]] resistance.

prince-bishopric-of-brixen.t: An Alpine prince-bishopric on the Brenner route, set up by emperors to guard the road to Italy, whose bishops ruled parts of Tyrol for nearly 800 years.
prince-bishopric-of-brixen.o: The bishopric moved from [[e:saben-abbey|Säben]] to [[e:brixen|Brixen]] (Bressanone) around 990. In 1027 [[e:conrad-ii-holy-roman-emperor|Emperor Conrad II]] granted [[e:bishop|Bishop]] Hartwig the counties of the [[e:inn-river|Inn]] and [[e:eisack|Eisack]] valleys, and in 1091 the [[e:puster-valley|Puster valley]] followed, so that loyal bishops would hold the passes on the imperial road to [[e:rome|Rome]].
prince-bishopric-of-brixen.r: The [[e:bishop|bishops]] entrusted their counties to advocates, chiefly the counts of [[e:tyrol|Tyrol]], who gradually absorbed most of their power. The bishopric retained [[e:brixen|Brixen]], [[e:bruneck|Bruneck]] and scattered lands. Cardinal [[e:nicholas-of-cusa|Nicholas of Cusa]], bishop from 1450, clashed bitterly with Duke [[e:sigismund-archduke-of-austria|Sigismund of Tyrol]] and was imprisoned in 1460.
prince-bishopric-of-brixen.e: The prince-bishopric was secularised in 1803 and annexed by [[e:austria|Austria]], then passed to [[e:bavaria|Bavaria]] from 1805 to 1814, and back to Austria. After the [[e:first-world-war|First World War]] [[e:brixen|Brixen]] became part of [[e:italy|Italy]], and in 1964 the see moved to [[e:bolzano|Bolzano]], becoming the [[e:diocese-of-bolzano-brixen|Diocese of Bolzano-Brixen]].

phocaea.t: Ionian city whose daring sailors founded Massalia and explored the western Mediterranean as far as Tartessos in Spain.
phocaea.o: Phocaea, the northernmost Ionian city, was founded on a peninsula north of the [[e:gediz-river|Hermus]] c. 1000 BCE by settlers said to have come from [[e:phocis|Phocis]]. Its rocky territory pushed the [[e:phocaeans|Phocaeans]] to the sea, and from the 7th century BCE they sailed long distances in fast fifty-oared ships.
phocaea.r: [[e:herodotus|Herodotus]] credits [[e:phocaeans|Phocaeans]] with opening the Adriatic, Tyrrhenian and Iberian seas. They founded [[s:lampsacus|Lampsacus]], [[s:massalia|Massalia]] c. 600 BCE, [[e:alalia|Alalia]] on [[s:corsican-republic|Corsica]] and [[s:emporion|Emporion]] in [[e:spain|Spain]], and won the friendship of King [[e:arganthonios|Arganthonius]] of [[s:tartessos|Tartessos]]. When [[e:harpagus|Harpagus]] besieged the city c. 545 BCE, most citizens sailed west; those at Alalia fought [[e:carthage|Carthaginians]] and [[e:etruscans|Etruscans]] c. 540 BCE.
phocaea.e: Phocaea recovered and provided [[e:dionysius-of-phocaea|Dionysius]], commander of the Greek fleet at [[e:battle-of-lade|Lade]] in 494 BCE. In 132 BCE it backed [[e:aristonicus|Aristonicus]] against [[e:rome|Rome]] and was spared destruction only through Massalia's appeal, then joined the province of Asia.

principality-of-mozhaysk.t: A western appanage of Moscow whose prince Ivan helped capture and blind Grand Prince Vasily II during Moscow's civil war.
principality-of-mozhaysk.o: [[e:mozhaysk|Mozhaysk]], on the [[e:moskva-river|Moskva]] river west of [[e:moscow|Moscow]], was taken from [[e:smolensk|Smolensk]] in 1303. In his will of 1389 [[e:dmitry-donskoy|Dmitry Donskoy]] left it, with [[e:vereya|Vereya]] and [[e:belozersk|Beloozero]], to his son Andrei, who ruled it as an [[e:appanage|appanage]] within the [[s:grand-duchy-of-moscow|Grand Duchy of Moscow]].
principality-of-mozhaysk.r: The principality guarded [[e:moscow|Moscow's]] approach from [[s:grand-duchy-of-lithuania|Lithuania]] and [[e:smolensk|Smolensk]]. During the long civil war over the Moscow throne, Andrei's son [[e:ivan-andreyevich-of-mozhaysk|Ivan of Mozhaysk]] joined [[e:dmitry-shemyaka|Dmitry Shemyaka]], and in 1446 he helped seize [[e:vasily-ii-of-moscow|Vasily II]] at the [[e:trinity-lavra-of-st-sergius|Trinity Monastery]], after which Vasily was blinded.
principality-of-mozhaysk.e: When [[e:vasily-ii-of-moscow|Vasily II]] regained power, he sent an army against [[e:mozhaysk|Mozhaysk]] in 1454. Ivan fled to the [[s:grand-duchy-of-lithuania|Grand Duchy of Lithuania]], and Mozhaysk was absorbed into [[e:moscow|Moscow's]] lands, while [[e:vereya|Vereya]] continued for a time under Ivan's brother Mikhail.

principality-of-sedan.t: A Protestant sovereign principality on the Meuse, ruled by the La Marck and La Tour d'Auvergne families, which sheltered Huguenots and French rebels.
principality-of-sedan.o: In 1424 Everard de la Marck acquired the lordship of Sedan on the [[e:meuse|Meuse]], at the frontier between [[e:france|France]], [[s:county-of-luxembourg|Luxembourg]] and [[s:prince-bishopric-of-liege|Liège]]. His descendants built a great fortress there and claimed [[e:sovereignty|sovereignty]], owing allegiance to neither the French king nor the emperor.
principality-of-sedan.r: [[e:robert-ii-de-la-marck|Robert II de la Marck]] and his successors were also dukes of [[s:duchy-of-bouillon|Bouillon]]. The princes adopted [[e:calvinism|Calvinism]], and Sedan became a [[e:huguenots|Huguenot]] refuge with a Protestant academy founded in 1602. In 1591 the heiress [[e:charlotte-de-la-marck|Charlotte de la Marck]] married [[e:henri-de-la-tour-dauvergne-duke-of-bouillon|Henri de La Tour d'Auvergne]], father of [[e:henri-de-la-tour-d-auvergne-viscount-of-turenne|Marshal Turenne]], who was born at Sedan in 1611. Sedan's cloth industry later flourished.
principality-of-sedan.e: [[e:frederic-maurice-de-la-tour-dauvergne|Frédéric-Maurice de La Tour d'Auvergne]] joined the conspiracy of [[e:henri-coiffier-de-ruze-marquis-of-cinq-mars|Cinq-Mars]] against [[e:cardinal-richelieu|Richelieu]], and to save his life ceded Sedan to [[e:louis-xiii-of-france|Louis XIII]] in 1642. The principality was absorbed into the [[s:kingdom-of-france|Kingdom of France]].
ru: Henri de La Tour d'Auvergne, Duke of Bouillon

principality-of-pronsk.t: An appanage principality of the Ryazan land whose princes repeatedly challenged the grand princes of Ryazan.
principality-of-pronsk.o: Pronsk, on the Pronya river south of [[s:grand-principality-of-ryazan|Ryazan]], was a fortified frontier town facing the steppe. In the 1180s it became the seat of a separate branch of the [[e:ryazan|Ryazan]] princely house, and for three centuries its rulers held it as an [[e:appanage|appanage]] of the Grand Principality of Ryazan.
principality-of-pronsk.r: Pronsk princes often fought their [[s:grand-principality-of-ryazan|Ryazan]] cousins for the senior throne, sometimes with the help of the [[s:golden-horde|Golden Horde]] or [[e:moscow|Moscow]]. In 1408 [[e:ivan-vladimirovich-of-pronsk|Ivan Vladimirovich of Pronsk]] briefly drove out the [[e:ryazan|Ryazan]] grand prince with [[e:tatars|Tatar]] support. Like other border lands, Pronsk suffered heavily from steppe raids and was sacked by the [[e:mongols|Mongols]] in 1237.
principality-of-pronsk.e: In the 15th century Pronsk was gradually reabsorbed into [[s:grand-principality-of-ryazan|Ryazan]], and by the 1480s its princes had lost their independent role. The territory followed [[e:ryazan|Ryazan]] into the [[s:grand-duchy-of-moscow|Grand Duchy of Moscow]] in 1521, while the Pronsky princely family served in the Russian nobility.

principality-of-birkenfeld.t: Hunsrück exclave of the Grand Duchy of Oldenburg, ruled from the North Sea coast for more than a century.
principality-of-birkenfeld.o: At the [[e:congress-of-vienna|Congress of Vienna]], the Grand Duke of [[s:county-of-oldenburg|Oldenburg]] was awarded territory on the left bank of the [[e:rhine|Rhine]]. In 1817 he received a district of the former [[e:sarre-department|French Saar]] [[e:departement|department]] around [[e:birkenfeld|Birkenfeld]] in the [[e:hunsruck|Hunsrück]], which became the Principality of Birkenfeld, an exclave hundreds of kilometres from Oldenburg.
principality-of-birkenfeld.r: The principality was governed by a regional government in [[e:birkenfeld|Birkenfeld]] under Oldenburg's laws and had its own provincial council. Its people were mostly Protestant farmers, with gemstone cutting and agate working around Idar and [[e:idar-oberstein|Oberstein]] as a distinctive industry. After 1918 it formed a part of the [[s:free-state-of-oldenburg|Free State of Oldenburg]].
principality-of-birkenfeld.e: Under the [[e:greater-hamburg-act|Greater Hamburg Act]] of 1937, [[s:county-of-oldenburg|Oldenburg]] ceded [[e:birkenfeld|Birkenfeld]] to [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]], which made it a district of the [[e:rhine-province|Rhine Province]]. It is now part of [[e:rhineland-palatinate|Rhineland-Palatinate]].

paser-sultanate.t: A Malay-Dayak sultanate in the southeast of East Kalimantan, ruled from Paser Belengkong until the Dutch took control in 1906.
paser-sultanate.o: Paser lay on the Kendilo River in southeast [[e:borneo|Borneo]], between the [[s:banjar-sultanate|Banjar Sultanate]] and [[s:kutai-kartanegara-sultanate|Kutai Kartanegara]]. Local tradition traces its royal house to Putri Petung, a princess born from a bamboo stem, who married a prince from [[e:java|Java]]. Its rulers adopted [[e:islam|Islam]] in the 16th century, and the register dates the sultanate from 1516.
paser-sultanate.r: Paser drew on [[e:rice|rice]] farming and forest products such as rattan and resin, and traded with [[e:banjarmasin|Banjarmasin]] and with [[e:bugis|Bugis]] merchants, many of whom settled on its coast in the 18th century and gained influence at court. It acknowledged Banjar overlordship at times.
paser-sultanate.e: The [[e:dutch|Dutch]] made treaties with Paser in the 19th century and annexed it into their administration in 1906, leaving the sultan as a figurehead. Its lands became [[e:paser-regency|Paser Regency]], and the old palace at Paser Belengkong is now a museum.

praeneste.t: Latin hill city east of Rome, famous for its princely tombs, its bronze cistae and the oracle of Fortuna Primigenia.
praeneste.o: Praeneste, modern Palestrina, occupied a spur of the Monti Prenestini commanding the routes from [[e:latium|Latium]] to [[e:campania|Campania]]. In the 7th century BCE its rulers were buried in the [[e:bernardini-tomb|Bernardini]] and Barberini tombs with gold, [[e:silver|silver]] and [[e:ivory-trade|ivory]] from the eastern [[e:mediterranean|Mediterranean]], among the richest burials in [[e:italy|Italy]].
praeneste.r: Praeneste was a powerful and often independent member of the [[s:latin-league|Latin League]]. Its workshops produced engraved bronze cistae, cylindrical boxes for toiletries such as the Ficoroni cista. The sanctuary of [[e:sanctuary-of-fortuna-primigenia|Fortuna Primigenia]], where oracles were drawn by lot, was later rebuilt on a vast terraced scale in the 2nd century BCE. Local [[e:latin|Latin]] had distinct features noted by Roman writers.
praeneste.e: Praeneste fought [[e:rome|Rome]] in the [[e:latin-war|Latin War]] and lost land in 338 BCE, but remained a separate allied city until it gained citizenship after the [[e:social-war-91-87-bce|Social War]]. It sheltered [[e:gaius-marius-the-younger|Gaius Marius the Younger]] in 82 BCE; [[e:sulla|Sulla]] took it, executed its men and planted a colony.

plataea.t: Small Boeotian city that defied Thebes, stood with Athens at Marathon and gave its name to the battle that ended the Persian invasion of Greece in 479 BCE.
plataea.o: [[e:battle-of-plataea|Plataea]] lay on the northern slopes of [[e:mount-cithaeron|Mount Cithaeron]], on the border between [[e:boeotia|Boeotia]] and [[e:attica|Attica]]. When [[s:thebes|Thebes]] pressed it to join the [[s:boeotian-league|Boeotian League]] in the late 6th century BCE, the Plataeans turned to [[s:athens|Athens]], traditionally in 519 BCE. That alliance shaped the rest of their history: alone among the [[e:greeks|Greeks]], they sent their whole levy to fight beside the Athenians at [[e:battle-of-marathon|Marathon]] in 490 BCE.
plataea.r: A modest farming community governed by its own citizen assembly, [[e:battle-of-plataea|Plataea]] mattered far beyond its size. In 479 BCE the allied Greek army under the Spartan [[e:pausanias-general|Pausanias]] defeated the Persian general [[e:mardonius|Mardonius]] on its territory, and the city was charged with tending the graves of the fallen and hosting a festival of freedom, the [[e:eleutheria-plataea|Eleutheria]]. Its people spoke the Boeotian dialect and kept close cultural ties with [[s:athens|Athens]].
plataea.e: Theban aggression began the [[e:peloponnesian-war|Peloponnesian War]] at Plataea in 431 BCE; after a famous siege the city surrendered to [[s:sparta|Sparta]] and was razed in 427 BCE. Restored in 386 BCE, it was destroyed again by [[s:thebes|Thebes]] in 373 BCE and rebuilt under [[e:philip-ii-of-macedon|Philip II]] and Alexander. It then belonged to the [[s:boeotian-league|Boeotian League]] until Roman conquest in 146 BCE.

peoples-republic-of-korea.t: A government proclaimed by Korean leaders in Seoul in September 1945, after liberation from Japan, and rejected by the American occupation.
peoples-republic-of-korea.o: On [[e:japan|Japan's]] surrender the moderate leftist [[e:lyuh-woon-hyung|Lyuh Woon-hyung]] formed the [[e:committee-for-the-preparation-of-korean-independence|Committee for the Preparation of Korean Independence]], which organised local committees to keep order. On 6 September 1945, two days before American troops landed, a national assembly in [[e:seoul|Seoul]] proclaimed the People's [[e:south-korea|Republic of Korea]].
peoples-republic-of-korea.r: Its cabinet named prominent figures, including [[e:syngman-rhee|Syngman Rhee]] as chairman, often without their consent, and leftists dominated. People's committees across the country ran local affairs, organised land and labour programmes and took over Japanese property in many areas.
peoples-republic-of-korea.e: The [[s:united-states-army-military-government-in-korea|United States Army Military Government in Korea]] refused to recognise it, declared in October 1945 that it had no authority and later suppressed its committees in the south; it faded by early 1946. In the north, its committees were absorbed into the Soviet-backed administration.

panchala.t: A powerful Vedic kingdom east of the Kurus, between the Ganges and the Yamuna, later one of the sixteen mahajanapadas of early Buddhist texts.
panchala.o: Formed in the Later Vedic period from an alliance of several clans, among them the Krivis, the Panchalas settled east of the Kuru lands. Vedic texts pair Kuru and Panchala as the heart of the Vedic world, and Panchala kings such as [[e:keshin-dalbhya|Keshin Dalbhya]] appear in the [[e:brahmanas|Brahmanas]] as patrons of sacrifice and ritual learning.
panchala.r: The Panchala king [[e:pravahana-jaivali|Pravahana Jaivali]] appears in the [[e:upanishads|Upanishads]] instructing [[e:brahmins|Brahmins]] on the doctrine of rebirth, a sign of the court's intellectual standing. The [[e:ganges-plain|Ganges]] divided the kingdom into a northern half with its capital at [[e:ahichchhatra|Ahichchhatra]] and a southern half centred on [[e:kampilya|Kampilya]]. Iron tools and [[e:rice|rice]] and barley farming supported a growing population in [[e:painted-grey-ware-culture|Painted Grey Ware]] settlements. The [[e:mahabharata|Mahabharata]] makes [[e:draupadi|Draupadi]] a Panchala princess.
panchala.e: By the 6th century BCE Panchala had become a sangha governed by leading clans. It was absorbed by the [[s:nanda-empire|Nanda Empire]] in the 4th century BCE and passed to the [[e:maurya-empire|Mauryas]]. Local kings of the [[e:mitra|Mitra]] line later issued coins at [[e:ahichchhatra|Ahichchhatra]] in the 2nd and 1st centuries BCE.

pogesanians.t: Prussian people between the Elbląg and Pasłęk rivers, whose land saw the founding of Elbing and fierce fighting in the Great Prussian Uprising.
pogesanians.o: Pogesania lay along the [[e:vistula-lagoon|Vistula Lagoon]] east of the [[e:elblag|Elbląg]] river, in modern northern [[e:poland|Poland]]. Its Prussian inhabitants lived near the old trading centre of [[e:truso|Truso]], a [[e:viking-age|Viking Age]] emporium described by the traveller Wulfstan around 890, and they are known from [[e:peter-of-dusburg|Peter of Dusburg's]] chronicle.
pogesanians.r: Pogesanian society was led by nobles holding hillforts, with farming, fishing and the amber trade as mainstays. They kept the Prussian gods and customs, including cremation of the dead, which Wulfstan described in detail.
pogesanians.e: The [[e:teutonic-order|Teutonic Order]] and the Hanseatic settlers of [[s:free-and-hanseatic-city-of-lubeck|Lübeck]] founded [[e:elblag|Elbing]] on their land in 1237. In the [[e:great-prussian-uprising|Great Prussian Uprising]] from 1260 the Pogesanians, led by [[e:auktume|Auktume]], attacked Elbing and other castles, but they were subdued by 1274. Their territory became part of the Order's state.

principality-of-serpukhov.t: An appanage of the Moscow princes south of the capital, ruled by Vladimir the Bold, hero of the Battle of Kulikovo.
principality-of-serpukhov.o: [[e:serpukhov|Serpukhov]] on the [[e:oka-river|Oka]] guarded [[e:moscow|Moscow's]] southern approaches against the steppe. In 1341 [[e:ivan-i-of-moscow|Ivan I Kalita's]] will took effect, and his youngest son Andrei received Serpukhov and surrounding lands, including [[e:borovsk|Borovsk]], as an [[e:appanage|appanage]] within the [[s:grand-duchy-of-moscow|Grand Duchy of Moscow]].
principality-of-serpukhov.r: Andrei's son [[e:vladimir-the-bold|Vladimir the Bold]], cousin of [[e:dmitry-donskoy|Dmitry Donskoy]], was [[e:moscow|Moscow's]] leading general. At [[e:battle-of-kulikovo|Kulikovo]] in 1380 he and the commander [[e:dmitry-bobrok-volynsky|Dmitry Bobrok]] led the ambush regiment whose attack decided the battle. He built the [[e:serpukhov|Serpukhov]] kremlin and founded monasteries, and his principality served as a buffer against [[e:tatars|Tatar]] and Lithuanian raids.
principality-of-serpukhov.e: During [[e:moscow|Moscow's]] civil war Vladimir's grandson [[e:vasily-yaroslavich-of-serpukhov|Vasily Yaroslavich]] supported [[e:vasily-ii-of-moscow|Vasily II]], but in 1456 the grand prince had him arrested and annexed [[e:serpukhov|Serpukhov]]. Vasily died in prison, and the [[e:appanage|appanage]] ended.

principality-of-lippe.t: Small Westphalian principality at Detmold that survived as a German state into the 20th century and played a part in Hitler's rise.
principality-of-lippe.o: The lords of Lippe held lands around [[e:detmold|Detmold]] and [[e:lemgo|Lemgo]] from the 12th century, becoming counts in 1528. Though granted princely rank in 1720, they did not use the title until Count [[e:leopold-i-prince-of-lippe|Leopold I]] accepted it in 1789, when the [[s:county-of-lippe|County of Lippe]]-Detmold became the Principality of Lippe.
principality-of-lippe.r: Princess Pauline, regent from 1802 to 1820, kept Lippe independent by joining the [[s:confederation-of-the-rhine|Confederation of the Rhine]] and introduced social reforms, including a nursery school. Lippe was rural and Calvinist, and many men worked seasonally as brickmakers elsewhere. A disputed succession between 1895 and 1905, involving [[e:kaiser|Kaiser]] William II's brother-in-law, was settled by arbitration in favour of the Biesterfeld line.
principality-of-lippe.e: Lippe joined the [[s:german-empire|German Empire]] in 1871. [[e:leopold-iv-prince-of-lippe|Prince Leopold IV]] abdicated in November 1918, and the state continued as the [[s:free-state-of-lippe|Free State of Lippe]] until 1947.

principality-of-nassau-diez.t: Nassau territory on the Lahn whose counts, as hereditary stadtholders of Friesland, became the House of Orange-Nassau that rules the Netherlands today.
principality-of-nassau-diez.o: Nassau-[[e:diez|Diez]] arose in the 1606 partition of the lands of [[e:john-vi-count-of-nassau-dillenburg|John VI of Nassau-Dillenburg]], when [[e:ernest-casimir-i-count-of-nassau-dietz|Ernst Casimir]] received Diez on the [[e:lahn|Lahn]]. Ernst Casimir served the [[s:dutch-republic|Dutch Republic]] as a general and became stadtholder of [[s:lordship-of-frisia|Friesland]] and [[e:groningen|Groningen]], beginning his line's long connection with the northern [[s:kingdom-of-the-netherlands|Netherlands]].
principality-of-nassau-diez.r: The German lands were small and governed from [[e:diez|Diez]] and later the [[e:oranienstein-palace|Oranienstein]] palace, while the counts spent their careers in the [[s:dutch-republic|Dutch Republic]], where they held the Frisian stadtholdership hereditarily. They were raised to princes of the Empire in 1654. [[e:john-william-friso|John William Friso]] inherited part of [[e:william-iii-of-england|William III]]'s [[s:principality-of-orange|Orange]] claims in 1702, and his son [[e:william-iv-prince-of-orange|William IV]] united all Nassau-Ottonian lands by 1743.
principality-of-nassau-diez.e: [[e:william-iv-prince-of-orange|William IV]] became stadtholder of all the [[s:dutch-republic|United Provinces]] in 1747. In 1806 [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]] confiscated the German lands, which went to the [[s:grand-duchy-of-berg|Grand Duchy of Berg]], and after 1815 they passed to the [[s:duchy-of-nassau|Duchy of Nassau]] and [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]]. William IV's grandson became [[e:william-i-of-the-netherlands|King William I of the Netherlands]].

provisional-government-of-western-thrace.t: Short-lived Muslim-led state in Western Thrace in 1913, set up by Ottoman officers to keep the region from Bulgaria after the Second Balkan War.
provisional-government-of-western-thrace.o: [[s:bulgaria|Bulgaria]] took [[e:western-thrace|Western Thrace]] in the [[e:first-balkan-war|First Balkan War]]. When the [[e:second-balkan-war|Second Balkan War]] broke out in 1913, the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]] retook [[e:edirne|Edirne]], and Ottoman officers led by [[e:suleyman-askeri|Süleyman Askerî]], together with local Turkish and [[e:pomaks|Pomak]] irregulars, drove Bulgarian forces from the region. In late August 1913 they proclaimed an independent government at [[e:komotini|Gümülcine]], today Komotini.
provisional-government-of-western-thrace.r: The government had a president, ministers, a flag, stamps and an army of a few thousand irregulars, drawing on the region's Muslim majority. It was effectively run by Ottoman officers acting unofficially, and no foreign power recognised it. It lasted about two months.
provisional-government-of-western-thrace.e: By the Treaty of Constantinople in September 1913 the Ottoman government recognised Bulgarian possession of [[e:western-thrace|Western Thrace]] and withdrew support, and Bulgarian troops took over in October. The region passed to [[e:greece|Greece]] after the [[e:first-world-war|First World War]], where its Muslim minority remains.

prince-bishopric-of-merseburg.t: An Ottonian bishopric on the Saale whose bishop Thietmar wrote a famous chronicle, later absorbed into Saxony after the Reformation.
prince-bishopric-of-merseburg.o: Otto I founded the bishopric of [[e:merseburg|Merseburg]] in 968 to fulfil a vow made before the Battle of Lechfeld, as a suffragan of [[e:magdeburg|Magdeburg]]. It was dissolved in 981, its lands divided among neighbours, but [[e:henry-ii-holy-roman-emperor|Henry II]] restored it in 1004. The [[e:bishop|bishops]] built a cathedral beside the royal palace at Merseburg.
prince-bishopric-of-merseburg.r: [[e:bishop|Bishop]] [[e:thietmar-of-merseburg|Thietmar of Merseburg]], from 1009 to 1018, wrote a chronicle that is a key source on the Ottonian empire, the [[e:slavs|Slavs]] and early [[e:poland|Poland]]. The bishops ruled a small territory along the [[e:saale|Saale]]. The cathedral library preserves the [[e:merseburg-charms|Merseburg Charms]], the only surviving [[e:old-high-german|Old High German]] pagan spells.
prince-bishopric-of-merseburg.e: [[e:merseburg|Merseburg]] came under the influence of the [[e:house-of-wettin|Wettin]] rulers of [[e:saxony|Saxony]]. After the [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]], a [[e:saxons|Saxon]] prince became administrator in 1561, and from 1565 the see was effectively a Saxon possession. From 1656 to 1738 it formed the [[s:duchy-of-saxe-merseburg|Duchy of Saxe-Merseburg]], before reverting to the electorate and passing to [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] in 1815.

paris-commune.t: The revolutionary government that ruled Paris for ten weeks in 1871, and whose bloody suppression became a lasting symbol for the socialist left.
paris-commune.o: After [[e:france|France's]] defeat by [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] and the long siege of [[e:paris|Paris]], the government of [[e:adolphe-thiers|Adolphe Thiers]] tried to remove the National Guard's [[e:field-artillery|cannons]] from [[e:montmartre|Montmartre]] on 18 March 1871. Parisians resisted, the government withdrew to [[e:versailles|Versailles]], and elections on 26 March created the Commune.
paris-commune.r: The Commune's council, a mix of [[e:jacobin-club|Jacobins]], socialists and followers of [[e:pierre-joseph-proudhon|Proudhon]] and [[e:louis-auguste-blanqui|Blanqui]], separated church and state, abolished night work in bakeries, let workers take over abandoned workshops and postponed rents. Women such as [[e:louise-michel|Louise Michel]] played prominent roles. The [[e:communards|Communards]] also pulled down the [[e:vendome-column|Vendôme Column]].
paris-commune.e: Government troops entered [[e:paris|Paris]] on 21 May, and during the 'Bloody Week' that followed thousands of [[e:communards|Communards]] were killed, many by summary execution; the Communards shot hostages and burned the [[e:tuileries-palace|Tuileries]]. Thousands more were tried and deported to [[s:new-caledonia|New Caledonia]]. The [[s:french-third-republic|French Third Republic]] survived.

principality-of-polotsk.t: The oldest principality of the Belarusian lands, a Dvina trading power that kept its own dynasty and long resisted Kiev.
principality-of-polotsk.o: [[e:polotsk|Polotsk]] on the [[e:western-dvina|Western Dvina]] was a [[e:krivichs|Krivich]] town ruled in the 10th century by the Scandinavian [[e:rogvolod|Rogvolod]], until [[e:vladimir-the-great|Vladimir I]] killed him and married his daughter [[e:rogneda-of-polotsk|Rogneda]]. Around 987 Vladimir gave Polotsk to their son [[e:izyaslav-of-polotsk|Izyaslav]], whose descendants held it as a separate dynasty.
principality-of-polotsk.r: [[e:polotsk|Polotsk]] controlled the [[e:western-dvina|Dvina]] route to the Baltic and traded with Riga and [[s:gotland|Gotland]]. Its princes often fought the rest of Rus', and [[e:vseslav-of-polotsk|Vseslav]], called the Sorcerer, who ruled for over fifty years, even held [[e:kyiv|Kiev]] briefly in 1068. The [[e:saint-sophia-cathedral-polotsk|Cathedral of Saint Sophia]] and the abbess [[e:euphrosyne-of-polotsk|Euphrosyne of Polotsk]] made it a religious centre.
principality-of-polotsk.e: By the 12th century the land split into smaller principalities, including [[e:minsk|Minsk]] and [[e:vitebsk|Vitebsk]], and German crusaders took its Livonian tributaries. [[e:polotsk|Polotsk]] came under the [[s:grand-duchy-of-lithuania|Grand Duchy of Lithuania]] in the early 14th century, and its separate princely rule ended in 1392 when [[e:vytautas-the-great|Vytautas]] installed his own governors.

principality-of-abkhazia.t: A principality on the Black Sea coast ruled by the Shervashidze family, between Georgian, Ottoman and Russian power, until Russia abolished it in 1864.
principality-of-abkhazia.o: As the [[s:kingdom-of-georgia|Kingdom of Georgia]] broke up in the 1460s, the [[e:house-of-shervashidze|Shervashidze]], or Chachba, family who governed the [[e:abkhaz-people|Abkhaz]] coast as eristavis under the [[e:house-of-dadiani|Dadiani of Mingrelia]] made themselves independent princes with their seat at Sukhumi and later [[e:lykhny|Lykhny]]. Family tradition traced the line to the [[s:shirvanshah-state|Shirvanshahs]], a claim that cannot be verified.
principality-of-abkhazia.r: The princes ruled a society of nobles and peasants living by livestock, farming and coastal trade, including a [[e:atlantic-slave-trade|slave trade]] with Ottoman ports. From the 16th century Ottoman influence grew: the coast came under Ottoman garrisons, and many [[e:abkhaz-people|Abkhaz]] nobles adopted [[e:islam|Islam]]. [[e:keleshbey-chachba|Keleshbey Chachba]] strengthened the principality but was assassinated in 1808.
principality-of-abkhazia.e: His son Giorgi accepted a Russian [[e:protectorate|protectorate]] in 1810. The [[s:russian-empire|Russian Empire]] abolished the principality in 1864, and after revolts many [[e:abkhaz-people|Abkhaz]] were deported to the [[s:ottoman-empire|Ottoman Empire]] in the exodus called the [[e:mahajirstvo|Mahajirstvo]].

patdi-state.t: A small state on the edge of the Little Rann of Kutch, unusual for being ruled by a Kanbi (Patidar) family of Desais rather than Rajputs.
patdi-state.o: Patdi emerged in the 18th century when a family of Kanbi Desais, holders of revenue rights in the region, established themselves as hereditary rulers of the town and surrounding villages.
patdi-state.r: The Desai of Patdi governed a small, dry territory near the salt flats of the [[e:little-rann-of-kutch|Little Rann]], where salt production was important. It was a minor state under British political supervision, and little else of its history is recorded.
patdi-state.e: After independence Patdi was absorbed into the Indian administration in 1948; it now lies in [[e:surendranagar-district|Surendranagar district]] of [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]].

pontianak-sultanate.t: Arab-founded Malay sultanate at the mouth of the Kapuas river in West Borneo, origin of the city of Pontianak.
pontianak-sultanate.o: [[e:syarif-abdurrahman-alkadrie|Syarif Abdurrahman Alkadrie]], son of a Hadhrami Arab cleric who had settled in [[e:mempawah|Mempawah]], built a trading settlement at the junction of the [[e:kapuas-river|Kapuas]] and [[e:landak-river|Landak]] rivers in 1771. With [[e:bugis|Bugis]] support he made it a thriving port and was proclaimed sultan in 1778, founding a dynasty of Arab descent.
pontianak-sultanate.r: Pontianak controlled the trade of the [[e:kapuas-river|Kapuas]] basin, exporting gold, diamonds, rattan and forest products. The [[s:dutch-east-india-company-territories|Dutch East India Company]] recognised the sultan in 1779 in return for a share of trade. The [[e:kadriah-palace|Kadriah]] palace and the [[e:jami|Jami]] mosque of [[e:sultan|Sultan]] [[e:syarif-abdurrahman-alkadrie|Syarif Abdurrahman]] survive in the city.
pontianak-sultanate.e: During the Japanese occupation [[e:sultan|Sultan]] [[e:syarif-muhammad-alkadrie|Syarif Muhammad Alkadrie]] and much of the West Bornean elite were executed in the [[e:mandor-affair|Mandor killings]]. [[e:hamid-ii-of-pontianak|Sultan Hamid II]], who designed the [[e:garuda-pancasila|Garuda Pancasila]] emblem, led West Kalimantan within the [[s:united-states-of-indonesia|United States of Indonesia]], but was arrested in 1950 and the sultanate was absorbed into [[s:indonesia|Indonesia]].

principality-of-badakhshan.t: A mountain principality of the Pamirs and upper Amu Darya, ruled by mirs from Faizabad until the Afghan Emirate absorbed it.
principality-of-badakhshan.o: Badakhshan, famed since antiquity for its lapis lazuli and rubies, was ruled in the 16th and early 17th centuries by [[e:timurid-empire|Timurid]] and [[e:uzbeks|Uzbek]] governors. Around 1657 a local dynasty of mirs of the Yarid family, claiming saintly descent, established independent rule from [[e:fayzabad-badakhshan|Faizabad]] on the [[e:kokcha-river|Kokcha River]].
principality-of-badakhshan.r: The mirs ruled a mountainous land of [[e:tajiks|Tajik]] farmers and herders, including [[e:ismailism|Ismaili]] communities in the [[e:pamir-mountains|Pamirs]] and [[e:sunni-islam|Sunni]] Muslims in the lowlands. Revenue came from mines, trade routes to [[s:kingdom-of-shule|Kashgar]] and [[s:chitral-state|Chitral]], and tribute from [[e:vassal|vassal]] valleys such as [[e:shughnan|Shughnan]] and [[e:wakhan|Wakhan]]. The state was frequently raided by the [[s:kataghan-khanate|Kataghan Khanate]] and the [[s:durrani-empire|Durrani Empire]].
principality-of-badakhshan.e: In 1859 the [[s:emirate-of-afghanistan|Emirate of Afghanistan]] made Badakhshan a [[e:vassal|vassal]], and around 1881 [[e:abdur-rahman-khan|Abdur Rahman Khan]] annexed it fully. The Anglo-Russian boundary settlements of the 1890s divided the region along the [[e:panj-river|Panj River]] between [[s:islamic-emirate-of-afghanistan-2021-present|Afghanistan]] and the Russian [[e:protectorate|protectorate]] of [[e:bukhara|Bukhara]].

principality-of-dombes.t: A small sovereign principality north of Lyon, with its own parliament and mint at Trévoux, held by royal relatives until it was sold to Louis XV.
principality-of-dombes.o: The Dombes, a plateau of ponds east of the [[e:saone|Saône]], belonged to the lords of [[e:beaujeu|Beaujeu]] and then the dukes of [[s:ile-bourbon|Bourbon]]. After the confiscation of the [[e:charles-iii-duke-of-bourbon|Constable of Bourbon's]] lands in 1523 it was held by the crown, then restored in 1560 to the [[e:house-of-bourbon-montpensier|Bourbon-Montpensier]] family, who ruled it as a sovereign principality outside the [[s:kingdom-of-france|Kingdom of France]].
principality-of-dombes.r: The princes kept a parliament at [[e:trevoux|Trévoux]], minted coin and taxed separately, though in practice the land was closely tied to [[e:france|France]]. [[e:anne-marie-louise-dorleans-duchess-of-montpensier|Anne Marie Louise d'Orléans]], La Grande Mademoiselle, held it and in 1681 ceded it to the Duke of [[s:county-of-maine|Maine]], [[e:louis-xiv|Louis XIV's]] legitimised son. [[e:jesuits|Jesuits]] at Trévoux published the [[e:journal-de-trevoux|Journal de Trévoux]] and the [[e:dictionnaire-de-trevoux|Dictionnaire de Trévoux]].
principality-of-dombes.e: In 1762 the Duke of Maine's son, the Count of Eu, exchanged the principality with [[e:louis-xv|Louis XV]] for lands in [[e:france|France]], and it became part of the kingdom.

prince-bishopric-of-warmia.t: A church principality in Prussia, ruled by its bishops for over 500 years, where Nicolaus Copernicus worked as a canon.
prince-bishopric-of-warmia.o: In 1243 the papal legate [[e:william-of-modena|William of Modena]] divided conquered [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] into four dioceses, one of them Warmia. Its [[e:bishop|bishop]] received a third of the diocese as his own territory, while the rest went to the [[e:teutonic-order|Teutonic Order]]. The bishops made [[e:lidzbark-warminski|Lidzbark]] their residence and the cathedral chapter settled at [[e:frombork|Frombork]].
prince-bishopric-of-warmia.r: The [[e:bishop|bishops]] ruled as territorial princes, with their own castles, towns and officials, and Warmia was settled by German colonists alongside [[e:old-prussians|Old Prussians]] and later [[e:poles|Poles]]. [[e:lucas-watzenrode|Lucas Watzenrode]], bishop from 1489, brought his nephew [[e:nicolaus-copernicus|Nicolaus Copernicus]] to serve the chapter, and Copernicus wrote his work on the heavens at [[e:frombork|Frombork]]. Bishop [[e:stanislaus-hosius|Stanislaus Hosius]] made it a stronghold of the [[e:counter-reformation|Counter-Reformation]].
prince-bishopric-of-warmia.e: After the [[e:second-peace-of-thorn|Second Peace of Thorn]] in 1466 Warmia came under the protection of the Polish Crown, keeping wide self-government as part of [[s:royal-prussia|Royal Prussia]]. The [[e:first-partition-of-poland|First Partition of Poland]] in 1772 gave it to the [[s:kingdom-of-prussia|Kingdom of Prussia]], which took over the [[e:bishop|bishops]]' lands. The last bishop-prince, the poet [[e:ignacy-krasicki|Ignacy Krasicki]], kept only his spiritual office.

pajang-sultanate.t: A short-lived inland Javanese sultanate under Hadiwijaya that moved power from the coast to the interior between Demak and Mataram.
pajang-sultanate.o: [[e:hadiwijaya|Hadiwijaya]], also known as Jaka Tingkir, was a son-in-law of [[e:trenggana|Sultan Trenggana of Demak]] and ruler of Pajang, near modern [[s:surakarta-sunanate|Surakarta]]. In the succession war after Trenggana's death he defeated [[e:arya-penangsang|Arya Penangsang]] with the help of [[e:ki-ageng-pemanahan|Ki Ageng Pemanahan]] and his son [[e:panembahan-senapati|Sutawijaya]], and took the title sultan, the register dating his rule from 1568.
pajang-sultanate.r: Pajang moved the centre of Javanese power from the north coast to the [[e:rice|rice]] lands of the interior. [[e:hadiwijaya|Hadiwijaya]] received the homage of the East Javanese lords at [[s:giri-kedaton|Giri Kedaton]] and rewarded [[e:ki-ageng-pemanahan|Ki Ageng Pemanahan]] with the land of [[s:mataram-sultanate|Mataram]].
pajang-sultanate.e: [[e:panembahan-senapati|Sutawijaya]] grew powerful at [[s:mataram-sultanate|Mataram]] and defied Pajang. After [[e:hadiwijaya|Hadiwijaya]] died in 1582, [[e:arya-pangiri|Arya Pangiri]] of [[s:demak-sultanate|Demak]] seized the throne, but in 1586 Sutawijaya, allied with Hadiwijaya's son [[e:pangeran-benawa|Pangeran Benawa]], deposed him. Pajang became a dependency of the Mataram Sultanate.

principality-of-vyazma.t: A small appanage of the Smolensk lands on the road to Moscow, taken by Lithuania in 1403.
principality-of-vyazma.o: [[e:vyazma|Vyazma]], on the upper Vyazma river east of [[e:smolensk|Smolensk]], is first mentioned in the 13th century as a town of the [[s:principality-of-smolensk|Principality of Smolensk]]. In the mid 13th century it became a separate [[e:appanage|appanage]] held by a junior line of the Smolensk princes, the ancestors of the Vyazemsky family.
principality-of-vyazma.r: Its importance came from its position on the main route between [[e:smolensk|Smolensk]] and [[e:moscow|Moscow]], which made it a trading post and a frontier fortress. Little is known of its individual rulers or institutions, and it was usually subordinate to Smolensk.
principality-of-vyazma.e: [[e:vytautas-the-great|Vytautas]] of the [[s:grand-duchy-of-lithuania|Grand Duchy of Lithuania]] took [[e:vyazma|Vyazma]] in 1403 in the course of his conquest of the [[e:smolensk|Smolensk]] lands, and its princes became Lithuanian [[e:vassal|vassals]]. The [[s:grand-duchy-of-moscow|Grand Duchy of Moscow]] captured it in 1494, and the Vyazemsky princes entered Russian service.

province-of-freedom.t: A short-lived settlement of freed Black Londoners on the Sierra Leone peninsula, the first attempt at what became Freetown.
province-of-freedom.o: The Province of Freedom grew out of the campaign by [[e:granville-sharp|Granville Sharp]] and the [[e:committee-for-the-relief-of-the-black-poor|Committee for the Relief of the Black Poor]] to resettle impoverished Black people in [[e:london|London]], many of them Loyalists from the [[e:american-revolutionary-war|American War of Independence]]. About 400 settlers sailed in 1787 and landed in May on land obtained from local Koya [[e:temne-people|Temne]] rulers, where they founded Granville Town.
province-of-freedom.r: Sharp designed it as a self-governing community with elected leaders, including Richard Weaver, and a frankpledge system of mutual responsibility. In practice the settlers suffered from disease, poor harvests and the rainy season, and many died or left to work for slave traders on nearby [[e:bunce-island|Bunce Island]]. Relations with neighbouring [[e:temne-people|Temne]] chiefs were uneasy.
province-of-freedom.e: In 1789 a [[e:temne-people|Temne]] ruler known as King Jimmy burned Granville Town after a dispute. The survivors regrouped, and the [[e:sierra-leone-company|Sierra Leone Company]] took over the project, founding the [[s:sierra-leone-colony-and-protectorate|Sierra Leone Colony and Protectorate]] at [[e:freetown|Freetown]] in 1792.

priene.t: Small Ionian city near Mount Mycale, home of the sage Bias and later rebuilt as the best-preserved example of a Hellenistic grid-planned town.
priene.o: Priene was one of the twelve Ionian cities, founded by tradition by settlers from [[s:athens|Athens]] and [[s:thebes|Thebes]] c. 1000 BCE. Its original site near the [[e:buyuk-menderes-river|Maeander]] has never been found. The [[s:ionian-league|Panionion]], the common sanctuary of the Ionian League on [[e:mount-mycale|Mount Mycale]], lay in its territory, giving Priene a role in Ionian affairs out of proportion to its size.
priene.r: In the 6th century BCE [[e:bias-of-priene|Bias of Priene]], counted among the [[e:seven-sages-of-greece|Seven Sages]], advised the [[e:ionians|Ionians]] to emigrate to [[e:sardinia|Sardinia]] rather than submit to [[e:persia|Persia]]. Priene fell to the [[s:kingdom-of-lydia|Kingdom of Lydia]] and then the [[s:achaemenid-empire|Achaemenid Empire]], sent 12 ships to the [[e:battle-of-lade|Battle of Lade]] in 494 BCE and later paid tribute in the [[s:delian-league|Delian League]].
priene.e: In the mid-4th century BCE the city was rebuilt on a terrace of [[e:mount-mycale|Mycale]] with a strict grid; Alexander dedicated its temple of [[e:athena-polias|Athena Polias]]. It passed to [[e:rome|Rome]] in 133 BCE. As the [[e:buyuk-menderes-river|Maeander]] silted its harbour, Priene declined, leaving its ruins remarkably intact.
priene.re: Greek religion; cult of Athena Polias

provisional-government-of-the-french-rep.t: The government that restored the Republic after liberation, gave French women the vote and built the post-war welfare state.
provisional-government-of-the-french-rep.o: In June 1944 the [[e:french-committee-of-national-liberation|French Committee of National Liberation]] in [[e:algiers|Algiers]] renamed itself the Provisional Government of the [[s:french-fifth-republic|French Republic]], led by [[e:charles-de-gaulle|Charles de Gaulle]]. After [[e:paris|Paris]] was liberated in August 1944, it moved to the capital and declared that [[s:vichy-france|Vichy France]] had never been legitimate.
provisional-government-of-the-french-rep.r: The government included [[e:gaullism|Gaullists]], communists, socialists and Christian democrats from the Resistance. Women voted for the first time in 1945. It nationalised [[e:renault|Renault]], [[e:coal|coal]], electricity and major banks, created the social security system and the [[e:monnet-plan|Monnet Plan]] for reconstruction, and oversaw the trials of collaborators. [[e:france|France]] gained a seat on the [[e:united-nations-security-council|UN Security Council]] and an occupation zone in [[e:germany|Germany]].
provisional-government-of-the-french-rep.e: [[e:charles-de-gaulle|De Gaulle]] resigned in January 1946 over disputes about the constitution, and [[e:felix-gouin|Félix Gouin]] and [[e:georges-bidault|Georges Bidault]] led the government. After a first draft was rejected, voters approved a new constitution in October 1946, founding the [[s:french-fourth-republic|French Fourth Republic]].

pakualaman.t: Small Javanese princely house carved out of Yogyakarta in 1812, whose ruler today serves as the region's vice-governor.
pakualaman.o: During [[s:british-java|British Java]], Prince [[e:paku-alam-i|Natakusuma]], a brother of the sultan of the [[s:yogyakarta-sultanate|Yogyakarta Sultanate]], sided with the British, who stormed the Yogyakarta kraton in 1812. As a reward [[e:stamford-raffles|Raffles]] granted him an apanage and the title Paku Alam I, creating an autonomous princely house modelled on [[s:mangkunegaran|Mangkunegaran]].
pakualaman.r: The Paku Alam ruled from the [[e:pura-pakualaman|Puro Pakualaman]] in [[s:yogyakarta-sultanate|Yogyakarta]] and a coastal district at Adikarto, holding a status below the sultan. The court was a centre of Javanese literature and arts, and the family produced [[e:ki-hajar-dewantara|Ki Hajar Dewantara]], founder of the [[e:taman-siswa|Taman Siswa]] school movement and pioneer of Indonesian national education.
pakualaman.e: [[e:paku-alam-viii|Paku Alam VIII]] supported the [[s:indonesia|Republic of Indonesia]], and when [[s:yogyakarta-sultanate|Yogyakarta]] became a Special Region in 1950 its rulers became vice-governors alongside the sultan, an arrangement confirmed in 2012. Paku Alam X holds the post today.

principality-of-serbia.t: Autonomous and then independent Serbian principality of the 19th century, built by the rival Obrenović and Karađorđević dynasties on the way to a modern kingdom.
principality-of-serbia.o: After the collapse of [[s:revolutionary-serbia|Revolutionary Serbia]] in 1813, [[e:milos-obrenovic|Miloš Obrenović]] launched the [[e:second-serbian-uprising|Second Serbian Uprising]] at Takovo in 1815. Combining fighting with negotiation, he won recognition as supreme prince in 1817, and an Ottoman decree of 1830 made [[s:serbia|Serbia]] an autonomous hereditary principality paying tribute, with Ottoman garrisons only in a few fortresses.
principality-of-serbia.r: Miloš ruled autocratically, but the [[e:sretenje-constitution|Sretenje Constitution]] of 1835 and the Ottoman-imposed constitution of 1838 set up a council that curbed him. Power swung between [[e:obrenovic-dynasty|Obrenović]] princes and [[e:alexander-karadordevic|Alexander Karađorđević]], who reigned from 1842 to 1858. [[e:michael-obrenovic|Michael Obrenović]] modernised the army and secured the departure of the last Ottoman garrisons in 1867. Peasant smallholders raised pigs for export to [[e:austria|Austria]].
principality-of-serbia.e: [[s:serbia|Serbia]] fought the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]] in 1876 to 1878, and the [[e:congress-of-berlin|Congress of Berlin]] in 1878 recognised its independence and added Niš and [[e:pirot|Pirot]]. In 1882 [[e:milan-i-of-serbia|Prince Milan Obrenović]] proclaimed the [[s:kingdom-of-serbia|Kingdom of Serbia]].

parthenopean-republic.t: The Neapolitan republic of 1799, whose idealistic leaders were crushed by Cardinal Ruffo's peasant army and executed in their hundreds.
parthenopean-republic.o: After the [[s:kingdom-of-naples|Kingdom of Naples]] attacked the French in [[e:rome|Rome]] in late 1798 and was defeated, [[e:ferdinand-i-of-the-two-sicilies|King Ferdinand IV]] fled to [[e:sicily|Sicily]]. French troops under General [[e:jean-etienne-championnet|Championnet]] fought their way into [[e:naples|Naples]], and in January 1799 local patriots proclaimed a republic named after [[s:neapolis|Parthenope]], the ancient Greek name for the city.
parthenopean-republic.r: The republic was led by intellectuals and liberal nobles such as [[e:carlo-lauberg|Carlo Lauberg]] and the jurist [[e:francesco-mario-pagano|Francesco Mario Pagano]], who drafted a constitution. [[e:eleonora-fonseca-pimentel|Eleonora Fonseca Pimentel]] edited its newspaper, the [[e:monitore-napoletano|Monitore Napoletano]]. It tried to abolish feudalism, but had little support among the poor and peasants, and depended on French troops, who withdrew in May.
parthenopean-republic.e: Cardinal [[e:fabrizio-ruffo|Fabrizio Ruffo's]] [[e:army-of-the-holy-faith|Sanfedisti]] army retook [[e:naples|Naples]] in June 1799. The surrender terms were broken with [[e:horatio-nelson|Nelson]]'s backing, and over a hundred republicans, including [[e:francesco-mario-pagano|Pagano]], [[e:eleonora-fonseca-pimentel|Pimentel]] and Admiral [[e:francesco-caracciolo|Francesco Caracciolo]], were executed.

portuguese-cape-verde.t: Atlantic island colony that became a key hub of the early slave trade and birthplace of a Creole society, until independence in 1975.
portuguese-cape-verde.o: The uninhabited [[e:cape-verde|Cape Verde]] islands were reached by navigators in Portuguese service between 1456 and 1462. Settlement began on [[s:spanish-jamaica|Santiago]] under the Genoese captain [[e:antonio-de-noli|Antonio de Noli]], and [[e:cidade-velha|Ribeira Grande]], today's Cidade Velha, became one of the first European towns in the tropics.
portuguese-cape-verde.r: [[e:cidade-velha|Ribeira Grande]] served as an [[e:entrepot|entrepot]] for enslaved Africans shipped to the [[e:americas|Americas]], and the islands grew [[e:cotton|cotton]] and bred horses and [[e:cattle|cattle]]. Portuguese settlers and enslaved Africans formed a [[e:criollo-people|Creole]] society with its own language, [[e:cape-verdean-creole|Kriolu]], and music. The capital moved to [[e:praia|Praia]] in 1770. Repeated droughts caused famines that killed tens of thousands.
portuguese-cape-verde.e: In the 20th century Cape Verdeans joined [[e:amilcar-cabral|Amilcar Cabral's]] [[e:paigc|PAIGC]], which fought for the independence of [[s:portuguese-guinea|Portuguese Guinea]] and the islands. After the 1974 revolution in Portugal, [[e:cape-verde|Cape Verde]] became independent on 5 July 1975.
