principality-of-galich-mersky.t: An appanage around Galich in the north-east of Rus', whose princes later fought Moscow in its great dynastic civil war.
principality-of-galich-mersky.o: [[e:galich-kostroma-oblast|Galich]], on [[e:lake-galich|Lake Galich]] in the old lands of the [[e:merya|Finnic Merya]], was a town of the [[s:vladimir-suzdal|Vladimir-Suzdal]] region known for its salt springs. In 1246 it became the [[e:appanage|appanage]] of Konstantin, son of Grand Prince [[e:yaroslav-ii-of-vladimir|Yaroslav Vsevolodovich]], and his descendants held it for over a century.
principality-of-galich-mersky.r: The principality was a remote northern land of forests and salt workings, with little recorded about its government. Its princes were minor figures in the struggles of the grand princes of Vladimir and the [[s:golden-horde|Golden Horde]], and [[e:galich-kostroma-oblast|Galich]] often served as a refuge from the turmoil further south.
principality-of-galich-mersky.e: In 1363 [[e:dmitry-donskoy|Dmitry Donskoy]] of the [[s:grand-duchy-of-moscow|Grand Duchy of Moscow]] expelled its last independent prince and annexed [[e:galich-kostroma-oblast|Galich]]. It was later granted to Donskoy's son Yuri, whose line fought [[e:vasily-ii-of-moscow|Vasily II]] for the throne of [[e:moscow|Moscow]] in the civil war of the 1420s to 1450s.

pashalik-of-yanina.t: Virtually independent domain of Ali Pasha of Tepelena, who ruled Epirus and much of mainland Greece from Ioannina and dealt with European powers as an equal.
pashalik-of-yanina.o: [[e:ali-pasha-of-yanina|Ali Pasha]], an Albanian notable from [[e:tepelene|Tepelena]], rose through brigandage and Ottoman service, becoming governor of [[e:trikala|Trikala]] and then, in the late 1780s, pasha of [[e:ioannina|Ioannina]]. By force, alliances and intrigue he extended his authority over [[e:epirus|Epirus]], southern [[s:albania|Albania]], [[e:thessaly|Thessaly]] and parts of the [[e:peloponnese|Peloponnese]], controlling the main routes of the western [[e:balkans|Balkans]].
pashalik-of-yanina.r: Ali ruled from his fortress palace in [[e:ioannina|Ioannina]] through a personal network of officials and Albanian troops, with Greek secretaries and merchants prominent at court. Ioannina became a centre of Greek learning and trade. He negotiated with [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]] and [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]], entertained [[e:lord-byron|Lord Byron]] in 1809, crushed the [[e:souliotes|Souliotes]] and acquired [[e:parga|Parga]] in 1819.
pashalik-of-yanina.e: [[e:sultan|Sultan]] [[e:mahmud-ii|Mahmud II]] declared Ali a rebel in 1820 and besieged [[e:ioannina|Ioannina]]; Ali was killed in January 1822. The long campaign tied down Ottoman forces just as the Greek War of Independence broke out in 1821, helping the revolt survive.

perusia.t: Etruscan hill city above the upper Tiber, known for its gates, its family tombs and a famous siege by Octavian in 41–40 BCE.
perusia.o: Perusia, Etruscan Persna, modern [[s:commune-of-perugia|Perugia]], grew on a group of hills west of the [[e:tiber-river|Tiber]], near the border with the [[s:umbrians|Umbrians]]. It developed into a city later than the coastal centres, gaining importance from the 6th century BCE and especially in the 4th and 3rd centuries BCE, when its great walls and gates were built.
perusia.r: Perusia controlled river routes and farmland on the upper [[e:tiber-river|Tiber]] and mixed with Umbrian neighbours. Its aristocratic families buried their dead in chamber tombs with carved urns, the finest being the [[e:hypogeum-of-the-volumni|Hypogeum of the Volumni]]. The [[e:cippus-perusinus|Cippus of Perugia]], a stone boundary text of about 130 words, is one of the longest Etruscan inscriptions, and the [[e:arco-etrusco|Arco Etrusco]] gate still stands.
perusia.e: Perusia joined other Etruscan cities against [[e:rome|Rome]], made truces in 310 and 294 BCE and became a Roman ally after the wars of the early 3rd century. In the [[e:perusine-war|Perusine War]] Octavian besieged [[e:lucius-antonius|Lucius Antonius]] there in 41–40 BCE; the city was taken and burned. Augustus rebuilt it as Augusta Perusia.

peru-bolivian-confederation.t: Andrés de Santa Cruz's union of Peru and Bolivia, which threatened the balance of power in South America and was destroyed by Chile in 1839.
peru-bolivian-confederation.o: In 1835 [[e:peru|Peru's]] president [[e:luis-jose-de-orbegoso|Luis José de Orbegoso]] asked the Bolivian president [[e:andres-de-santa-cruz|Andrés de Santa Cruz]] for help against rebels. Santa Cruz invaded, defeated [[e:agustin-gamarra|Agustín Gamarra]] and [[e:felipe-santiago-salaverry|Felipe Santiago Salaverry]] in 1835 and 1836, and divided Peru into the [[s:north-peruvian-republic|North Peruvian Republic]] and [[s:south-peruvian-republic|South Peruvian Republic]], which joined the [[s:republic-of-bolivia|Republic of Bolivia]] in a confederation.
peru-bolivian-confederation.r: The [[e:congress-of-tacna|Pact of Tacna]] of 1837 made [[e:andres-de-santa-cruz|Santa Cruz]] Supreme Protector, with broad powers over foreign affairs and the army. He introduced legal codes modelled on [[e:napoleon|Napoleon's]] and promoted trade. [[s:republic-of-chile|Chile]], under the influence of [[e:diego-portales|Diego Portales]], saw the confederation as a threat, and Chile declared war in December 1836, followed by the [[s:argentine-confederation|Argentine Confederation]] of [[e:juan-manuel-de-rosas|Rosas]] in 1837. Peruvian exiles and many in [[e:lima|Lima]] resented Bolivian dominance.
peru-bolivian-confederation.e: A Chilean army under [[e:manuel-bulnes|Manuel Bulnes]], joined by Peruvian exiles, defeated [[e:andres-de-santa-cruz|Santa Cruz]] at [[e:battle-of-yungay|Yungay]] on 20 January 1839. The confederation was dissolved, and Santa Cruz went into exile. [[e:peru|Peru]] and [[s:republic-of-bolivia|Bolivia]] were never united again, and [[s:republic-of-chile|Chile]] emerged as the leading power on the Pacific coast.

principality-of-galicia.t: A rich principality on the upper Dniester, built around the salt trade and the town of Halych, whose boyars were famously powerful.
principality-of-galicia.o: In the 1080s three [[e:rurik-dynasty|Rurikid]] brothers, [[e:rurik|Rurik]], [[e:volodar-rostyslavych|Volodar]] and [[e:vasylko-rostyslavych|Vasylko Rostislavich]], took control of the towns of [[e:przemysl|Peremyshl]], [[e:zvenyhorod-lviv-oblast|Zvenyhorod]] and [[e:terebovlia|Terebovl]] in the far south-west of Rus'. Their heir [[e:volodymyrko-volodarovych|Volodymyrko]] united these lands and in 1141 made Halych on the [[e:dniester|Dniester]] his capital, creating the Principality of [[s:kingdom-of-galicia-and-lodomeria|Galicia]].
principality-of-galicia.r: [[s:kingdom-of-galicia-and-lodomeria|Galicia]] prospered from salt mines, which supplied much of Rus', and from trade along the [[e:dniester|Dniester]] to the [[e:black-sea|Black Sea]] and with [[e:hungary|Hungary]] and [[e:poland|Poland]]. Its landholding boyars were unusually strong and repeatedly deposed or defied their princes. [[e:yaroslav-osmomysl|Yaroslav Osmomysl]], who ruled from 1153 to 1187, was praised in the [[e:the-tale-of-igors-campaign|Lay of Igor's Campaign]] as a mighty ruler.
principality-of-galicia.e: The dynasty of [[e:volodymyrko-volodarovych|Volodymyrko]] died out with [[e:vladimir-yaroslavich-of-galicia|Vladimir Yaroslavich]] in 1199. [[e:roman-the-great|Roman Mstislavich]] of the [[s:principality-of-volhynia|Principality of Volhynia]] then took Halych and joined the two lands into the [[s:kingdom-of-galicia-volhynia|Kingdom of Galicia-Volhynia]], though [[e:hungary|Hungary]] and [[e:poland|Poland]] long contested [[s:kingdom-of-galicia-and-lodomeria|Galicia]].

principality-of-luneburg.t: Guelph principality of the Lüneburg Heath ruled from Celle, which embraced the Reformation early and merged into the Electorate of Hanover in 1705.
principality-of-luneburg.o: In 1269 the brothers Albert and John divided the [[s:duchy-of-brunswick-luneburg|Duchy of Brunswick-Lüneburg]], which their father [[e:otto-the-child|Otto the Child]] had received in 1235. John received the northern lands around [[e:luneburg|Lüneburg]] and [[e:celle|Celle]], founding the Principality of Lüneburg, while Albert took the [[s:principality-of-wolfenbuttel|Principality of Wolfenbüttel]].
principality-of-luneburg.r: The salt city of [[e:luneburg|Lüneburg]] was wealthy and largely independent, and after the [[e:war-of-the-luneburg-succession|War of the Lüneburg Succession]] in 1371 to 1388 the dukes moved their residence to [[e:celle|Celle]]. Duke [[e:ernest-i-duke-of-brunswick-luneburg|Ernest the Confessor]] introduced the [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]] from 1527. The principality was rural, with heathland, sheep and forests. [[e:george-william-duke-of-brunswick-luneburg|George William]], the last duke of Celle, saw his daughter [[e:sophia-dorothea-of-celle|Sophia Dorothea]] marry the future [[e:george-i-of-great-britain|George I of Great Britain]].
principality-of-luneburg.e: When [[e:george-william-duke-of-brunswick-luneburg|George William]] died in 1705, [[e:luneburg|Lüneburg]] passed to his nephew and son-in-law [[e:george-i-of-great-britain|George Louis]] of [[s:principality-of-calenberg|Calenberg]] and was merged into the [[s:electorate-of-hanover|Electorate of Hanover]]. It later formed part of the [[s:kingdom-of-hanover|Kingdom of Hanover]] and is now in [[e:lower-saxony|Lower Saxony]].

polyrrhenia.t: Fortified hill city of western Crete, the leading power of the island's far west in the Hellenistic period.
polyrrhenia.o: Polyrrhenia stood on a steep hill south of the [[e:gulf-of-kissamos|Gulf of Kissamos]] in western [[e:crete|Crete]]. [[e:strabo|Strabo]] says it was founded by [[e:achaeans-achaea|Achaeans]] and Laconians, who united the scattered villages of the area. Its name, meaning rich in flocks, reflects its pastoral economy.
polyrrhenia.r: Polyrrhenia controlled the west of [[e:crete|Crete]], with harbours at [[e:phalasarna|Phalasarna]] and [[e:kissamos|Kisamos]] at times under its influence. It had [[e:kosmoi|kosmoi]] magistrates like other Cretan cities. In the Lyttian War of 220 BCE it broke with [[s:knossos|Knossos]] and allied with Philip V of the [[s:antigonid-kingdom-of-macedonia|Antigonid Kingdom of Macedonia]]. Its walls and cisterns survive.
polyrrhenia.e: Polyrrhenia came under Roman rule in the conquest of [[e:crete|Crete]] in 69 to 67 BCE and continued as a town, later a Byzantine bishopric.

peoples-republic-of-china.t: The Communist state proclaimed by Mao Zedong in 1949, which has governed mainland China ever since and grown into the world's second-largest economy.
peoples-republic-of-china.o: The [[e:chinese-communist-party|Chinese Communist Party]], which had governed rural base areas since the [[s:chinese-soviet-republic|Chinese Soviet Republic]] of the 1930s, won the civil war against the [[s:nationalist-government|Nationalist government]]. On 1 October 1949 [[e:mao-zedong|Mao Zedong]] proclaimed the People's Republic in [[e:beijing|Beijing]], while the [[s:republic-of-china|Republic of China]] retreated to [[e:taiwan|Taiwan]].
peoples-republic-of-china.r: The party-state carried out land reform, fought in the [[e:korean-war|Korean War]] and adopted Soviet-style planning. The [[e:great-leap-forward|Great Leap Forward]] of 1958 to 1962 caused a famine that killed tens of millions, and the [[e:cultural-revolution|Cultural Revolution]] from 1966 to 1976 brought political persecution and chaos. From 1978 [[e:deng-xiaoping|Deng Xiaoping's]] reforms opened the economy to markets and foreign investment, while the party kept its monopoly of power, crushing the [[e:1989-tiananmen-square-protests-and-massacre|Tiananmen protests]] in 1989.
peoples-republic-of-china.e: The People's Republic regained [[e:hong-kong|Hong Kong]] in 1997 and [[e:macau|Macau]] in 1999, joined the [[e:world-trade-organization|World Trade Organization]] in 2001 and became a leading manufacturing and trading power. Under [[e:xi-jinping|Xi Jinping]], leader since 2012, central party control has been reinforced.
peoples-republic-of-china.re: State atheism, Chinese folk religion, Buddhism, Taoism

parisii.t: Gallic people of the middle Seine whose town Lutetia became Paris.
parisii.o: The [[s:parisii-britain|Parisii]] settled on the [[e:seine|Seine]] in the 3rd century BCE and controlled river traffic across the [[e:paris|Paris]] basin. Caesar mentions that he held a council of [[e:gaul|Gaul]] at [[e:lutetia|Lutetia]] in 53 BCE. The exact site of their oppidum is debated; excavations at [[e:nanterre|Nanterre]] have revealed a large Gallic settlement.
parisii.r: They struck fine gold coins, among the most elegant in [[e:gaul|Gaul]]. Their wealth came from trade on the [[e:seine|Seine]], and Roman inscriptions later record a powerful [[e:guild|guild]] of boatmen.
parisii.e: In 52 BCE they joined the revolt; the Aulercan leader [[e:camulogenus|Camulogenus]] burned [[e:lutetia|Lutetia]] and was defeated by Caesar's legate [[e:titus-labienus|Labienus]]. Under [[e:rome|Rome]] Lutetia was rebuilt on the [[e:montagne-sainte-genevieve|Montagne Sainte-Geneviève]], and on the [[e:ile-de-la-cite|Île de la Cité]] the boatmen dedicated the Pillar of the Boatmen to [[e:jupiter-god|Jupiter]] under [[e:tiberius|Tiberius]]. In late antiquity the town took the name of the people, [[e:paris|Paris]].

principality-of-lampang.t: A northern Thai principality whose Chet Ton dynasty led the expulsion of the Burmese from Lan Na and later ruled Chiang Mai.
principality-of-lampang.o: In 1732 [[e:nan-thip-chang|Nan Thip Chang]], a hunter turned local leader, drove out a Burmese-backed governor from Lampang and was recognised as ruler. His descendants, known as the [[e:chet-ton-dynasty|Chet Ton]] or Chao Chet Ton dynasty, governed Lampang under Burmese overlordship.
principality-of-lampang.r: Lampang was a [[e:rice|rice]]-growing principality on the Wang river with the revered [[e:wat-phra-that-lampang-luang|Wat Phra That Lampang Luang]]. In the 1770s its ruler [[e:kawila|Kawila]] allied with the [[s:thonburi-kingdom|Thonburi Kingdom]] and helped drive the Burmese out of [[s:lan-na|Lan Na]]. Thereafter Lampang was a Siamese [[e:vassal|vassal]], and Kawila's family also governed [[s:kingdom-of-chiang-mai|Chiang Mai]] and [[e:lamphun|Lamphun]].
principality-of-lampang.e: Lampang kept its own princes during the 19th century, while British [[e:timber|timber]] firms logged teak in its forests. The provincial reforms of the [[s:rattanakosin-kingdom|Rattanakosin Kingdom]] brought it under direct administration from 1899, and Lampang is now a province of [[s:thailand|Thailand]].

pahang-sultanate.t: Largest state of the Malay Peninsula, held by the Bendahara family of Johor before becoming a sultanate in 1882.
pahang-sultanate.o: Pahang had been a dependency of [[s:johor-sultanate|Johor]] since the 17th century. Around 1770 it was granted as a hereditary fief to the [[e:johor|Johor]] Bendahara, [[e:tun-abdul-majid|Tun Abdul Majid]], whose descendants ruled from [[e:pekan|Pekan]] as Raja Bendahara. The breakup of the Johor-[[e:riau|Riau]] realm in the early 19th century left them effectively independent.
pahang-sultanate.r: Pahang was thinly populated, with [[e:rice|rice]] villages, gold workings and [[e:tin|tin]] along its long rivers and great forests inland. A civil war from 1857 to 1863 brought [[e:ahmad-muadzam-shah-of-pahang|Wan Ahmad]] to power, and in 1882 he proclaimed himself [[e:sultan|Sultan]] Ahmad Muadzam Shah. Chiefs ruled their districts with wide autonomy.
pahang-sultanate.e: The British forced a resident on Pahang in 1888, provoking the Pahang uprising of 1891 to 1895 led by [[e:dato-bahaman|Dato Bahaman]] and [[e:mat-kilau|Mat Kilau]]. Pahang then joined the [[s:federated-malay-states|Federated Malay States]] and later [[s:malaysia|Malaysia]]; [[e:sultan|Sultan]] [[e:abdullah-of-pahang|Abdullah]] served as king from 2019 to 2024.

cr.a: Sanson, Nicolas (1600-1667). Cartographe Idrīsī, Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad al-Šarīf Abū ʿAbd Allâh al- (1100?-1165?). Aut...

principality-of-armenia.t: Armenia under Arab rule, when native princes governed beside the caliph's governor at Dvin and the Bagratid family rose towards kingship.
principality-of-armenia.o: As Arab armies overran the Sasanian lands, the Armenian commander [[e:theodore-rshtuni|Theodore Rshtuni]] made a treaty with [[e:muawiya-i|Muawiya]] in 653 accepting Arab overlordship in return for autonomy and keeping Armenian troops. The province of Arminiya, which also took in [[s:georgia|Georgia]] and [[s:albania|Albania]], was established with its centre at [[e:dvin|Dvin]].
principality-of-armenia.r: An Arab governor, the ostikan, sat at [[e:dvin|Dvin]] while a native presiding prince represented the Armenian nobility. Heavy taxes provoked revolts, notably in 774-775, which were crushed and weakened the Mamikonian house. Arab [[e:emir|emirs]] settled in towns, while monasteries preserved Armenian learning. The [[e:bagratuni-dynasty|Bagratids]] grew rich through lands and trade.
principality-of-armenia.e: With the [[s:abbasid-caliphate|Abbasid Caliphate]] weakening, [[e:ashot-i-of-armenia|Ashot Bagratuni]] was named prince of princes in 862, and around 884 the [[e:caliphate|caliph]] sent him a crown, founding [[s:bagratid-armenia|Bagratid Armenia]]. The period had preserved the noble houses, the church and a sense of separate identity that made this revival of Armenian kingship possible.

prince-bishopric-of-verdun.t: One of the Three Bishoprics of Lorraine, a church principality on the Meuse that passed from the Empire to France between 1552 and 1648.
prince-bishopric-of-verdun.o: [[e:verdun|Verdun]], where the Carolingian empire was divided in 843, was an ancient bishopric. In 997 Emperor [[e:otto-iii-holy-roman-emperor|Otto III]] granted [[e:bishop|Bishop]] Haimo the comital rights over the city and its district, making the bishops princes of the [[s:holy-roman-empire|Holy Roman Empire]].
prince-bishopric-of-verdun.r: The [[e:bishop|bishops]]' temporal lands were small and lay along the [[e:meuse|Meuse]], and they faced constant pressure from the counts of Bar and the dukes of [[s:duchy-of-lorraine|Lorraine]]. The citizens of [[e:verdun|Verdun]] gained wide self-government and imperial-city status, limiting the bishops' power at home. The city was a trading centre, known for its sugared almonds.
prince-bishopric-of-verdun.e: [[e:henry-ii-of-france|Henry II of France]] occupied [[e:verdun|Verdun]] with [[e:metz|Metz]] and [[e:toul|Toul]] in 1552, and the [[e:peace-of-westphalia|Peace of Westphalia]] in 1648 confirmed French [[e:sovereignty|sovereignty]] over the [[e:three-bishoprics|Three Bishoprics]]. Verdun became part of the [[s:kingdom-of-france|Kingdom of France]] and later a major fortress.

papal-states.t: The territories of central Italy ruled by the popes as temporal sovereigns for over a thousand years, from Pepin's donation to the capture of Rome in 1870.
papal-states.o: When the [[e:kingdom-of-the-lombards|Lombards]] threatened [[e:rome|Rome]], [[e:pope-stephen-ii|Pope Stephen II]] won the protection of the Frankish king [[e:pepin-the-short|Pepin the Short]] in 754. Pepin defeated the [[e:lombards|Lombards]] and in 756 gave the pope the lands of the former [[s:exarchate-of-ravenna|Exarchate of Ravenna]] together with the [[s:duchy-of-rome|Duchy of Rome]]. [[e:charlemagne|Charlemagne]] confirmed and extended the grant in 774.
papal-states.r: The pope ruled as an elected monarch through cardinals, [[e:legatus|legates]] and governors, but for centuries real control was weak, contested by Roman nobles and local lords. [[e:pope-innocent-iii|Innocent III]] expanded papal power, and [[e:gil-alvarez-carrillo-de-albornoz|Cardinal Albornoz]] reasserted it in the 1350s with the [[e:egidian-constitutions|Egidian Constitutions]]. [[e:renaissance|Renaissance]] popes such as [[e:pope-alexander-vi|Alexander VI]] and [[e:pope-julius-ii|Julius II]] fought to bring the [[e:romagna|Romagna]] under control and built the new St Peter's. [[e:ferrara|Ferrara]] (1598) and [[s:duchy-of-urbino|Urbino]] (1631) were later absorbed.
papal-states.e: [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]] annexed the States in 1809; they were restored in 1815. In 1860 [[e:romagna|Romagna]], the [[e:marche|Marche]] and [[e:umbria|Umbria]] joined the [[s:kingdom-of-italy|Kingdom of Italy]], and on 20 September 1870 Italian troops entered [[e:rome|Rome]]. [[e:pope-pius-ix|Pius IX]] refused to recognise the loss, and the dispute was settled by the [[e:lateran-treaty|Lateran Treaty]] of 1929, creating [[s:vatican-city|Vatican City]].

principality-of-bulgaria.t: Autonomous Bulgarian principality created after the Russo-Turkish War, which united with Eastern Rumelia and proclaimed full independence in 1908.
principality-of-bulgaria.o: [[e:russia|Russia's]] victory over the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]] led to the [[e:treaty-of-san-stefano|Treaty of San Stefano]] in March 1878, which created a large [[s:bulgaria|Bulgaria]]. The [[e:congress-of-berlin|Congress of Berlin]] reduced it to an autonomous principality between the [[e:danube|Danube]] and the Balkan mountains, under Ottoman suzerainty. In 1879 the [[e:tarnovo-constitution|Tarnovo Constitution]] was adopted and [[e:alexander-of-battenberg|Alexander of Battenberg]] elected prince, with [[e:sofia|Sofia]] as capital.
principality-of-bulgaria.r: The liberal [[e:tarnovo-constitution|Tarnovo Constitution]] created a parliament elected by male suffrage, though princes and strong premiers often ruled forcefully. Unification with [[s:eastern-rumelia|Eastern Rumelia]] in 1885 was defended by victory over [[s:serbia|Serbia]] at [[e:battle-of-slivnitsa|Slivnitsa]]. Russian anger forced Alexander's abdication in 1886, and [[e:ferdinand-i-of-bulgaria|Ferdinand of Saxe-Coburg]] was chosen in 1887, while premier [[e:stefan-stambolov|Stefan Stambolov]] built a modern state and army.
principality-of-bulgaria.e: On 5 October 1908, during the crisis over [[e:bosnia|Bosnia]], Ferdinand proclaimed full independence at [[e:veliko-tarnovo|Tarnovo]] and took the title of tsar, creating the [[s:kingdom-of-bulgaria|Kingdom of Bulgaria]]. The [[e:tarnovo-constitution|Tarnovo Constitution]] remained in force until 1947.

province-of-venezuela.t: The Spanish governorate of the Caribbean coast of South America, centred first on Coro and then Caracas, which grew rich on cacao.
province-of-venezuela.o: [[e:spain|Spain]] founded [[e:coro-venezuela|Coro]] in 1527, and from 1528 the province was leased to the [[e:welser-family|Welser]] bankers as [[s:klein-venedig|Klein-Venedig]]. After the Welser lease ended in the 1540s, Spanish governors took over. [[e:diego-de-losada|Diego de Losada]] founded [[e:caracas|Santiago de León de Caracas]] in 1567, and it became the capital in 1578.
province-of-venezuela.r: The province was governed by a governor and captain-general under the [[s:captaincy-general-of-santo-domingo|Audiencia of Santo Domingo]] and later of [[e:bogota|Santa Fe de Bogotá]]. Its economy grew on [[e:cacao|cacao]] plantations worked by enslaved Africans, and [[e:caracas|Caracas]] cacao was exported to [[s:new-spain|New Spain]] and [[e:europe|Europe]]. From 1728 the [[e:guipuzcoan-company-of-caracas|Guipuzcoan Company of Caracas]] held a trade monopoly, provoking the revolt of [[e:juan-francisco-de-leon|Juan Francisco de León]] in 1749. The [[e:criollo-people|Creole]] elite, known as mantuanos, dominated society.
province-of-venezuela.e: In 1777 [[e:charles-iii-of-spain|Charles III]] united the province with [[e:cumana|Cumaná]], [[e:guayana-province|Guayana]], [[e:maracaibo|Maracaibo]] and the islands of [[e:trinidad|Trinidad]] and [[e:margarita-island|Margarita]] to form the [[s:captaincy-general-of-venezuela|Captaincy General of Venezuela]]. The province's [[e:criollo-people|Creole]] elite later led the independence movement of 1810.

palembang-sultanate.t: Javanese-influenced Malay sultanate of south Sumatra that grew rich on pepper and Bangka tin until Dutch conquest in 1821.
palembang-sultanate.o: [[e:palembang|Palembang]] had long been ruled by princes of Javanese descent loyal to [[s:mataram-sultanate|Mataram]]. In 1659 the [[s:dutch-east-india-company-territories|Dutch East India Company]] burned the town after its envoys were killed, and the ruler Kimas Hindi broke with Mataram and proclaimed himself sultan with the title Abdurrahman, founding an independent sultanate on the Musi river.
palembang-sultanate.r: The court combined Javanese ceremony with Malay [[e:islam|Islam]]. [[e:palembang|Palembang]] sold [[e:pepper|pepper]] to the Company under monopoly contracts, and after [[e:tin|tin]] was found on [[e:bangka|Bangka]] around 1710 it became one of the richest states of the archipelago. [[e:sultan|Sultan]] [[e:mahmud-badaruddin-i|Mahmud Badaruddin I]] built the Great Mosque, and a later sultan built the brick kraton of [[e:kuto-besak|Kuto Besak]].
palembang-sultanate.e: [[e:sultan|Sultan]] [[e:mahmud-badaruddin-ii|Mahmud Badaruddin II]] resisted both the British during [[s:british-java|British Java]] and the returning [[e:dutch|Dutch]], defeating a Dutch fleet in 1819. A larger expedition took [[e:palembang|Palembang]] in 1821, the sultan was exiled to [[s:ternate-sultanate|Ternate]], and the sultanate was abolished in 1823. He is now an Indonesian national hero.

prince-bishopric-of-hildesheim.t: Lower Saxon church state famed for Bishop Bernward's Romanesque art, which lost most of its land in a 1519 feud and won it back in 1643.
prince-bishopric-of-hildesheim.o: [[e:louis-the-pious|Louis the Pious]] founded the diocese of [[e:hildesheim|Hildesheim]] in 815. Around 1000 [[e:bishop|Bishop]] [[e:bernward-of-hildesheim|Bernward]] made the city a centre of art, building [[e:st-michaels-church-hildesheim|St. Michael's Church]] and commissioning its bronze doors and column. The bishops built up a territory between the [[e:leine|Leine]] and [[e:oker|Oker]], and by the 13th century, around 1235, they ruled as imperial princes.
prince-bishopric-of-hildesheim.r: The cathedral chapter and estates shared power with the [[e:bishop|bishops]]. In the [[e:hildesheim-diocesan-feud|Hildesheim Diocesan Feud]] of 1519 to 1523 the see lost most of its territory to the [[e:house-of-welf|Guelph]] dukes, retaining only the Small Diocese. The city of [[e:hildesheim|Hildesheim]] turned Lutheran, while the bishops stayed Catholic; [[e:house-of-wittelsbach|Wittelsbach]] princes such as [[e:clemens-august-of-bavaria|Clemens August of Bavaria]] often held the see alongside [[s:free-imperial-city-of-cologne|Cologne]].
prince-bishopric-of-hildesheim.e: The lost lands were restored in 1643. The see was secularised in 1803 and given to [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]], then belonged to the [[s:kingdom-of-westphalia|Kingdom of Westphalia]], and in 1815 to the [[s:kingdom-of-hanover|Kingdom of Hanover]]. Its cathedral and St. Michael's are a [[e:unesco-world-heritage-site|UNESCO World Heritage Site]].

prince-bishopric-of-lubeck.t: The only prince-bishopric to survive the Reformation in Protestant hands, ruled from Eutin by Holstein-Gottorp princes until secularised in 1803.
prince-bishopric-of-lubeck.o: [[e:henry-the-lion|Henry the Lion]] moved the bishopric of [[s:county-of-oldenburg|Oldenburg]] in [[s:county-of-holstein|Holstein]] to the new town of [[s:free-and-hanseatic-city-of-lubeck|Lübeck]] in 1160, and the [[e:bishop|bishops]] gathered estates in eastern Holstein. After [[e:prince-henry-the-navigator|Henry's]] fall in 1180 they held these lands as imperial princes. Conflicts with the citizens of the Free and Hanseatic City of [[e:lubeck|Lübeck]] led them to govern from [[e:eutin|Eutin]].
prince-bishopric-of-lubeck.r: The territory was a small rural principality of lakes and estates around [[e:eutin|Eutin]]. After the [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]] the cathedral chapter turned Lutheran and from 1586 elected princes of the house of [[s:duchy-of-holstein-gottorp|Holstein-Gottorp]], an arrangement the [[e:peace-of-westphalia|Peace of Westphalia]] protected. One of them, [[e:adolf-frederick-king-of-sweden|Adolf Frederick]], became King of [[e:sweden|Sweden]] in 1751. Eutin grew into a small court town of the [[e:age-of-enlightenment|Enlightenment]], later called the [[e:weimar|Weimar]] of the North.
prince-bishopric-of-lubeck.e: In 1803 the see was secularised as the Principality of [[s:free-and-hanseatic-city-of-lubeck|Lübeck]] and joined to the [[s:duchy-of-oldenburg|Duchy of Oldenburg]], whose ruler had been its last prince-[[e:bishop|bishop]]. It stayed Oldenburg's exclave until the [[e:greater-hamburg-act|Greater Hamburg Act]] of 1937 merged it into Prussian [[s:provisional-government-of-schleswig-holstein|Schleswig-Holstein]].

palace-state-of-zakros.t: The easternmost Minoan palace on Crete, a harbour centre for trade with Egypt and the Levant, found unplundered with its treasures in place.
palace-state-of-zakros.o: Zakros lies in a sheltered bay at the eastern tip of [[e:crete|Crete]], a natural harbour facing [[e:egypt|Egypt]], [[e:cyprus|Cyprus]] and the [[e:levant|Levant]]. A settlement existed in the [[e:early-minoan-period|Early Minoan period]], and a palace was built c. 1900 BCE. The surviving palace, smaller than [[s:palace-state-of-knossos|Knossos]] or [[s:palace-state-of-phaistos|Phaistos]], dates mostly from the [[e:neopalatial-period|Neopalatial period]] after c. 1700 BCE.
palace-state-of-zakros.r: The palace followed the standard Minoan plan with a central court, storerooms, workshops, a lustral basin and a cistern room. It likely controlled trade in [[e:copper|copper]], [[e:ivory-trade|ivory]] and elephant tusks, some of which were found on site. Its treasury held stone ritual vessels, including a rock-crystal rhyton, and [[e:linear-a|Linear A]] tablets show local record-keeping.
palace-state-of-zakros.e: Zakros was destroyed by fire c. 1450 BCE and abandoned so suddenly that it was never looted. It was not reoccupied as a palace. [[e:nikolaos-platon|Nikolaos Platon]] excavated it from 1961, recovering one of the richest collections of Minoan objects found in place.

polans-east-slavs.t: The East Slavic tribe of the middle Dnieper whose town of Kiev became the capital of Kievan Rus'.
polans-east-slavs.o: The Polans, the people of the fields, settled the wooded steppe on the middle [[e:dnieper|Dnieper]]. The chronicle credits their legendary founder [[e:kyi-shchek-and-khoryv|Kyi]], with his brothers Shchek and Khoriv and his sister Lybid, with founding [[e:kyiv|Kiev]]. For a time they paid tribute to the [[e:khazar-khaganate|Khazars]], said to have been one sword for every household.
polans-east-slavs.r: The chronicler, himself from [[e:kyiv|Kiev]], praises the Polans as gentle and well mannered compared with their neighbours, particularly the [[s:drevlians|Drevlians]]. They farmed the fertile soil, and Kiev's position on the [[e:dnieper|Dnieper]] made it a centre of trade between [[e:scandinavia|Scandinavia]], [[s:byzantium|Byzantium]] and the steppe. In the mid 9th century Kiev was held by the [[e:varangians|Varangians]] [[e:askold-and-dir|Askold and Dir]].
polans-east-slavs.e: In 882 [[e:oleg-of-novgorod|Oleg of Novgorod]] killed [[e:askold-and-dir|Askold and Dir]] and made [[e:kyiv|Kiev]] his capital, so the Polan lands became the core of [[s:kievan-rus|Kievan Rus']]. The tribal name faded as the people of the region came to be called the Rus'.

portuguese-india.t: Portugal's Estado da India, ruled from Goa for over four centuries and the hub of its maritime empire from East Africa to Macau.
portuguese-india.o: After [[e:vasco-da-gama|Vasco da Gama]] reached [[e:calicut|Calicut]] in 1498, Portugal appointed [[e:francisco-de-almeida|Francisco de Almeida]] as first [[e:viceroy-of-india|viceroy]] in 1505. [[e:afonso-de-albuquerque|Afonso de Albuquerque]] captured [[e:goa|Goa]] from the [[s:bijapur-sultanate|Bijapur Sultanate]] in 1510, making it the capital of the [[e:estado-da-india|Estado da India]], an empire of forts and ports including [[e:daman|Daman]], Diu, [[e:vasai|Bassein]], [[e:kochi|Cochin]], [[e:malacca|Malacca]] and [[s:kingdom-of-ormus|Hormuz]].
portuguese-india.r: The [[e:estado-da-india|Estado]] controlled sea trade through the cartaz pass system and fortified posts rather than large territories. [[e:goa|Goa]] became a centre of Catholic missions, with [[e:francis-xavier|Francis Xavier]] based there and the Goa [[e:portuguese-inquisition|Inquisition]] from 1560. Its churches, such as the [[e:basilica-of-bom-jesus|Basilica of Bom Jesus]], are a [[e:unesco-world-heritage-site|World Heritage Site]]. A Luso-Indian society emerged, and Konkani and Portuguese were both spoken.
portuguese-india.e: The [[e:dutch|Dutch]] and English took most Portuguese posts in the 17th century, and the [[e:maratha-empire|Marathas]] captured [[e:vasai|Bassein]] in 1739. [[e:goa|Goa]], [[e:daman|Daman]] and Diu remained Portuguese until the [[s:republic-of-india|Republic of India]] annexed them by military action in December 1961.

providence-island-colony.t: Short-lived Puritan colony off the coast of Central America, a sister venture of New England that turned to privateering and slavery before Spain destroyed it.
providence-island-colony.o: The [[e:providence-island-company|Providence Island Company]], whose investors included the [[e:robert-rich-2nd-earl-of-warwick|Earl of Warwick]], [[e:john-pym|John Pym]] and [[e:william-fiennes-1st-viscount-saye-and-sele|Lord Saye and Sele]], settled the small island of Santa Catalina in 1630. It was meant as a godly Puritan colony in the [[e:caribbean|Caribbean]], planted with tobacco and [[e:cotton|cotton]], and its leaders hoped it would outshine [[s:massachusetts-bay-colony|Massachusetts Bay]].
providence-island-colony.r: The company governed from [[e:london|London]] through appointed governors and a council, with [[e:new-westminster|New Westminster]] as the main settlement. Crops failed to pay, so the colony turned to privateering against Spanish shipping and came to rely on enslaved Africans, who by 1641 outnumbered the English settlers. An enslaved revolt in 1638 was among the earliest in English America. Church life followed Puritan practice.
providence-island-colony.e: [[e:spain|Spain]] saw the island as a pirate base on its treasure routes and attacked it, failing in 1635 and 1640 before capturing it in May 1641. The settlers were deported and the enslaved people seized. The company's leaders went on to play prominent parts on the Parliamentary side in the [[e:english-civil-war|English Civil War]].

palatinate-mosbach.t: A minor Wittelsbach duchy on the Neckar and in the Odenwald, created when King Rupert's lands were divided in 1410.
palatinate-mosbach.o: When [[e:rupert-of-germany|King Rupert]], [[e:elector-palatine|Elector Palatine]], died in 1410, his lands were divided among his four sons. Otto I received the territory around [[e:mosbach|Mosbach]] on the [[e:neckar|Neckar]] and in the [[e:odenwald|Odenwald]], founding the Palatinate-Mosbach line, and in 1448 he also inherited [[e:neumarkt-in-der-oberpfalz|Neumarkt]] in the [[s:upper-palatinate|Upper Palatinate]].
palatinate-mosbach.r: The [[e:mosbach|Mosbach]] dukes ruled a modest territory of small towns, forests and farms from Mosbach and [[e:neumarkt-in-der-oberpfalz|Neumarkt]], closely tied to the senior electoral line at [[e:heidelberg|Heidelberg]]. Their lands were scattered and their revenues small. [[e:otto-ii-count-palatine-of-mosbach|Otto II]], the second and last duke, never married and left no heirs.
palatinate-mosbach.e: When [[e:otto-ii-count-palatine-of-mosbach|Otto II]] died in 1499, Palatinate-[[e:mosbach|Mosbach]] passed back to the [[s:electoral-palatinate|Electoral Palatinate]]. Mosbach remained Palatine until 1803, when it went to the princes of [[s:principality-of-leiningen|Leiningen]] and then to the [[s:grand-duchy-of-baden|Grand Duchy of Baden]].

principality-of-lucca-and-piombino.t: The Tuscan principality Napoleon created for his sister Elisa Bonaparte, who governed it as an energetic reforming ruler.
principality-of-lucca-and-piombino.o: In 1805 [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]] abolished the [[s:republic-of-lucca|Republic of Lucca]] and joined it to the [[s:principality-of-piombino|Principality of Piombino]], granting the new state to his sister [[e:elisa-bonaparte|Elisa]] and her husband [[e:felice-baciocchi|Felice Baciocchi]]. [[s:duchy-of-massa-and-carrara|Massa and Carrara]] were added in 1806.
principality-of-lucca-and-piombino.r: [[e:elisa-bonaparte|Elisa]], not her husband, held real power. She introduced the [[e:napoleonic-code|Napoleonic Code]], closed many convents, reorganised schools and finances, and promoted the [[e:carrara|Carrara]] marble industry, founding an academy and workshops that produced busts of the Bonaparte family for all [[e:europe|Europe]]. She patronised the violinist [[e:niccolo-paganini|Niccolò Paganini]] at her court. In 1809 [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]] also made her Grand Duchess of [[s:grand-duchy-of-tuscany|Tuscany]], ruling from [[s:duchy-of-florence|Florence]].
principality-of-lucca-and-piombino.e: [[e:elisa-bonaparte|Elisa]] fled as [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]]'s empire collapsed in 1814. The [[e:congress-of-vienna|Congress of Vienna]] gave [[s:republic-of-lucca|Lucca]] to [[e:maria-luisa-duchess-of-lucca|Maria Luisa of Bourbon]] as the [[s:duchy-of-lucca|Duchy of Lucca]], while [[s:principality-of-piombino|Piombino]] went to the [[s:grand-duchy-of-tuscany|Grand Duchy of Tuscany]].

provisional-government-of-the-republic-o.t: The first major Chinese collaborationist regime of the Sino-Japanese War, set up in Beijing in 1937 to govern occupied northern China.
provisional-government-of-the-republic-o.o: After the [[e:lugou-bridge|Marco Polo Bridge]] incident of July 1937, the Japanese [[e:north-china|North China]] Area Army occupied [[e:beijing|Beijing]] and [[e:tianjin|Tianjin]] and pushed south. On 14 December 1937, the day after [[e:nanjing|Nanjing]] fell, it installed the Provisional Government of the [[s:republic-of-china|Republic of China]] in Beijing, headed by the former [[e:beiyang-government|Beiyang]] finance minister [[e:wang-kemin|Wang Kemin]].
provisional-government-of-the-republic-o.r: The regime claimed to govern [[e:hebei|Hebei]], [[e:shandong|Shandong]], [[e:shanxi|Shanxi]] and parts of [[e:henan|Henan]] under the old five-coloured flag of the [[s:beiyang-government|Beiyang government]], though Japanese advisers controlled policy and much of the countryside was held by Communist and Nationalist [[e:guerrilla-warfare|guerrillas]]. It founded the [[e:xinmin-hui|Xinmin Hui]], a mass organisation promoting cooperation with [[e:japan|Japan]], and absorbed the [[s:east-hebei-autonomous-government|East Hebei Autonomous Government]] in 1938.
provisional-government-of-the-republic-o.e: In March 1940 it was merged into the [[s:wang-jingwei-regime|Wang Jingwei regime]] at [[e:nanjing|Nanjing]], continuing as the semi-autonomous [[e:north-china|North China]] Political Council until 1945. [[e:wang-kemin|Wang Kemin]] was arrested after the war and died in prison in 1945.

provisional-government-of-national-defen.t: Rival Greek government set up in Thessaloniki in 1916 by Eleftherios Venizelos, which took Greece into the First World War on the Allied side.
provisional-government-of-national-defen.o: During the [[e:first-world-war|First World War]], [[e:constantine-i-of-greece|King Constantine I]] insisted on neutrality while Prime Minister [[e:eleftherios-venizelos|Eleftherios Venizelos]] wanted to join the [[e:triple-entente|Entente]]. After Venizelos was forced out, officers in Allied-held [[e:thessaloniki|Thessaloniki]] launched the National Defence movement in August 1916. In September and October Venizelos formed a provisional government there with Admiral [[e:pavlos-kountouriotis|Pavlos Kountouriotis]] and General [[e:panagiotis-danglis|Panagiotis Danglis]].
provisional-government-of-national-defen.r: The government, led by this triumvirate, controlled northern [[e:greece|Greece]], [[e:crete|Crete]] and most of the [[e:aegean|Aegean]] islands with Allied support, raised an army and declared war on [[s:bulgaria|Bulgaria]] and [[e:germany|Germany]]. Greece was split in two, the National Schism, while Allied pressure on [[s:athens|Athens]] led to the armed clash of December 1916, the [[e:noemvriana|Noemvriana]].
provisional-government-of-national-defen.e: In June 1917 the [[e:allies|Allies]] forced [[e:constantine-i|Constantine I]] to leave the country. [[e:eleftherios-venizelos|Venizelos]] returned to [[s:athens|Athens]] as prime minister of a united [[s:kingdom-of-greece|Kingdom of Greece]], which entered the war fully. The bitterness of the schism shaped Greek politics for decades.

pedi-kingdom.t: The Maroteng kingdom of the north-eastern Transvaal, which dominated its region and resisted Boer and British conquest until 1879.
pedi-kingdom.o: The Pedi Maroteng dynasty, of [[e:sotho-tswana-peoples|Sotho-Tswana]] origin, settled around the [[e:steelpoort-river|Steelpoort]] river in the 17th century. Under [[e:thulare-i|Thulare]] in the late 18th and early 19th centuries it became a paramountcy dominating many smaller chiefdoms of the region.
pedi-kingdom.r: The Pedi king ruled through royal kin and tributary chiefs, with initiation regiments forming the army. After defeat by [[e:ndebele-kingdom|Mzilikazi's Ndebele]] in the 1820s, Sekwati rebuilt the kingdom on fortified hilltops. Pedi men worked as migrant labourers in the Cape and on the diamond fields, buying guns, and [[e:christianity|Christianity]] divided the court in the 1860s.
pedi-kingdom.e: [[e:sekhukhune-i|Sekhukhune I]] defeated a [[s:south-african-republic|Transvaal]] [[e:boers|Boer]] army in 1876, but after [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] annexed the [[e:transvaal|Transvaal]], a British and Swazi force stormed the capital Tsate in 1879 and captured him. The kingdom became part of the Transvaal, though the Pedi royal house survives.

purepecha-empire.t: The second largest state of Mesoamerica at the Spanish arrival, centred on Lake Pátzcuaro in Michoacán, which defeated the Aztecs and worked copper and bronze.
purepecha-empire.o: The Purépecha (Tarascans) developed in the [[e:lake-patzcuaro|Lake Pátzcuaro]] basin of [[e:michoacan|Michoacán]]. According to the [[e:relacion-de-michoacan|Relación de Michoacán]], the leader Tariacuri united the lake communities in the 14th century, and his heirs divided the realm among [[e:patzcuaro|Pátzcuaro]], [[e:ihuatzio|Ihuatzio]] and [[e:tzintzuntzan|Tzintzuntzan]], later reunited under Tzintzuntzan.
purepecha-empire.r: The Purépecha state was highly centralised under a king (cazonci) who ruled through officials and governors, and it worshipped the fire god [[e:curicaueri|Curicaueri]]. Its people, speaking a language unrelated to others in [[e:mesoamerica|Mesoamerica]], were skilled in [[e:copper|copper]] and bronze metallurgy, featherwork and lacquer. Its capital had distinctive keyhole-shaped yácata temples. In 1478-79 it routed an Aztec army under [[e:axayacatl|Axayacatl]].
purepecha-empire.e: The last king, [[e:tangaxuan-ii|Tangaxuan II]], submitted to the Spanish peacefully in 1522 but was burnt to death by [[e:nuno-de-guzman|Nuño de Guzmán]] in 1530. [[e:bishop|Bishop]] [[e:vasco-de-quiroga|Vasco de Quiroga]] later organised the Purépecha communities, and their language is still spoken.

prince-bishopric-of-munster.t: The largest church state in the Holy Roman Empire, scene of the Anabaptist kingdom of 1534 and of the peace talks that ended the Thirty Years War.
prince-bishopric-of-munster.o: The Frisian missionary [[e:ludger|Liudger]] founded a monastery at Mimigernaford around 793 and became the first [[e:bishop|bishop]] of Münster in 805. The bishops acquired counties across [[e:westphalia|Westphalia]], and after [[e:henry-the-lion|Henry the Lion]] fell in 1180 they ruled as imperial princes. Their lands later stretched from the [[e:lippe-river|Lippe]] to the Ems and beyond to the [[e:dutch|Dutch]] border.
prince-bishopric-of-munster.r: The cathedral chapter and estates kept a strong voice beside the [[e:bishop|bishop]]. In 1534 to 1535 radical [[e:anabaptism|Anabaptists]] under [[e:john-of-leiden|Jan van Leiden]] turned the city into a theocratic kingdom until [[e:franz-von-waldeck|Bishop Franz von Waldeck]] retook it after a siege. The territory remained firmly Catholic. [[e:christoph-bernhard-von-galen|Christoph Bernhard von Galen]] waged wars against the [[s:dutch-republic|Dutch Republic]], and in the 18th century the minister Franz von [[s:principality-of-furstenberg|Fürstenberg]] reformed schools and founded the university.
prince-bishopric-of-munster.e: The [[e:peace-of-westphalia|Peace of Westphalia]] was negotiated partly in Münster in 1648. The see was secularised in 1802 to 1803 and divided, with the largest share going to [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] and smaller parts to [[s:county-of-oldenburg|Oldenburg]], Salm and [[s:duchy-of-arenberg|Arenberg]]. Münster became capital of the [[e:province-of-westphalia|Prussian Province of Westphalia]].

principality-of-wolfenbuttel.t: Guelph principality ruled from Wolfenbüttel, home of the great Herzog August Library and the University of Helmstedt, and forerunner of the Duchy of Brunswick.
principality-of-wolfenbuttel.o: In the division of the [[s:duchy-of-brunswick-luneburg|Duchy of Brunswick-Lüneburg]] in 1269, Albert I the Tall received the southern lands around [[e:brunswick|Brunswick]]. After further partitions the [[e:wolfenbuttel|Wolfenbüttel]] line took shape in the 15th century, with its residence at the castle of Wolfenbüttel, as the city of Brunswick largely governed itself.
principality-of-wolfenbuttel.r: [[e:henry-v-duke-of-brunswick-luneburg|Henry the Younger]] was a fierce Catholic opponent of the [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]], but his son Julius introduced [[e:lutheranism|Lutheranism]] in 1568 and founded the [[e:university-of-helmstedt|University of Helmstedt]] in 1576. [[e:augustus-the-younger-duke-of-brunswick-luneburg|Augustus the Younger]] built the [[e:herzog-august-library|Herzog August Library]], one of the great libraries of [[e:europe|Europe]], where [[e:gotthold-ephraim-lessing|Lessing]] later served as librarian. The dukes subdued [[e:brunswick|Brunswick]] in 1671 and moved their court there in 1753.
principality-of-wolfenbuttel.e: The principality was absorbed into the [[s:kingdom-of-westphalia|Kingdom of Westphalia]] in 1807. Restored in 1813, it became the [[s:duchy-of-brunswick|Duchy of Brunswick]] in 1815, which lasted until 1918. The territory is now in [[e:lower-saxony|Lower Saxony]].

principality-of-nassau-usingen.t: Walramian Nassau principality in the Taunus that moved its court to Biebrich on the Rhine and co-founded the Duchy of Nassau.
principality-of-nassau-usingen.o: Nassau-[[e:usingen|Usingen]] was created in 1659 when the lands of [[s:county-of-nassau-saarbrucken|Nassau-Saarbrücken]] were divided among the sons of Count William Louis, and [[e:walrad-prince-of-nassau-usingen|Walrad]] received Usingen in the [[e:taunus|Taunus]]. Walrad, a general in [[e:dutch|Dutch]] and imperial service, was raised to prince in 1688.
principality-of-nassau-usingen.r: The territory was Lutheran and mostly rural, but it grew as other Walramian lines died out: Nassau-[[e:usingen|Usingen]] inherited [[s:county-of-nassau-saarbrucken|Nassau-Saarbrücken]] and Nassau-Idstein in the 18th century. [[e:charles-prince-of-nassau-usingen|Prince Charles]] moved the residence to [[e:biebrich-palace|Biebrich Palace]] on the [[e:rhine|Rhine]], near [[e:wiesbaden|Wiesbaden]], in 1744, and the spa town of Wiesbaden grew under the princes. After 1797 it lost its left-bank lands but gained [[e:mainz|Mainz]] territory in 1803.
principality-of-nassau-usingen.e: In 1806 Nassau-[[e:usingen|Usingen]] and [[s:county-of-nassau-weilburg|Nassau-Weilburg]] united as the [[s:duchy-of-nassau|Duchy of Nassau]] within the [[s:confederation-of-the-rhine|Confederation of the Rhine]], with [[e:frederick-augustus-duke-of-nassau|Frederick Augustus]] of Usingen as duke. When he died without sons in 1816, the Usingen line ended and [[s:county-of-nassau|Nassau]] passed to the [[e:weilburg|Weilburg]] line.

patiala-and-east-punjab-states-union.t: PEPSU, the union of the Sikh and other princely states of east Punjab, an Indian state from 1948 to 1956 with Patiala as its capital.
patiala-and-east-punjab-states-union.o: In 1948 eight [[e:princely-state|princely states]], [[s:patiala-state|Patiala State]], [[s:nabha-state|Nabha State]], [[s:jind-state|Jind State]], [[s:kapurthala-state|Kapurthala State]], [[s:faridkot-state|Faridkot State]], [[e:malerkotla|Malerkotla]], Nalagarh and [[s:kalsia-state|Kalsia State]], were merged into the Patiala and East Punjab States Union, with [[e:maharaja|Maharaja]] [[e:yadavindra-singh|Yadavindra Singh]] of Patiala as [[e:rajpramukh|Rajpramukh]].
patiala-and-east-punjab-states-union.r: PEPSU became a Part B state in 1950. Its politics were unstable: after the 1952 elections an Akali-led coalition under [[e:gian-singh-rarewala|Gian Singh Rarewala]] collapsed, and President's rule was imposed in 1953. It had a predominantly [[e:sikhism|Sikh]] rural population and fertile irrigated farmland.
patiala-and-east-punjab-states-union.e: Under the [[e:states-reorganisation-act-1956|States Reorganisation Act]] PEPSU was merged into [[e:punjab|Punjab]] on 1 November 1956. Its lands were later divided between Punjab, [[e:haryana|Haryana]] and [[e:himachal-pradesh|Himachal Pradesh]] in 1966.

pashalik-of-timbuktu.t: State created by the Moroccan conquest of Songhai in 1591, ruled from Timbuktu by pashas of the Arma, descendants of Moroccan soldiers.
pashalik-of-timbuktu.o: In 1591 an army sent by the [[s:saadi-sultanate|Saadi Sultanate]] under [[e:judar-pasha|Judar Pasha]] crossed the [[e:sahara|Sahara]] and defeated the [[s:songhai-empire|Songhai Empire]] at [[e:battle-of-tondibi|Tondibi]]. The Moroccans occupied [[e:gao|Gao]], [[e:timbuktu|Timbuktu]] and Djenne and set up a government under a pasha, intended to send gold and slaves to [[e:marrakesh|Marrakesh]].
pashalik-of-timbuktu.r: Moroccan soldiers married local women, and their descendants, the [[e:arma-people|Arma]], became a ruling [[e:caste|caste]] who elected the pashas from their own ranks after about 1612. Allegiance to [[s:kingdom-of-morocco|Morocco]] faded after the mid-17th century. [[e:timbuktu|Timbuktu]] remained a centre of scholarship, and local historians wrote the [[e:tarikh-al-sudan|Tarikh al-Sudan]] and other chronicles in this period.
pashalik-of-timbuktu.e: The pashalik weakened in the 18th century under [[e:tuareg|Tuareg]] raids and [[e:bambara-people|Bambara]] expansion, and the pashas became little more than town governors. [[e:timbuktu|Timbuktu]] came under the [[s:massina-empire|Massina Empire]] in the 1820s and 1830s. [[e:arma-people|Arma]] families remain a distinct group in the [[e:niger-bend|Niger bend]].

principality-of-pereyaslavl.t: The frontier principality of Kievan Rus' facing the steppe, home base of Vladimir Monomakh in his wars against the Cumans.
principality-of-pereyaslavl.o: [[e:pereiaslav|Pereyaslavl]], south-east of [[e:kyiv|Kiev]] on the [[e:trubizh|Trubizh]] river, was one of the oldest towns of Rus'. When [[e:yaroslav-the-wise|Yaroslav the Wise]] died in 1054 he left it to his son [[e:vsevolod-i-of-kiev|Vsevolod]], and it became a principality of its own, third in rank after Kiev and [[e:chernigov|Chernigov]].
principality-of-pereyaslavl.r: Lying on the edge of the steppe, [[e:pereiaslav|Pereyaslavl]] was a military land of fortresses and earthen walls defending Rus' against the [[s:pechenegs|Pechenegs]] and then the [[e:cumans|Cumans]]. [[e:vladimir-ii-monomakh|Vladimir Monomakh]] ruled here from 1094 to 1113 and led campaigns deep into the steppe. The town was briefly the seat of a metropolitan in the 11th century.
principality-of-pereyaslavl.e: Usually held by [[e:vladimir-ii-monomakh|Monomakh]]'s descendants as a stepping stone to [[e:kyiv|Kiev]], the principality declined in the 12th century. The [[e:mongols|Mongols]] sacked [[e:pereiaslav|Pereyaslavl]] in 1239, and the land later passed to the [[s:grand-duchy-of-lithuania|Grand Duchy of Lithuania]]. The town, now Pereiaslav, is where the [[s:cossack-hetmanate|Cossack Hetmanate]] swore allegiance to [[e:moscow|Moscow]] in 1654.

proto-kingdom-of-naqada.t: A predynastic chiefdom centred on Nubt in Upper Egypt, one of the early power centres whose rivalries led to the unification of Egypt.
proto-kingdom-of-naqada.o: Nubt, the Ombos of the [[e:greeks|Greeks]], grew on the west bank of the [[e:nile|Nile]] near modern [[e:naqada|Naqada]] during the Naqada I and II phases of the 4th millennium BCE. Its position opposite the [[e:wadi-hammamat|Wadi Hammamat]], the route to the gold-bearing [[e:eastern-desert|Eastern Desert]], brought wealth, and by c. 3500 BCE a walled town and rich graves show a ruling elite taking shape.
proto-kingdom-of-naqada.r: No written records survive, so almost everything is inferred from archaeology. Cemetery T at [[e:naqada|Naqada]] held large brick-lined tombs furnished with fine pottery, stone vessels, maceheads and imported goods, pointing to a hereditary chiefly class. Nubt was the cult centre of the god Set, later called 'the Ombite', and its workshops produced painted pottery traded along the [[e:nile|Nile]].
proto-kingdom-of-naqada.e: By c. 3200 BCE Nubt appears to have been eclipsed by, or absorbed into, the [[s:proto-kingdom-of-thinis|Proto-kingdom of Thinis]], which went on to unite [[e:egypt|Egypt]]. The town survived as a temple centre of Set, and the [[e:naqada|Naqada]] culture gave its name to the whole predynastic period.

principality-of-kiev.t: The principality of the old capital of Rus', a prize fought over by rival princes, which later became a Lithuanian vassal state.
principality-of-kiev.o: When [[e:mstislav-i-of-kiev|Mstislav the Great]] died in 1132, the unity of [[s:kievan-rus|Kievan Rus']] broke down. [[e:kyiv|Kiev]] itself and its surrounding lands became one principality among many, though still senior in prestige and the seat of the metropolitan. Princes of the Monomakh and Olgovichi lines competed for its throne.
principality-of-kiev.r: [[e:kyiv|Kiev]] changed hands dozens of times in the 12th century. The armies of [[e:andrei-bogolyubsky|Andrei Bogolyubsky]] sacked it in 1169, and [[e:rurik-rostislavich|Rurik Rostislavich]] and his Cuman allies sacked it again in 1203. The [[e:mongols|Mongols]] destroyed the city in 1240, and for a century it was ruled by minor princes and Mongol officials.
principality-of-kiev.e: Around 1362 [[e:algirdas|Algirdas]] of the [[s:grand-duchy-of-lithuania|Grand Duchy of Lithuania]] took [[e:kyiv|Kiev]] and gave it to his son Volodymyr. Under the [[e:olelkovich|Olelkovich]] princes it was a Lithuanian [[e:vassal|vassal]] state with an [[e:eastern-orthodox-church|Orthodox]] court. When [[e:semen-olelkovich|Semen Olelkovich]] died in 1470, [[e:casimir-iv-jagiellon|Casimir IV]] abolished the principality in 1471 and made it a voivodeship.

portuguese-malacca.t: Portugal's fortified trading base on the Strait of Malacca, seized in 1511 and held for 130 years until the Dutch took it in 1641.
portuguese-malacca.o: [[e:afonso-de-albuquerque|Afonso de Albuquerque]] captured the city of the [[s:malacca-sultanate|Malacca Sultanate]] in August 1511, aiming to control the spice trade between the [[e:indian-ocean|Indian Ocean]] and the Far East. He built the fortress of [[e:a-famosa|A Famosa]] on the hill by the river, and [[e:malacca|Malacca]] became a key link in Portugal's [[s:portuguese-india|Estado da India]] between [[e:goa|Goa]] and [[e:macau|Macau]].
portuguese-malacca.r: A Portuguese captain governed the city, with a [[e:bishop|bishop]] from 1557. [[e:malacca|Malacca]] remained a cosmopolitan port, though many Muslim merchants moved to rival ports such as [[e:aceh|Aceh]], [[s:johor-sultanate|Johor]] and [[e:banten|Banten]]. [[e:francis-xavier|Francis Xavier]] preached there in 1545. Intermarriage produced the [[e:kristang|Kristang]], a Portuguese-Eurasian community whose [[e:criollo-people|creole]] language still survives.
portuguese-malacca.e: The city withstood repeated sieges by the [[s:aceh-sultanate|Aceh Sultanate]] and the [[s:johor-sultanate|Johor Sultanate]]. In 1640 to 1641 the [[s:dutch-east-india-company-territories|Dutch East India Company]], allied with [[e:johor|Johor]], besieged it for five months, and it fell in January 1641. The [[e:a-famosa|Porta de Santiago]] gate and the [[e:kristang|Kristang]] community remain.

cr.a: myself, based on ancient national symbol.

portuguese-muscat.t: Muscat under Portuguese control, a fortified port guarding the approach to Hormuz until the Omani imams drove the Portuguese out in 1650.
portuguese-muscat.o: In 1507 [[e:afonso-de-albuquerque|Afonso de Albuquerque]] attacked the Omani coast and sacked [[e:muscat|Muscat]], then a dependency of the [[s:kingdom-of-ormus|Kingdom of Ormus]]. Muscat came under the [[s:portuguese-empire|Portuguese Empire]] as part of its system of forts protecting the [[e:persian-gulf|Gulf]] trade and the route to [[e:india|India]].
portuguese-muscat.r: For much of the period [[e:muscat|Muscat]] was governed through Hormuzi officials with Portuguese oversight and a garrison. After an Ottoman fleet under [[e:piri-reis|Piri Reis]] sacked the town in 1552, the Portuguese built the Jalali and Mirani forts in the 1580s, which still overlook the harbour. Muscat grew in importance after the Portuguese lost [[s:kingdom-of-ormus|Hormuz]] in 1622 and moved their [[e:persian-gulf|Gulf]] base there.
portuguese-muscat.e: The [[e:imam|imams]] of the [[s:yaaruba-dynasty|Ya'aruba dynasty]] took the Omani coast step by step; [[e:sultan-ibn-saif|Sultan ibn Saif]] captured [[e:muscat|Muscat]] in 1650, ending Portuguese rule in [[e:oman|Oman]] and beginning Oman's rise as a naval power.

prince-bishopric-of-montenegro.t: Mountain theocracy ruled by Orthodox metropolitans of Cetinje, which kept Montenegro self-governing against the Ottomans for more than three centuries.
prince-bishopric-of-montenegro.o: After the last [[e:crnojevic-noble-family|Crnojević]] rulers left [[e:zeta-region|Zeta]] in the 1490s and the land was absorbed into the Ottoman sanjak of [[e:shkoder|Scutari]], the metropolitans of [[e:cetinje|Cetinje]] became the recognised leaders of the highland clans; their secular role is traditionally dated from 1516. In 1697 the office passed to [[e:danilo-i-metropolitan-of-cetinje|Danilo Petrović-Njegoš]], whose family kept it, usually from uncle to nephew.
prince-bishopric-of-montenegro.r: The vladika was both [[e:bishop|bishop]] and prince, ruling a confederation of fiercely independent clans with little central administration, bound together by Orthodoxy and war against the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]]. From [[e:peter-the-great|Peter the Great]] onwards the prince-bishops sought Russian support. [[e:petar-i-petrovic-njegos|Petar I]] defeated [[e:kara-mahmud-pasha-bushati|Kara Mahmud Pasha Bushati]] in 1796, and [[e:petar-ii-petrovic-njegos|Petar II]], author of the epic [[e:the-mountain-wreath|The Mountain Wreath]], created a senate and taxes.
prince-bishopric-of-montenegro.e: When [[e:petar-ii-petrovic-njegos|Petar II]] died in 1851, his nephew [[e:danilo-i-prince-of-montenegro|Danilo]] refused ordination and in 1852, with Russian approval, proclaimed himself secular prince, creating the [[s:principality-of-montenegro|Principality of Montenegro]]. The [[e:house-of-petrovic-njegos|Petrović-Njegoš]] dynasty continued to rule until 1918, and the monastery at [[e:cetinje|Cetinje]] remains the seat of the Metropolitanate.

pellene.t: Easternmost city of Achaea, a loyal Spartan ally famous for the woollen cloaks given as prizes at its games.
pellene.o: Pellene stood on a high hill in eastern [[e:achaea|Achaea]], near the border with [[s:sicyon|Sicyon]], a short way inland from the [[e:gulf-of-corinth|Gulf of Corinth]]. It was one of the twelve Achaean cities, formed in the early [[e:iron-age|Iron Age]].
pellene.r: Pellene was known for its warm woollen cloaks, awarded as prizes at its local games, and for its sanctuary of [[e:athena|Athena]]. Unlike most Achaean cities, it sided with [[s:sparta|Sparta]] at the start of the [[e:peloponnesian-war|Peloponnesian War]]. In the 4th century BCE it was ruled at times by tyrants, including the wrestler Chaeron, who was installed with Macedonian backing.
pellene.e: Pellene joined the revived [[s:achaean-league|Achaean League]]. In 241 BCE the [[s:aetolian-league|Aetolian League]] sacked it, and [[e:aratus-of-sicyon|Aratus]] routed the [[e:aetolians|Aetolians]] in its streets. It passed under Roman control in 146 BCE and later dwindled.

provisional-government-of-albania.t: First government of independent Albania, proclaimed at Vlorë in 1912 while Balkan armies occupied most of the country.
provisional-government-of-albania.o: During the [[e:first-balkan-war|First Balkan War]], as Serbian, Montenegrin and Greek armies overran the Ottoman [[e:balkans|Balkans]], Albanian delegates gathered in [[e:vlore|Vlorë]]. On 28 November 1912 they declared independence, raised [[e:skanderbeg|Skanderbeg's]] flag and formed a provisional government headed by the veteran Ottoman official [[e:ismail-qemali|Ismail Qemali]], with [[e:luigj-gurakuqi|Luigj Gurakuqi]] among its ministers.
provisional-government-of-albania.r: The government controlled little beyond [[e:vlore|Vlorë]] and its surroundings, lacking an army, money or international recognition, while [[e:durres|Durrës]], [[e:shkoder|Shkodër]] and much of the south were occupied or contested. It set up ministries, schools and a gendarmerie on paper. Its fate depended on the [[e:london-conference-of-1912-1913|Conference of Ambassadors]] in [[e:london|London]], which recognised [[s:albania|Albania]] in 1913 but left [[e:kosovo|Kosovo]] outside its borders.
provisional-government-of-albania.e: An [[e:international-commission-of-control|International Commission of Control]] took over administration in late 1913, and [[e:ismail-qemali|Ismail Qemali]] resigned in January 1914 amid rivalry with [[e:essad-pasha-toptani|Essad Pasha]]'s [[s:republic-of-central-albania|Republic of Central Albania]]. In March 1914 the Great Powers' chosen ruler, [[e:william-prince-of-albania|Wilhelm of Wied]], arrived to found the [[s:principality-of-albania|Principality of Albania]].
provisional-government-of-albania.re: Sunni Islam, Orthodox and Catholic Christianity

polonnaruwa-kingdom.t: The second great Sinhalese kingdom, which drove out the Cholas and under Parakramabahu I built the Parakrama Samudra and the Gal Vihara.
polonnaruwa-kingdom.o: After the [[s:chola-empire|Chola Empire]] conquered the [[s:anuradhapura-kingdom|Anuradhapura Kingdom]] in the early 11th century, it ruled northern [[s:sri-lanka|Sri Lanka]] from [[e:polonnaruwa|Polonnaruwa]]. [[e:vijayabahu-i|Vijayabahu I]], leading resistance from the [[s:kingdom-of-ruhuna|Kingdom of Ruhuna]], expelled the [[e:chola-empire|Cholas]] in 1070 and kept Polonnaruwa as his capital.
polonnaruwa-kingdom.r: [[e:parakramabahu-i|Parakramabahu I]], who ruled from 1153 to 1186, reunited the island after a civil war, built the vast reservoir called the [[e:parakrama-samudra|Parakrama Samudra]], reformed and unified the Buddhist sangha and sent expeditions to [[s:myanmar|Burma]] and [[e:south-india|South India]]. [[e:polonnaruwa|Polonnaruwa's]] palaces, image houses and the rock-cut Buddhas of the [[e:gal-vihara|Gal Vihara]] date from this time. [[e:nissanka-malla|Nissanka Malla]], from [[s:kingdom-of-kalinga|Kalinga]], left many inscriptions. [[e:rice|Rice]] grown with irrigation and trade sustained the kingdom.
polonnaruwa-kingdom.e: After [[e:nissanka-malla|Nissanka Malla]] the kingdom was torn by rivalries. In 1215 the invader [[e:kalinga-magha|Kalinga Magha]] sacked [[e:polonnaruwa|Polonnaruwa]], and around 1232 the Sinhalese capital moved south-west to [[s:kingdom-of-dambadeniya|Dambadeniya]]. The irrigation network of the dry zone fell into decay.

province-of-queen-adelaide.t: A short-lived British annexation of Xhosa land between the Keiskamma and Kei rivers, reversed by London after barely a year.
province-of-queen-adelaide.o: During the Sixth Frontier War of 1834-1836, the Cape governor [[e:benjamin-durban|Sir Benjamin D'Urban]] proclaimed in May 1835 that the territory between the [[e:keiskamma-river|Keiskamma]] and Kei rivers was British, naming it after [[e:adelaide-of-saxe-meiningen|Queen Adelaide]], wife of [[e:william-iv-of-the-united-kingdom|William IV]]. The [[e:xhosa-people|Xhosa]] king [[e:hintsa-kakhawuta|Hintsa]] was shot while in British custody during the campaign.
province-of-queen-adelaide.r: [[e:sir-harry-smith-1st-baronet|Colonel Harry Smith]] governed the province from the new military headquarters of [[e:king-williams-town|King William's Town]]. The plan was to expel or control the [[s:rharhabe-xhosa-kingdom|Rharhabe]] [[e:xhosa-people|Xhosa]], settle loyal [[e:mfengu|Mfengu]] and open land to colonists, but it required a costly garrison and provoked continued resistance.
province-of-queen-adelaide.e: The Colonial Secretary [[e:charles-grant-1st-baron-glenelg|Lord Glenelg]], influenced by humanitarian critics, ordered the annexation reversed, and the province was abandoned in December 1836 in favour of treaties with [[e:xhosa-people|Xhosa]] chiefs. [[e:sir-harry-smith-1st-baronet|Smith]] restored the idea in 1847 as [[s:british-kaffraria|British Kaffraria]].

cr.a: I created the map, based partly on the source map: Eastern frontier of the Colony of the Cape of Good Hope from Algoa Bay to the …

prince-bishopric-of-osnabruck.t: Westphalian church state where the Peace of Westphalia was negotiated and where, uniquely, Catholic and Lutheran bishops alternated after 1648.
prince-bishopric-of-osnabruck.o: [[e:charlemagne|Charlemagne]] founded the diocese of [[e:osnabruck|Osnabrück]] around 780 after his conquest of the [[s:saxons|Saxons]]. Its [[e:bishop|bishops]] acquired estates and comital rights between the Ems and the [[e:weser|Weser]], and in the 13th century, around 1225, they emerged as imperial princes ruling a consolidated territory free of the counts of [[s:county-of-tecklenburg|Tecklenburg]].
prince-bishopric-of-osnabruck.r: The cathedral chapter and estates held strong rights. [[e:osnabruck|Osnabrück]] and Münster hosted the negotiations of the [[e:peace-of-westphalia|Peace of Westphalia]]. Under its terms the see alternated between a Catholic [[e:bishop|bishop]] and a Lutheran prince of the house of Brunswick-[[e:luneburg|Lüneburg]]; [[e:ernest-augustus-elector-of-hanover|Ernest Augustus]], father of [[e:george-i-of-great-britain|George I of Great Britain]], and later [[e:prince-frederick-duke-of-york-and-albany|Frederick, Duke of York]], held it. The territory was known for linen and for the writer and statesman [[e:justus-moser|Justus Möser]].
prince-bishopric-of-osnabruck.e: In 1803 the see was secularised and given to [[e:hanover|Hanover]]. After the Napoleonic interlude it remained Hanoverian until [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] annexed the [[s:kingdom-of-hanover|Kingdom of Hanover]] in 1866. The Catholic diocese continues.
