praetorian-prefecture-of-africa.t: Justinian's government for reconquered North Africa, set up at Carthage after the fall of the Vandals.
praetorian-prefecture-of-africa.o: After [[e:belisarius|Belisarius]] destroyed the [[s:vandal-kingdom|Vandal Kingdom]] in 533 to 534, Justinian created a Praetorian Prefecture of [[e:africa|Africa]] with its seat at [[e:carthage|Carthage]]. It covered the former Roman provinces from [[s:tripolitania|Tripolitania]] to [[s:kingdom-of-mauretania|Mauretania]], with [[e:sardinia|Sardinia]] and [[s:corsican-republic|Corsica]], under a civil prefect and a separate military commander.
praetorian-prefecture-of-africa.r: Restoration of [[e:roman-law|Roman law]], taxation and the [[e:nicene-christianity|Nicene]] church came with confiscation of Arian property. The general [[e:solomon|Solomon]], who also served as prefect, built fortresses across [[s:numidia|Numidia]] and [[s:byzacena|Byzacena]], many still visible today. The new regime faced army mutinies, notably that of [[e:stotzas|Stotzas]] in 536, and repeated wars with [[e:berbers|Berber]] powers such as the [[s:kingdom-of-capsus|Kingdom of Capsus]] and the [[s:laguatan|Laguatan]], until [[e:john-troglita|John Troglita]] restored order around 548.
praetorian-prefecture-of-africa.e: To strengthen defence against the [[e:berbers|Berbers]], the emperor Maurice combined civil and military authority under an exarch around 591. The prefecture was thus replaced by the [[s:exarchate-of-africa|Exarchate of Africa]], though [[e:prefect|prefects]] remained as subordinate officials.

portuguese-mozambique.t: Portugal's East African colony for almost five centuries, from the fort at Sofala in 1505 to independence in 1975.
portuguese-mozambique.o: Portugal built a fort at [[e:sofala|Sofala]] in 1505 to tap the [[e:gold-trade|gold trade]] of the [[e:zimbabwean-plateau|Zimbabwe plateau]] and took over [[e:mozambique-island|Mozambique Island]] soon after, making it the capital and a stop on the route to [[e:india|India]]. In the 16th and 17th centuries Portuguese traders and soldiers pushed up the [[e:zambezi|Zambezi]] to [[e:sena-mozambique|Sena]] and [[e:tete|Tete]], competing with [[e:swahili|Swahili merchants]] and the [[e:mutapa-empire|Mutapa]] state.
portuguese-mozambique.r: For centuries Portuguese control was limited to coastal towns and the [[e:zambezi|Zambezi]] [[e:prazo|prazos]], huge estates held by Afro-Portuguese families with private armies. The 19th-century [[e:atlantic-slave-trade|slave trade]] and then forced labour and [[e:chartered-company|chartered companies]], such as the [[s:mozambique-company|Mozambique Company]], shaped the economy. Effective occupation came only after the defeat of the [[s:gaza|Gaza]] ruler [[e:ngungunhane|Gungunhana]] in 1895, and the capital moved to [[e:maputo|Lourenco Marques]] in 1898.
portuguese-mozambique.e: From 1964 [[e:frelimo|FRELIMO]] waged a [[e:guerrilla-warfare|guerrilla]] war for independence. After the [[e:carnation-revolution|Carnation Revolution]] in [[e:lisbon|Lisbon]] in 1974, Portugal negotiated withdrawal, and [[e:mozambique|Mozambique]] became independent on 25 June 1975 under [[e:samora-machel|Samora Machel]].

cr.a: Original: Columbano Bordalo Pinheiro Vector: Vítor Luís Rodrigues, António Martins-Tuválkin

prince-bishopric-of-cambrai.t: An imperial church principality on the French border, which gave its name to the League of Cambrai and the Ladies' Peace before Louis XIV annexed it.
prince-bishopric-of-cambrai.o: Cambrai was a Merovingian bishopric whose diocese stretched across [[s:county-of-hainaut|Hainaut]] and [[s:duchy-of-brabant|Brabant]]. In 1007 [[e:henry-ii-holy-roman-emperor|Emperor Henry II]] granted the county of Cambrai to [[e:bishop|Bishop]] Erluin, making the bishops princes of the [[s:holy-roman-empire|Holy Roman Empire]] on its frontier with [[e:france|France]].
prince-bishopric-of-cambrai.r: The Cambrésis was a small but rich land of cloth and linen, its name later given to the fine fabric cambric. The [[e:bishop|bishops]] often struggled with the townspeople and with the counts of [[s:county-of-flanders|Flanders]] and [[s:county-of-hainaut|Hainaut]]. The city hosted the [[e:league-of-cambrai|League of Cambrai]] against [[e:venice|Venice]] in 1508 and the [[e:peace-of-cambrai|Ladies' Peace]] of 1529. [[e:charles-v-holy-roman-emperor|Charles V]] built a citadel there in 1543.
prince-bishopric-of-cambrai.e: Cambrai became an archbishopric in 1559 under strong Spanish influence. [[e:louis-xiv|Louis XIV]] captured it in 1677, and the [[e:treaties-of-nijmegen|Treaty of Nijmegen]] of 1678 gave it to the [[s:kingdom-of-france|Kingdom of France]]. [[e:francois-fenelon|Fénelon]] was its most famous archbishop.

provisional-peoples-committee-for-north-.t: The Soviet-backed government led by Kim Il Sung that ruled northern Korea from 1946 and laid the groundwork for the North Korean state.
provisional-peoples-committee-for-north-.o: In February 1946 the [[s:soviet-civil-administration|Soviet Civil Administration]] convened a meeting of political parties and local people's committees in [[e:pyongyang|Pyongyang]], which created the Provisional People's Committee for [[e:north-korea|North Korea]], with [[e:kim-il-sung|Kim Il Sung]] as chairman and [[e:kim-tu-bong|Kim Tu-bong]] as vice chairman.
provisional-peoples-committee-for-north-.r: The committee carried out a radical programme in a few months: a land reform in March 1946 that confiscated landlords' estates and distributed them to farmers, a labour law, a law on equality of the sexes and the nationalisation of major industries in August 1946. Elections to local people's committees with single lists were held in November 1946. In February 1947 it was replaced by the People's Committee of [[e:north-korea|North Korea]], again chaired by [[e:kim-il-sung|Kim Il Sung]].
provisional-peoples-committee-for-north-.e: A constitution was adopted in 1948, and the [[e:north-korea|Democratic People's Republic of Korea]] was proclaimed in September 1948, with [[e:kim-il-sung|Kim Il Sung]] as premier.

palatinate-zweibrucken.t: A Wittelsbach duchy in the western Palatinate whose family gave Sweden three kings and Bavaria its first king.
palatinate-zweibrucken.o: In 1453 the lands of Duke Stephen of [[s:palatinate-simmern|Palatinate-Simmern]] were divided, and his son Louis I the Black received [[e:zweibrucken|Zweibrücken]] and [[s:county-of-veldenz|Veldenz]], founding the Palatinate-Zweibrücken line. Louis spent much of his reign in conflict with his cousins of the [[s:electoral-palatinate|Electoral Palatinate]].
palatinate-zweibrucken.r: The dukes ruled scattered lands in the western [[s:electoral-palatinate|Palatinate]] and [[e:alsace|Alsace]] from [[e:zweibrucken|Zweibrücken]]. [[e:wolfgang-count-palatine-of-zweibrucken|Wolfgang]] introduced [[e:lutheranism|Lutheranism]] and founded the Hornbach school in 1559, while John I later adopted [[e:calvinism|Calvinism]]. A cadet branch, [[e:palatinate-kleeburg|Palatinate-Kleeburg]], gave [[e:sweden|Sweden]] three kings, beginning with [[e:charles-x-gustav|Charles X Gustav]] in 1654, and from 1681 to 1718 Zweibrücken itself was ruled by the kings of Sweden.
palatinate-zweibrucken.e: In 1793 French armies occupied [[e:zweibrucken|Zweibrücken]], and [[e:france|France]] annexed it in 1797. Its duke [[e:maximilian-i-joseph-of-bavaria|Maximilian Joseph]] inherited the [[s:electorate-of-bavaria|Electorate of Bavaria]] in 1799 and in 1806 became the first king of the [[s:kingdom-of-bavaria|Kingdom of Bavaria]], whose royal house descended from Zweibrücken.

cr.a: Sir Iain; derivative work by Furfur

palmyrene-egypt.t: Egypt under Queen Zenobia of Palmyra, held for two years during her challenge to Roman authority in the East.
palmyrene-egypt.o: In 270 [[e:zenobia|Zenobia]], ruling [[s:palmyrene-empire|Palmyra]] for her young son [[e:vaballathus|Vaballathus]], sent her general [[e:zabdas|Zabdas]] into [[e:egypt|Egypt]], helped by the local supporter Timagenes. After fighting with the Roman prefect [[e:tenagino-probus|Tenagino Probus]], the Palmyrenes gained control of [[e:alexandria|Alexandria]] and the province, making it part of the [[e:palmyrene-empire|Palmyrene Empire]].
palmyrene-egypt.r: The Palmyrene regime kept the Roman administration and at first claimed to act within the Empire: the [[e:alexandria|Alexandria]] mint issued coins with [[e:vaballathus|Vaballathus]] beside the emperor Aurelian. Control of [[e:egypt|Egypt's]] grain gave [[e:zenobia|Zenobia]] leverage over [[e:rome|Rome]]. By 272 she declared herself and her son emperors.
palmyrene-egypt.e: Aurelian responded in 272, defeating the Palmyrene armies in [[s:syrian-arab-republic|Syria]] while Roman forces, led according to later sources by the future emperor [[e:probus-emperor|Probus]], recovered [[e:egypt|Egypt]]. [[e:zenobia|Zenobia]] was captured and Egypt returned to direct Roman rule as [[s:roman-egypt|Roman Egypt]].

panormus.t: Phoenician and Punic city on the bay of Palermo, Carthage's chief stronghold in western Sicily until Rome captured it in 254 BCE.
panormus.o: [[e:phoenicians|Phoenicians]] settled [[e:palermo|Panormus]], called Ziz ('flower') on its coins, on a promontory between two river inlets by the late 8th or 7th century BCE. Its deep natural harbour gave it the Greek name Panormos, 'all-harbour'. With [[s:motya|Motya]] and [[e:solunto|Soloeis]] it formed the cluster of Phoenician towns in western [[e:sicily|Sicily]] that came under Carthaginian protection.
panormus.r: [[e:palermo|Panormus]] prospered from trade between [[e:carthage|Carthage]], [[e:sardinia|Sardinia]] and the Greek and Elymian towns of [[e:sicily|Sicily]] and served as a key Carthaginian military base: [[e:hamilcar-i-of-carthage|Hamilcar]] landed there before the battle of [[s:himera|Himera]] in 480 BCE. Its necropolis shows a mixed population of [[e:phoenicians|Phoenicians]], [[e:greeks|Greeks]] and [[e:elymians|Elymians]]. It minted coins with Punic and Greek legends and was ruled by local magistrates under Carthaginian oversight.
panormus.e: In the [[e:first-punic-war|First Punic War]] [[e:rome|Rome]] took [[e:palermo|Panormus]] in 254 BCE, and in 250 BCE the consul [[e:lucius-caecilius-metellus-consul-251-bce|Lucius Caecilius Metellus]] defeated a Carthaginian army with elephants beneath its walls. The city became a free town of the Roman province of [[e:sicily|Sicily]] and later grew into Palermo, capital of the [[s:emirate-of-sicily|Emirate of Sicily]] and the Norman kingdom.

prince-bishopric-of-paderborn.t: Westphalian church state rooted in Charlemagne's Saxon wars and his 799 meeting with Pope Leo III, a Catholic bastion until 1802.
prince-bishopric-of-paderborn.o: [[e:charlemagne|Charlemagne]] held assemblies at [[e:paderborn|Paderborn]] from 777 and met [[e:pope-leo-iii|Pope Leo III]] there in 799, the prelude to his imperial coronation. The diocese was founded around the same time. [[e:bishop|Bishop]] [[e:meinwerk|Meinwerk]] in the early 11th century built up its wealth and churches. The bishops gradually acquired comital rights, ruling a territorial principality by the late 13th century, around 1281.
prince-bishopric-of-paderborn.r: The cathedral chapter and estates shared power with the prince-[[e:bishop|bishop]]. [[e:lutheranism|Lutheranism]] spread in the 16th century, but Bishop [[e:dietrich-von-furstenberg|Dietrich von Fürstenberg]] restored [[e:catholicism|Catholicism]] and founded a [[e:jesuits|Jesuit]] university in 1614. His relative [[e:ferdinand-von-furstenberg|Ferdinand von Fürstenberg]] was a noted scholar-bishop. The territory, in the fertile [[e:hellweg|Hellweg]] and the [[e:egge-hills|Egge hills]], was agricultural with small towns.
prince-bishopric-of-paderborn.e: In 1802 the see was secularised and annexed by [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]]. It belonged to the [[s:kingdom-of-westphalia|Kingdom of Westphalia]] from 1807 to 1813 and then returned to Prussia. The diocese, raised to an archdiocese in 1930, continues.

provisional-government-of-judea.t: The rebel government of the First Jewish Revolt, which minted its own coins and held Jerusalem against Rome until the city and Temple fell in 70.
provisional-government-of-judea.o: Riots in [[s:lordship-of-caesarea|Caesarea]] and the plundering of the Temple treasury by the procurator [[e:gessius-florus|Florus]] led to open revolt in 66. After rebels routed the Syrian governor [[e:cestius-gallus|Cestius Gallus]] at [[e:battle-of-beth-horon-66|Beth Horon]], an assembly in [[e:jerusalem|Jerusalem]] appointed the former high priest [[e:ananus-ben-ananus|Ananus ben Ananus]] and Joseph ben Gurion to lead it and sent commanders to the districts, [[e:josephus|Josephus]] among them to [[e:galilee|Galilee]].
provisional-government-of-judea.r: The government struck [[e:silver|silver]] shekels dated by years of the revolt and inscribed '[[e:jerusalem|Jerusalem]] the Holy', a declaration of [[e:sovereignty|sovereignty]]. Its moderate priestly leadership was overthrown in 68 by [[e:zealots|Zealots]] allied with [[e:idumaeans|Idumaeans]], who killed [[e:ananus-ben-ananus|Ananus]]. Jerusalem then split between rival factions under [[e:john-of-gischala|John of Gischala]], [[e:simon-bar-giora|Simon bar Giora]] and [[e:eleazar-ben-simon|Eleazar ben Simon]], who fought each other and burned food stores.
provisional-government-of-judea.e: Vespasian subdued [[e:galilee|Galilee]] in 67 and [[e:titus|Titus]] besieged [[e:jerusalem|Jerusalem]] in 70, destroying the city and the [[e:temple-in-jerusalem|Second Temple]] that summer. The last strongholds, including [[e:masada|Masada]], fell by 73-74. [[e:judaea|Judea]] became a separate province with a legion stationed in the ruins of Jerusalem.

persian-socialist-soviet-republic.t: A short-lived Soviet republic in the Caspian province of Gilan, born from an alliance between the Jangali rebels of Mirza Kuchik Khan and the Bolsheviks.
persian-socialist-soviet-republic.o: From 1915 [[e:mirza-kuchik-khan|Mirza Kuchik Khan]] led the [[e:jangal-movement|Jangali]] ('forest') movement in [[e:gilan|Gilan]] against foreign intervention and the weak [[e:qajar-dynasty|Qajar]] government. In May 1920 a Bolshevik fleet landed at [[e:bandar-e-anzali|Anzali]] in pursuit of White Russian ships. With Soviet support, Kuchik Khan proclaimed the Persian Socialist Soviet Republic at [[e:rasht|Rasht]] in June 1920.
persian-socialist-soviet-republic.r: The republic was a fragile coalition of [[e:mirza-kuchik-khan|Kuchik Khan's]] nationalist and religious followers, radical leftists under [[e:ehsanollah-khan-dustdar|Ehsanollah Khan]] and the new Communist Party of [[e:iran|Iran]], backed by Soviet troops. Disputes over land reform and religion split the leadership within weeks; Kuchik Khan withdrew to the forests, and the communists took over [[e:rasht|Rasht]]. A later reconciliation brought in [[e:haydar-khan-amu-oghli|Haydar Khan Amu-oghli]], who was killed in renewed infighting in 1921.
persian-socialist-soviet-republic.e: Under the [[e:russo-persian-treaty-of-friendship-1921|Soviet-Persian Treaty]] of February 1921, [[s:russian-sfsr|Soviet Russia]] withdrew its forces. [[e:reza-shah|Reza Khan's]] [[e:cossacks|Cossack]] troops crushed the republic in late 1921, and [[e:mirza-kuchik-khan|Kuchik Khan]] died of exposure in the mountains that December; he is remembered in [[e:iran|Iran]] as a national hero.

principality-of-correggio.t: The small Emilian state of the da Correggio lords, birthplace of the painter Antonio Allegri, called Correggio.
principality-of-correggio.o: The da [[e:antonio-da-correggio|Correggio]] family had ruled the town of Correggio, between [[e:reggio-emilia|Reggio]] and [[s:lordship-of-carpi|Carpi]], since the 12th century and had been powerful in [[s:duchy-of-parma-and-piacenza|Parma]]. In 1452 [[e:frederick-iii-holy-roman-emperor|Emperor Frederick III]] recognised their lands as a county, raised to a principality in 1616.
principality-of-correggio.r: The counts governed a small farming territory and a fortified town with a lively court. [[e:veronica-gambara|Veronica Gambara]], poet and widow of Count Giberto, ruled as regent in the early 16th century and corresponded with leading writers. The painter [[e:antonio-da-correggio|Antonio Allegri]], known as Correggio, was born in the town around 1489. The rulers depended on the protection of the emperor and their [[e:house-of-este|Este]] neighbours.
principality-of-correggio.e: Prince Siro da [[e:antonio-da-correggio|Correggio]] was accused of minting debased coins and was deposed by the emperor in 1630. In 1635 the principality was sold to Francesco I d'[[e:house-of-este|Este]] and joined to the [[s:duchy-of-modena-and-reggio|Duchy of Modena and Reggio]].

province-of-yucatan.t: The Spanish colonial province of the Yucatán peninsula, governed from Mérida, where Maya communities kept much of their language and identity.
province-of-yucatan.o: After two failed attempts, [[e:francisco-de-montejo-the-younger|Francisco de Montejo the Younger]] conquered western Yucatán and founded [[e:merida-yucatan|Mérida]] in 1542 on the site of [[e:tho|T'ho]]. Campaigns of 1543-46 subdued the eastern provinces, and the [[e:great-maya-revolt|Great Maya Revolt]] of 1546-47 was crushed.
province-of-yucatan.r: Yucatán was governed by a governor and captain-general with considerable autonomy within [[s:new-spain|New Spain]]. With no precious metals, its economy rested on Maya tribute in [[e:cotton|cotton]] cloth, wax and honey, and later on [[e:cattle|cattle]] estates and logwood. [[e:franciscans|Franciscans]] led evangelisation; [[e:diego-de-landa|Bishop Diego de Landa]] burnt Maya books in 1562. [[e:san-francisco-de-campeche|Campeche]] was its fortified port, often raided by [[e:piracy|pirates]], and Maya revolts such as [[e:jacinto-canek|Jacinto Canek's]] in 1761 recurred.
province-of-yucatan.e: Yucatán became an intendancy in 1786 and joined independent [[s:mexico|Mexico]] in 1821. Its strong regional identity later produced attempts at secession and the [[e:caste-war-of-yucatan|Caste War of Yucatán]].

portuguese-gold-coast.t: Portugal's chain of trading forts on the Gold Coast, centred on Sao Jorge da Mina, which for over a century channelled West African gold to Lisbon.
portuguese-gold-coast.o: Portuguese ships reached the gold-trading coast of present-day Ghana in 1471. In 1482, on the orders of [[e:john-ii-of-portugal|King John II]], [[e:diogo-de-azambuja|Diogo de Azambuja]] built the fortress of Sao Jorge da [[e:meena|Mina]] at [[e:elmina|Elmina]], after negotiating with a local chief remembered as [[e:caramansa|Caramansa]]. Smaller forts followed at [[e:axim|Axim]], [[e:shama-ghana|Shama]] and other points.
portuguese-gold-coast.r: The forts were run by a royal monopoly whose governor bought gold from [[e:akan|Akan]] traders with cloth, brass, [[e:bead|beads]] and slaves brought from elsewhere in [[e:africa|Africa]]. At its height the [[e:meena|Mina]] trade supplied a large share of Portugal's gold. The garrisons were small and depended on agreements with coastal rulers such as the [[s:kingdom-of-eguafo|Kingdom of Eguafo]].
portuguese-gold-coast.e: The [[e:dutch|Dutch]], rivals in the trade, captured [[e:elmina|Elmina]] in 1637 and [[e:axim|Axim]] in 1642, ending Portuguese power on the coast. Their posts became the core of the [[s:dutch-gold-coast|Dutch Gold Coast]], and Elmina Castle is now a [[e:unesco-world-heritage-site|World Heritage Site]].

cr.a: myself, based on ancient national symbol.

principality-of-salm-1802.t: Napoleonic-era principality in the Münsterland, given to two Salm princes in compensation for lands lost to France.
principality-of-salm-1802.o: The princes of [[s:principality-of-salm|Salm-Salm]] and [[s:wild-and-rhinegraviate|Salm-Kyrburg]] lost their territories in the [[e:vosges|Vosges]] and on the left bank of the [[e:rhine|Rhine]] to revolutionary [[e:france|France]]. Under the settlement of 1802 and the [[e:reichsdeputationshauptschluss|Imperial Recess of 1803]], they jointly received the districts of [[e:bocholt|Bocholt]] and [[e:ahaus|Ahaus]] from the secularised [[s:prince-bishopric-of-munster|Prince-Bishopric of Münster]], forming the Principality of Salm.
principality-of-salm-1802.r: The two princely houses held the state jointly, with [[s:principality-of-salm|Salm-Salm]] taking two-thirds and [[s:wild-and-rhinegraviate|Salm-Kyrburg]] one third, and governed from [[e:bocholt|Bocholt]] and Anholt. The territory was Catholic and agrarian. In 1806 it joined the [[s:confederation-of-the-rhine|Confederation of the Rhine]] as a sovereign member. The Salm-[[e:kyrburg|Kyrburg]] prince [[e:frederick-iii-prince-of-salm-kyrburg|Frederick III]] had been guillotined in [[e:paris|Paris]] in 1794, and his young son [[e:frederick-iv-prince-of-salm-kyrburg|Frederick IV]] succeeded him.
principality-of-salm-1802.e: In December 1810 [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]] annexed north-western [[e:germany|Germany]] to secure the coast against British trade, and Salm was incorporated into [[e:france|France]] in 1811. In 1815 the territory passed to [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]], where the Salm families remained as mediatised landowners.

prince-bishopric-of-passau.t: Danube church state at the meeting of three rivers, whose vast diocese once stretched to Vienna and whose court may have produced the Nibelungenlied.
prince-bishopric-of-passau.o: [[e:saint-boniface|Saint Boniface]] organised the diocese of [[e:passau|Passau]] in 739. As the Bavarian church expanded eastwards, its diocese came to cover much of today's [[e:austria|Austria]]. In 1217 [[e:frederick-ii|Emperor Frederick II]] recognised the [[e:bishop|bishop]]'s secular lordship over the city and nearby lands, making Passau a prince-bishopric directly under the Empire.
prince-bishopric-of-passau.r: The cathedral chapter elected the prince-[[e:bishop|bishops]], who ruled a small territory around [[e:passau|Passau]] and in the Bavarian Forest, with [[e:salt-trade|salt trade]] on the [[e:danube|Danube]] and [[e:inn-river|Inn]]. The [[e:nibelungenlied|Nibelungenlied]] may have been composed around 1200 at the court of Bishop [[e:wolfger-von-erla|Wolfger von Erla]]. Conflicts with the citizens recurred. After a fire in 1662 Italian architects rebuilt the city and St. [[e:st-stephens-cathedral-passau|Stephen's Cathedral]] in baroque style.
prince-bishopric-of-passau.e: The prince-bishopric was secularised in 1803 and divided between [[e:bavaria|Bavaria]] and the [[s:electorate-of-salzburg|Electorate of Salzburg]]; by 1805 all of it belonged to Bavaria. The Catholic diocese of [[e:passau|Passau]] continues, and the baroque old town still clusters on the narrow peninsula between the [[e:danube|Danube]] and the [[e:inn-river|Inn]].

principality-of-philaretos-brachamios.t: A short-lived Armenian-ruled domain in the Taurus and northern Syria, built by a Byzantine general after the empire's collapse in the East.
principality-of-philaretos-brachamios.o: [[e:philaretos-brachamios|Philaretos Brachamios]] was an Armenian officer in Byzantine service. After the defeat at [[e:battle-of-manzikert|Manzikert]] in 1071 and the civil wars that followed, he gathered soldiers and Armenian refugees and made himself master of [[e:kahramanmaras|Marash]], [[e:malatya|Melitene]] and other towns in the [[e:taurus-mountains|Taurus]] and [[e:cilicia|Cilicia]].
principality-of-philaretos-brachamios.r: [[e:philaretos-brachamios|Philaretos]] acted independently but sought recognition from [[e:constantinople|Constantinople]], which gave him high titles and appointed him governor in the East. At its height around 1078-1083 his domain stretched from [[e:cilicia|Cilicia]] to [[s:principality-of-antioch|Antioch]] and [[s:county-of-edessa|Edessa]]. He was a Chalcedonian Christian, which made him unpopular with many [[e:armenians|Armenians]] of the national church, and he is said to have considered accepting [[e:islam|Islam]] to keep [[e:seljuk-empire|Seljuk]] favour.
principality-of-philaretos-brachamios.e: The [[e:seljuk-empire|Seljuk]] prince [[e:suleiman-ibn-qutalmish|Suleiman ibn Qutalmish]] took [[s:principality-of-antioch|Antioch]] in 1084, and [[s:county-of-edessa|Edessa]] fell soon after. [[e:philaretos-brachamios|Philaretos]] disappears from the record around 1086. Armenian lords of the region, among them the [[e:rubenid-dynasty|Rubenids]], later formed the core of the [[s:armenian-kingdom-of-cilicia|Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia]].

principality-of-oettingen-wallerstein.t: The Catholic line of the Ries counts of Oettingen, raised to princes in 1774, whose court at Wallerstein kept a renowned orchestra.
principality-of-oettingen-wallerstein.o: The 1522 division of the house of [[s:county-of-oettingen|Oettingen]] gave the [[e:wallerstein|Wallerstein]] line lands in the southern [[e:nordlinger-ries|Ries]], with castles at Wallerstein and [[e:harburg-swabia|Harburg]]. While the [[s:principality-of-oettingen-spielberg|Oettingen-Oettingen]] line became Lutheran, Wallerstein remained Catholic and supported the [[e:counter-reformation|Counter-Reformation]].
principality-of-oettingen-wallerstein.r: The counts, raised to princes in 1774, ruled a farming territory in the [[e:swabian-circle|Swabian Circle]] from [[e:wallerstein|Wallerstein]] and [[e:harburg-swabia|Harburg]] castle. Prince [[e:kraft-ernst-prince-of-oettingen-wallerstein|Kraft Ernst]] maintained one of the finest court orchestras in [[e:germany|Germany]], employing the composer [[e:antonio-rosetti|Antonio Rosetti]], and the family built up a famous library rich in medieval [[e:manuscript|manuscripts]].
principality-of-oettingen-wallerstein.e: Mediatised in 1806, Oettingen-[[e:wallerstein|Wallerstein]] came under the [[s:kingdom-of-bavaria|Kingdom of Bavaria]]. Prince [[e:ludwig-of-oettingen-wallerstein|Ludwig of Oettingen-Wallerstein]] served as a Bavarian minister in the 1830s and 1840s, and the family still owns [[e:harburg-swabia|Harburg]] castle.

pratiharas-of-mandavyapura.t: An early Pratihara family of Marwar in Rajasthan, ruling from Mandore and known from the inscriptions of its later kings.
pratiharas-of-mandavyapura.o: According to inscriptions set up by its kings Bauka in 837 and Kakkuka in 861, the dynasty was founded by Harichandra, a [[e:brahmins|Brahmin]] who had one Brahmin and one [[e:kshatriya|Kshatriya]] wife; the sons of the latter founded the ruling line. They established themselves at [[e:mandore|Mandavyapura]], modern Mandore near [[e:jodhpur|Jodhpur]], in the 6th century.
pratiharas-of-mandavyapura.r: The family ruled a small kingdom in [[s:jodhpur-state|Marwar]], at first independently and later as feudatories of the more powerful [[s:gurjara-pratihara|Gurjara-Pratihara]] of [[e:kannauj|Kannauj]]. Kakkuka's Ghatiyala inscriptions describe him founding markets and settling merchants, and praise his skill in arms and [[e:sanskrit|Sanskrit]] learning. The family's history illustrates the emergence of the [[e:rajputs|Rajput]] clans.
pratiharas-of-mandavyapura.e: The [[e:mandore|Mandore]] Pratiharas disappear from the record after the late 9th century. Mandore later passed to other [[e:rajputs|Rajput]] clans, and around 1400 the [[e:rathore|Rathores]] made it their capital before founding [[e:jodhpur|Jodhpur]] in 1459.

protectorate-of-peru.t: The provisional government of San Martín in Lima, which declared Peru's independence while royalist armies still held the highlands.
protectorate-of-peru.o: [[e:jose-de-san-martin|José de San Martín]] landed his [[e:liberating-expedition-of-peru|Liberating Expedition]], transported from [[s:republic-of-chile|Chile]] by [[e:thomas-cochrane-10th-earl-of-dundonald|Lord Cochrane]], on the Peruvian coast in 1820. When the [[e:viceroy-of-india|viceroy]] abandoned [[e:lima|Lima]] in July 1821, San Martín entered the city, proclaimed independence on 28 July and on 3 August took the title of Protector of [[e:peru|Peru]].
protectorate-of-peru.r: [[e:jose-de-san-martin|San Martín]] governed with [[e:bernardo-de-monteagudo|Bernardo de Monteagudo]] as his chief minister. [[s:the-protectorate|The Protectorate]] abolished the Indian tribute and forced labour, declared that children of enslaved mothers would be born free, founded the National Library and created the [[e:order-of-the-sun-of-peru|Order of the Sun]]. Monteagudo's harsh treatment of Spaniards made him unpopular. Royalist forces still held [[e:cusco|Cusco]] and the highlands, and San Martín favoured a [[e:constitutional-monarchy|constitutional monarchy]] for [[e:peru|Peru]].
protectorate-of-peru.e: After his meeting with [[e:simon-bolivar|Bolívar]] at [[e:guayaquil|Guayaquil]] in July 1822, [[e:jose-de-san-martin|San Martín]] resigned before the first Peruvian Congress in September 1822 and left [[e:peru|Peru]]. Power passed to a governing junta of the [[s:republic-of-peru|Republic of Peru]].

principality-of-galilee.t: The largest lordship of the Kingdom of Jerusalem, centred on Tiberias, whose siege in 1187 drew the Frankish army to defeat at Hattin.
principality-of-galilee.o: [[e:tancred-prince-of-galilee|Tancred]], the Norman crusader, took [[e:tiberias|Tiberias]] and the surrounding region soon after the capture of [[e:jerusalem|Jerusalem]] in 1099 and styled himself Prince of [[e:galilee|Galilee]]. When he left for [[s:principality-of-antioch|Antioch]] in 1101, Baldwin I gave the fief to [[e:hugh-of-saint-omer|Hugh of Saint-Omer]].
principality-of-galilee.r: [[e:galilee|Galilee]] owed the king a large contingent of knights and had its own [[e:vassal|vassals]], including the [[s:lordship-of-toron|Lordship of Toron]], whose castle [[e:hugh-of-saint-omer|Hugh of Saint-Omer]] built. Its lords collected revenue from fertile farmland around the [[e:sea-of-galilee|Sea of Galilee]] and faced [[e:damascus|Damascus]] across the [[s:hashemite-kingdom-of-jordan|Jordan]]. In the 12th century it passed to the [[e:bure|Bures]] family, and through [[e:eschiva-of-bures|Eschiva of Bures]] to her husband [[e:raymond-iii-of-tripoli|Raymond III of Tripoli]].
principality-of-galilee.e: In July 1187 [[e:saladin|Saladin]] besieged [[e:eschiva-of-bures|Eschiva]] in [[e:tiberias|Tiberias]]. The royal army marched to relieve her and was destroyed at [[e:battle-of-hattin|Hattin]], and [[e:galilee|Galilee]] fell to Saladin. The title survived among exiled Frankish nobles, but the principality was never restored.

prince-bishopric-of-trent.t: An Alpine prince-bishopric on the road from Germany to Italy, best known as the host city of the Council of Trent.
prince-bishopric-of-trent.o: [[e:trento|Trent]] was a bishopric from the 4th century. In 1027 [[e:conrad-ii-holy-roman-emperor|Emperor Conrad II]] granted [[e:bishop|Bishop]] Udalrich II the counties of Trento, [[e:bolzano|Bolzano]] and [[e:vinschgau|Vinschgau]], to secure the [[e:adige|Adige]] valley route between [[e:germany|Germany]] and [[e:italy|Italy]]. The bishops became princes of the Empire.
prince-bishopric-of-trent.r: The [[e:bishop|bishops]] faced their own advocates, the counts of [[e:tyrol|Tyrol]], who after 1363 passed to the [[e:habsburg-dynasty|Habsburgs]] and dominated the bishopric through treaties. Bishop [[e:friedrich-von-wangen|Frederick Vanga]] issued an important mining code in 1208. Bishop [[e:bernardo-clesio|Bernardo Clesio]] rebuilt the city in [[e:renaissance|Renaissance]] style, and under his successor [[e:cristoforo-madruzzo|Cristoforo Madruzzo]] the [[e:council-of-trent|Council of Trent]] met there between 1545 and 1563, launching the [[e:counter-reformation|Catholic Reformation]].
prince-bishopric-of-trent.e: The prince-bishopric was secularised in 1803 and annexed to [[e:austria|Austria]], passing to [[e:bavaria|Bavaria]] and the [[s:kingdom-of-italy-napoleonic|Napoleonic Kingdom of Italy]] before returning to Austria in 1815. After 1918 [[e:trentino|Trentino]] became part of [[e:italy|Italy]], and the see remains as the [[e:archdiocese-of-trento|Archdiocese of Trento]].

prince-bishopric-of-basel.t: A prince-bishopric on the upper Rhine whose bishops, driven out of Protestant Basel, ruled the Jura from Porrentruy until 1792.
prince-bishopric-of-basel.o: [[s:canton-of-basel|Basel]] had been a bishopric since the 7th century. In 999 [[e:rudolf-iii-of-burgundy|King Rudolf III of Burgundy]] gave the [[e:bishop|bishop]] the abbey of Moutier-Grandval in the [[e:jura-mountains|Jura]], the basis of later territory. When [[s:duchy-of-burgundy|Burgundy]] fell to the Empire in 1032, Basel's bishops became imperial princes, later gaining further lands in the Jura and [[e:alsace|Alsace]].
prince-bishopric-of-basel.r: The [[e:bishop|bishops]] ruled the city of [[s:canton-of-basel|Basel]] until its citizens won self-government, and Basel joined the [[s:old-swiss-confederacy|Swiss Confederacy]] in 1501. The [[e:council-of-basel|Council of Basel]] met there from 1431, and the university was founded in 1460. With the [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]] in 1529 the bishop moved to [[e:porrentruy|Porrentruy]], ruling a mainly French-speaking territory.
prince-bishopric-of-basel.e: French revolutionary troops occupied the territory in 1792, creating the short-lived [[s:rauracian-republic|Rauracian Republic]], which [[e:france|France]] annexed in 1793. The prince-bishopric was formally dissolved in 1803. In 1815 most of its lands were given to Bern, and the [[e:guangzhou|Canton]] of [[e:jura-mountains|Jura]] was created from part of them in 1979.

pomesanians.t: Prussian people on the east bank of the lower Vistula, the first to be conquered by the Teutonic Knights in the 1230s.
pomesanians.o: The Pomesanians lived in Pomesania, between the [[e:vistula|Vistula]], the [[e:nogat|Nogat]] and the [[e:drweca|Drwęca]], in what is now northern [[e:poland|Poland]]. Like other Prussian groups they emerged as a distinct territory in the [[e:viking-age|Viking Age]], with farming villages and hillforts and contacts with [[s:duchy-of-pomerania|Pomerania]] and [[e:masovia|Masovia]].
pomesanians.r: They were organised in districts led by nobles rather than a single ruler, and kept the Prussian pagan cults. Their nearness to Christian [[e:poland|Poland]] and [[s:duchy-of-pomerania|Pomerania]] exposed them to missions and raids from the early 13th century.
pomesanians.e: The [[e:teutonic-order|Teutonic Order]], invited by [[e:konrad-i-of-masovia|Konrad of Masovia]], attacked Pomesania first, founding [[e:kwidzyn|Kwidzyn]] (Marienwerder) in 1233 and winning at the Sirgune river in 1234; by 1236 the land was subdued. The Pomesanians joined the [[e:great-prussian-uprising|Great Prussian Uprising]] in 1260 but were reconquered, and their land became the [[s:bishopric-of-pomesania|Bishopric of Pomesania]] and Order territory.

potchefstroom-republic.t: The first Boer republic north of the Vaal, founded at Potchefstroom by Andries Potgieter and forerunner of the Transvaal.
potchefstroom-republic.o: After driving the [[e:ndebele-kingdom|Ndebele]] north, [[e:voortrekkers|Voortrekkers]] led by [[e:andries-hendrik-potgieter|Andries Hendrik Potgieter]] founded [[e:potchefstroom|Potchefstroom]] in 1838, the first European town north of the [[e:vaal-river|Vaal River]]. A Volksraad was formed and from 1843 the community was linked with [[s:republic-of-winburg|Winburg]] across the river.
potchefstroom-republic.r: The republic was a loose community of [[e:cattle|cattle]] farmers governed by a [[e:volksraad|Volksraad]] and commandants, prone to rivalry between leaders. [[e:andries-hendrik-potgieter|Potgieter]], wary of British reach, moved north to found [[e:ohrigstad|Andries-Ohrigstad]] in 1845, while [[e:andries-pretorius|Andries Pretorius]] gained influence in the west. Labour came partly from captured children, called inboekelinge.
potchefstroom-republic.e: In the [[e:sand-river-convention|Sand River Convention]] of 1852 [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] recognised the independence of the [[e:boers|Boers]] north of the [[e:vaal-river|Vaal]], and the communities were gradually merged into the [[s:south-african-republic|South African Republic]].

principality-of-ferghana.t: The early medieval kingdom of the Ferghana valley, a contested prize between Tang China, the Turks and the Arab caliphate.
principality-of-ferghana.o: After the ancient [[s:kingdom-of-dayuan|Kingdom of Dayuan]], the [[e:fergana-valley|Ferghana]] valley was ruled by local dynasties whose kings took the title ikhshid. By the 6th century the principality was within the sphere of the [[s:western-turkic-khaganate|Western Turkic Khaganate]], and in the 7th century it was nominally attached to the [[s:later-tang|Tang]] [[e:protectorate|protectorate]] system.
principality-of-ferghana.r: [[e:fergana-valley|Ferghana]] was a fertile valley of farming towns and pastures, famed for horses. Its rulers alternated between Turkic and local Sogdian-speaking houses, and at times the valley was split between rival kings. Chinese records list embassies to the [[s:later-tang|Tang]] court, and Arab armies under [[e:qutayba-ibn-muslim|Qutayba ibn Muslim]] campaigned there from 713.
principality-of-ferghana.e: [[e:fergana-valley|Ferghana]] was contested between the [[e:umayyad-caliphate|Umayyads]], the [[s:turgesh-khaganate|Turgesh Khaganate]] and [[e:tang-dynasty|Tang China]] until after the [[e:battle-of-talas|Battle of Talas]]. Its ikhshids accepted Abbasid suzerainty, and around 820 the valley passed under the [[s:samanid-empire|Samanid Empire]], ending its independence.

principality-of-pontecorvo.t: A tiny papal enclave in southern Lazio that Napoleon granted to Marshal Bernadotte, the future king of Sweden.
principality-of-pontecorvo.o: Pontecorvo, a small town on the Liri river surrounded by the [[s:kingdom-of-naples|Kingdom of Naples]], belonged to the [[s:papal-states|Papal States]]. In 1806 [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]] seized it and made [[e:charles-xiv-john|Marshal Jean-Baptiste Bernadotte]] its sovereign prince.
principality-of-pontecorvo.r: [[e:charles-xiv-john|Bernadotte]] never visited and ruled through local administrators who applied French laws. In 1810 he was elected crown prince of [[e:sweden|Sweden]] and gave up the principality, which [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]] in 1812 granted to [[e:lucien-murat|Lucien Murat]], son of King [[e:joachim-murat|Joachim Murat]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-naples|Kingdom of Naples]] (1806–1815).
principality-of-pontecorvo.e: After [[e:napoleon|Napoleon's]] fall, the [[e:congress-of-vienna|Congress of Vienna]] returned Pontecorvo to the [[s:papal-states|Papal States]] in 1815. [[e:charles-xiv-john|Bernadotte]] became King Charles XIV John of [[e:sweden|Sweden]] in 1818.

prince-provostry-of-berchtesgaden.t: An Alpine church principality of Augustinian canons whose salt mine made it a coveted little state between Bavaria and Salzburg.
prince-provostry-of-berchtesgaden.o: Augustinian canons settled at [[e:berchtesgaden|Berchtesgaden]] early in the 12th century, endowed by the family of the counts of Sulzbach. [[e:frederick-barbarossa|Frederick Barbarossa]] granted the provost rights over forests and salt in 1156, and in 1380 [[e:wenceslaus-iv-of-bohemia|King Wenceslaus]] confirmed the provostry's direct dependence on the empire; from 1559 its provosts were counted among the princes.
prince-provostry-of-berchtesgaden.r: The provost, elected by the canons, ruled a small mountain land enclosed by [[e:salzburg|Salzburg]] and [[e:bavaria|Bavaria]]. Its wealth came from salt, mined in the [[e:berchtesgaden|Berchtesgaden]] salt mine from 1517, which caused long disputes with the [[s:prince-archbishopric-of-salzburg|Prince-Archbishopric of Salzburg]] and Bavaria over the trade. Woodcarving became a famous local craft. For long periods [[e:house-of-wittelsbach|Wittelsbach]] princes held the provostry alongside other sees.
prince-provostry-of-berchtesgaden.e: Secularised in 1803, [[e:berchtesgaden|Berchtesgaden]] went to the [[s:electorate-of-salzburg|Electorate of Salzburg]], then to [[e:austria|Austria]] in 1805 and to the [[s:kingdom-of-bavaria|Kingdom of Bavaria]] in 1810. In the 20th century [[e:berghof|Hitler's Berghof]] stood on the [[e:obersalzberg|Obersalzberg]] above the town.

principality-of-panjikent.t: A small Sogdian town-state whose excavated houses and murals give the most vivid picture of everyday life on the early medieval Silk Road.
principality-of-panjikent.o: [[e:panjikent|Panjikent]], on the Zarafshan River east of [[e:samarkand|Samarkand]], was founded in the 5th century and grew into a walled town of merchants and landowners. It was one of several principalities of [[s:principality-of-samarkand|Sogdiana]], often under the influence of the Principality of Samarkand, and within the orbit of the [[s:western-turkic-khaganate|Western Turkic Khaganate]].
principality-of-panjikent.r: Excavations since 1946 have revealed a citadel, two temples and streets of two-storey houses whose reception halls were covered in wall paintings of epics, gods and banquets, including scenes from the [[e:rostam|Rustam]] cycle. Its ruler [[e:divashtich|Divashtich]] styled himself king of [[s:principality-of-samarkand|Sogdiana]] and ikhshid of [[e:samarkand|Samarkand]]. Its archive of documents on leather and wood was found at [[e:mount-mugh|Mount Mugh]].
principality-of-panjikent.e: [[e:divashtich|Divashtich]] resisted the [[e:umayyad-caliphate|Umayyad]] advance, was captured at [[e:mount-mugh|Mount Mugh]] in 722 and crucified. The town declined and was abandoned in the late 8th century, which preserved its ruins for archaeologists.

philippolis-griqua-state.t: Adam Kok's Griqua captaincy north of the Orange River, squeezed out by Boer settlers until its people trekked to Griqualand East.
philippolis-griqua-state.o: [[e:philippolis|Philippolis]] began in 1823 as a [[e:london-missionary-society|London Missionary Society]] station for [[e:san-people|San]]. In 1826 [[e:adam-kok-ii|Adam Kok II]] and his [[e:griqua|Griqua]] followers, who had split from the community at [[e:griquatown|Griquatown]], settled there and made it the centre of their own captaincy.
philippolis-griqua-state.r: The Kok family ruled with a council and a mission-backed legal order, and the [[e:griqua|Griqua]] farmed sheep and [[e:cattle|cattle]]. From the 1830s [[e:boers|Boer]] trekboers leased and bought Griqua farms. [[e:adam-kok-iii|Adam Kok III]], kaptein from 1837, sought British support, signing a treaty with the Cape in 1843, but under the [[s:orange-river-sovereignty|Orange River Sovereignty]] and then the [[s:orange-free-state|Orange Free State]] the Griqua steadily lost land.
philippolis-griqua-state.e: In 1861 [[e:adam-kok-iii|Adam Kok III]] sold the remaining land to the [[s:orange-free-state|Orange Free State]] and led about 2,000 people across the [[e:drakensberg|Drakensberg]] to [[s:griqualand-east|Nomansland]], where they founded Griqualand East.

principality-of-aschaffenburg.t: Mainz territory on the Main formed into a principality for the archchancellor Dalberg during the Napoleonic reorganisation.
principality-of-aschaffenburg.o: [[e:aschaffenburg|Aschaffenburg]] had been the second residence of the archbishops of [[e:mainz|Mainz]] for centuries, with the large [[e:renaissance|Renaissance]] [[e:johannisburg-palace|Johannisburg]] palace. When the [[s:electorate-of-mainz|Electorate of Mainz]] lost its left-bank lands, the [[e:reichsdeputationshauptschluss|Imperial Recess of 1803]] formed its remaining territories on the Main and [[e:spessart|Spessart]] into the Principality of Aschaffenburg for [[e:karl-theodor-von-dalberg|Karl Theodor von Dalberg]].
principality-of-aschaffenburg.r: [[e:aschaffenburg|Aschaffenburg]] was the core of the [[s:archchancellors-electorate|Archchancellor's Electorate]] and [[e:karl-theodor-von-dalberg|Dalberg]]'s main residence. It was Catholic and rural, with forestry in the [[e:spessart|Spessart]]. Dalberg promoted education, founding a school of forestry and maintaining the [[e:mainz|Mainz]] university's remnants as a Karlsuniversität in Aschaffenburg.
principality-of-aschaffenburg.e: In 1810 the principality became a [[e:departement|department]] of the [[s:grand-duchy-of-frankfurt|Grand Duchy of Frankfurt]]. After [[e:napoleon|Napoleon's]] fall it was given to the [[s:kingdom-of-bavaria|Kingdom of Bavaria]] in 1814, to which it still belongs.

cr.a: Sodacan, wheel from File:Coat of Arms of Ernest August, Duke of Brunswick-Lüneburg (1661-1692).svg

principality-of-pereslavl-zalessky.t: An appanage principality on Lake Pleshcheyevo, birthplace of Alexander Nevsky, bequeathed to Moscow by its last prince in 1302.
principality-of-pereslavl-zalessky.o: [[e:yuri-dolgoruky|Yuri Dolgoruky]] founded [[e:pereslavl-zalessky|Pereslavl-Zalessky]], Pereslavl beyond the forests, in 1152 on the shore of [[e:lake-pleshcheyevo|Lake Pleshcheyevo]], naming it after [[e:pereiaslav|Pereyaslavl]] in the south. He began the [[e:transfiguration-cathedral-pereslavl-zalessky|Transfiguration Cathedral]] there, one of the oldest white-stone churches in [[e:russia|Russia]]. After the death of [[e:andrei-bogolyubsky|Andrei Bogolyubsky]] it became a separate [[e:appanage|appanage]] of the [[s:vladimir-suzdal|Vladimir-Suzdal]] lands.
principality-of-pereslavl-zalessky.r: [[e:pereslavl-zalessky|Pereslavl]] was a fortified town with earthen ramparts that guarded the route from Vladimir to the north. [[e:yaroslav-ii-of-vladimir|Yaroslav Vsevolodovich]] held it from 1212, and his son [[e:alexander-nevsky|Alexander Nevsky]] was born there around 1220. Its princes were close kin of the grand princes of Vladimir, and the town played a part in their many succession struggles.
principality-of-pereslavl-zalessky.e: The last prince, [[e:ivan-dmitrievich-of-pereslavl|Ivan Dmitrievich]], a grandson of [[e:alexander-nevsky|Alexander Nevsky]], died childless in 1302 and left [[e:pereslavl-zalessky|Pereslavl]] to his uncle Daniel of [[e:moscow|Moscow]]. This bequest was an early step in the growth of the [[s:grand-duchy-of-moscow|Grand Duchy of Moscow]]. [[e:peter-the-great|Peter the Great]] later built his first toy fleet on the lake.

principality-of-iberia.t: The rule of presiding princes over eastern Georgia between the fall of its ancient monarchy and the rise of the Bagratids, a time of Arab conquest and church building.
principality-of-iberia.o: After the [[s:sasanian-empire|Sasanian Empire]] abolished the [[s:kingdom-of-iberia|Kingdom of Iberia]] in 580, the Georgian nobility was left without a king. In 588, with Byzantine backing, [[e:guaram-i-of-iberia|Guaram I]] of the [[e:guaramid-dynasty|Guaramid]] family was recognised as presiding prince, holding the Byzantine title of kouropalates, and the office passed among leading families for three centuries.
principality-of-iberia.r: The presiding princes, or erismtavari, were first among equals over regional nobles rather than true monarchs, balancing between the [[s:byzantine-empire|Byzantine Empire]], [[e:persia|Persia]] and later the [[e:caliphate|caliphate]]. [[e:stephen-i-of-iberia|Stephen I]] built the Jvari church above [[e:mtskheta|Mtskheta]], a model for Georgian architecture. Arab armies took [[e:tbilisi|Tbilisi]] in 645, and by 736 the city became the seat of the [[s:emirate-of-tbilisi|Emirate of Tbilisi]], pushing princely power west and south.
principality-of-iberia.e: The [[e:bagrationi-dynasty|Bagratid]] prince [[e:ashot-i-of-iberia|Ashot I]] moved the family's base to [[s:kingdom-of-the-iberians|Tao-Klarjeti]] in the early 9th century. In 888 his descendant [[e:adarnase-iv-of-iberia|Adarnase IV]] revived the royal title, creating the Kingdom of the [[e:iberians|Iberians]].

portuguese-morocco.t: Portugal's chain of fortified enclaves on the Moroccan coast, from Ceuta to Mazagan, the first European overseas expansion of the Age of Discovery.
portuguese-morocco.o: The [[s:kingdom-of-portugal|Kingdom of Portugal]] captured [[e:ceuta|Ceuta]] from the [[s:marinid-sultanate|Marinid Sultanate]] in 1415, launching its overseas expansion. Afonso V added [[e:ksar-es-seghir|Ksar es-Seghir]] in 1458 and [[e:asilah|Arzila]] and [[e:tangier|Tangier]] in 1471. Under [[e:manuel-i-of-portugal|Manuel I]] the Portuguese built or seized Atlantic posts at [[e:agadir|Agadir]], [[e:safi-morocco|Safi]], [[e:azemmour|Azemmour]] and [[e:el-jadida|Mazagan]] between 1505 and 1514.
portuguese-morocco.r: The enclaves were garrison towns governed by captains, supplied by sea and living from raids, tribute from nearby tribes and trade in grain, horses and textiles, partly for the [[e:guinea|Guinea]] trade. Portuguese kings styled themselves lords of the [[e:algarve|Algarve]] beyond the sea in [[e:africa|Africa]]. Life was precarious, with constant warfare against Wattasid and Saadi forces.
portuguese-morocco.e: After the [[s:saadi-sultanate|Saadi Sultanate]] took [[e:agadir|Agadir]] in 1541, Portugal abandoned [[e:safi-morocco|Safi]], [[e:azemmour|Azemmour]] and other posts. King [[e:sebastian-of-portugal|Sebastian]]'s disastrous invasion ended at [[e:battle-of-alcacer-quibir|Alcácer Quibir]] in 1578. [[e:ceuta|Ceuta]] passed to [[e:spain|Spain]] after 1640, [[e:tangier|Tangier]] went to [[e:england|England]] in 1661, and [[e:el-jadida|Mazagan]] was evacuated in 1769.

parsua.t: A Zagros land of many small chiefdoms first named in 843 BCE, whose name may be the earliest mention of the Persians.
parsua.o: Parsua (Parsuash) is first recorded in 843 BCE in the annals of [[e:shalmaneser-iii|Shalmaneser III]] of the [[s:assyrian-empire|Assyrian Empire]], who in 835 BCE received tribute from 27 kings of Parsua. It lay in the central [[e:zagros-mountains|Zagros]], probably near the upper [[e:diyala-river|Diyala]] and [[e:kermanshah|Kermanshah]] region.
parsua.r: Parsua was not a unified kingdom but a cluster of chiefdoms under local lords who paid horses and livestock to [[e:assyrian-empire|Assyria]]. The similarity of the name to Parsa, the [[e:persians|Persians]], has led many historians to connect Parsua with early Iranian groups who later settled in [[e:fars|Fars]], but whether the same people moved south, or the name simply meant 'borderland', is debated.
parsua.e: Tiglath-Pileser III turned Parsua into an Assyrian province in 744 BCE, and it remained in the [[s:assyrian-empire|Assyrian Empire]] until the rise of the [[s:median-empire|Median Empire]]. The [[e:persians|Persians]] of [[e:fars|Fars]], rulers of the later [[s:kingdom-of-anshan|Kingdom of Anshan]], may preserve its name.

principality-of-belz.t: A small Ruthenian principality on the Polish border, passed between Volhynia, Lithuania and Masovia before joining the Polish Crown.
principality-of-belz.o: [[e:belz|Belz]], on a tributary of the [[e:western-bug|Bug]], was one of the Cherven towns contested between [[e:poland|Poland]] and Rus'. It became the seat of an [[e:appanage|appanage]] of the Volhynian princes in the later 12th century, when [[e:vsevolod-mstislavich-of-belz|Vsevolod Mstislavich]], a brother of [[e:roman-the-great|Roman Mstislavich]], ruled there.
principality-of-belz.r: It was a border land of fortified towns and farmland, part of the [[s:kingdom-of-galicia-volhynia|Kingdom of Galicia-Volhynia]] in the 13th century. After that state collapsed in the 1340s [[e:belz|Belz]] was contested by [[e:poland|Poland]] and the [[s:grand-duchy-of-lithuania|Grand Duchy of Lithuania]], then from 1388 held as a fief by the dukes of [[e:masovia|Masovia]], beginning with [[e:siemowit-iv-of-masovia|Siemowit IV]].
principality-of-belz.e: When the Masovian line of [[e:belz|Belz]] died out in 1462, [[e:casimir-iv-jagiellon|King Casimir IV]] incorporated it into the [[s:kingdom-of-poland-1025-1385|Kingdom of Poland]] (1385-1569) as the [[e:belz-voivodeship|Belz Voivodeship]]. The town later became famous as the seat of the [[e:belz-hasidic-dynasty|Belz Hasidic dynasty]].

principality-of-khuttal.t: A mountain principality north of the Amu Darya, famed for its horses, whose kings resisted the Arab conquest for decades.
principality-of-khuttal.o: Khuttal lay between the [[e:vakhsh-river|Vakhsh]] and [[e:panj-river|Panj]] rivers in what is now southern [[s:tajikistan|Tajikistan]]. It emerged in the 6th and 7th centuries as one of the principalities of [[e:tokharistan|Tokharistan]] under Hephthalite and then Turkic overlordship, ruled by kings with the title Khuttalan-shah, and its capital is identified with [[e:hulbuk|Hulbuk]].
principality-of-khuttal.r: Khuttal was a land of valleys and mountain pastures known for horses and for its warrior aristocracy. Its rulers bore Turkic or Hephthalite titles and maintained ties with the [[s:yabghus-of-tokharistan|Yabghus of Tokharistan]], the [[s:turgesh-khaganate|Turgesh Khaganate]] and [[e:tang-dynasty|Tang China]]. The king al-Sabal fought the [[e:umayyad-caliphate|Umayyad]] governors in the 720s and 730s.
principality-of-khuttal.e: Khuttal accepted Abbasid suzerainty after the mid-8th century, and its local dynasty continued as [[e:vassal|vassals]] for a time. It later became a province of the [[s:samanid-empire|Samanid Empire]], and the palace of [[e:hulbuk|Hulbuk]] flourished under its Islamic-era governors.

post-angkorian-cambodia.t: The Khmer kingdom between the abandonment of Angkor and French protection, ruled from Longvek and Oudong and squeezed between Siam and Vietnam.
post-angkorian-cambodia.o: After [[e:ayutthaya-kingdom|Ayutthaya's]] sack of [[e:angkor|Angkor]] around 1431, the [[e:khmer-empire|Khmer]] court under [[e:ponhea-yat|Ponhea Yat]] moved south toward the [[e:mekong-river|Mekong]] and the [[e:tonle-sap|Tonle Sap]] confluence, eventually settling at [[e:phnom-penh|Phnom Penh]]. Under [[e:ang-chan-i|Ang Chan I]] in the 16th century the capital moved to Longvek, and later to Oudong.
post-angkorian-cambodia.r: The kingdom drew wealth from river trade at the [[e:chaktomuk|Quatre Bras]], with Chinese, Malay, Japanese, Portuguese and Spanish merchants present. [[e:theravada-buddhism|Theravada Buddhism]] replaced the older [[e:hinduism|Hindu]] and [[e:mahayana-buddhism|Mahayana]] cults, and the [[e:reamker|Reamker]] version of the [[e:ramayana|Ramayana]] flourished. Royal factions sought Siamese or Vietnamese backing, and Spanish adventurers intervened in the 1590s. [[s:ayutthaya-kingdom|Ayutthaya]] captured Longvek in 1594.
post-angkorian-cambodia.e: From the 17th century the [[s:nguyen-lords|Nguyen lords]] gained the [[e:mekong-river|Mekong]] delta, and in the 1830s [[s:socialist-republic-of-vietnam|Vietnam]] occupied [[s:kingdom-of-cambodia-1953-1970|Cambodia]] until a Siamese-Vietnamese settlement of the mid-1840s installed [[e:ang-duong|Ang Duong]]. His son Norodom accepted the [[s:french-protectorate-of-cambodia|French protectorate of Cambodia]] in 1863.

pechenegs.t: Turkic nomads who dominated the Black Sea steppe for two centuries, killed Sviatoslav of Kiev and were crushed by Byzantium in 1091.
pechenegs.o: The Pechenegs lived between the [[e:volga|Volga]] and the [[e:ural-river|Ural]] until the [[e:oghuz-turks|Oghuz]] and [[e:khazar-khaganate|Khazars]] drove them west around 890. Allied with the [[s:first-bulgarian-empire|First Bulgarian Empire]], they expelled the [[e:magyars|Magyars]] from their lands between the [[e:dnieper|Dnieper]] and the [[e:danube|Danube]] around 895 and took over the steppe north of the [[e:black-sea|Black Sea]].
pechenegs.r: [[e:constantine-vii|Constantine VII]] describes eight tribes, each with its own chief, grouped into two wings either side of the [[e:dnieper|Dnieper]]. [[s:byzantium|Byzantium]] paid them to hold back the Rus' and the [[e:bulgarians|Bulgarians]], and they controlled the Dnieper rapids, where in 972 their chief [[e:kurya|Kurya]] killed [[e:sviatoslav-i-of-kiev|Sviatoslav I]] and made his skull into a drinking cup.
pechenegs.e: Defeated outside [[e:kyiv|Kiev]] by [[e:yaroslav-the-wise|Yaroslav the Wise]] in 1036, and pressed by the [[e:oghuz-turks|Oghuz]] and [[e:cumans|Cumans]], many Pechenegs moved into the [[e:balkans|Balkans]]. In 1091 [[e:alexios-i-komnenos|Alexios I Komnenos]] and his Cuman allies annihilated them at [[e:battle-of-levounion|Levounion]], and a final defeat in 1122 ended them as a people. Survivors settled in [[e:hungary|Hungary]] and [[s:byzantium|Byzantium]].

province-of-massachusetts-bay.t: The royal province that united Massachusetts, Plymouth and Maine in 1691, and whose capital Boston became the flashpoint of the American Revolution.
province-of-massachusetts-bay.o: After the fall of the [[s:dominion-of-new-england|Dominion of New England]], [[e:increase-mather|Increase Mather]] negotiated a new charter from [[e:william-iii-of-england|William III]] and [[e:mary-ii-of-england|Mary II]] in 1691. It merged the [[s:massachusetts-bay-colony|Massachusetts Bay Colony]], [[s:plymouth-colony|Plymouth Colony]], [[s:county-of-maine|Maine]], [[e:marthas-vineyard|Martha's Vineyard]] and [[e:nantucket|Nantucket]] into one province. Governor [[e:william-phips|William Phips]] arrived in 1692, just as the [[e:salem-witch-trials|Salem witch trials]] began.
province-of-massachusetts-bay.r: The Crown now appointed the governor, but the elected assembly chose the council and controlled salaries, leading to constant friction. Property, not church membership, now qualified voters. [[e:boston|Boston]] thrived on shipbuilding, fishing and [[e:atlantic-slave-trade|Atlantic trade]]. Massachusetts led [[e:new-england|New England's]] wars against [[s:new-france|New France]], and in 1745 forces raised by governor [[e:william-shirley|William Shirley]] captured [[e:louisbourg|Louisbourg]] on [[s:ile-royale|Ile Royale]]. [[e:thomas-hutchinson-governor|Thomas Hutchinson]], a native-born merchant, became the province's last civilian governor.
province-of-massachusetts-bay.e: Resistance to British taxes grew through the [[e:stamp-act-1765|Stamp Act]] riots, the [[e:boston|Boston]] Massacre of 1770 and the [[e:boston-tea-party|Boston Tea Party]] of 1773. After the [[e:massachusetts-government-act|Massachusetts Government Act]] of 1774, General [[e:thomas-gage|Thomas Gage]] ruled, and fighting at [[e:battles-of-lexington-and-concord|Lexington and Concord]] in 1775 began the war that made Massachusetts a state of the [[s:united-states|United States]].

parisii-britain.t: East Yorkshire people known for the Arras culture of square-barrow and chariot burials, sharing their name with the Parisii of Gaul.
parisii-britain.o: The [[s:parisii|Parisii]] are identified with the [[e:arras-culture|Arras culture]] of the [[e:yorkshire-wolds|Yorkshire Wolds]], which from about the 4th century BCE buried its dead under small square barrows, sometimes with dismantled two-wheeled vehicles, as at [[e:wetwang|Wetwang]] and [[e:garton-slack|Garton Slack]]. The likeness of these burials to rites in northern [[e:gaul|Gaul]], and the shared name with the Parisii of the [[e:seine|Seine]], has fuelled long debate over migration or contact.
parisii-britain.r: Society was based on mixed farming on the chalk [[e:yorkshire-wolds|Wolds]] and in the [[e:vale-of-pickering|Vale of Pickering]], with large cemeteries of thousands of barrows. [[e:chariot|Chariot]] burials of men and women, with harness fittings, mirrors and brooches, point to an elite who displayed status through horses and fine metalwork. No coinage is attributed to them and no rulers are named.
parisii-britain.e: The area came under Roman control during the campaigns of [[e:quintus-petillius-cerialis|Petillius Cerialis]] against the [[s:brigantes|Brigantes]] from 71. Ptolemy later listed [[e:petuaria|Petuaria]] as their town, and an inscription from [[e:brough-east-riding-of-yorkshire|Brough-on-Humber]] names an aedile of the vicus of Petuaria; the Parisi probably formed a small civitas of [[s:roman-britain|Roman Britain]].

principality-of-castiglione.t: A small Lombard state of a Gonzaga branch, birthplace of Saint Aloysius Gonzaga, who gave up its succession to become a Jesuit.
principality-of-castiglione.o: [[e:castiglione-delle-stiviere|Castiglione delle Stiviere]], south of [[e:lake-garda|Lake Garda]], belonged to a cadet branch of the [[e:house-of-gonzaga|Gonzaga]] of [[s:duchy-of-mantua|Mantua]]. [[e:ferrante-gonzaga-marquis-of-castiglione|Ferrante Gonzaga]], its lord, was made marquis by the emperor in 1579, and the state became a principality under his son Francesco in 1612.
principality-of-castiglione.r: The rulers governed a few small towns and farmland as an imperial fief. [[e:ferrante-gonzaga-marquis-of-castiglione|Ferrante]]'s eldest son [[e:aloysius-gonzaga|Aloysius]], born in 1568, renounced his rights to join the [[e:jesuits|Jesuits]] and died in 1591 nursing plague victims in [[e:rome|Rome]]; he was canonised in 1726 and the town became a pilgrimage centre. His brother Rodolfo was murdered in 1593 by his own subjects. Later princes faced revolts and imperial intervention.
principality-of-castiglione.e: Prince Ferdinando II was deposed after local unrest, and Austrian troops occupied the state in 1691. After long disputes over compensation for the family, the principality was finally incorporated into Austrian [[e:lombardy|Lombardy]] in 1773.

principality-of-reuss-gera.t: The Younger Line of the house of Reuss in eastern Thuringia, whose princes all bore the name Heinrich, ruling until 1918.
principality-of-reuss-gera.o: The [[e:house-of-reuss|Reuss]] lords descended from the [[e:vogt|Vögte]] (advocates) of [[e:weida|Weida]], Gera and [[e:plauen|Plauen]], who ruled the [[s:lordship-of-plauen|Vogtland]] from the 12th century. In 1564 their lands were divided into Elder, Middle and Younger Lines; the Younger Line, centred on Gera and [[e:schleiz|Schleiz]], later absorbed the Middle Line's lands.
principality-of-reuss-gera.r: Every male member of the family was named Heinrich and given a number, a custom said to honour [[e:henry-vi-holy-roman-emperor|Emperor Henry VI]]. The Younger Line's lands were repeatedly divided, producing the [[s:principality-of-reuss-schleiz|Principality of Reuss-Schleiz]], the [[s:principality-of-reuss-lobenstein|Principality of Reuss-Lobenstein]] and the [[s:principality-of-reuss-ebersdorf|Principality of Reuss-Ebersdorf]]. Gera grew into a centre of woollen textiles. The house was Lutheran and gained princely rank in 1806.
principality-of-reuss-gera.e: The branches of the Younger Line were reunited in 1848 as a single principality ruled from Gera, which joined the [[s:german-empire|German Empire]] in 1871. Its last prince abdicated in 1918, and in 1919 it merged with the Elder Line into the [[s:peoples-state-of-reuss|People's State of Reuss]], which joined [[e:thuringia|Thuringia]] in 1920.
