prince-bishopric-of-utrecht.t: The Sticht, a church principality covering much of the northern Netherlands, whose bishops fought Holland and Guelders for five centuries.
prince-bishopric-of-utrecht.o: [[s:lordship-of-utrecht|Utrecht]] had been the seat of [[e:willibrord|Willibrord's]] mission to the [[s:frisii|Frisians]] since the late 7th century. In the early 11th century the German kings granted [[e:bishop|Bishop]] [[e:adalbold-ii-of-utrecht|Adalbold]] and his successors counties and secular rights, including lands in [[e:drenthe|Drenthe]] and along the [[e:ijssel|IJssel]], turning the see into a principality of the [[s:holy-roman-empire|Holy Roman Empire]].
prince-bishopric-of-utrecht.r: The territory had two parts: the [[e:nedersticht|Nedersticht]] around [[s:lordship-of-utrecht|Utrecht]] and the [[s:lordship-of-overijssel|Oversticht]], today Overijssel and [[e:drenthe|Drenthe]]. Utrecht was an imperial favourite, where [[e:conrad-ii-holy-roman-emperor|Conrad II]] and Henry V died. The [[e:bishop|bishops]] were elected by chapters but often imposed by neighbours: [[e:david-of-burgundy|David of Burgundy]], son of [[e:philip-the-good|Philip the Good]], held the see from 1456. Towns such as [[e:deventer|Deventer]] and [[e:kampen|Kampen]] grew rich in the Hanseatic trade.
prince-bishopric-of-utrecht.e: Weakened by wars with Holland and the [[s:duchy-of-guelders|Duchy of Guelders]], [[e:henry-of-the-palatinate|Bishop Henry of Bavaria]] transferred his temporal power to [[e:charles-v-holy-roman-emperor|Charles V]] in 1528. The lands became the [[s:lordship-of-utrecht|Lordship of Utrecht]] and [[s:lordship-of-overijssel|Lordship of Overijssel]] in the [[s:habsburg-netherlands|Habsburg Netherlands]].

portuguese-bahrain.t: Bahrain under Portuguese overlordship, ruled through Hormuz from a rebuilt fort, until Safavid Persia took the island in 1602.
portuguese-bahrain.o: In 1521 a Portuguese and Hormuzi force under [[e:antonio-correia|Antonio Correia]] attacked [[s:sheikhdom-of-bahrain|Bahrain]], defeating and fatally wounding the Jabrid ruler [[e:muqrin-ibn-zamil|Muqrin ibn Zamil]]. The islands passed to the [[s:kingdom-of-ormus|Kingdom of Ormus]], a [[e:vassal|vassal]] of the [[s:portuguese-empire|Portuguese Empire]].
portuguese-bahrain.r: [[s:sheikhdom-of-bahrain|Bahrain]] was governed by Hormuzi governors, while the Portuguese kept a garrison and rebuilt the fort at [[e:qalat-al-bahrain|Qal'at al-Bahrain]]. The islands' value lay in their pearls and dates and in their position. Local revolts broke out, notably in 1529, and an Ottoman attempt to take the island in 1559 failed. The Portuguese presence itself was small for most of the period.
portuguese-bahrain.e: In 1602 the local governor was overthrown and the Safavid governor of [[e:fars|Fars]] took [[s:sheikhdom-of-bahrain|Bahrain]] for the [[s:safavid-empire|Safavid Empire]], which held it for most of the next 120 years. The fort, now part of a [[e:unesco-world-heritage-site|World Heritage Site]], is the main relic.

principality-of-neuchatel.t: A small principality on Lake Neuchâtel ruled for 150 years by the kings of Prussia while also allied to, and later part of, the Swiss Confederacy.
principality-of-neuchatel.o: [[e:neuchatel|Neuchâtel]] ('new castle') appears in 1011 when [[e:rudolf-iii-of-burgundy|King Rudolf III of Burgundy]] gave the castle to his wife; in 1034 it passed with [[s:duchy-of-burgundy|Burgundy]] to the Empire. Counts of Neuchâtel ruled from the 12th century, and the county passed to the [[s:margraviate-of-hachberg|Hochberg]] family and in 1504 to the French house of [[e:house-of-orleans-longueville|Orléans-Longueville]].
principality-of-neuchatel.r: The county became Protestant under [[e:guillaume-farel|Guillaume Farel]] in 1530 and was closely allied with Bern and other Swiss cantons. Its estates and towns enjoyed liberties. When the [[e:house-of-orleans-longueville|Longueville]] line ended in 1707, the estates chose [[e:frederick-i-of-prussia|King Frederick I of Prussia]] as prince. Watchmaking in the [[e:jura-mountains|Jura]] valleys, at [[e:la-chaux-de-fonds|La Chaux-de-Fonds]] and [[e:le-locle|Le Locle]], became the chief industry.
principality-of-neuchatel.e: [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]] gave [[e:neuchatel|Neuchâtel]] to Marshal [[e:louis-alexandre-berthier|Berthier]] from 1806 to 1814. In 1815 it became a Swiss canton while remaining a Prussian principality, an anomaly ended by the republican revolution of 1848. [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] renounced its claims in 1857.

principality-of-monaco.t: A rock on the Riviera seized by the Grimaldis in 1297 and still ruled by them, now one of the world's smallest and richest sovereign states.
principality-of-monaco.o: In January 1297 [[e:francois-grimaldi|François Grimaldi]], a Genoese Guelph exile, took the fortress of Monaco disguised as a Franciscan friar, an event recalled in the monk on the family arms. The [[e:house-of-grimaldi|Grimaldis]] lost and regained the rock several times before establishing lasting control in the 15th century.
principality-of-monaco.r: The [[e:house-of-grimaldi|Grimaldis]] governed as lords, later princes, balancing between [[s:republic-of-genoa|Genoa]], [[e:spain|Spain]], [[e:france|France]] and [[s:duchy-of-savoy|Savoy]]. [[e:honore-ii-prince-of-monaco|Honoré II]] placed Monaco under French protection in 1641 and adopted the title of prince. Revenues came from tolls, [[e:olive-oil|olive oil]] and citrus from [[s:free-cities-of-menton-and-roquebrune|Menton and Roquebrune]], until [[e:charles-iii-prince-of-monaco|Charles III]] founded the [[e:monte-carlo|Monte Carlo]] casino in 1863.
principality-of-monaco.e: Monaco was annexed by [[e:france|France]] in 1793 and restored in 1814 under Sardinian protection. [[s:free-cities-of-menton-and-roquebrune|Menton and Roquebrune]] broke away in 1848 and were sold to France in 1861. Constitutions of 1911 and 1962 limited princely power; under [[e:rainier-iii-prince-of-monaco|Rainier III]] and [[e:albert-ii-prince-of-monaco|Albert II]] it became a banking and tourism centre.

principality-of-yaroslavl.t: A Volga principality around the city founded by Yaroslav the Wise, ruled by its own princes until it passed to Moscow in 1463.
principality-of-yaroslavl.o: [[e:yaroslavl|Yaroslavl]] was founded in the early 11th century by [[e:yaroslav-the-wise|Yaroslav the Wise]] at the meeting of the [[e:volga|Volga]] and the [[e:kotorosl|Kotorosl]]; a legend has him killing a bear there. In 1218 [[e:konstantin-of-rostov|Konstantin Vsevolodovich of Rostov]] gave it to his son Vsevolod, who founded a separate princely line.
principality-of-yaroslavl.r: Its position on the [[e:volga|Volga]] made [[e:yaroslavl|Yaroslavl]] a trading town. Vsevolod was killed fighting the [[e:mongols|Mongols]] on the Sit in 1238. [[e:fyodor-the-black|Fyodor the Black]], who ruled from the 1260s, spent years at the court of the [[s:golden-horde|Golden Horde]], married a daughter of the khan and was later venerated as a saint. The principality later split into many small [[e:appanage|appanages]].
principality-of-yaroslavl.e: Its princes increasingly served the [[s:grand-duchy-of-moscow|Grand Duchy of Moscow]], and in 1463 [[e:ivan-iii|Ivan III]] annexed the principality. The [[e:yaroslavl|Yaroslavl]] princes survived as noble families such as the Shakhovskoy and Kurbsky. The city became one of [[e:russia|Russia's]] richest commercial centres in the 17th century.

pingnan-guo.t: The Muslim-led state of Du Wenxiu in western Yunnan, born of the Panthay rebellion against the Qing, which ruled from Dali for sixteen years.
pingnan-guo.o: Tension between Hui Muslims and [[e:han-chinese|Han Chinese]] over the mines of [[e:yunnan|Yunnan]] led to massacres of Muslims, including at [[e:kunming|Kunming]] in 1856. In the uprising that followed, the Hui leader [[e:du-wenxiu|Du Wenxiu]] took Dali in 1856 and established a state, taking the title [[e:sultan|Sultan]] Suleiman as well as the Chinese title of generalissimo.
pingnan-guo.r: Pingnan Guo ('the state that pacifies the south') was multi-ethnic, including Bai, Yi and Han officials as well as Hui. [[e:du-wenxiu|Du Wenxiu]] revived Ming-style dress, promoted the jade, [[e:cotton|cotton]] and opium trade with [[s:myanmar|Burma]], and kept mosques and markets open. In 1872 he sent his adopted son Hassan to [[e:london|London]] to seek British recognition, without success.
pingnan-guo.e: Qing forces under [[e:cen-yuying|Cen Yuying]] retook eastern [[e:yunnan|Yunnan]] and besieged Dali in 1872. [[e:du-wenxiu|Du Wenxiu]] took poison and surrendered at the end of that year, hoping to save the people; he was beheaded, and the city's Muslim population was massacred.

principality-of-kashin.t: An appanage of the Tver lands on the upper Volga, linked with Saint Anna of Kashin and reabsorbed by Tver in 1426.
principality-of-kashin.o: Kashin, north-east of Tver, was part of the [[s:grand-principality-of-tver|Grand Principality of Tver]]. After [[e:mikhail-of-tver|Mikhail Yaroslavich]] was executed at the [[s:golden-horde|Golden Horde]] in 1318, his youngest son Vasily received Kashin as his [[e:appanage|appanage]], founding a separate line of princes.
principality-of-kashin.r: The principality was small, with an economy based on farming and local trade. Mikhail's widow Anna lived her last years in Kashin as a nun and was later venerated as [[e:anna-of-kashin|Saint Anna of Kashin]]. Its princes repeatedly quarrelled with their Tver cousins and sometimes sought the support of [[e:moscow|Moscow]] against them.
principality-of-kashin.e: After several periods of union and separation, Kashin was finally merged back into the [[s:grand-principality-of-tver|Grand Principality of Tver]] in 1426. Together with Tver, it was annexed by the [[s:grand-duchy-of-moscow|Grand Duchy of Moscow]] in 1485.

pagan-kingdom.t: The first kingdom to unite the Irrawaddy valley, whose rulers built over 10,000 Buddhist monuments on the plain of Bagan and laid the foundations of Burmese culture.
pagan-kingdom.o: Burman settlers from the north occupied the [[e:kyaukse|Kyaukse]] plain and the middle [[e:irrawaddy-river|Irrawaddy]] in the 9th century, and chronicles date the walls of Pagan to 849. The town became a regional power under [[e:anawrahta|Anawrahta]], who took the throne in 1044, conquered the [[s:thaton-kingdom|Thaton Kingdom]] in 1057 and brought much of present-day [[s:myanmar|Myanmar]] under his rule.
pagan-kingdom.r: Pagan's kings ruled a core of irrigated [[e:rice|rice]] lands around [[e:kyaukse|Kyaukse]] and [[e:minbu|Minbu]], with tributary regions beyond. Royal and private donors gave land and labour to the Buddhist sangha on a vast scale, building temples such as the [[e:shwezigon-pagoda|Shwezigon]], [[e:ananda-temple|Ananda]] and [[e:dhammayangyi-temple|Dhammayangyi]]. Old Burmese emerged as a written language, recorded in the Myazedi inscription of 1113 alongside Pyu, [[e:mon-people|Mon]] and Pali.
pagan-kingdom.e: The flow of tax-free land to monasteries weakened royal revenues, and Mongol invasions under the [[e:yuan-dynasty|Yuan dynasty]] in the 1280s led to Pagan's fall in 1287. Real power passed to the [[s:myinsaing-kingdom|Myinsaing]] brothers, who deposed the last puppet king in 1297. Bagan became a [[e:unesco-world-heritage-site|World Heritage Site]] in 2019.

prince-of-wales-island.t: British East India Company settlement on Penang, founded by Francis Light, the first British base on the Strait of Malacca.
prince-of-wales-island.o: Seeking a naval and trading base on the eastern side of the [[e:bay-of-bengal|Bay of Bengal]], the [[e:east-india-company|East India Company]] trader [[e:francis-light|Francis Light]] negotiated with the [[e:sultan|Sultan]] of [[s:kedah-sultanate|Kedah]], who hoped for protection against Siam. Light landed on [[e:penang|Penang]] in August 1786, renamed it [[e:prince-of-wales|Prince of Wales]] Island and founded [[e:george-town-penang|George Town]].
prince-of-wales-island.r: The settlement was a free port that drew Chinese, Indian, Malay, Acehnese and Eurasian traders, and [[e:spice-trade|spices]] and [[e:pepper|pepper]] were planted. In 1800 [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] added the mainland strip of [[e:province-wellesley|Province Wellesley]]. In 1805 it was raised to the status of a presidency of [[s:british-raj|British India]], with [[e:stamford-raffles|Thomas Stamford Raffles]] serving as assistant secretary.
prince-of-wales-island.e: Hopes of a naval dockyard faded and the rise of [[s:singapore|Singapore]] overshadowed [[e:penang|Penang]]. In 1826 it was merged with [[e:singapore|Singapore]] and [[e:malacca|Malacca]] to form the [[s:straits-settlements|Straits Settlements]], and [[e:george-town-penang|George Town]] later became the capital of the Malaysian state of Penang.
prince-of-wales-island.re: Sunni Islam, Chinese folk religion, Christianity

principality-of-besleney.t: An eastern Circassian princely tribe on the upper Kuban and Laba, closely related to the Kabardians, whose descendants are the Cherkess of Karachay-Cherkessia.
principality-of-besleney.o: The Besleney lived on the upper Kuban, [[e:laba-river|Laba]] and [[e:urup|Urup]] rivers, between [[s:principality-of-kabarda|Kabarda]] and the western [[e:circassians|Circassians]]. Tradition links their princely house to the Kabardian aristocracy, and their speech is close to Kabardian. They appear as a distinct community from the 16th and 17th centuries; earlier history is not separately recorded.
principality-of-besleney.r: Princes and nobles ruled over free peasants and serfs according to the [[e:circassians|Adyghe]] code of conduct. The Besleney were horse breeders and herders, and their princes alternately allied with [[s:principality-of-kabarda|Kabarda]], the [[s:crimean-khanate|Crimean Khanate]] and [[e:russia|Russia]]. Their position on the routes between east and west [[s:circassia|Circassia]] gave them influence beyond their size.
principality-of-besleney.e: The [[s:russian-empire|Russian Empire]] brought them under its control in the course of the [[e:russo-circassian-war|Russo-Circassian War]], completed in 1864. Many emigrated to the [[s:ottoman-empire|Ottoman Empire]], but part remained, and their descendants form much of the [[e:circassians|Cherkess]] people of [[e:karachay-cherkessia|Karachay-Cherkessia]].

prome-kingdom.t: A small Burmese kingdom based at Prome on the lower Irrawaddy that broke from Ava in 1482 and fell to the rising Toungoo in 1542.
prome-kingdom.o: In 1482 [[e:thado-minsaw-of-prome|Thado Minsaw]], the governor of Prome and a son of King [[e:narapati-i-of-ava|Narapati]] of the [[s:ava-kingdom|Ava Kingdom]], rebelled during a succession crisis and made his town, on the [[e:irrawaddy-river|Irrawaddy]] near the old Pyu city of [[s:sri-ksetra-kingdom|Sri Ksetra]], the seat of an independent kingdom.
prome-kingdom.r: Prome controlled the river trade between [[e:upper-burma|Upper Burma]] and the [[e:mon-people|Mon]] coast and played Ava, the [[s:hanthawaddy-kingdom|Hanthawaddy Kingdom]] and Toungoo against each other. Its kings at times allied with the Shan rulers who took Ava in 1527, receiving support from the [[s:confederation-of-shan-states|Confederation of Shan States]].
prome-kingdom.e: [[e:tabinshwehti|Tabinshwehti]] of the [[s:first-toungoo-empire|First Toungoo Empire]] besieged Prome after taking [[e:bago|Pegu]], and in 1542 the city fell despite help from the Shan confederation and [[s:mrauk-u-kingdom|Arakan]]. Prome was absorbed into the Toungoo realm and later served as a provincial centre; it is the modern city of Pyay.

phaistos.t: Greek city-state built on the ruins of the Minoan palace in southern Crete, rival of Gortyn until destroyed by it c. 150 BCE.
phaistos.o: After the [[e:bronze-age|Bronze Age]] palace fell, [[s:palace-state-of-phaistos|Phaistos]] survived as a settlement on its ridge above the [[e:mesara-plain|Mesara]] plain. In the early [[e:iron-age|Iron Age]] Dorian-speaking [[e:greeks|Greeks]] dominated it, and by the Archaic period it was an independent polis, one of many on [[e:crete|Crete]], with Greek temples built over parts of the old palace.
phaistos.r: [[s:palace-state-of-phaistos|Phaistos]] controlled the western [[e:mesara-plain|Mesara]] and the harbour of [[e:matala|Matala]]. It minted coins from the 4th century BCE showing [[e:talos|Talos]], the bronze giant of myth, and [[e:heracles|Heracles]]. Like other Cretan cities it had an aristocratic constitution with [[e:kosmoi|kosmoi]] magistrates and men's messes. Its great rival was [[s:gortyn|Gortyn]], a few kilometres east.
phaistos.e: [[s:palace-state-of-phaistos|Phaistos]] was destroyed by [[s:gortyn|Gortyn]] in the mid-2nd century BCE and its territory absorbed. The site was later known chiefly for its Minoan palace, described separately as the Palace State of Phaistos.

prince-bishopric-of-toul.t: The smallest of the Three Bishoprics of Lorraine, an ecclesiastical principality of the Empire that produced a reforming pope and was absorbed by France.
prince-bishopric-of-toul.o: [[e:toul|Toul]] had been a bishopric since late Roman times. In the 10th century, as the German kings sought loyal counterweights to the [[s:duchy-of-lorraine|Lorraine]] nobility, the [[e:bishop|bishops]] received comital rights over the city and its surroundings, traditionally dated to 928 under [[e:henry-the-fowler|Henry the Fowler]], making them princes of the [[s:holy-roman-empire|Holy Roman Empire]].
prince-bishopric-of-toul.r: The [[e:bishop|bishops]] ruled a small territory on the upper [[e:moselle|Moselle]], often clashing with the dukes of [[s:duchy-of-lorraine|Lorraine]] and with the citizens of [[e:toul|Toul]], who won considerable self-government. Bishop [[e:pope-leo-ix|Bruno of Egisheim]] became Pope Leo IX in 1049 and drove the Gregorian reform. The diocese itself was far larger than the temporal principality.
prince-bishopric-of-toul.e: In 1552 [[e:henry-ii-of-france|Henry II of France]] occupied [[e:toul|Toul]], [[e:metz|Metz]] and [[e:verdun|Verdun]] as 'protector' during his war with [[e:charles-v-holy-roman-emperor|Charles V]]. French control of the [[e:three-bishoprics|Three Bishoprics]] was confirmed by the [[e:peace-of-westphalia|Peace of Westphalia]] in 1648, and Toul became part of the [[s:kingdom-of-france|Kingdom of France]].

principality-of-gottingen.t: Guelph principality on the upper Leine whose turbulent dukes, including Otto the Bad, struggled with their own town of Göttingen until 1463.
principality-of-gottingen.o: After the death of Albert I of [[e:brunswick|Brunswick]] in 1279, his sons divided the [[s:principality-of-wolfenbuttel|Principality of Wolfenbüttel]], and around 1291 [[e:albert-ii-duke-of-brunswick-luneburg|Albert II the Fat]] received the southern lands around [[e:gottingen|Göttingen]], [[e:hann-munden|Münden]] and [[e:uslar|Uslar]], founding a separate [[e:house-of-welf|Guelph]] principality on the upper [[e:leine|Leine]] and [[e:weser|Weser]].
principality-of-gottingen.r: The dukes ruled a land of hills, forests and small towns, with [[e:gottingen|Göttingen]] the main town. The town grew increasingly independent, joined the [[s:hanseatic-league|Hanseatic League]] and expelled Duke [[e:otto-i-duke-of-brunswick-gottingen|Otto the Bad]], whose feuds and debts weakened the principality in the late 14th century. His son [[e:otto-cocles|Otto Cocles]], the One-Eyed, was nearly blind and handed government to the estates in 1435.
principality-of-gottingen.e: When [[e:otto-cocles|Otto Cocles]] died in 1463, the principality passed to the [[e:wolfenbuttel|Wolfenbüttel]] branch and was later joined to the [[s:principality-of-calenberg|Principality of Calenberg]]. [[e:gottingen|Göttingen]] became part of the [[s:electorate-of-hanover|Electorate of Hanover]], where its university was founded in 1734.

principality-of-minden.t: Secularised Westphalian bishopric on the Weser that became a Prussian principality and gave its name to a famous battle of 1759.
principality-of-minden.o: The Bishopric of [[e:minden|Minden]], founded by [[e:charlemagne|Charlemagne]] around 800, had turned Protestant in the [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]]. At the [[e:peace-of-westphalia|Peace of Westphalia]] in 1648 it was secularised and assigned to the [[s:margraviate-of-brandenburg|Margraviate of Brandenburg]] as part of its compensation for ceding [[e:pomerania|Western Pomerania]] to [[e:sweden|Sweden]].
principality-of-minden.r: [[e:brandenburg-prussia|Brandenburg-Prussia]] governed [[e:minden|Minden]] through a provincial administration, later combined with the [[s:county-of-ravensberg|County of Ravensberg]] in a single chamber of war and domains. The town was fortified and garrisoned, and the region produced grain and linen. During the [[e:seven-years-war|Seven Years' War]] an Anglo-German army under [[e:ferdinand-of-brunswick-wolfenbuttel|Ferdinand of Brunswick]] defeated the French nearby at the [[e:battle-of-minden|Battle of Minden]] on 1 August 1759.
principality-of-minden.e: After [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia's]] collapse in 1806, [[e:minden|Minden]] was divided between the [[s:kingdom-of-westphalia|Kingdom of Westphalia]] and, from 1810, [[e:france|France]]. In 1815 it returned to Prussia as part of the [[e:province-of-westphalia|Province of Westphalia]]; the area is now in [[e:north-rhine-westphalia|North Rhine-Westphalia]].

principality-of-prosek.t: Short-lived lordship of the adventurer Dobromir Chrysos in the Vardar gorge, carved out during the Bulgarian revolt against Byzantium.
principality-of-prosek.o: [[e:dobromir-chrysos|Dobromir Chrysos]], a [[e:vlachs|Vlach]] or Bulgarian commander who had served in the Byzantine army, broke away during the [[e:ivan-asen-i|Asen]] revolt that founded the [[s:second-bulgarian-empire|Second Bulgarian Empire]]. Around 1197 he seized the fortress of Prosek, in the [[e:demir-kapija|Demir Kapija]] gorge of the [[e:vardar|Vardar]], and nearby [[e:strumica|Strumica]].
principality-of-prosek.r: Known mainly from the Byzantine historian [[e:niketas-choniates|Niketas Choniates]], his realm rested on the near-impregnable fortress of Prosek and on several hundred warriors. The emperor [[e:alexios-iii-angelos|Alexios III]] failed to take it and recognised him, marrying him to a relative.
principality-of-prosek.e: [[e:dobromir-chrysos|Chrysos]] rebelled again, and around 1201–1202 [[e:alexios-iii-angelos|Alexios III]] defeated him and recovered his lands; Prosek soon passed to [[e:kaloyan-of-bulgaria|Kaloyan of Bulgaria]].

provisional-government-of-the-republic-o.t: The Korean government-in-exile founded in Shanghai after the March First Movement of 1919, which kept the cause of independence alive until 1945.
provisional-government-of-the-republic-o.o: In the wake of the [[e:march-first-movement|March First Movement]], independence activists met in [[e:shanghai|Shanghai's]] [[e:shanghai-french-concession|French Concession]] and in April 1919 proclaimed the [[e:south-korea|Republic of Korea]] with a provisional constitution and assembly. Rival groups in [[e:seoul|Seoul]] and [[e:vladivostok|Vladivostok]] merged with it later that year, and [[e:syngman-rhee|Syngman Rhee]] was chosen as president.
provisional-government-of-the-republic-o.r: The government drew funds from [[e:koreans|Koreans]] abroad and ran diplomacy and propaganda, but it was weakened by factional disputes; [[e:syngman-rhee|Rhee]] was impeached in 1925. Under [[e:kim-gu|Kim Gu]] it organised attacks on Japanese leaders, including [[e:yun-bong-gil|Yun Bong-gil's]] bombing in [[e:shanghai|Shanghai]] in 1932, then moved through several Chinese cities before settling in [[e:chongqing|Chongqing]] in 1940, where it formed the [[e:korean-liberation-army|Korean Liberation Army]] and declared war on [[e:japan|Japan]] in 1941.
provisional-government-of-the-republic-o.e: The [[e:allies|Allies]] never recognised it, and its leaders returned to [[e:korea|Korea]] in late 1945 only as private individuals. The [[e:south-korea|Republic of Korea's]] constitution claims descent from it, and it ceased to exist when that state was founded in 1948.

phagmodrupa-dynasty.t: The dynasty that replaced the Mongol-backed Sakya and restored native rule over central Tibet, patrons of the rising Gelug school.
phagmodrupa-dynasty.o: [[e:changchub-gyaltsen|Changchub Gyaltsen]], myriarch of Phagmodru, a domain linked to the [[e:kagyu|Kagyu]] monastery of [[e:densatil|Densatil]], fought the [[s:sakya-regime|Sakya regime]]'s administrators from the 1340s. By 1354 he controlled most of central [[s:tibet-1912-1951|Tibet]] and ruled from [[e:nedong|Nedong]] in the [[e:yarlung-valley|Yarlung]] valley.
phagmodrupa-dynasty.r: [[e:changchub-gyaltsen|Changchub Gyaltsen]] reorganised the country into districts governed by appointed officials from fortresses (dzong), issued a law code inspired by the age of the [[s:tibetan-empire|Tibetan Empire]], and encouraged a revival of imperial traditions. His successors, called gongma, received titles from the [[s:ming-empire|Ming Empire]]. [[e:drakpa-gyaltsen-phagmodrupa|Drakpa Gyaltsen]] supported [[e:tsongkhapa|Tsongkhapa]], who founded [[e:ganden-monastery|Ganden]] monastery in 1409, the start of the [[e:gelug|Gelug]] school.
phagmodrupa-dynasty.e: After a succession crisis in 1434, real power passed to the [[s:rinpungpa|Rinpungpa]] ministers and later to the [[s:tsangpa-dynasty|Tsangpa dynasty]]. The Phagmodrupa rulers survived as nominal kings at [[e:nedong|Nedong]] until the early 17th century.

principality-of-reuss-lobenstein.t: Tiny Thuringian lordship of the Reuss family, where every male ruler was named Heinrich.
principality-of-reuss-lobenstein.o: The Younger Line of the [[e:house-of-reuss|House of Reuss]] divided its lands in 1647 into Gera, [[e:schleiz|Schleiz]], [[e:bad-lobenstein|Lobenstein]] and Saalburg. [[e:heinrich-x-reuss-of-lobenstein|Heinrich X]] received Lobenstein in the [[e:thuringian-highlands|Thuringian Highlands]], and his descendants later split off Ebersdorf and Hirschberg as further sub-lines.
principality-of-reuss-lobenstein.r: [[e:bad-lobenstein|Lobenstein]] was small, hilly and poor, with some mining and [[e:timber|timber]]. Like all [[e:house-of-reuss|Reuss]] branches, its counts named every son Heinrich, distinguished by numbers counted across the century. The rulers were Lutheran and governed through a modest court in Lobenstein. They were raised to princely rank in 1790.
principality-of-reuss-lobenstein.e: The [[e:bad-lobenstein|Lobenstein]] line died out in 1824, and its lands passed to the [[s:principality-of-reuss-ebersdorf|Principality of Reuss-Ebersdorf]], which became [[e:house-of-reuss|Reuss]]-Lobenstein-Ebersdorf. In 1848 all these lands joined the [[s:principality-of-reuss-schleiz|Principality of Reuss-Schleiz]] to form the [[e:principality-of-reuss-younger-line|Principality of Reuss Younger Line]].

pedir.t: A pepper port on the north coast of Sumatra that flourished in the 15th century before falling to Aceh in 1524.
pedir.o: Pedir, the modern district of Pidie in [[e:aceh|Aceh]], grew as a port on the [[e:strait-of-malacca|Strait of Malacca]] in the 15th century. It is mentioned in Chinese records and by early Portuguese writers. Its rulers were Muslim, following the example of nearby [[e:samudera-pasai-sultanate|Samudera Pasai]].
pedir.r: [[e:tome-pires|Tome Pires]], writing around 1515, described Pedir as one of the leading [[e:pepper|pepper]] exporters of [[e:sumatra|Sumatra]], rivalling [[s:samudera-pasai-sultanate|Pasai]], with merchants from [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]], [[e:bengal|Bengal]] and the Malay ports. It also exported [[e:silk|silk]] and [[e:benzoin-resin|benzoin]], and was a stopping place on the route from [[e:india|India]] to [[e:malacca|Malacca]].
pedir.e: In the early 16th century Pedir was drawn into the struggle between the Portuguese and the rising [[s:aceh-sultanate|Aceh Sultanate]]. [[e:sultan|Sultan]] [[e:ali-mughayat-syah|Ali Mughayat Syah]] of [[e:aceh|Aceh]] conquered it around 1524, and it became one of Aceh's districts.

piploda-state.t: A small Rajput chiefship of western Malwa, long a dependency of the Nawabs of Jaora.
piploda-state.o: Piploda was held by a [[e:rajputs|Rajput]] Thakur family in western [[e:malwa|Malwa]] from the late 18th century. When the British settled Malwa after 1818, it was placed under the Nawab of [[s:jaora-state|Jaora]] as a tributary holding.
piploda-state.r: The Thakurs governed a few dozen villages and paid tribute to [[s:jaora-state|Jaora State]]. In the 20th century Piploda was separated from Jaora and placed directly under the [[e:malwa-agency|Malwa Agency]]. Little else is recorded.
piploda-state.e: After accession to [[e:india|India]] Piploda was merged into [[s:madhya-bharat|Madhya Bharat]] in 1948 and joined [[e:madhya-pradesh|Madhya Pradesh]] in 1956; it lies in [[s:ratlam-state|Ratlam]] district.

principality-of-guria.t: A small principality on Georgia's Black Sea coast, ruled by the Gurieli family between the Kingdom of Imereti and the Ottoman Empire.
principality-of-guria.o: Guria, the land south of the Rioni along the [[e:black-sea|Black Sea]] coast, was governed by a branch of the Vardanidze family, later called [[e:house-of-gurieli|Gurieli]], as eristavis of the [[s:kingdom-of-georgia|Kingdom of Georgia]]. As the kingdom broke apart in the 1460s, the Gurieli became effectively independent princes, nominally owing allegiance to the [[s:kingdom-of-imereti|Kingdom of Imereti]].
principality-of-guria.r: The princes ruled from [[e:ozurgeti|Ozurgeti]] over a land of [[e:maize|maize]], vineyards and forested hills. Guria lay on the frontier with the [[s:ottoman-empire|Ottoman Empire]], which seized its coastal fortresses and drew tribute; the [[e:atlantic-slave-trade|slave trade]] through Ottoman ports was a persistent evil. The [[e:house-of-gurieli|Gurieli]] took part in Imereti's dynastic wars, sometimes ruling it themselves, as [[e:mamia-iii-gurieli|Mamia III]] did.
principality-of-guria.e: In 1810 [[e:mamia-v-gurieli|Mamia V]] accepted a Russian [[e:protectorate|protectorate]]. After his death in 1826 his young son [[e:david|David]] succeeded under the regency of his mother Sophia; a revolt in 1828 was crushed, and in 1829 the [[s:russian-empire|Russian Empire]] annexed Guria.

paemani.t: One of the Germani Cisrhenani of the Belgian Ardennes, remembered in the name of the Famenne region.
paemani.o: Caesar lists the Paemani with the [[s:condrusi|Condrusi]], [[s:eburones|Eburones]] and [[s:caeroesi|Caeroesi]] as Germani living west of the [[e:rhine|Rhine]]. Their name is usually linked to the [[e:famenne|Famenne]], in the modern Belgian provinces of [[s:county-of-namur|Namur]] and [[s:county-of-luxembourg|Luxembourg]].
paemani.r: Nothing is known of their rulers or settlements.
paemani.e: They joined the Belgic coalition against Caesar in 57 BCE. After the conquest they disappear from the sources, their land absorbed into the civitas of the [[s:tungri|Tungri]].

prince-bishopric-of-speyer.t: A prince-bishopric on the Rhine whose cathedral holds the tombs of Salian emperors, its bishops ruling from Bruchsal until 1803.
prince-bishopric-of-speyer.o: [[s:free-imperial-city-of-speyer|Speyer]] had been a bishopric since the 7th century, and Salian kings made it their family church; [[e:conrad-ii-holy-roman-emperor|Conrad II]] began the great cathedral around 1030. In 1111 [[e:henry-v-holy-roman-emperor|Emperor Henry V]] granted the citizens of Speyer privileges, and the [[e:bishop|bishops]]' secular rule over their territory developed in the 11th and 12th centuries.
prince-bishopric-of-speyer.r: The [[e:bishop|bishops]] ruled a territory on both banks of the [[e:rhine|Rhine]] but not the city of [[s:free-imperial-city-of-speyer|Speyer]], which became a free imperial city; they moved their residence to [[e:philippsburg|Udenheim]], renamed Philippsburg, and in 1720 to [[e:bruchsal|Bruchsal]], where Cardinal [[e:damian-hugo-philipp-von-schonborn|Damian Hugo von Schönborn]] built a baroque palace. The cathedral, burial place of eight emperors and kings, is a [[e:unesco-world-heritage-site|World Heritage Site]].
prince-bishopric-of-speyer.e: [[e:france|France]] annexed the left-bank lands during the [[e:french-revolutionary-wars|Revolutionary Wars]], and in 1803 the right-bank territory, including [[e:bruchsal|Bruchsal]], was secularised and given to [[e:baden|Baden]]. The diocese of [[s:free-imperial-city-of-speyer|Speyer]] was re-founded in 1817 under [[e:bavaria|Bavaria]].

principality-of-kakheti.t: An eastern Georgian principality ruled by chorepiscopi, leaders with a churchly title, that resisted the Arab emirs of Tbilisi and the Bagratid kings.
principality-of-kakheti.o: [[s:kingdom-of-kakheti|Kakheti]], the land east of [[e:tbilisi|Tbilisi]], broke away from the [[s:principality-of-iberia|Principality of Iberia]] in 786, when the nobleman [[e:grigol-of-kakheti|Grigol]] took the title chorepiscopus and united its mountain communities. The weakening of central power under Arab rule allowed it to become a separate state.
principality-of-kakheti.r: Its rulers, whose title meant rural [[e:bishop|bishop]] although they were lay princes, ruled from [[e:ujarma|Ujarma]] and later [[e:telavi|Telavi]] with the support of the mountain peoples of [[e:tusheti|Tusheti]] and [[e:pshavi|Pshavi]]. They fought the [[s:emirate-of-tbilisi|Emirate of Tbilisi]] and the [[s:kingdom-of-abkhazia|Kingdom of Abkhazia]], and in the 10th century absorbed the [[s:principality-of-hereti|Principality of Hereti]]. Viticulture and farming in the Alazani valley sustained it.
principality-of-kakheti.e: Around 1010 [[e:kvirike-iii-of-kakheti|Kvirike III]] took the title king, forming the [[s:kingdom-of-kakheti-hereti|Kingdom of Kakheti-Hereti]], which held out against the united Georgian monarchy until 1104. [[s:kingdom-of-kakheti|Kakheti]] later re-emerged as a separate Georgian kingdom in the 15th century.

pskov-republic.t: A fortified city-republic on Russia's western frontier, which governed itself through its veche until Moscow annexed it in 1510.
pskov-republic.o: [[e:pskov|Pskov]] was long a dependency of the [[s:novgorod-republic|Novgorod Republic]], though it already had its own princes, among them the Lithuanian exile [[e:daumantas-of-pskov|Daumantas]], who defended it in the late 13th century. In 1348 the [[e:treaty-of-bolotovo|Treaty of Bolotovo]] recognised Pskov's self-government, and it became an independent republic.
pskov-republic.r: Power lay with the veche, which met by the [[e:trinity-cathedral-pskov|Trinity Cathedral]] in the stone citadel known as the [[e:pskov-krom|Krom]], and with elected posadniks. [[e:pskov|Pskov]] hired princes to command its troops, often from [[s:grand-duchy-of-lithuania|Lithuania]] or [[e:moscow|Moscow]]. Its Judicial Charter is one of the most important legal texts of medieval [[e:russia|Russia]]. A frontier fortress, it repeatedly fought the [[s:livonian-order|Livonian Order]].
pskov-republic.e: In the 15th century [[e:pskov|Pskov]] relied increasingly on [[e:moscow|Moscow]] for protection. In 1510 [[e:vasily-iii-of-moscow|Vasily III]] ended its independence, removed the veche bell and deported hundreds of leading families. The city became a Muscovite fortress and withstood the siege of [[e:stephen-bathory|Stefan Batory]] in 1581.

prince-archbishopric-of-bremen.t: Archbishopric of the North Sea coast, heir to Ansgar's mission to Scandinavia, which ruled the land between the Weser and Elbe until Sweden took it in 1648.
prince-archbishopric-of-bremen.o: The archdiocese of [[s:free-and-hanseatic-city-of-hamburg|Hamburg]] was founded in 831 for [[e:ansgar|Ansgar]], apostle of the North, and joined to [[s:free-hanseatic-city-of-bremen|Bremen]] after [[e:vikings|Vikings]] sacked [[e:hamburg|Hamburg]] in 845. Under Archbishop [[e:adalbert-of-hamburg|Adalbert]] in the 11th century it claimed authority over all of [[e:scandinavia|Scandinavia]]. After [[e:henry-the-lion|Henry the Lion]] fell in 1180 the archbishops built a secular principality between the lower [[e:weser|Weser]] and [[e:elbe|Elbe]].
prince-archbishopric-of-bremen.r: The archbishops governed marshland and moor from [[e:stade|Stade]] and [[e:bremervorde|Bremervörde]], while the wealthy city of [[s:free-hanseatic-city-of-bremen|Bremen]] slipped from their control. Free peasant communities in the marshes resisted lordship. The estates, including the cathedral chapter, nobles and towns, shared power. In the 16th century the land became Lutheran, and administrators came from princely houses such as [[s:duchy-of-holstein-gottorp|Holstein-Gottorp]] and [[e:denmark|Denmark]].
prince-archbishopric-of-bremen.e: The [[e:peace-of-westphalia|Peace of Westphalia]] in 1648 secularised it as the Duchy of [[s:free-hanseatic-city-of-bremen|Bremen]] under [[e:sweden|Sweden]], which ruled it with [[e:verden|Verden]]. [[e:denmark|Denmark]] took it in 1712 and sold it to the [[s:electorate-of-hanover|Electorate of Hanover]] in 1715. The land is now in [[e:lower-saxony|Lower Saxony]].

protectorate-of-southern-nigeria.t: The British protectorate over south-eastern Nigeria, later joined with Lagos, that formed the southern half of Nigeria before amalgamation in 1914.
protectorate-of-southern-nigeria.o: On 1 January 1900 [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] combined the [[s:niger-coast-protectorate|Niger Coast Protectorate]] with the southern lands of the [[s:royal-niger-company-territories|Royal Niger Company]] to form the [[e:protectorate|Protectorate]] of Southern [[e:nigeria|Nigeria]], under the high commissioner [[e:ralph-moor|Ralph Moor]], with headquarters at [[s:old-calabar|Old Calabar]]. It took over the delta trading states, the lands of the [[e:igbo-people|Igbo]] and [[e:ibibio-people|Ibibio]], and the remains of the [[s:benin-empire|Benin Empire]].
protectorate-of-southern-nigeria.r: The new administration conquered the interior by force, most notably in the [[e:anglo-aro-war|Anglo-Aro War]] of 1901-1902, which destroyed the [[s:aro-confederacy|Aro Confederacy]] and its oracle. It built roads and courts, recruited labour and promoted the export of [[e:palm-oil|palm oil]] and palm kernels. Christian missions expanded rapidly, spreading schools among the [[e:igbo-people|Igbo]] and other peoples. In 1906 it merged with the [[s:lagos-colony|Lagos Colony]], and [[s:kingdom-of-lagos|Lagos]] became its capital under Governor [[e:walter-egerton|Walter Egerton]].
protectorate-of-southern-nigeria.e: On 1 January 1914 the Southern [[e:protectorate|Protectorate]] was amalgamated with the [[s:protectorate-of-northern-nigeria|Protectorate of Northern Nigeria]] to form [[s:colonial-nigeria|Colonial Nigeria]], while remaining a separate group of provinces. The southern provinces later became the Western and Eastern Regions of the Nigerian federation.

principality-of-herat.t: The last outpost of Sadozai rule, a frontier city-state whose sieges by Persia drew Britain and Russia into the Great Game.
principality-of-herat.o: When the [[e:barakzai-dynasty|Barakzai]] brothers took over most of the [[s:durrani-empire|Durrani Empire]] around 1818, the [[e:sadozai|Sadozai]] prince [[e:mahmud-shah-durrani|Mahmud Shah]] and his son [[e:kamran-shah-durrani|Kamran Shah]] held on to [[e:herat|Herat]], ruling it as an independent principality.
principality-of-herat.r: [[e:kamran-shah-durrani|Kamran Shah's]] [[e:vizier|vizier]] [[e:yar-muhammad-khan-alakozai|Yar Muhammad Khan Alakozai]] became the real power and in 1842 killed Kamran, ruling himself until 1851. [[e:herat|Herat]] was a walled city on the route between [[e:persia|Persia]], [[e:central-asia|Central Asia]] and [[e:india|India]], and its strategic value made it central to the [[e:the-great-game|Great Game]]. Persia besieged it in 1837 to 1838, with a young British officer, [[e:eldred-pottinger|Eldred Pottinger]], helping the defence, and again in 1856, when [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] went to war with Persia to force its withdrawal.
principality-of-herat.e: By the Treaty of Paris in 1857 [[e:persia|Persia]] renounced its claims. [[e:dost-mohammad-khan|Dost Mohammad Khan]] took [[e:herat|Herat]] in 1863 after a ten-month siege, dying there days later, and Herat joined the [[s:emirate-of-afghanistan|Emirate of Afghanistan]].

peoples-state-of-hesse.t: Republican successor of the Grand Duchy of Hesse, a Social Democratic state on both sides of the Rhine.
peoples-state-of-hesse.o: [[e:ernest-louis-grand-duke-of-hesse|Grand Duke Ernest Louis]] was deposed in November 1918, and [[s:grand-duchy-of-hesse|Hesse-Darmstadt]] became the People's State of [[e:hesse|Hesse]], with a democratic constitution adopted in December 1919. It kept the grand duchy's three provinces: [[e:starkenburg|Starkenburg]], [[e:upper-hesse|Upper Hesse]] around [[e:giessen|Giessen]], and [[e:rhenish-hesse|Rhenish Hesse]] with [[e:mainz|Mainz]] and [[s:free-imperial-city-of-worms|Worms]].
peoples-state-of-hesse.r: Social Democrats led the state for most of the [[e:weimar|Weimar]] years under [[e:carl-ulrich|Carl Ulrich]]. [[e:rhenish-hesse|Rhenish Hesse]] and [[e:mainz|Mainz]] were under French occupation until 1930. [[e:darmstadt|Darmstadt]] had a technical university and the [[e:merck-group|Merck]] chemical company. The [[e:nazism|Nazis]] took power in March 1933 under Reich governor [[e:jakob-sprenger|Jakob Sprenger]], and the Jewish communities of Mainz and [[s:free-imperial-city-of-worms|Worms]], among the oldest in [[e:germany|Germany]], were destroyed.
peoples-state-of-hesse.e: In 1945 the parts east of the [[e:rhine|Rhine]] were combined with Prussian territories into [[e:greater-hesse|Greater Hesse]] in the American zone, now the state of [[e:hesse|Hesse]]. [[e:rhenish-hesse|Rhenish Hesse]] went to the French zone and later to [[e:rhineland-palatinate|Rhineland-Palatinate]].

pal-state.t: A minor Rajput chiefship of the Mahi Kantha country in northern Gujarat.
pal-state.o: Pal was one of the many petty holdings of the [[e:mahi-kantha-agency|Mahi Kantha]] region, held by a [[e:rajputs|Rajput]] family from around 1700. Its founding is not well documented.
pal-state.r: Its ruler held a few villages in the hilly country near the [[e:rajasthan|Rajasthan]] border, paid tribute through the [[e:gaekwads|Gaekwads of Baroda]] and was supervised by the [[e:mahi-kantha-agency|British Mahi Kantha Agency]]. Little else is recorded.
pal-state.e: Pal merged into [[s:bombay-presidency|Bombay Province]] in 1948 and became part of [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]] in 1960, in [[e:sabarkantha-district|Sabarkantha district]].

paduspanid-dynasty.t: A dynasty of mountain princes in Ruyan and Rustamdar that lasted over nine centuries, from the fall of the Sasanians to the reign of Shah Abbas.
paduspanid-dynasty.o: According to [[e:ibn-isfandiyar|Ibn Isfandiyar]], Paduspan, a son of [[e:gil-gavbara|Gil Gavbara]] and brother of [[e:dabuya|Dabuya]], founder of the [[s:dabuyid-dynasty|Dabuyid dynasty]], received the mountain region of [[e:ruyan|Ruyan]] in western [[e:tabaristan|Tabaristan]] around 665. His descendants ruled this upland between [[e:gilan|Gilan]] and [[e:amol|Amol]] as hereditary ostandars.
paduspanid-dynasty.r: The Paduspanids survived by submitting in turn to the [[s:abbasid-caliphate|Abbasid Caliphate]], the [[s:alavid-dynasty|Alavid dynasty]], the [[s:buyid-dynasty|Buyids]], the [[s:seljuk-empire|Seljuk Empire]], the [[s:ilkhanate|Ilkhanate]] and the [[s:timurid-empire|Timurid Empire]], while keeping local power in fortresses such as Nur and Kojur. They converted from [[e:zoroastrianism|Zoroastrianism]] to [[e:islam|Islam]] and later to Shia Islam. In 1453 the dynasty split into two branches, at Nur and at Kojur, which often quarrelled. The region's economy rested on forests, [[e:rice|rice]] and livestock.
paduspanid-dynasty.e: [[e:abbas-i-of-persia|Shah Abbas I]] of the [[s:safavid-empire|Safavid Empire]] annexed [[e:mazandaran|Mazandaran]] and its principalities in the 1590s, deposing the last Paduspanid rulers by 1598 and ending their rule.

prince-bishopric-of-cammin.t: Pomeranian church state founded as the bishopric of the newly converted Pomeranians and secularised into a Brandenburg principality in 1650.
prince-bishopric-of-cammin.o: The bishopric of [[s:duchy-of-pomerania|Pomerania]] was founded in 1140 at [[e:wolin|Wolin]] after the mission of [[e:otto-of-bamberg|Otto of Bamberg]], with [[e:adalbert-of-pomerania|Adalbert]] as first [[e:bishop|bishop]], and moved to [[e:kamien-pomorski|Cammin]] by 1176. Exempt from any archbishop, it answered directly to the pope. In 1248 the bishops acquired the land of [[e:kolobrzeg|Kolberg]], forming their secular territory with [[e:koszalin|Köslin]] and [[e:bobolice|Bublitz]].
prince-bishopric-of-cammin.r: The [[e:bishop|bishops]] ruled a small but distinct territory, with [[e:koszalin|Köslin]] and [[e:kolobrzeg|Kolberg]] its main towns and residences. They claimed imperial immediacy, which the dukes of [[s:duchy-of-pomerania|Pomerania]] contested, and the Pomeranian estates drew the bishopric into ducal politics. After the [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]] in the 1530s the see became Lutheran and was administered by members of the Pomeranian ducal house.
prince-bishopric-of-cammin.e: The last administrator, [[e:ernst-bogislaw-von-croy|Ernst Bogislaw of Croÿ]], handed it over after the [[e:peace-of-westphalia|Peace of Westphalia]] gave [[e:kamien-pomorski|Cammin]] to [[e:brandenburg|Brandenburg]], which took possession in 1650 as the Principality of Cammin. The region has been part of [[e:poland|Poland]] since 1945.

paracas.t: A culture of Peru's southern desert coast celebrated for the finest embroidered textiles of the ancient Andes, preserved in hundreds of mummy bundles at the Paracas peninsula.
paracas.o: The Paracas culture developed on the south coast of [[e:peru|Peru]], around the Paracas peninsula and the [[e:ica-river|Ica]] and [[e:pisco-river|Pisco]] valleys, from about 800 BCE. Early phases show the influence of the [[s:chavin|Chavín]] style in pottery and imagery before local traditions took over.
paracas.r: Paracas society was organised in chiefdoms supported by irrigation farming and rich fishing grounds. It is best known from its cemeteries: the necropolis of Wari Kayan, excavated by [[e:julio-c-tello|Julio C. Tello]] in 1927, held more than 400 mummy bundles wrapped in brilliantly coloured embroidered mantles of [[e:cotton|cotton]] and camelid wool. Paracas people practised cranial deformation and trepanation of the skull. Their pottery was painted with resin-based colours after firing.
paracas.e: Around 100 BCE the late Paracas tradition, known as Necropolis, merged gradually into the [[s:nazca|Nazca culture]], which inherited its iconography and textile techniques. The large [[e:paracas-candelabra|Paracas Candelabra]] geoglyph is sometimes attributed to it, though its date is uncertain.

principality-of-anhalt-plotzkau.t: Short-lived Anhalt principality, a minor appanage whose line went on to rule Anhalt-Köthen.
principality-of-anhalt-plotzkau.o: [[e:plotzkau|Plötzkau]], a small castle district on the [[e:saale|Saale]], was assigned in the 1603 partition of [[s:principality-of-anhalt|Anhalt]] to August, a younger son of [[e:joachim-ernest-prince-of-anhalt|Joachim Ernst]]. It began as an [[e:appanage|appanage]] of limited territory rather than a full share, and was formally set up as a principality in 1611.
principality-of-anhalt-plotzkau.r: Little distinguishes its government from the other [[s:principality-of-anhalt|Anhalt]] states: it was a small Calvinist territory administered from [[e:plotzkau|Plötzkau]] castle, with revenues from farming along the [[e:saale|Saale]]. Its prince August acted as regent for the young princes of [[s:principality-of-anhalt-kothen|Anhalt-Köthen]] and served the joint interests of the Anhalt house during the [[e:thirty-years-war|Thirty Years' War]].
principality-of-anhalt-plotzkau.e: In 1665 the [[e:kothen|Köthen]] line died out and Lebrecht and Emanuel of Anhalt-[[e:plotzkau|Plötzkau]] inherited [[s:principality-of-anhalt-kothen|Anhalt-Köthen]], giving up Plötzkau, which returned to [[s:principality-of-anhalt-bernburg|Anhalt-Bernburg]]. The Plötzkau branch thus continued as the ruling house of Köthen until 1847.

province-of-maryland.t: The proprietary colony of the Calvert family on Chesapeake Bay, founded as a refuge for English Catholics and known for its 1649 Toleration Act.
province-of-maryland.o: [[e:george-calvert-1st-baron-baltimore|George Calvert]], first Baron Baltimore, sought a colony where Catholics could live freely, and in 1632 Charles I granted the charter to his son [[e:cecil-calvert|Cecil Calvert]]. In 1634 the ships Ark and Dove brought the first settlers, led by [[e:leonard-calvert|Leonard Calvert]], to [[e:st-marys-city-maryland|St Mary's City]] on the lower [[e:potomac-river|Potomac]].
province-of-maryland.r: The Calverts held the colony as a proprietary palatinate with wide powers, though an elected assembly met from 1635. Catholics remained a minority, and the [[e:maryland-toleration-act|Toleration Act]] of 1649 protected Trinitarian Christians. Tobacco grown by servants and enslaved Africans was the mainstay. After the Protestant revolt of 1689 the Crown took over, the [[e:church-of-england|Church of England]] was established, and the capital moved to [[e:annapolis-maryland|Annapolis]] in 1694. The Protestant Calverts regained the province in 1715.
province-of-maryland.e: The [[e:mason-dixon-line|Mason-Dixon line]], surveyed from 1763, settled the long border dispute with the [[s:province-of-pennsylvania|Province of Pennsylvania]]. Governor [[e:robert-eden-governor-of-maryland|Robert Eden]] left in 1776, and Maryland declared independence as a state of the [[s:united-states|United States]].

palatinate-birkenfeld.t: A Wittelsbach line in the Hunsrück, from whose descendants came the kings of Bavaria and the dukes in Bavaria.
palatinate-birkenfeld.o: In 1569 [[e:wolfgang-count-palatine-of-zweibrucken|Duke Wolfgang of Palatinate-Zweibrücken]] divided his lands among his sons, and [[e:charles-i-count-palatine-of-birkenfeld|Charles I]] received [[e:birkenfeld|Birkenfeld]], part of the old [[s:county-of-sponheim|County of Sponheim]] in the [[e:hunsruck|Hunsrück]], founding the line of Palatinate-Birkenfeld.
palatinate-birkenfeld.r: The dukes ruled a small, scattered territory from [[e:birkenfeld|Birkenfeld]], sharing the [[s:county-of-sponheim|Sponheim]] lands with [[e:baden|Baden]], and kept a modest Lutheran court. Branches formed at Bischweiler and [[s:free-imperial-city-of-gelnhausen|Gelnhausen]]. [[e:christian-ii-count-palatine-of-zweibrucken-birkenfeld|Christian II]] acquired the lordship of [[e:lordship-of-rappoltstein|Rappoltstein]] (Ribeaupierre) in [[e:alsace|Alsace]] by marriage in 1673.
palatinate-birkenfeld.e: In 1731 [[e:christian-iii-count-palatine-of-zweibrucken|Christian III]] inherited [[s:palatinate-zweibrucken|Palatinate-Zweibrücken]], and the line moved there as Zweibrücken-[[e:birkenfeld|Birkenfeld]]. His grandson [[e:maximilian-i-joseph-of-bavaria|Maximilian Joseph]] became the first king of the [[s:kingdom-of-bavaria|Kingdom of Bavaria]] in 1806, while the [[s:free-imperial-city-of-gelnhausen|Gelnhausen]] branch became the dukes in [[e:bavaria|Bavaria]], family of Empress Elisabeth of [[e:austria|Austria]].

palace-state-of-knossos.t: The largest Minoan palace centre and later a Mycenaean-ruled capital whose Linear B tablets are the earliest written Greek from Crete.
palace-state-of-knossos.o: [[s:knossos|Knossos]], near modern [[e:heraklion|Heraklion]], was occupied from the [[e:neolithic|Neolithic]] and became [[e:crete|Crete's]] largest settlement. Around 1950 BCE the first palace was built around a central court. Rebuilt after an earthquake c. 1700 BCE, it grew into a complex of more than a thousand rooms, with a town of perhaps several thousand people around it.
palace-state-of-knossos.r: [[s:knossos|Knossos]] was the centre of [[e:minoan-civilisation|Minoan civilisation]], with frescoes such as the bull-leaping scene, light [[e:well|wells]], storerooms of pithoi and a theatral area. Administration used [[e:linear-a|Linear A]]. After c. 1450 BCE Greek-speaking rulers took control and kept records in [[e:linear-b|Linear B]], listing sheep, wool, textiles and offerings to gods such as [[e:potnia|Potnia]]. The palace then dominated much of central and western [[e:crete|Crete]].
palace-state-of-knossos.e: The palace was destroyed by fire, traditionally c. 1375 BCE, though the date is debated and some scholars place the final destruction later. [[s:knossos|Knossos]] survived as a town and became the Greek city-state described separately as Knossos. [[e:arthur-evans|Arthur Evans]] excavated and partly reconstructed the site from 1900.
palace-state-of-knossos.re: Minoan religion; later Mycenaean Greek religion

principality-of-samtskhe.t: A south-west Georgian principality ruled by the Jaqeli atabegs, which broke from the Georgian crown and was finally absorbed by the Ottoman Empire.
principality-of-samtskhe.o: [[e:samtskhe|Samtskhe]], the upland borderland around [[e:akhaltsikhe|Akhaltsikhe]], was governed by the Jaqeli family as royal lieutenants. In 1268 [[e:sargis-i-jaqeli|Sargis I Jaqeli]] secured direct recognition from the Mongol [[s:ilkhanate|Ilkhanate]], making his lands effectively separate from the [[s:kingdom-of-georgia|Kingdom of Georgia]], and his heirs held the title of atabeg.
principality-of-samtskhe.r: The atabegs ruled from [[e:akhaltsikhe|Akhaltsikhe]] over farming valleys, the cave monastery of [[e:vardzia|Vardzia]] and routes to [[e:anatolia|Anatolia]]. [[e:beka-i-jaqeli|Beka I Jaqeli]] issued a law code in the early 14th century. [[e:samtskhe|Samtskhe]] rejoined [[s:georgia|Georgia]] under [[e:george-v|George V]] but broke away again in the 15th century, becoming a battleground between the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]] and [[e:safavid-empire|Safavids]] after 1500 and a [[e:vassal|vassal]] of the [[s:ottoman-empire|Ottoman Empire]] from 1578.
principality-of-samtskhe.e: The Jaqeli rulers converted to [[e:islam|Islam]], and in 1628 the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]] turned [[e:samtskhe|Samtskhe]] into the [[s:childir-eyalet|Childir Eyalet]], with [[e:safar-pasha|Safar Pasha]], a Jaqeli, as its first governor. Much of the population was gradually Islamised, and the region returned to Georgian rule only after the Russian conquest of 1829.

principality-of-hersfeld.t: A Benedictine abbey in Hesse founded by a disciple of Saint Boniface, whose abbots ruled a principality until it became part of Hesse-Kassel.
principality-of-hersfeld.o: Hersfeld began as a hermitage of Saint [[e:sturmi|Sturmi]] around 736 and was refounded as a Benedictine monastery by Archbishop [[e:lullus|Lullus]] of [[e:mainz|Mainz]] around 769. [[e:charlemagne|Charlemagne]] granted it royal protection in 775, making it an imperial abbey. Its relics of [[e:wigbert|Saint Wigbert]] made it an important pilgrimage centre.
principality-of-hersfeld.r: Hersfeld held lands across [[e:hesse|Hesse]] and [[e:thuringia|Thuringia]], recorded in the Breviarium Lulli. Its scholars included the chronicler [[e:lambert-of-hersfeld|Lambert of Hersfeld]], who wrote a major account of the reign of [[e:henry-iv-holy-roman-emperor|Henry IV]]. The abbots were princes of the Empire, but rivalry with the town of Hersfeld and with the landgraves of Hesse slowly weakened them.
principality-of-hersfeld.e: The landgraves of [[e:hesse|Hesse]] became protectors of the abbey and, after the [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]], effectively controlled it. In 1648 the [[e:peace-of-westphalia|Peace of Westphalia]] secularised Hersfeld as a principality granted to [[s:electorate-of-hesse|Hesse-Kassel]]. The ruins of its [[e:romanesque-architecture|Romanesque]] abbey church are among the largest in [[e:germany|Germany]].

phaselis.t: Phaselis, a Rhodian colony with three harbours on the Lycian coast, a trading city later held by pirates and taken by Rome.
phaselis.o: Colonists from [[s:lindos|Lindos]] on [[s:rhodes|Rhodes]] founded Phaselis, traditionally in 690 BCE, on a peninsula at the border of [[s:lycian-dynasts|Lycia]] and [[e:pamphylia|Pamphylia]]. Its position on the coastal route between the [[e:aegean|Aegean]] and the eastern [[e:mediterranean|Mediterranean]] made it a natural port of call.
phaselis.r: Phaselis was a Greek city governed by its citizens and a member of the [[s:delian-league|Delian League]]. It traded [[e:timber|timber]], rose oil and other goods and had a share in the [[e:hellenion|Hellenion]] at [[e:naucratis|Naukratis]] in [[e:egypt|Egypt]]. Alexander of the [[s:macedonian-empire|Macedonian Empire]] stayed there in the winter of 334/333 BCE.
phaselis.e: In the 1st century BCE the pirate leader [[e:zenicetes|Zenicetes]] held Phaselis. The Roman general [[e:publius-servilius-vatia-isauricus|Publius Servilius Isauricus]] captured it in 77 BCE, and the city was then absorbed into the Roman world, later joining the [[s:lycian-league|Lycian League]].

protectorate-of-bohemia-and-moravia.t: Nazi-occupied Czech lands, nominally autonomous but ruled through terror, deportations and forced labour from 1939 to 1945.
protectorate-of-bohemia-and-moravia.o: After the [[e:munich-agreement|Munich Agreement]] and the loss of the [[e:sudetenland|Sudetenland]] in 1938, [[e:germany|Germany]] occupied the rest of [[s:kingdom-of-bohemia|Bohemia]] and [[s:margraviate-of-moravia|Moravia]] on 15 March 1939, as [[e:slovakia|Slovakia]] declared independence. The next day [[e:adolf-hitler|Hitler]] proclaimed the [[e:protectorate|Protectorate]] of [[e:bohemia|Bohemia]] and [[e:moravia|Moravia]] from [[e:prague-castle|Prague Castle]].
protectorate-of-bohemia-and-moravia.r: A Czech government under President [[e:emil-hacha|Emil Hácha]] remained in place, but real power lay with the [[e:reich-protector|Reich Protector]], first [[e:konstantin-von-neurath|Konstantin von Neurath]] and then [[e:reinhard-heydrich|Reinhard Heydrich]]. Czech universities were closed in 1939, and Czech industry, such as the [[e:skoda|Škoda]] works, served the German war effort. Heydrich was assassinated by Czech parachutists in 1942, and the Nazis destroyed the villages of [[e:lidice|Lidice]] and [[e:lezaky|Ležáky]] in reprisal. Most Czech [[e:jews|Jews]] were deported via [[e:theresienstadt-ghetto|Theresienstadt]] and murdered.
protectorate-of-bohemia-and-moravia.e: The [[e:prague|Prague]] uprising broke out on 5 May 1945, and the [[e:red-army|Red Army]] entered Prague on 9 May. The territory was restored to [[s:czechoslovakia|Czechoslovakia]], which expelled most of its German population in the following two years.

principality-of-kandahar.t: The principality ruled by the Barakzai 'Kandahar Sardars', half-brothers of Dost Mohammad Khan, between the fall of the Durranis and Afghan reunification.
principality-of-kandahar.o: As the [[s:durrani-empire|Durrani Empire]] fell apart after 1818, the powerful [[e:barakzai-dynasty|Barakzai]] brothers divided its lands. [[e:kandahar|Kandahar]] went to a group of brothers known as the Kandahar [[e:sardar|Sardars]], led by [[e:purdil-khan|Purdil Khan]] and later [[e:kohandil-khan|Kohandil Khan]], who were half-brothers of [[e:dost-mohammad-khan|Dost Mohammad Khan]] of [[e:kabul|Kabul]].
principality-of-kandahar.r: The [[e:sardar|sardars]] ruled jointly over [[e:kandahar|Kandahar]] and its [[e:pashtuns|Pashtun]] tribes, relying on tribal levies and revenue from trade on the route to [[e:herat|Herat]] and [[e:india|India]]. They negotiated with [[e:persia|Persia]] and [[e:russia|Russia]] as well as with their relatives in [[e:kabul|Kabul]]. During the [[e:first-anglo-afghan-war|First Anglo-Afghan War]] the British occupied Kandahar from 1839 to 1842, and the sardars took refuge in Persia before returning.
principality-of-kandahar.e: After [[e:kohandil-khan|Kohandil Khan]] died in 1855, [[e:dost-mohammad-khan|Dost Mohammad Khan]] seized [[e:kandahar|Kandahar]] and incorporated it into the [[s:emirate-of-afghanistan|Emirate of Afghanistan]], a key step towards reuniting the Afghan lands.

principality-of-kesh.t: A Sogdian principality south of Samarkand, centred on the city later called Shahrisabz, the birthplace of Timur.
principality-of-kesh.o: Kesh lay on the [[e:kashkadarya|Qashqadarya River]] in southern [[s:principality-of-samarkand|Sogdiana]]. It became one of the Sogdian principalities in the 6th century, under the overlordship of the [[s:western-turkic-khaganate|Western Turkic Khaganate]], and was ruled by local lords who issued their own coins.
principality-of-kesh.r: Like its neighbours, Kesh was a town of farmers, craftsmen and merchants governed by a local dynasty and nobility. Chinese sources call it Shi, and it traded through [[e:samarkand|Samarkand]] and over the [[e:iron-gate-central-asia|Iron Gate]] pass to [[e:tokharistan|Tokharistan]]. Very little detail survives about its rulers or institutions.
principality-of-kesh.e: Arab armies conquered Kesh during the campaigns of [[e:qutayba-ibn-muslim|Qutayba ibn Muslim]] in the early 8th century, and it was absorbed into [[e:umayyad-caliphate|Umayyad]] and Abbasid [[e:transoxiana|Transoxiana]]. The city, renamed [[e:shahrisabz|Shahrisabz]], later became the home town of [[e:timur|Timur]].

portuguese-timor.t: Portugal's colony on the eastern half of Timor for nearly three centuries, whose sudden end in 1975 led to Indonesian invasion.
portuguese-timor.o: Dominican missionaries and traders from the Portuguese base on [[e:solor|Solor]] had been active on [[e:timor|Timor]] since the 16th century, buying sandalwood. In 1702 [[e:antonio-coelho-guerreiro|António Coelho Guerreiro]] arrived at [[e:lifau|Lifau]] as the first governor, but real power on the island was long contested by the [[e:topasses|Topasses]], mixed-race Portuguese-speaking warlords.
portuguese-timor.r: Portugal ruled through alliances with local kings (liurai) and the Catholic Church. The capital moved to [[e:dili|Dili]] in 1769. Sandalwood gave way to [[e:coffee-economy|coffee]] in the 19th century, and borders with the [[e:dutch|Dutch]] were settled in 1859 and 1914, leaving the [[e:oecusse|Oecusse]] enclave. Governor [[e:jose-celestino-da-silva|José Celestino da Silva]] extended control by force, and the Manufahi revolt of 1912 was crushed.
portuguese-timor.e: Occupied by [[e:japan|Japan]] from 1942 to 1945 at great cost to its people, the colony returned to Portugal. After the [[e:carnation-revolution|Carnation Revolution]] of 1974 [[e:fretilin|Fretilin]] declared independence in November 1975, but [[s:indonesia|Indonesia]] invaded in December. Independence finally came as [[s:east-timor|East Timor]] in 2002.

pukara.t: The first major political and ceremonial centre of the Lake Titicaca basin, whose stone sculpture and sunken courts foreshadowed the later power of Tiwanaku.
pukara.o: Pukará grew from about 500 BCE on the northern side of the [[e:lake-titicaca|Titicaca]] basin in [[e:puno-region|Puno]], [[e:peru|Peru]]. A large terraced ceremonial complex was built against a red sandstone outcrop, with sunken rectangular courts at its summit. It became the dominant centre of the northern basin.
pukara.r: Pukará is thought to have been a chiefdom or early regional polity whose leaders controlled herding of llamas and alpacas, raised-field farming and trade in obsidian and other goods. It is known for carved stone stelae and statues, including figures holding trophy heads, and for polychrome incised pottery with feline and human images. Its sunken courts and stone sculpture tradition influenced later highland architecture.
pukara.e: The site declined after about 200 CE, and the centre of power in the basin shifted south to [[s:tiwanaku|Tiwanaku]], which absorbed elements of its art and ritual. The modern town of Pucará is known for its ceramic bulls, an unrelated colonial tradition.

poonch-state.t: A Dogra principality subordinate to Jammu and Kashmir, whose 1947 rebellion led to the creation of Azad Kashmir.
poonch-state.o: In 1850 [[e:maharaja|Maharaja]] [[e:gulab-singh|Gulab Singh]] granted Poonch to his nephew [[e:moti-singh-of-poonch|Moti Singh]], son of the [[e:lahore|Lahore]] minister [[e:dhian-singh|Dhian Singh]], as a [[e:jagir|jagir]] under [[s:jammu-and-kashmir-princely-state|Jammu and Kashmir]]. Its rulers held the title of Raja.
poonch-state.r: The Rajas governed a hilly region with a largely Muslim population, many of whom served in the British [[e:indian-army|Indian Army]]. The [[e:maharaja|Maharajas]] of [[s:jammu-and-kashmir-princely-state|Jammu and Kashmir]] repeatedly sought to curtail Poonch's autonomy, and in 1936 its subordinate status was confirmed.
poonch-state.e: In 1947 Muslim ex-servicemen in Poonch rose against [[e:hari-singh|Maharaja Hari Singh's]] government, a rebellion that merged into the war over [[e:kashmir|Kashmir]]. The district was divided by the 1949 ceasefire line between Pakistani-administered [[e:azad-kashmir|Azad Kashmir]] and Indian [[s:jammu-and-kashmir-princely-state|Jammu and Kashmir]].

province-of-pennsylvania.t: William Penn's Quaker colony, a 'holy experiment' in religious freedom whose capital Philadelphia became the largest city in British America.
province-of-pennsylvania.o: In 1681 [[e:charles-ii-of-england|Charles II]] granted [[e:william-penn|William Penn]] a vast tract west of the [[e:delaware-river|Delaware River]] to settle a debt owed to Penn's father. Penn planned a refuge for [[e:quakers|Quakers]] and other persecuted groups, issued a Frame of Government in 1682, laid out [[e:philadelphia|Philadelphia]] on a grid and, by tradition, made a treaty of friendship with the [[e:lenape|Lenape]] at [[e:shackamaxon|Shackamaxon]].
province-of-pennsylvania.r: The Charter of Privileges of 1701 created a single elected assembly and guaranteed freedom of worship to all who believed in God. [[e:quakers|Quakers]], Germans, beginning with [[e:germantown-philadelphia|Germantown]] in 1683, and later [[e:scotch-irish-americans|Scots-Irish]] settlers poured in, and grain exports made [[e:philadelphia|Philadelphia]] prosperous. The [[e:william-penn|Penn]] heirs remained proprietors, and the Walking Purchase of 1737 cheated the [[e:lenape|Lenape]] of land. [[e:benjamin-franklin|Benjamin Franklin]] made Philadelphia a centre of [[e:printing-press|printing]], science and civic institutions.
province-of-pennsylvania.e: [[e:philadelphia|Philadelphia]] hosted the [[e:continental-congress|Continental Congress]], which declared independence there in 1776. That year [[e:pennsylvania|Pennsylvania]] adopted a radical democratic constitution, ending proprietary rule, and became a state of the [[s:united-states|United States]].
