principality-of-reuss-greiz.t: The Elder Line of the house of Reuss, ruling from Greiz, one of the smallest states of the German Empire.
principality-of-reuss-greiz.o: In the division of the [[e:house-of-reuss|Reuss]] lands in 1564, the Elder Line received [[e:greiz|Greiz]] and the surrounding part of the [[s:lordship-of-plauen|Vogtland]]. After a split into Upper and Lower Greiz, the branches were reunited in 1768, and in 1778 [[e:heinrich-xi-prince-reuss-of-greiz|Heinrich XI]] was raised to prince of the empire.
principality-of-reuss-greiz.r: Like their cousins, all male members were named Heinrich, but the Elder Line numbered them in a sequence that restarted at intervals. The principality was small, Lutheran and agrarian, later with textile mills in [[e:greiz|Greiz]] and Zeulenroda. Its upper and lower castles still dominate the town.
principality-of-reuss-greiz.e: [[e:house-of-reuss|Reuss]] Elder Line sided with [[e:austria|Austria]] in 1866 and was occupied by [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]], but joined the [[s:german-empire|German Empire]] in 1871, and Prince [[e:heinrich-xxii-prince-reuss-of-greiz|Heinrich XXII]] remained a noted opponent of Prussian policy. After the revolution of 1918 it merged with the Younger Line in 1919 into the [[s:peoples-state-of-reuss|People's State of Reuss]], part of [[e:thuringia|Thuringia]] from 1920.

piedmontese-republic.t: The provisional republic set up in Piedmont after the French forced King Charles Emmanuel IV to abandon the mainland in 1798.
piedmontese-republic.o: In December 1798 French troops occupied [[e:turin|Turin]] and forced [[e:charles-emmanuel-iv-of-sardinia|Charles Emmanuel IV]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-sardinia|Kingdom of Sardinia]] to give up his mainland states and withdraw to the island of [[e:sardinia|Sardinia]]. A provisional government of Piedmontese patriots took over in Turin, proclaiming a republic.
piedmontese-republic.r: The provisional government abolished feudal rights and noble titles and held votes in which the Piedmontese communities asked to be annexed to [[e:france|France]]; the [[s:french-first-republic|French Directory]] approved the annexation in early 1799. Real power lay with French commissioners and generals, and French requisitions caused unrest in the countryside.
piedmontese-republic.e: In 1799 the Austro-Russian army under [[e:alexander-suvorov|Suvorov]] drove the French out of [[e:piedmont|Piedmont]], ending the regime. After [[e:napoleon|Napoleon's]] victory at [[e:battle-of-marengo|Marengo]] in 1800, the French set up the [[s:subalpine-republic|Subalpine Republic]].

principality-of-mingrelia.t: A western Georgian principality ruled by the Dadiani princes, which under Levan II dominated western Georgia and kept autonomy until 1867.
principality-of-mingrelia.o: Mingrelia, or Odishi, the lowland between the Rioni and the [[e:enguri|Inguri]], had been governed by the [[e:house-of-dadiani|Dadiani]] family as eristavis since the [[e:middle-ages|Middle Ages]]. As the [[s:kingdom-of-imereti|Kingdom of Imereti]] weakened, the Dadiani became effectively independent, and from 1557 they ruled as sovereign princes, paying tribute to the [[s:ottoman-empire|Ottoman Empire]].
principality-of-mingrelia.r: The princes ruled from [[e:zugdidi|Zugdidi]] and other residences over nobles and a largely enserfed peasantry. [[e:levan-ii-dadiani|Levan II Dadiani]], from 1611, made Mingrelia the leading power of western [[s:georgia|Georgia]], fighting [[s:kingdom-of-imereti|Imereti]] and [[s:principality-of-abkhazia|Abkhazia]]; Catholic missionaries such as [[e:arcangelo-lamberti|Arcangelo Lamberti]] described his court. The [[e:atlantic-slave-trade|slave trade]] with Ottoman ports was a lasting curse. The Mingrelian language was spoken alongside Georgian.
principality-of-mingrelia.e: [[e:grigol-dadiani|Grigol Dadiani]] accepted a Russian [[e:protectorate|protectorate]] in 1803. After the [[e:crimean-war|Crimean War]] and a peasant revolt, [[e:russia|Russia]] took over the administration in 1857 and formally annexed the principality in 1867. Princess [[e:ekaterine-dadiani|Ekaterine Dadiani]] was the last ruling figure.

principality-of-moldavia.t: Romanian principality between the Carpathians and the Dniester, celebrated for Stephen the Great and its painted monasteries, which merged with Wallachia in 1859.
principality-of-moldavia.o: Around 1346 the Hungarian king sent [[e:dragos-voivode-of-moldavia|Dragoș]], a Romanian noble from [[e:maramures|Maramureș]], to set up a march east of the [[e:carpathian-mountains|Carpathians]] against the [[s:golden-horde|Golden Horde]]. In 1359 another Maramureș noble, [[e:bogdan-i-of-moldavia|Bogdan I]], drove out Dragoș's heirs and made Moldavia independent of [[e:hungary|Hungary]].
principality-of-moldavia.r: The voivode ruled with boyars and the [[e:eastern-orthodox-church|Orthodox Church]] from [[e:suceava|Suceava]] and, after 1564, Iași. [[e:alexander-the-good|Alexander the Good]] gave the country stable institutions. [[e:stephen-the-great|Stephen the Great]] (1457–1504) defeated the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]] at [[e:battle-of-vaslui|Vaslui]] in 1475 and built churches such as [[e:putna-monastery|Putna]] and [[e:voronet-monastery|Voroneț]]; Voroneț and other Moldavian churches received their famous exterior frescoes in the 16th century. From the 16th century Moldavia paid tribute to the Ottomans, and from 1711 to 1821 it was ruled by [[e:phanariotes|Phanariot]] princes.
principality-of-moldavia.e: It lost [[s:duchy-of-bukovina|Bukovina]] to [[e:austria|Austria]] in 1775 and [[e:bessarabia|Bessarabia]] to [[e:russia|Russia]] in 1812. In 1859 it elected [[e:alexandru-ioan-cuza|Alexandru Ioan Cuza]], as did the [[s:principality-of-wallachia|Principality of Wallachia]], creating the union that became [[s:kingdom-of-romania|Romania]].

peloponnesian-league.t: Sparta's network of alliances, the leading military coalition of classical Greece and Athens' opponent in the Peloponnesian War.
peloponnesian-league.o: The league grew in the mid-6th century BCE when [[s:sparta|Sparta]], after defeating [[s:tegea|Tegea]] around 550 BCE, turned from conquest to alliance. City by city, Peloponnesian states such as Tegea, [[s:corinth|Corinth]], [[s:elis|Elis]] and later [[s:megara|Megara]] swore to have the same friends and enemies as the Lacedaemonians and to follow them wherever they led.
peloponnesian-league.r: There was no common treasury or capital beyond [[s:sparta|Sparta]]. Each ally was bound to [[e:sparta|Sparta]] by its own treaty; from the late 6th century a congress of allies voted on war, each city having one vote, and Sparta commanded the joint army. Sparta favoured friendly oligarchies in member cities. The league formed the core of Greek resistance to [[e:persia|Persia]] in 480-479 BCE.
peloponnesian-league.e: It fought and won the [[e:peloponnesian-war|Peloponnesian War]] against the [[s:delian-league|Delian League]] (431-404 BCE), but the Theban victory at [[e:battle-of-leuctra|Leuctra]] in 371 BCE and invasions of [[e:laconia|Laconia]] broke [[e:sparta|Sparta's]] hold. The liberation of [[s:messene|Messenia]] and separate peace deals by [[s:corinth|Corinth]] and others in 366-365 BCE ended the league.

perge.t: Perge, a Greek city of the Pamphylian plain, famous for its sanctuary of Artemis and the mathematician Apollonius.
perge.o: Greek tradition says Perge was founded after the [[e:trojan-war|Trojan War]] by heroes such as [[e:mopsus|Mopsus]] and [[e:calchas|Calchas]], and a city called Parha appears in a Hittite treaty. By the 7th century BCE it was a Greek-speaking city near the coast, inland on the [[e:kestros|Kestros]] river.
perge.r: Perge was a self-governing city whose patron was [[e:artemis-pergaia|Artemis Pergaia]], worshipped at a rich temple. It surrendered to Alexander of the [[s:macedonian-empire|Macedonian Empire]] in 333 BCE and later passed through [[e:seleucid-empire|Seleucid]] and [[e:attalid-dynasty|Attalid]] rule. The mathematician [[e:apollonius-of-perga|Apollonius of Perga]] wrote his work on conic sections in the 3rd century BCE.
perge.e: Perge came under Roman control, and in 25 BCE it became part of the Roman province of [[s:galatia|Galatia]], later [[e:pamphylia|Pamphylia]]. Its finest monuments, including colonnaded streets and a [[e:theatre|theatre]], date from the Roman period.

pagania.t: Slavic principality of the Narentines between the Cetina and Neretva, whose pirate fleets challenged Venice for two centuries.
pagania.o: The Narentines were [[e:slavs|Slavs]] who settled the coast between the [[e:cetina|Cetina]] and [[e:neretva|Neretva]] rivers in the 7th century. By the 9th century they formed a principality, called Pagania by the [[e:byzantine-empire|Byzantines]] because they accepted [[e:christianity|Christianity]] late. [[e:constantine-vii|Constantine VII]] lists its towns, including Mokro and Ostrog, and the islands of [[e:brac|Brač]], [[e:hvar|Hvar]], [[e:korcula|Korčula]] and [[e:mljet|Mljet]].
pagania.r: Ruled by its own princes and assembly of clans, Pagania lived largely from the sea, raiding and taxing Adriatic shipping. [[e:venice|Venice]] had to pay for safe passage, and in 887 the Narentines killed Doge [[e:pietro-i-candiano|Pietro I Candiano]] in battle. They accepted Byzantine missionaries in the late 9th century.
pagania.e: In 1000 Doge [[e:pietro-ii-orseolo|Pietro II Orseolo]] led a fleet that broke Narentine sea power. Pagania then came under the [[s:kingdom-of-croatia-925-1102|Kingdom of Croatia]] (925-1102) and later [[s:zachlumia|Zachlumia]], and the name fades by the 11th century.

principality-of-montenegro.t: Secular Montenegrin principality of the Petrović-Njegoš dynasty, which won international recognition of its independence at the Congress of Berlin.
principality-of-montenegro.o: In 1852 [[e:danilo-i-prince-of-montenegro|Danilo Petrović-Njegoš]], heir of the [[s:prince-bishopric-of-montenegro|Prince-Bishopric of Montenegro]], declined to become a [[e:bishop|bishop]] and proclaimed himself secular prince with Russian backing. He issued a legal code in 1855, imposed taxes on the clans, and his brother [[e:mirko-petrovic-njegos|Mirko Petrović]] defeated the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]] at [[e:battle-of-grahovac|Grahovac]] in 1858, after which Montenegro's borders were first drawn.
principality-of-montenegro.r: After [[e:danilo-i-prince-of-montenegro|Danilo]]'s assassination in 1860, his nephew Nikola ruled for over half a century as a patriarchal autocrat from [[e:cetinje|Cetinje]], where foreign legations were built. [[s:montenegro|Montenegro]] remained a poor land of clans and herders, heavily subsidised by [[e:russia|Russia]]. Nikola married his daughters into the royal houses of [[e:italy|Italy]], [[s:serbia|Serbia]] and Russia, and granted a constitution only in 1905.
principality-of-montenegro.e: War against the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]] in 1876 to 1878 won recognition of independence at [[e:berlin|Berlin]] in 1878, nearly doubling the territory and gaining [[e:niksic|Nikšić]], [[e:podgorica|Podgorica]], [[e:bar-montenegro|Bar]] and later [[e:ulcinj|Ulcinj]]. On his jubilee in 1910 Nikola proclaimed the [[s:kingdom-of-montenegro|Kingdom of Montenegro]].

palitana-state.t: A Gohil Rajput state in Saurashtra whose territory held Shatrunjaya, the hill of nearly a thousand Jain temples and one of Jainism's holiest sites.
palitana-state.o: Palitana was ruled by a branch of the [[e:gohil|Gohil Rajputs]], the clan that also ruled [[s:bhavnagar-state|Bhavnagar State]]; the Gohils entered [[e:kathiawar|Saurashtra]] in the 13th century, and tradition gives Palitana's line an early date. Firm records are mainly from the 17th century onward.
palitana-state.r: The state's fame came from [[e:shatrunjaya|Shatrunjaya]] hill, covered with Jain temples built over many centuries by merchant patrons. The Thakore levied payments on pilgrims, which led to long disputes with the Jain community's trust, [[e:anandji-kalyanji-trust|Anandji Kalyanji]]. British officials brokered a series of agreements in the 19th century fixing an annual sum paid by the [[e:jainism|Jains]].
palitana-state.e: Palitana joined the [[s:saurashtra-state|United State of Saurashtra]] in 1948 and is now a town in [[s:bhavnagar-state|Bhavnagar]] district, [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]]. [[e:shatrunjaya|Shatrunjaya]] remains a major pilgrimage centre.

cr.a: Dr. Andreas Birken at German Wikipedia

paros.t: Cycladic island famed for its fine white marble and its poet Archilochus, and coloniser of Thasos.
paros.o: Paros, in the central [[e:cyclades|Cyclades]], was settled by [[e:ionia|Ionian Greeks]] in the early [[e:iron-age|Iron Age]]. Its translucent marble, quarried in underground galleries, became the prized stone of Greek sculptors. By the 7th century BCE Paros was strong enough to colonise [[s:thasos|Thasos]] c. 680 BCE and later [[e:parion|Parion]] on the [[e:hellespont|Hellespont]].
paros.r: [[e:archilochus|Archilochus]], a pioneering lyric and iambic poet, was a Parian who joined the settlement of [[s:thasos|Thasos]]. Paros was a commercial and religious centre with a temple of [[e:demeter|Demeter]]. It supported [[e:persia|Persia]] in 490 BCE, and the Athenian [[e:miltiades|Miltiades]] failed to take it in 489 BCE. In the [[s:delian-league|Delian League]] Paros paid one of the largest island tributes.
paros.e: Paros came under Hellenistic kings and later Roman control by 146 BCE. Its inscribed Parian Chronicle of 264 BCE, now in [[e:oxford|Oxford]], is a key source for Greek chronology, and Parian marble remained in demand.

petrocorii.t: Gallic people of the Dordogne whose name lives on in the Périgord and whose town Vesunna became Périgueux.
petrocorii.o: The Petrocorii lived in the valleys of the [[e:isle-river|Isle]] and the [[e:dordogne|Dordogne]], in the modern Dordogne. Their name is usually read as the four armies, perhaps a league of four communities. [[e:strabo|Strabo]] notes their iron workings.
petrocorii.r: Little is known of their rulers. Their main oppidum stood at La Curade near [[e:perigueux|Périgueux]].
petrocorii.e: They sent five thousand men to relieve [[e:battle-of-alesia|Alesia]] in 52 BCE. Under [[e:rome|Rome]] their capital was [[e:perigueux|Vesunna]], a well-preserved town whose temple tower, the [[e:tour-de-vesone|Tour de Vésone]], still stands. The city became Périgueux, and the medieval [[s:county-of-perigord|County of Périgord]] kept their name.

cr.a: Pétrocores (peuple celtique de Gaule). Autorité émettrice de monnaie

pinya-kingdom.t: A short-lived central Burmese kingdom founded by Thihathu in 1313, rival of Sagaing and forerunner of the Ava Kingdom.
pinya-kingdom.o: [[e:thihathu|Thihathu]], the last surviving of the three [[s:myinsaing-kingdom|Myinsaing]] brothers, founded a new capital at Pinya near the [[e:kyaukse|Kyaukse]] [[e:rice|rice]] lands in 1313 and proclaimed himself heir to the Pagan kings. His son [[e:saw-yun|Saw Yun]] soon broke away and set up a rival court at [[s:sagaing-kingdom|Sagaing]] in 1315.
pinya-kingdom.r: Pinya ruled the [[e:kyaukse|Kyaukse]] granary and parts of central [[s:myanmar|Myanmar]], but its kings struggled with rebellious [[e:vassal|vassals]], the breakaway [[s:sagaing-kingdom|Sagaing Kingdom]] and Shan raids from the north. Royal patronage of [[e:buddhism|Buddhism]] continued, and the court maintained Pagan-era titles and administration on a smaller scale. [[e:uzana-i-of-pinya|Uzana I]] and [[e:kyawswa-i-of-pinya|Kyawswa I]] were among its kings.
pinya-kingdom.e: In 1364 Shan forces from [[s:mong-mao|Mong Mao]] sacked both Pinya and [[s:sagaing-kingdom|Sagaing]]. [[e:thado-minbya|Thado Minbya]], a prince of the Sagaing line linked to the Pinya house, reunited the region and in 1365 founded the [[s:ava-kingdom|Ava Kingdom]] at a new capital nearby, which absorbed Pinya.

principality-of-reuss-ebersdorf.t: Tiny Reuss lordship in Thuringia that became a stronghold of Pietism and the Moravian Brethren.
principality-of-reuss-ebersdorf.o: Ebersdorf was separated from Reuss-[[e:bad-lobenstein|Lobenstein]] in 1678 for [[e:heinrich-x-reuss-of-ebersdorf|Heinrich X]], a younger son of the Lobenstein line, creating a small county within the Younger Line of the [[e:house-of-reuss|House of Reuss]] in the [[e:thuringian-highlands|Thuringian Highlands]].
principality-of-reuss-ebersdorf.r: The counts of Ebersdorf were devout [[e:pietism|Pietists]] who turned their small residence into a religious centre. Count [[e:nikolaus-ludwig-von-zinzendorf|Nikolaus Ludwig von Zinzendorf]], founder of the renewed [[e:moravian-church|Moravian Church]] at [[e:herrnhut|Herrnhut]], married [[e:erdmuthe-dorothea-von-zinzendorf|Erdmuthe Dorothea of Reuss-Ebersdorf]] in 1722, and a Moravian congregation settled in Ebersdorf. [[e:queen-victoria|Queen Victoria's]] maternal grandmother came from the family. The rulers became princes in 1806.
principality-of-reuss-ebersdorf.e: Ebersdorf inherited Reuss-[[e:bad-lobenstein|Lobenstein]] in 1824. Prince [[e:heinrich-lxxii-prince-reuss-of-lobenstein-and-ebersdorf|Heinrich LXXII]], an eccentric absolutist, abdicated during the revolution of 1848, and his lands passed to Reuss-[[e:schleiz|Schleiz]], forming the [[e:principality-of-reuss-younger-line|Principality of Reuss Younger Line]].

perlis.t: Smallest state of Malaysia, separated from Kedah by Siam in 1843 and ruled by a dynasty of Arab descent.
perlis.o: After suppressing revolts in the [[s:kedah-sultanate|Kedah Sultanate]] in the 1830s, Siam divided the sultanate and in 1843 created Perlis as a separate dependency. Its first raja was [[e:syed-hussain-jamalullail|Syed Hussain Jamalullail]], a Kedah noble of Hadhrami Arab descent, whose family has ruled ever since with the title of raja rather than sultan.
perlis.r: Perlis was a small [[e:rice|rice]]-growing state on the Thai border, with limestone hills, [[e:tin|tin]] and a modest population of Malay farmers. It sent tribute to [[e:bangkok|Bangkok]] and was governed by the raja with a small council. The royal seat was at [[e:arau|Arau]], and Islamic law and Malay custom shaped administration.
perlis.e: The [[e:anglo-siamese-treaty-of-1909|Anglo-Siamese Treaty of 1909]] transferred Perlis to British protection; it accepted a British adviser and became one of the [[s:unfederated-malay-states|Unfederated Malay States]]. It later joined the [[s:federation-of-malaya|Federation of Malaya]] and [[s:malaysia|Malaysia]], and Raja [[e:tuanku-syed-sirajuddin|Tuanku Syed Sirajuddin]] served as king from 2001 to 2006.

province-of-santo-domingo-1861-1865.t: Spain's brief reannexation of the Dominican Republic, the only time a former Spanish American colony returned to Spanish rule, ended by the War of Restoration.
province-of-santo-domingo-1861-1865.o: Facing debt, political rivalry and the threat of invasion from [[s:republic-of-haiti|Haiti]], President [[e:pedro-santana|Pedro Santana]] arranged for the [[s:first-dominican-republic|First Dominican Republic]] to be annexed by [[e:spain|Spain]], proclaimed on 18 March 1861. Spain, under [[e:isabella-ii-of-spain|Queen Isabella II]] and the government of [[e:leopoldo-odonnell|Leopoldo O'Donnell]], accepted, partly to strengthen its position in the [[e:caribbean|Caribbean]] while the [[s:united-states|United States]] was engulfed in civil war.
province-of-santo-domingo-1861-1865.r: [[e:pedro-santana|Santana]] became captain general but resigned in 1862 as Spanish officials took over. The new regime offended Dominicans: it imposed Spanish officials and soldiers, new taxes and church rules, and treated mixed-race and black Dominicans with contempt, raising fears that [[e:slavery|slavery]] would return. Early revolts were suppressed with executions, including that of [[e:francisco-del-rosario-sanchez|Francisco del Rosario Sánchez]] in 1861.
province-of-santo-domingo-1861-1865.e: In August 1863 rebels raised the flag at Capotillo, starting the [[e:dominican-restoration-war|War of Restoration]], with [[s:spanish-jamaica|Santiago]] as their capital and [[e:gregorio-luperon|Gregorio Luperón]] among the leaders. Disease and [[e:guerrilla-warfare|guerrilla]] warfare broke the Spanish army. [[e:spain|Spain]] repealed the annexation in March 1865 and left in July, creating the [[s:second-dominican-republic|Second Dominican Republic]].

palatinate-veldenz.t: A small Wittelsbach duchy on the Glan and in the northern Vosges, created in 1543 for a younger branch of the Zweibrücken line.
palatinate-veldenz.o: By the Treaty of [[e:marburg|Marburg]] in 1543, [[e:count-palatine|Count Palatine]] Rupert, uncle and former guardian of [[e:wolfgang-count-palatine-of-zweibrucken|Duke Wolfgang of Palatinate-Zweibrücken]], received the old [[s:county-of-veldenz|County of Veldenz]] with [[e:lauterecken|Lauterecken]] and lands in the [[e:vosges|Vosges]], founding the line of Palatinate-Veldenz.
palatinate-veldenz.r: The dukes ruled from [[e:lauterecken|Lauterecken]] and from [[e:la-petite-pierre|Lützelstein]] (La Petite-Pierre) in the northern [[e:vosges|Vosges]], a scattered and poor territory of farming villages. They were Lutheran, and Duke [[e:george-john-i-count-palatine-of-veldenz|George John]] founded the town of [[e:phalsbourg|Phalsbourg]] in 1570. The [[e:thirty-years-war|Thirty Years' War]] and [[e:louis-xiv|Louis XIV's]] [[e:reunions|Reunions]], which claimed the Vosges lands for [[e:france|France]] after 1680, devastated the little state.
palatinate-veldenz.e: When Duke [[e:leopold-louis-count-palatine-of-veldenz|Leopold Louis]] died without male heirs in 1694, a long inheritance dispute followed among the Palatine branches. It was settled only in 1733, when the lands were shared among the [[s:electoral-palatinate|Electoral Palatinate]] and other Wittelsbach lines.

cr.a: Gustav Droysen; derivative work by Beckstet

portuguese-ceylon.t: The Portuguese colony on the coasts of Sri Lanka, created by the bequest of the last Kotte king and lost to the Dutch.
portuguese-ceylon.o: The Portuguese had held a fort at [[e:colombo|Colombo]] since the early 16th century and dominated the [[s:kingdom-of-kotte|Kingdom of Kotte]]. When its Christian king [[e:dharmapala-of-kotte|Dharmapala]] died in 1597, the Portuguese Crown claimed his realm under his will, making the Sinhalese lowlands a colony; [[e:jaffna|Jaffna]] was added in 1619.
portuguese-ceylon.r: The colony was administered by a captain-general at [[e:colombo|Colombo]] under the [[e:viceroy-of-india|viceroy]] of [[s:portuguese-india|Portuguese India]]. The Portuguese drew revenue from [[e:cinnamon|cinnamon]], collected by [[e:salagama|Salagama]] peelers as a service obligation, and from areca and elephants. Catholic missions converted many coastal people, especially fishing communities, and Portuguese words entered [[e:sinhala-language|Sinhala]] and Tamil. Repeated campaigns against the [[s:kingdom-of-kandy|Kingdom of Kandy]] failed.
portuguese-ceylon.e: The [[s:dutch-east-india-company-territories|Dutch East India Company]], allied with [[e:rajasinha-ii-of-kandy|Rajasinha II of Kandy]], captured [[e:galle|Galle]] in 1640, [[e:colombo|Colombo]] in 1656 and [[e:jaffna|Jaffna]] in 1658, ending Portuguese rule. The [[e:dutch|Dutch]] kept the coast, creating [[s:dutch-ceylon|Dutch Ceylon]].

cr.a: myself, based on ancient national symbol.

prince-bishopric-of-constance.t: The temporal lordship of the bishops of Germany's largest medieval diocese, ruled from Meersburg after the Reformation drove them from Constance.
prince-bishopric-of-constance.o: [[e:konstanz|Constance]] became a bishopric around 600, serving the [[s:alemanni|Alemanni]], and grew into the largest diocese of the German lands, stretching from the [[e:alps|Alps]] to the [[e:neckar|Neckar]]. In 1155 [[e:frederick-barbarossa|Frederick Barbarossa]] confirmed the [[e:bishop|bishop]]'s possessions and rights, the basis of a small secular territory around [[e:lake-constance|Lake Constance]].
prince-bishopric-of-constance.r: The city of [[e:konstanz|Constance]] became an imperial city independent of its [[e:bishop|bishop]] and hosted the [[e:council-of-constance|Council of Constance]] from 1414 to 1418, which ended the [[e:western-schism|Western Schism]] and burned [[e:jan-hus|Jan Hus]]. The bishops acquired the [[e:reichenau-island|Reichenau]] abbey in 1540. After Constance became Protestant in 1527, they moved to [[e:meersburg|Meersburg]], where they built a baroque New Palace.
prince-bishopric-of-constance.e: In 1803 the prince-bishopric was secularised and its lands went to [[e:baden|Baden]]. The diocese itself was dissolved in 1821, its parts divided between the new [[e:archdiocese-of-freiburg|Archdiocese of Freiburg]] and Swiss dioceses.

portuguese-syriam.t: A Portuguese adventurer's private fief at the port of Syriam in Lower Burma, which lasted fourteen years before the Burmese retook it.
portuguese-syriam.o: [[e:filipe-de-brito-e-nicote|Filipe de Brito e Nicote]], a Portuguese [[e:mercenary|mercenary]] in the service of the king of the [[s:mrauk-u-kingdom|Mrauk U Kingdom]], was placed in charge of the port of Syriam, near present-day [[e:yangon|Yangon]], after the fall of [[e:bago|Pegu]] in 1599. He soon turned it into his own base, obtained backing from the Portuguese [[e:viceroy-of-india|viceroy]] in [[e:goa|Goa]] and was recognised as its governor.
portuguese-syriam.r: [[e:filipe-de-brito-e-nicote|De Brito]] ruled with a small Portuguese garrison and local allies, collecting customs on the [[e:rice|rice]] and [[e:timber|timber]] trade and controlling access to the [[e:irrawaddy-river|Irrawaddy]]. He built a fort and church, encouraged Catholic conversions and allied with local [[e:mon-people|Mon]] leaders. He was notorious among Burmese for looting pagodas to melt down their bells for [[e:field-artillery|cannon]].
portuguese-syriam.e: [[e:anaukpetlun|Anaukpetlun]] of the [[s:restored-toungoo-kingdom|Restored Toungoo Kingdom]] besieged Syriam in 1613 and took it after a few months. [[e:filipe-de-brito-e-nicote|De Brito]] was executed by impalement, and the Portuguese captives were resettled in [[e:upper-burma|Upper Burma]] as royal gunners, where their descendants, the Bayingyi, still live.

principality-of-albania.t: Albania's first internationally recognised state, a principality that survived foreign occupation in the First World War and was rebuilt as a nation in 1920.
principality-of-albania.o: The [[e:conference-of-ambassadors|Conference of Ambassadors]] in [[e:london|London]] made [[s:albania|Albania]] an independent principality under the Great Powers' guarantee and chose the German [[e:william-prince-of-albania|Prince Wilhelm of Wied]] as ruler. He arrived in [[e:durres|Durrës]] on 7 March 1914, replacing the [[s:provisional-government-of-albania|Provisional Government of Albania]] and [[e:essad-pasha-toptani|Essad Pasha]]'s [[s:republic-of-central-albania|Republic of Central Albania]].
principality-of-albania.r: Wied's rule collapsed within months amid [[e:essad-pasha-toptani|Essad]]'s intrigues, a Muslim peasant revolt in central [[s:albania|Albania]] and Greek-backed autonomy in the south; he left in September 1914. During the [[e:first-world-war|First World War]] Italian, Austrian, Serbian, Greek and French troops occupied the country. The [[e:congress-of-lushnje|Congress of Lushnjë]] in 1920 created a regency council, moved the capital to [[e:tirana|Tirana]] and secured [[e:league-of-nations|League of Nations]] membership.
principality-of-albania.e: The 1920s saw instability, with [[e:fan-noli|Fan Noli's]] [[e:june-revolution-albania|June Revolution]] of 1924 overthrown by [[e:zog-i|Ahmet Zogu]] in December. In January 1925 a constituent assembly abolished the principality and created the [[s:albanian-republic|Albanian Republic]], with Zogu as president.
principality-of-albania.re: Sunni Islam, Orthodox and Catholic Christianity

principality-of-schwarzenberg.t: Franconian territory of the Schwarzenberg family, whose princes became some of the greatest landowners and statesmen of the Habsburg monarchy.
principality-of-schwarzenberg.o: The lords of Seinsheim took the name Schwarzenberg from a castle near [[e:scheinfeld|Scheinfeld]] in [[e:franconia|Franconia]] in the 15th century. In 1599 the family was raised to the rank of imperial counts, and in 1670 [[e:johann-adolf-i-prince-of-schwarzenberg|Johann Adolf von Schwarzenberg]], a senior adviser of [[e:leopold-i-holy-roman-emperor|Emperor Leopold]] I, was made a prince of the Empire, with the lands around Scheinfeld forming the core of the family's immediate territory.
principality-of-schwarzenberg.r: The Franconian lands were small, but the family's real weight lay in service to the [[e:habsburg-dynasty|Habsburgs]] and in vast estates acquired in [[s:kingdom-of-bohemia|Bohemia]], including [[e:hluboka-nad-vltavou|Frauenberg]] (Hluboká), bought in 1661, and [[e:cesky-krumlov|Krumau]] (Český Krumlov), inherited from the [[e:house-of-eggenberg|Eggenberg]] family in 1719. The territory was Catholic and administered by officials while the princes lived at court in [[e:vienna|Vienna]] or on their Bohemian estates.
principality-of-schwarzenberg.e: In 1806 the Franconian lands were mediatised and placed under the [[s:kingdom-of-bavaria|Kingdom of Bavaria]]. The family remained prominent: [[e:karl-philipp-prince-of-schwarzenberg|Karl Philipp zu Schwarzenberg]] commanded the allied armies at [[e:leipzig|Leipzig]] in 1813, and [[e:felix-zu-schwarzenberg|Felix zu Schwarzenberg]] led the [[e:austrian-empire|Austrian Empire's]] government after the 1848 revolution.

plymouth-colony.t: The settlement founded by the Mayflower Pilgrims in 1620, remembered for the Mayflower Compact and the 1621 harvest feast with the Wampanoag.
plymouth-colony.o: English Separatists who had left the [[e:church-of-england|Church of England]], many of them after years of exile in [[e:leiden|Leiden]], sailed on the [[e:mayflower|Mayflower]] in 1620 and landed at Plymouth on [[e:cape-cod-bay|Cape Cod Bay]]. Before landing, 41 men signed the [[e:mayflower-compact|Mayflower Compact]], agreeing to form a civil body politic. Half the settlers died in the first winter.
plymouth-colony.r: The Pilgrims survived with help from the [[s:wampanoag-confederacy|Wampanoag Confederacy]], whose sachem [[e:massasoit|Massasoit]] made an alliance with them in 1621. [[e:william-bradford-governor|William Bradford]], governor for most years until 1657, wrote the history [[e:of-plymouth-plantation|Of Plymouth Plantation]]. The colony had no royal charter, governing itself through an annual General Court of freemen, and lived by farming, fishing and the [[e:fur-trade|fur trade]]. It remained small, with perhaps 7,000 people by 1690.
plymouth-colony.e: [[e:king-philips-war|King Philip's War]] in 1675 to 1676 devastated the colony. It was absorbed into the [[s:dominion-of-new-england|Dominion of New England]] in 1686, and after that collapsed, the charter of 1691 merged Plymouth into the [[s:province-of-massachusetts-bay|Province of Massachusetts Bay]].

political-committee-of-national-liberati.t: The 'Mountain Government' created by the Greek resistance in 1944, which held the first Greek elections in which women voted.
political-committee-of-national-liberati.o: By 1944 the left-wing resistance movement [[e:national-liberation-front-greece|EAM]] and its army [[e:greek-peoples-liberation-army|ELAS]] controlled much of mountainous [[e:greece|Greece]]. On 10 March 1944 EAM created the Political Committee of National Liberation (PEEA) at Viniani in [[e:evrytania|Evrytania]], as a rival to both the collaborationist [[s:hellenic-state-1941-1944|Hellenic State]] and the government-in-exile in [[e:cairo|Cairo]].
political-committee-of-national-liberati.r: PEEA was led first by [[e:evripidis-bakirtzis|Colonel Evripidis Bakirtzis]] and then by the law professor [[e:alexandros-svolos|Alexandros Svolos]]. It organised local self-government, people's courts and schools in liberated areas, and in April 1944 held elections for a National Council, which met at Koryschades; women voted for the first time in [[e:greece|Greece]]. The Greek forces in [[e:egypt|Egypt]] mutinied in its support.
political-committee-of-national-liberati.e: At the [[s:lebanese-republic|Lebanon]] Conference in May 1944, PEEA agreed to join a government of national unity under [[e:georgios-papandreou|Georgios Papandreou]], and its ministers entered that government in September. It dissolved after liberation in November 1944, shortly before fighting in [[s:athens|Athens]] began.

principality-of-chach.t: The early medieval principality of the Tashkent oasis, a Sogdian-Turkic borderland whose ruler's execution helped bring about the Battle of Talas.
principality-of-chach.o: [[e:tashkent|Chach]], or Shash, was the oasis on the [[e:chirchiq-river|Chirchiq River]] where Tashkent now stands. It emerged as a principality in the 6th century, closely tied to the [[s:western-turkic-khaganate|Western Turkic Khaganate]], whose rulers often installed Turkic tuduns or relatives as local lords alongside a Sogdian-speaking population.
principality-of-chach.r: [[e:tashkent|Chach]] controlled a fertile irrigated plain at the meeting point of farmland and steppe, trading with Turkic nomads and producing [[e:silver|silver]] and weapons. Its coins blended Sogdian and Turkic features, and the ruling house bore Turkic titles. Chinese sources call it Shi, the 'stone' country.
principality-of-chach.e: In 750 the [[s:later-tang|Tang]] general [[e:gao-xianzhi|Gao Xianzhi]] executed the ruler of [[e:tashkent|Chach]], whose son sought help from the [[e:abbasid-caliphate|Abbasids]]; the resulting [[e:battle-of-talas|Battle of Talas]] in 751 ended Chinese influence west of the [[e:tian-shan|Tian Shan]]. Chach then came under Muslim rule, later as part of the [[s:samanid-empire|Samanid Empire]].

peoples-state-of-reuss.t: Brief Thuringian republic uniting the two old Reuss principalities before they merged into Thuringia.
peoples-state-of-reuss.o: The Principality of [[s:principality-of-reuss-greiz|Reuss Elder Line]] at [[e:greiz|Greiz]] and the [[e:principality-of-reuss-younger-line|Principality of Reuss Younger Line]] at Gera both became free states in November 1918 after their princes abdicated. In April 1919 the two united as the People's State of Reuss, with Gera as capital.
peoples-state-of-reuss.r: The state was industrial, with textile and machine-building works around Gera and [[e:greiz|Greiz]], and its politics were dominated by the Social Democrats and [[e:independent-social-democratic-party-of-germany|Independent Socialists]]. It existed mainly to manage the transition from monarchy and to negotiate the union of the small Thuringian states.
peoples-state-of-reuss.e: On 1 May 1920 the People's State of Reuss merged with six other states to form the [[s:free-state-of-thuringia|Free State of Thuringia]]. Gera, its capital, became one of [[e:thuringia|Thuringia's]] main industrial cities and later a district capital in [[e:east-germany|East Germany]].

prince-bishopric-of-verden.t: Small church principality between the Weser and Elbe, rooted in Charlemagne's conquest of the Saxons and handed to Sweden in 1648.
prince-bishopric-of-verden.o: The diocese of [[e:verden|Verden]] was founded around 800 in the wake of [[e:charlemagne|Charlemagne's]] wars against the [[s:saxons|Saxons]]. Its [[e:bishop|bishops]] acquired estates on the [[e:aller|Aller]] and the lower [[e:weser|Weser]]. After the fall of [[e:henry-the-lion|Henry the Lion]] in 1180 they ruled a secular territory as imperial princes, though their cathedral city of Verden was largely self-governing and they resided at [[e:rotenburg-an-der-wumme|Rotenburg]].
prince-bishopric-of-verden.r: The territory was a thinly settled land of heath and moor. Its [[e:bishop|bishops]] were usually drawn from the princely houses of northern [[e:germany|Germany]], especially Brunswick-[[e:luneburg|Lüneburg]]. The [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]] spread in the 16th century, and Lutheran administrators such as [[e:philip-sigismund-of-brunswick-wolfenbuttel|Philip Sigismund of Brunswick-Wolfenbüttel]] replaced Catholic bishops. In the [[e:thirty-years-war|Thirty Years War]] the see was held by the Danish prince Frederick, later [[e:frederick-iii-of-denmark|Frederick III of Denmark]].
prince-bishopric-of-verden.e: The [[e:peace-of-westphalia|Peace of Westphalia]] in 1648 secularised the see as the Duchy of [[e:verden|Verden]] and gave it to [[e:sweden|Sweden]], which ruled it with [[s:free-hanseatic-city-of-bremen|Bremen]]. [[e:denmark|Denmark]] seized it in 1712 and sold it to the [[s:electorate-of-hanover|Electorate of Hanover]] in 1715. It is now in [[e:lower-saxony|Lower Saxony]].

proto-kingdom-of-nekhen.t: The predynastic chiefdom of Hierakonpolis, home of the falcon god Horus and one of the cradles of Egyptian kingship.
proto-kingdom-of-nekhen.o: [[e:nekhen|Nekhen]], the Greek Hierakonpolis, lay on the west bank of the [[e:nile|Nile]] in southern [[e:upper-egypt|Upper Egypt]] and was among the largest settlements of the [[e:naqada|Naqada]] period. By c. 3500 BCE it had a ceremonial precinct, breweries, pottery kilns and an elite cemetery, and its chiefs controlled trade with [[e:nubia|Nubia]] and along desert routes to the south.
proto-kingdom-of-nekhen.r: [[e:nekhen|Nekhen]] was the cult centre of [[e:horus|Horus]], the falcon god later embodied by every Egyptian king. Its Tomb 100, the 'Painted Tomb', bears the earliest known Egyptian wall painting, with boats, hunting scenes and a figure smiting captives. Excavations have revealed an oval ceremonial court and an elite cemetery with buried animals, including elephants, hippopotami and baboons, signs of an ambitious ruling ideology.
proto-kingdom-of-nekhen.e: Around 3150 BCE its rulers seem to have merged with, or been overtaken by, the kings of the [[s:proto-kingdom-of-thinis|Proto-kingdom of Thinis]]. The town remained a royal religious centre: the [[e:narmer-palette|Narmer Palette]] and the [[e:scorpion-macehead|Scorpion Macehead]] were found in its temple's Main Deposit, and [[e:nekhen|Nekhen]] stayed the symbolic capital of [[e:upper-egypt|Upper Egypt]].
